The qualifier of the <s>dharmin</s>, beginning with 'desire' and ending with 'having form and formlessness,' excludes the class of eternals such as space (<s>ākāśa</s>). The other qualifier of the <s>dharmin</s>, 'other than what is fashioned by us and the like,' excludes pots and the like that have a well-known maker. And: desire, pleasure, atoms, and material form; their substrates are space, the self (<s>ātman</s>), and the atom; remoteness and proximity, by which are inferred direction and time; universals and the rest are to be understood as commonly known.

body.text: tathā narasiṃhaḥ prāha -
body.translated_text: Likewise, <s>Narasiṃha</s> states:

body.text: vijñānādhārādhīnajanma(a) janmāvacchinnātmobhayavādyavivādāspadapuruṣapūrvakavyatireki bhāvānubhāvi prameyajātam /
body.translated_text: The totality of knowable things — whose birth depends on a substratum of consciousness, which are distinguished from the unborn <s>ātman</s>, which are accepted by both disputants, which are the subject of dispute regarding being preceded by a <s>puruṣa</s> (intelligent agent), and which are positive entities capable of being experienced —

body.text: utpattimattvāt /
body.translated_text: [have a conscious cause] because of possessing origination.

body.text: yad yadākhyātasādhanasambandhi tattaduktasādhyadharmādhikaraṇam / yathā vāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: Whatever is connected with the stated reason is a locus of the stated <s>sādhya</s> property. Like cloth.

body.text: tathā cedam /
body.translated_text: And this [totality of knowables] is so [connected].

body.text: tasmādidamapi tatheti /
body.translated_text: Therefore this too is so [i.e., has a conscious cause].

body.text: asyāyamarthaḥ / prameyajātaṃ dharmi / vijñānādhārādhīnajanmeti sādhyam / ajanmāvacchinnātmeti dharmiviśeṣaṇam / etenākāśādinityavargaparihāraḥ / ubhayavādyavivādāspadapuruṣapūrvakavyatirekītyanenāpi prasiddhakartṛkaghaṭādiparihāraḥ / bhāvānubhāvīti vasturūpam / etena pradhvaṃsādiparihāraḥ / yad yadākhyātasādhanasaṃbandhīti vyāptivacanaṃ yaddharmirūpaṃ kathitasādhanayogītyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning of this is: 'the totality of knowable things' is the <s>dharmin</s>; 'having its birth dependent on a substratum of consciousness' is the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Distinguished from the unborn <s>ātman</s>' is a qualifier of the <s>dharmin</s>; by this, the class of eternals such as space is excluded. 'Accepted by both disputants, [whose] being preceded by a <s>puruṣa</s> is excluded [from the debate subject]' — by this, pots and the like that have a well-known maker are excluded. 'Positive entities capable of being experienced' — [this means] having the nature of a real thing; by this, <s>pradhvaṃsa</s> (destruction) and the like are excluded. 'Whatever is connected with the stated reason' is the statement of <s>vyāpti</s>; it means: whatever <s>dharmin</s>-form possesses the connection with the stated reason.

body.text: trilocanastu vyatirekiṇamimaṃ prayogamāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>, however, states this argument in the negative (<s>vyatirekin</s>) form:

body.text: sarvaṃ kāryaṃ prabodhavaddhetukam /
body.translated_text: Every effect has a cause possessing intelligence (<s>prabodhavaddhetuka</s>).

body.text: utpattidharmakatvāt /
body.translated_text: Because it has the nature of origination.

body.text: yannityaṃ dṛṣṭamabodhavaddhetukaṃ tasyākāśādestathotpattirnāstīti dṛṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Whatever is seen to be permanent is seen to lack a cause possessing intelligence — and of that, such as space, it is seen that there is no origination.

body.text: utpattidharmakaṃ ca pakṣīkṛtamasmadādivinirmitetarat /
body.translated_text: And what is taken as the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject) — [namely, the world] other than what is fashioned by us and the like — has the nature of origination.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 40#)
tasmād bodhavaddhetukamiti /
body.translated_text: (Nibandha 40) Therefore it too has a cause possessing intelligence.

body.text: punardvyaṇukeśvarasiddhau trilocana eva prāha -
body.translated_text: Furthermore, for the establishment of <s>Īśvara</s> through [the example of] <s>dvyaṇuka</s> (dyads), <s>Trilocana</s> himself states:

body.text: vivādāspadībhūtaṃ dvitvamātmotpattau kasyacidekaikaviṣayāṃ buddhimapekṣate /
body.translated_text: The duality (<s>dvitva</s>) that is the subject of dispute requires, for its production, the cognition of some one [being] having each [atom] as its object.

body.text: dvitvasaṃkhyātvāt /
body.translated_text: Because it is <s>dvitvasaṃkhyā</s> (the number 'two').

body.text: yad yad dvitvaṃ tat tathā / yathā dve dravye /
body.translated_text: Whatever is duality is so [i.e., requires such a cognition]. Like [the duality inhering in] two substances.

body.text: tathā cedaṃ dvayaṇukagataṃ dvitvam /
body.translated_text: And this duality residing in <s>dvyaṇukas</s> (dyads) is likewise [a duality].

body.text: tasmāttatheti /
body.translated_text: Therefore it is so [i.e., requires such a cognition].

body.text: yasya cātra buddhirapekṣyate sa bhagavānīśvaraḥ //
body.translated_text: And the one whose cognition is required here is the Blessed Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>).

body.text: tathā ca vācaspatiḥ pramāṇayati -
body.translated_text: And likewise, <s>Vācaspati</s> establishes [the thesis] by means of valid cognition:

body.text: vivādāṣyāsitatanutarugirisāgarādayaḥ upādānādyabhijñakartṛkāḥ /
body.translated_text: The body, trees, mountains, oceans, and the like that are the subject of dispute have a maker who knows the material cause and other [factors].

body.text: kāryatvāt /
body.translated_text: Because of being effects.

body.text: yadyat kāryaṃ tattadupādānādyabhijñakartṛkam / yathā prāsādādi /
body.translated_text: Whatever is an effect has a maker who knows the material cause and other [factors]. Like a palace and the like.

body.text: tathā va vivādādhyāsitāstanvādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: And the body, trees, and the like that are the subject of dispute are likewise [effects].

body.text: tasmāttatheti /
body.translated_text: Therefore they are so [i.e., have such a maker].

body.text: evaṃ sthitvā sthitvā pravṛttidharmakatvāt, sanniveśavattvāt, arthakriyākāritvādityādayo hetavaḥ kathitapañcāvayavakrameṇa boddhavyā iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, having established [the argument] in this manner, the reasons — [such as] 'because of having the nature of activity after remaining [quiescent] for a time,' 'because of possessing arrangement,' 'because of being capable of serving a purpose' and so forth — should be understood in the format of the previously stated five-membered [syllogism].

body.text: tadetaddurmativispanditaṃ jagadandhīkaraṇaṃ na satāmupekṣitumucitamiti kiñciducyate / iha khalu buddhimatkāryamātrayoḥ sādhyasādhanayoḥ sarvopasaṃhāravatī vyāptistāvadavaśyaṃ grahītavyā / anyathā gamyagamakabhāvāyogāt / sā ca gṛhyamāṇā kiṃ kāraṇakāryamātrayoriva viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalād grāhyā / yadvāgnidhūmayoriva viśiṣṭānvayavyatirekagrahaṇapravaṇaviśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ boddhavyā / uta svavyavasthayā sapakṣāsapakṣayorbhūyodarśanādarśanābhyāṃ pratyetavyā / āhosvit sapakṣāsapakṣayoḥ sakṛddarśanādarśanābhyāṃ jñātavyeti catvāro vikalpāḥ /
body.translated_text: This reckless display of foolish reasoning, which blinds the world, is not fit to be disregarded by the wise — therefore something [in refutation] is said. Now, for [the relationship between] effect-ness in general and an intelligent [cause] as <s>sādhya</s> (thesis) and <s>sādhana</s> (reason), the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) covering all instances must certainly be grasped — otherwise, the relation of what is to be inferred and the inferential mark would be impossible. And when grasping it, [is it done] through the force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) that refutes the contrary, as in [the case of] cause and effect in general? Or is it to be understood through distinguished perception and non-perception that are inclined toward grasping distinguished positive and negative concomitance, as in [the case of] fire and smoke? Or is it to be ascertained by its own determination, through frequent seeing and not-seeing in the <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>asapakṣa</s>? Or is it to be known from a single seeing and not-seeing in the <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>asapakṣa</s>? — [these are] the four alternatives.

body.text: na tāvadādyaḥ pakṣaḥ / sādhyaviparyaye buddhimadabhāve kāryatvasāmānyasya sādhanasya bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt / nanu bādhakapramāṇābhāvo 'siddhaḥ / tathā hīdaṃ kāryatvaṃ yathā buddhimatā vyāptamiṣyate tathā deśakālasvabhāvaniyatatvenāpi, kādācitkakāraṇasannidhimattayāpi, sāmagrīkāryatvenāpi vyāptamupalabdham / sa ca deśādi niyamaḥ kādācitkakāraṇasannidhiḥ sāmagrī vā buddhimatpūrvikā siddhā / yadi punaracetanāni cetanānadhiṣṭhitāni kāryaṃ kuryuḥ tato patra kvacanāvasthitāni janayeyuriti na deśakālasvabhāvaniyataprasavaṃ kāryamupalabhyeta /
body.translated_text: The first alternative does not hold, because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) that contradicts the proving property — effectness (<s>kāryatva</s>) in general — in the absence of an intelligent [agent], which is the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved). Objection: The absence of a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> is not established. For this effectness, just as it is accepted as pervaded by [the presence of] an intelligent [agent], is also observed as pervaded by spatial, temporal, and essential determination; by the proximity of an occasional cause; and by being the effect of a totality of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>). And that determination by space and so forth, or the proximity of an occasional cause, or the totality of conditions, is [itself] established as preceded by an intelligent [agent]. For if unconscious things, not directed by a conscious [agent], were to produce effects, then, being situated anywhere, they would produce [effects] anywhere; and thus effects determined by space, time, and nature would not be observed.

body.text: hetusamavadhānajanmatayā na kāryaṃ pratyekaṃ kāraṇairjanyata iti cet / samavadhānameva tu kāraṇānāṃ kutaḥ / kādācitkaparipākādadṛṣṭaviśeṣāditi cet / nanvayamacetanaḥ kathaṃ yathāvat kāraṇāni sannidhāpayet / no khalu kvacidavasthitāni (#Nibandh 41#) daṇḍādīni vinā kumbhakāraprayatnamadṛṣṭaviśeṣavaśādeva parasparaṃ sannidhīyante / sannihitāni vā kāryāya prabhavantīti buddhimatā deśakālasvabhāvaniyamasya kādācitkakāraṇasannidheḥ sāmagryāśca vyāptisiddhiḥ / buddhimadabhāve caiṣāṃ vyāpakānāṃ nivṛttau nivartamānaṃ kāryatvaṃ buddhimatpūrvakatvena vyāpyata iti pratibandhasiddhaye vyāpakānupalambhatrayamupanyastam / tathā ca na kāryaṃ buddhimatparityāgāt ahetukameva bhavatīti saṃbhāvyam, deśakālasvabhāvaniyamābhāvaprasaṅgāt / nāpi buddhimato 'nyasmādeva bhavatīti śaṅkanīyam, sakṛdapyutpādābhāvaprasaṅgāt / na cānyasmādasmādapi bhavatīti saṃbhāvyam, aniyatahetutve 'hetutvaprasaṅgāt / tathā buddhimantamantareṇācetanena karaṇe sarvadā kriyāyā avirāmaprasaṅgaścetyapi viparyayabādhakamatiprasaṅgacatuṣṭayaṃ vyāptiprasādhakamiti kāryatvasya hetupūrvakatvamiva buddhimatpūrvakatvamapyavāryamiti cet /
body.translated_text: If [objected]: 'Effects are not produced by causes individually, but through the convergence of causes' — then, from where does the convergence of causes [arise]? If from occasional maturation or from a special unseen force (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) — but this [unseen force] is unconscious: how can it properly bring causes together? Surely, sticks and the like, situated anywhere, do not come together of their own accord through the power of a special unseen force alone, without the effort of a potter. Nor, when brought together, do they produce an effect [without such effort]. Therefore, the pervasion of spatial-temporal-essential determination, occasional-cause proximity, and the totality of conditions by an intelligent [agent] is established. And when, in the absence of an intelligent [agent], these pervaders are absent, effectness, which ceases [along with them], is pervaded by being preceded by an intelligent [agent]. Thus, a threefold non-perception of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) has been presented for establishing the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>). Accordingly, it is not to be supposed that, by abandoning an intelligent [agent], the effect simply arises without a cause, because there would be the undesirable consequence of the absence of spatial-temporal-essential determination. Nor should it be suspected that it arises from something other than an intelligent [agent], because there would be the undesirable consequence of never arising even once. Nor is it to be supposed that it arises from both [the other and this], because if the cause were indeterminate, there would be the undesirable consequence of its not being a cause at all. Moreover, if unconscious [entities] produced [effects] without an intelligent [agent], there would be the undesirable consequence of activity never ceasing. Thus, the four undesirable consequences that contradict the counter-thesis serve to establish the pervasion. Therefore, just as effectness is inevitably preceded by a cause, so too its being preceded by an intelligent [agent] cannot be denied — if [so objected].

body.text: atrocyate / sidhyatyevedaṃ manorājyaṃ yadi deśakālasvabhāvaniyamasya kādācitkakāraṇasannidheḥ sāmagryāśca buddhimatpūrvakatvena vyāptiḥ sidhyati / kevalametadeva durāpam / buddhimadabhāve 'pi hi svahetubalasamutpannasannidhe(ḥ) pratiniyatadeśakālaśaktinācetanenāpi sāmagrīlakṣaṇakāraṇaviśeṣeṇa kriyamāṇāni deśakālasvabhāvaniyamakādācitkakāraṇasannidhisāmagrīkāryatvāni yujyanta iti sandigdhāsiddhā vyāpakānupalabdhayaḥ //
body.translated_text: To this we reply: This castle in the air would succeed only if the being-preceded-by-an-intelligent-agent of spatial-temporal-essential determination, occasional-cause proximity, and the totality of conditions were established. But it is not established. For:

body.text: buddhimadabhāve samavadhānameva kuta iti cet / tadapi cetanānadhiṣṭhitayathoktācetanasāmagrīviśeṣādeva / so 'pi tādṛśādityanādyacetanasāmagrīparamparāto 'pideśādiniyamasaṃbhāvanāyāṃ nāvaśyaṃ buddhimadapekṣā / ghaṭāderdeśakālasvabhāvaniyamaḥ kādācitkakāraṇasannidhiśca, sāmagrī ca buddhimatpūrvikā dṛṣṭā ityaparopi deśakālasvabhāvaniyamādistathaiveti cet / yadyevaṃ ghaṭādikamapi kāryaṃ bahuśo buddhimatpūrvakamupalabdhamiti sarvameva kāryaṃ tathāstu, kimanena vyāpakānu (pa)lambhopanyāsaduarvyasanena / ghaṭāderbahuśo buddhimatpūrvakatvadarśane 'pi na sarvatra kāryamātrasya tathābhāvaniścayaścet / deśādiniyamādīnāmapīdaṃ samānamiti kathamatrāpi śaṅkāvyudāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'From where does convergence [arise] in the absence of an intelligent [agent]?' — if [asked], that too [arises] from a specific totality of unconscious conditions not directed by a conscious agent, of the kind described above. And that [specific totality] too [arises] from similar [conditions], and so on — it is beginningless. Therefore, the being-preceded-by-an-intelligent-agent is not established. Even if you say that the totality of conditions is preceded by an intelligent agent, that intelligent agent too [requires] a cause, and so on — resulting in infinite regress, nothing at all is accomplished.

body.text: astu tadā pratyakṣameva sarvatra vyāptigrāhakamiti cet / na tarhi viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalād vyāptigrahanirvāhaḥ / pratyakṣaṃ ca tatrāśaktamiti dvitīyavikalpāvasare nivedayiṣyate / tathā siddhe kāryakāraṇabhāve dhūmasyāhetukotpatāvanyasmādevo tpattāvanyasmādapyutpattau saṃbhāvyamānāyāṃ deśādiniyamābhāva (klṛptahetu) tyāga (anya) hetutvaprasaṅgāḥ saṅgacchante / prastute tu buddhimatkāryamātrayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo nādyāpi siddhaḥ / sādhayituṃ vā śakyaḥ / na cācetanasya kartṛtve kriyāyā (#Nibandh 42#) avirāmaprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ / na hyacetanamityeva sarvadā sāmarthyayogi, tasyāpi svahetuparamparāpratibaddhasāmarthyatvādityacetanakāraṇaviśeṣaparamparāsaṃbhāvanāyāṃ nāvaśyaṃ buddhimadākṣepa iti svamatavyālopaviklavavikrośitamātramevedaṃ na punaratra nyāyagandho 'pi /
body.translated_text: If [objected]: 'Then let perception alone be the grasper of pervasion everywhere' — then the establishment of pervasion through the force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that contradicts the counter-thesis is not maintained. [And] perception too

body.text: tadevaṃ vyāptisādhanārthamupanyastaṃ vyāpakānupalambhatrayaṃ sandigdhāsiddhamatiprasaṅgatucaṣṭayaṃ ca buddhimatkāryamātrayorvyāptyasiddhāvasaṅgatam / ataḥ kāryatvaṃ sādhanaṃ sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvādanaikāntikam //
body.translated_text: does not establish [the pervasion]. Thus, the threefold non-perception of the pervader presented for establishing the pervasion, and the fourfold [set of] undesirable consequences — which are of doubtful non-establishment — merely [prove] that effects are preceded by an intelligent [agent] in general,

body.text: atra vācaspatiḥ prāha -
body.translated_text: On this, <s>Vācaspati</s> [Miśra] says:

body.text: sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvaṃ nāma hetudoṣa eva na bhavati / tatkathaṃ nirasyate / tathā hi ya eva vipakṣe dṛṣṭo hetuḥ sa eva prameyatvādivadabhimataṃ na sādhayet / yastu mahatāpi prayatnena mṛgyamāṇo 'sapakṣe nopalakṣitaḥ sa kathaṃ sādhyaṃ na sādhayet /
body.translated_text: 'Having doubtful exclusion from the counter-instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>) is not actually a defect of the reason. How then is it refuted? For the very reason that is observed in the counter-instance',

body.text: avaśyaṃśaṅkayā bhāvyaṃ niyāmakamapaśyatām /
body.translated_text: 'Doubt must necessarily arise for those who do not see a determining factor.'

body.text: iti tu datāvakāśā laukikamaryādātikrameṇa saṃśayapiśācī labdhaprasarā na kvacinnāstoti nāyaṃ kvacitpravarteta / sarvasyaivārthasya kathañcicchaṅkāspadatvādarśanāt / anarthaśaṅkāyāśca prekṣāvatāṃ nivṛttyaṅgatvāt / antataḥ snigdhānnapānopayoge 'pi maraṇadarśanāt / tasmāt prāmāṇikalokayātrāmanupālayatā yathādarśanaṃ śaṅkanīyam, na tvadṛṣṭamapi / viśeṣasmṛtyapekṣo hi saṃśayo nāsmṛterbhavati / na ca smṛtirananubhūtacare bhavati /
body.translated_text: [He argues:] Having thus been given an opening, the demon of doubt, having overstepped the bounds of worldly convention, having gained free rein, would exist nowhere and [hence] one would never act anywhere. For all

body.text: taduktaṃ mīmāṃsāvārttikakṛtā adhyuṣṭasahasrikāyām -
body.translated_text: Thus the author of the <s>Mīmāṃsāvārttika</s> (<s>Kumārila</s>) said in the <s>Adhyuṣṭasāhasrikā</s>:

body.text: nāśaṅkā niḥpramāṇiketi /
body.translated_text: 'Suspicion without a [supporting] <s>pramāṇa</s> [is groundless].'

body.text: tathā tenaiva bṛhaṭṭīkāyām -
body.translated_text: And the same [author] in the <s>Bṛhaṭṭīkā</s> [says]:

children.translated_text: 'He who, out of delusion, would imagine an obstruction that has not arisen,

children.text: sa sarvavyavahāreṣu saṃśayātmā kṣayaṃ vrajet // iti //
children.translated_text: that person, being of a doubting nature in all transactions, would come to ruin.' Thus.

body.text: tadetat pralāpamātram / na hi mahatāpi prayatnena vipakṣe mṛgyamāṇasya hetoradarśanamātreṇa vyatirekaḥ sidhyati / tathā hi vipakṣe heturnopalabhyata ityanena tadupalambhakapramāṇanivṛttirucyate / pramāṇaṃ ca prameyasya kāryam, nākāraṇaṃ viṣaya iti nyāyāt / na ca kāryanivṛttau kāraṇanivṛtirupalabdhā, nirdhūmasyāpi bahnerupalambhāt / yadi punaḥ pramāṇasattayā prameyasattā vyāptā syāt, tadā yuktametat / kevalamiyameva vyāptirasaṃbhavinī, sarvasya sarvadarśitvaprasaṅgāt / tannādarśanamātreṇa vyatirekasiddhiḥ / yathoktam -
body.translated_text: All this is mere babbling. For the exclusion [of the reason from the counter-instance] is not established by the mere non-observation of the reason when sought in the counter-instance, even with the greatest effort. For

children.translated_text: (Nibandh 43)
'All non-observation [by another] is doubtful; one's own non-observation is deviant [from the universal claim];
because of the real existence [of grass] even when unseen in the crevices of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains — like <s>dūrvā</s> grass.' Thus,

body.text: sakalavipakṣasyārvācīnaṃ pratyadṛśyatvāt //
body.translated_text: because the entirety of the counter-instance is not visible to a person of the present.

body.text: yaccoktam - saṃśayapiśācī labdhaprasarā na kvacinnāstīti na kvacit pravarteteti / tadasaṅgatam / arthasaṃśayasyāpi prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛttyaṅgatvāt pravṛttiravirodhinyeva / anarthasandehaḥ sarvatra kartuṃ śakyate / antataḥ snigdhānnapānopayoge 'pi maraṇadarśanādapravṛttiriti cet / duarjñānametat / tathā hi arthasandeho 'narthasandeho veti nāyaṃ ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaḥ / kintvarthonmukhaḥ sandeho 'rthasandehaḥ, anarthonmukhaḥ sandeho 'nartha sandeha iti śākapārthivādivanmadhyapadalopī samāsaḥ / evaṃ sati snigdhānnapānādāvarthasandeha eva, tajjātīyasya svaparasantāne dṛṣṭipuṣṭyādyarthasya koṭiśaḥ karaṇadarśanāt, maraṇāderanarthasya kvacit kadāciddarśanāt / etadviviparīto 'narthasandeho draṣṭavyaḥ / tasmāt pramāṇādivārthasaṃśayādapi prekṣāvatāṃ tatra tatra pravṛttirdurvāraiva //
body.translated_text: And as for what was said — 'the demon of doubt, having gained free rein, would exist nowhere, and hence one would never act anywhere' — that is incoherent. For even doubt about the object, for one who examines [matters],

body.text: yadapīdaṃ lapitaṃ yathādarśanaṃ śaṅkanīyaṃ nādṛṣṭapūrvamapi viśeṣasmṛtyapekṣo hi saṃśaya ityādi / tadasaṃbaddham / sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvādeva paryudāsavṛttyā vasvantararūpāt sarvatra saṃśayotpatteḥ / kiṃca viśeṣasmṛtyapekṣa evāyaṃ saṃśayaḥ / tathā hi lakṣaṇayogitvāyogitvābhyāmeva tajjātīyātajjātīye vaktavye / anyathā lakṣaṇapraṇayanamanarthakaṃ syāt / evaṃ ca sati tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇapratibandhaviyogitvena sādhāraṇena dharmeṇa prameyatvadhūmatvakāryatvādīnāṃ tvanmatena sajātīyatvāt prameyatvavyabhicāradarśanameva śaṅkāmupasthāpayatīti yathādarśanamevedamāśaṅkitam /
body.translated_text: And as for this prattle — 'Doubt should be raised only with respect to what has been observed; doubt does not apply to what has never been observed before, because doubt requires the recollection of a specific [alternative]' and so forth — that is irrelevant. [For] the proof of exclusion from the counter-instance [requires more than mere non-observation]

body.text: yaśca kumārilasya sākṣitvenopanyāsaḥ sa khalu
body.translated_text: And as for the citation of <s>Kumārila</s> as a witness — that indeed

body.text: dadhibhāṇḍe viḍālaḥ sākṣīti
body.translated_text: does not go beyond the saying 'The cat is the witness at the curd-pot'

body.text: pravādaṃ nātipatatīti kimatra vaktavyam / tadevaṃ vipakṣe 'darśanamātreṇa heto 'rvyatirekāsiddheḥ sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvaṃ nāma hetudūṣaṇaṃ durvārameva / ata evāsyopanyāso 'doṣodbhāvanaṃ nāma nigrahasthānamiti yadanenāveditaṃ tadapi sāvadyam / pratyutāsmin hetoḥ saddūṣaṇe parihartavye nāyaṃ hetudoṣo 'to na parihartavyo 'sya copanyāso 'doṣodbhāvanaṃ nāma nigrahasthānamiti bruvannayameva tapasvī svamatena niranuyojyānuyogalakṣaṇena nigrahasthānena nigṛhyata iti kṛpāmarhati / tadevaṃ viparyayabādhakapramāṇābhāvādavyāpterasiddheḥ
body.translated_text: [i.e., is absurdly self-defeating] — so what is there to say about that? Thus, since the exclusion of the reason [from the counter-instance] is not established by mere non-observation in the counter-instance, the doubtful exclusion from the counter-instance

body.text: sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvādanaikāntikaḥ kāryatvalakṣaṇo hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: The reason characterized as effectness (<s>kāryatva</s>) is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) because of having doubtful exclusion from the counter-instance.

body.text: athāgnidhūmayoriva viśiṣṭānvayavyatirekagrahaṇapravaṇaviśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ vyaptirniśvīyata iti dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ / atrocyate / kiṃ dṛśyaśarīropādhinā buddhimanmātreṇa vyāptirgṛhyate, āhosvit dṛśyaśarīropādhiviśureṇa dṛśyādṛśyasādhāraṇeneti (#Nibandh 44#) vikalpau / yadyādyaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadā tathābhūtasādhyamantareṇāpyutpadyamāne viṭapādau kāryatvadarśanāt prameyatvādivat sādhāraṇānaikāntiko hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, if pervasion is ascertained — as in the case of fire and smoke — through a special perception-and-non-perception directed toward grasping the specific positive and negative concomitance, [that constitutes] the second alternative.

body.text: nanu vṛkṣādayaḥ pakṣīkṛtāḥ / kathaṃ tairvyabhicāraḥ / trividho hi bhāvarāśiḥ / sandigdhakartṛko yathā vṛkṣādiḥ / prasiddhakartṛko yathā ghaṭādiḥ / akartṛko yathā ākāśādiḥ / tatra prasiddhakartṛke ghaṭādau pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ vyāptimādāya sandehapade kṣmāruhādau kāryatvamupasaṃhṛtya buddhimānanumīyate / na punarasau vyabhicāraviṣayo bhavitumarhati /
body.translated_text: Objection: Trees and the like have been made the subject of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>). How is there deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) with respect to them? For the totality of entities is threefold: those of doubtful authorship, such as trees and the like; those of known authorship, such as a pot and the like; and those without an author, such as space and the like. Among these, with respect to pots and the like, whose authorship is well-known, the invariable concomitance is taken through perceptual non-apprehension, and then, transferring the property of being an effect to the doubtful case of trees and the like, an intelligent [maker] is inferred. And that [subject] should not be the locus of deviation.

body.text: yadāha - na sādhyenaiva vyabhicāra iti / ayuktametat / na hi vyabhicāraviṣaya eva pakṣe bhavitumarhati,
body.translated_text: As [the opponent] says: 'There is no deviation with respect to what is to be proved itself.' This is unjust. For the subject of the thesis should not be the very locus of deviation,

body.text: sandigdhe hetuvacanād vyasto hetoranāśrayaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Since the statement of the reason in the doubtful [case] means the counter-positive of the reason has no locus [there]'

body.text: iti nyāyāt / vyabhicāraviṣayatā ca dṛśyaśarīropādherbuddhimanmātrasya tṛṇādyutpattau dṛśyānupalambhena pratikṣiptatvāt / tataśca kṣmādharādireva sandigdhakartṛkaḥ pakṣīkartumucitaḥ kṣmāruhādistvacetanakartṛka iti caturtho bhāvarāśirneṣṭavyaḥ / atha vyabhicāracamatkārāstrividhabhāvarāśivyavasthāpanārthaṃ ca viṭapādau pratyakṣāpratikṣiptena dṛśyādṛśyasādhāraṇena buddhimanmātreṇa vyaptiravagamyata iti dvitīyaḥ saṅkalpaḥ / tadā viṭapādau buddhimanmātrasya saṃbhāvyamānatvāt na sādhāraṇānaikāntikatāṃ brū maḥ / kiṃ tarhi vyāptigrahaṇakāle dṛśyādṛśyasādhāraṇasya buddhimanmātrasya sādhyasyādṛśyatayā dṛśyānupalambhena vyatirekāsiddhervyāpterabhāvāt sandigdhavyāvṛttikatvamācakṣmahe / tathā hi / yadā kumbhakāravyāpārātpūrvaṃ kumbhasya vyatirekaḥ pratyetavyastadā na sādhyābhāvakṛto ghaṭavyatirekaḥ pratyetuṃ śakyaḥ / yathā hi viṭapādijanmasamaye buddhimanmātrasyādṛśyatvena niṣeddhumaśakyatvāt sattāsaṃbhāvanā tathā ghaṭādāvapi vyatirekaniścayakāle buddhimanmātrasyādṛśyatvāt sattvasaṃbhāvanāyāṃ sādhyābhāvaprayuktasya sādhanābhāvasyāsiddhatvena vyāpterabhāvāt kathaṃ na sandigdhavyatireko hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: — by this principle. And [the subject's] being the locus of deviation [is established] because 'mere intelligent being,' with the condition of having a visible body, is rejected by the non-apprehension of the visible in the production of grass and the like. Therefore, it is the earth-bearer (mountain) and the like — which are of doubtful authorship — that are properly made the subject of the thesis. And a fourth class of entities must be postulated, namely trees and the like as having a non-sentient author. Now, if the second hypothesis is [adopted] — for the sake of establishing the wonder of deviation and the arrangement of the threefold class of entities, the invariable concomitance is apprehended with respect to trees and the like through 'mere intelligent being' in general, which is common to the visible and invisible and is not rejected by perception — then, since 'mere intelligent being' is possible with respect to trees and the like, we do not assert the fallacy of being an inconclusive reason common [to both sapakṣa and vipakṣa]. Rather, since at the time of grasping the invariable concomitance, the thing to be proved — 'mere intelligent being,' which is common to the visible and invisible — is invisible, the exclusion [of the reason from the counter-example] cannot be established by the non-apprehension of the visible, and hence the invariable concomitance is absent — this is what we call 'having a doubtful exclusion.' For when the absence of the pot must be ascertained prior to the operation of the potter, the absence of the pot caused by the absence of the thing to be proved cannot be ascertained. For just as at the time of the birth of trees and the like, since 'mere intelligent being' cannot be negated due to its invisibility, there is the supposition of its existence — so too, at the time of ascertaining the exclusion with respect to pots and the like, since 'mere intelligent being' is invisible, there is the supposition of its existence; and since the absence of the means of proof, caused by the absence of what is to be proved, is unestablished, and hence the invariable concomitance is absent — how is the reason not one of doubtful exclusion?

body.text: yathoktam - na ca yathā kāryaṃ ca syānnirupādānaṃ ceti nāśaṅkanīyam, tathā kāryaṃ ca bhavedakartṛkaṃ ceti nāśaṅkanīyamiti, tatrāpi kāryaṃ ca syānnirupādānaṃ ca bhavediti na vaktavyamiti kenaiva pratārito 'si / yadi hyatra pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ vyāptirgṛhyate tadā kathamupādānapūrvakaṃ kāryamātra sidhyati / vyāptigrahaṇaprakārāntaraṃ ca tvayāpi nopanyastam / dṛśyādṛśyasādhāraṇayorupādānakāryamātrayordṛśyaviṣayābhyāṃ pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ vyāpterabhyūhitumaśakyatvāt / svamatavyālopaprasaṅgastu pramāṇacintāvasare 'prāptāvakāśaḥ / viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalādvātra vyāptisiddhiḥ / tathā hi yathāṅkurādikaṃ kāryaṃ niyatadeśakālasvabhāvatvena vyāptaṃ tathā śālitvādināpi (#Nibandh 45#) jātibhedena vyāptamupalabdham / tataścānupādānapūrvakatvādvipakṣātmanaḥ śālitvādijātibhedasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau nivartamānaṃ kāryatvamupādānapūrvakatve viśrāmyat tena vyāptaṃ sidhyati / na cānupādānenāpi kriyamāṇaḥ śālitvādijātibhedo yujyate, upādānaṃ vinā kṛtānupādānādeva kevalādekajātīyakāraṇāt tadatajjātīyakāryotpattau kāryabhedasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgāt taduktam -
body.translated_text: As it is said: 'And just as one should not suspect that it might be an effect and yet without a material cause, likewise [one should not suppose] that it might be an effect and yet without a maker' —

body.text: tadatadrūpiṇo bhāvāstadatadrūpahetujāḥ //iti /
body.translated_text: 'Entities that are of such-and-such a nature are born from causes of such-and-such a nature.'

body.text: anyathānupādānādeva kṣityāderaṅkurādikamutpadyetetyaṅkurārthino bījaṃ nānusareyuḥ / tasmādviparyayabādhakapramāṇabalādeva kāryatvasya hetumātrapūrvakatvenevopādānapūrvakatvenāpi vyāptisiddhiriti nyāyaḥ / na caivaṃ kāryamātrakartṛtvamātrayorapi vyāptiprasādhakaṃ viparyaye bādhakaṃ pramāṇamasti, pūrvoktasya vyāpakānupalambhatrayasyāti prasaṅgacatuṣṭayasya ca prāgeva pratyākhyātatvāt / tasmātkāryaṃ ca syāt na ca dhīmatkartṛpūrvakamiti śaṅkāṃ kurvāṇaḥ prativādī vinā caraṇamardanādinā niṣeddhumaśakyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Otherwise, since sprouts and the like would arise from the earth itself without a material cause, those desiring sprouts would not seek seeds. Therefore, from the counter-example [it follows that]...

body.text: nanu yadi dṛśyāgnidhūmasāmānyayoriva dṛśyātmanoreva kāryakāraṇasāmānyayoḥ pratyakṣānupalambhato vyāptistadā paracittānumānakṣatiḥ / svaparasantānasādhāraṇena dṛśyādṛśyena cinmātreṇa pratyakṣato dṛśyaviṣayād vyāptigrahaṇāyogādityapi na vācyam / bāhyārthasthitau hi svaparasantānasādhāraṇasya cinmātrasya svarūpeṇādṛśyatve 'pi dṛśyaśarīreṇa sahaikasāmagrīpratibandhādavinirbhāgavartitvamastyeva / tato yathā ghaṭaviṣayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ rūpaikadeśapravṛttamapyavyabhicārāt samudāyopasthāpakam tathā dehagrāhakameva pratyakṣaṃ dehāvinirbhāgavarti svaparasantānasādhāraṇaṃ cinmātraṃ kampādervyāpakamadhigacchati / tadevaṃ dṛśyātmano dṛśyāvinirbhāgavartino vā padārthasya vyāvahārikapaṭupratyakṣataḥ siddhirvyāptigrahaśca, na tu tathātvavinākṛtādṛśyasādhāraṇacinmātrasyeti santānāntarānumānamucitam / tasmād yadi pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ vyāptigrahastadā dṛśyenaiva dṛśyasyeti nyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: If, just as with visible fire and smoke in general, the invariable concomitance between the effect-nature and the cause-nature is grasped through perceptual non-apprehension only when both are visible,

body.text: tadayaṃ saṃkṣepārthaḥ -
body.translated_text: this is the summary meaning:

children.translated_text: If a supersensory maker is postulated to destroy the presence [of the reason] in the counter-example of the property of being an effect,

children.text: kartā ced vyatirekasiddhividhurā vyāptiḥ kathaṃ sidhyati /
children.translated_text: then how can the invariable concomitance, which is devoid of the establishment of the exclusion, be established?
But if a visible maker is resorted to with the mind [seeking] to establish the exclusion,

children.text: tattyāge 'pi tadā tṛṇādikamiti vyaktaṃ vipakṣe kṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: then, even upon his abandonment, at that moment, grass and the like clearly [exist] in the counter-example.

body.text: ato na pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāmapi vyāptisiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, even through perceptual non-apprehension, the establishment of the invariable concomitance is not achieved.

body.text: nanu bhūyodarśanādarśanābhyāṃ pratibandhaḥ pratīyata iti tṛtīya evāsmākaṃ pakṣaḥ / kevalaṃ sa pratibandho na tadutpattilakṣaṇo grahītavyaḥ / kintu svābhāvikaḥ / sa eva darśanādarśanābhyāṃ pratīyate / tathā caitamevārthaṃ vācaspatiḥ prāha -
body.translated_text: Objection: The natural connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is ascertained through repeated observation and non-observation — this is precisely our third thesis. However, that connection

body.text:
(#Nibandh 46#)
na sapakṣāsapakṣayordarśanābhyāṃ kāryatvasya gamakatvamapi tu svābhāvikapratibandhabalāditi brū maḥ / sa eva tu sapakṣāsapakṣayordarśanādarśanābhyāṃ bakṣyamāṇena krameṇa pratīyata iti tadupakṣepo 'pi yuktaḥ / tena yasyāsau svābhāvikapratibandho niyataḥ siddhaḥ sa eva gamako gamyaścetaraḥ sambandhīti yujyate / tathā hi dhūmādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ saha sambandhaḥ svābhāviko na tu vahnyādīnāṃ dhūmādibhiḥ / te hi vinā dhūmādibhirupalabhyante / yadā tvārdrendhanasaṃbandhamanubhavanti tadā dhūmādibhiḥ saṃbadhyante / tasmād vahnyādīnāmārdrendhanādyupādhikṛtaḥ sambandho na tu svābhāvikastato na niyataḥ / svābhāvikastu dhūmādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ sambandhaḥ, tadupādheranupalabhyamānatvāt / kvacid vyabhicārasyādarśanāt / anupalabhyamānasyāpi kalpanānupapatteḥ / na cānupalabhyamāno darśanānarhatayā sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvena sandihyamāna upādhiḥ saṃbandhasya svābhāvikatvaṃ pratibadhnātīti yuktam / yathoktaṃ prāk seyaṃ saṃśayapiśācītyādi / tasmādupādhiṃ prayatnenānviṣyanto 'nupalabhamānā nāstītyavagamya svābhāvikatvaṃ niścinumaḥ //
body.translated_text: is not [established] through observation in the concordant and discordant instances of the property of being an effect; rather, on the basis of the natural connection (<s>svābhāvikapratibandha</s>),

body.text: syādetat / anyasyānyena sahākāraṇena cet svābhāvikaḥ sambandho bhavet, sarvaṃ sarveṇa sambadhyeta / tathā ca sarvaṃ sarvasmād gamyeta / athānyaccedanyasya kāryaṃ kasmāt sarvaṃ sarvasmānna bhavati anyatvāviśeṣāt / tataśca sa evātiprasaṅgaḥ / yadyucyeta svabhāvā na paryanuyojyāḥ / tasmādanyatvāviśeṣe 'pi kiñcideva kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ ca kiñciditi / nanveṣa svabhāvānanuyogo 'kāryakāraṇabhūtānāmapi svabhāvaprativandhe tulya eva / tasmād yatkiñcidetadapi //
body.translated_text: [someone may say:] If there were a natural connection of one thing with another merely through co-occurrence, then everything would be connected with everything. [Reply:] ...

body.text:
kimasya saṃbandhasya vyāptigrāhakaṃ pramāṇamiti cet /
ucyate bhūyodarśanagamyā hi vyāptiḥ sāmānyadharmayoḥ /
body.translated_text: If asked: What is the <s>pramāṇa</s> that grasps this connection? [We reply:] The invariable concomitance is indeed apprehended through repeated observation — in the generality of <s>dharma</s> (property)...

body.text: iti prasiddhameva / asyāyamarthaḥ kāśikākāreṇa vyākhyātaḥ - prācīnānekadarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāye carame darśane cetasi vakāsti dhūmasyāgniniyatasvabhāvatvam, ratnatattvamiva parokṣakasya, śabdatattvamiva vyākaraṇasmṛtisaṃskṛtasya, brāhmaṇatvamiva mātāpitṛsaṃbandhasmaraṇasacivasyetyādi / na hyetat sarvamāpātato na pratibhātamiti purastādapi pratibhāsamānamanyathā bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: This is well known. Its meaning has been explained by the author of the <s>Kāśikā</s>: 'When a cognition aided by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated by prior repeated observations...'

body.text: trilocanena punarayamarthaḥ kathitaḥ - bhūyodarśanena bhūyodarśanasahāyena manasā tajjātīyānāṃ saṃbandho gṛhīto bhavati / ato dhūmo 'gniṃ na vyabhicarati / tadvayabhicārepyupādhirahitaṃ sambandhamatikrāmet / hetorvipakṣaśaṅkānivartakaṃ pramāṇamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptopādhivirahaniścayaheturanupalambhākhyaṃ pratyakṣameva / tataḥ siddhaḥ svābhāvikaḥ sambandhaḥ / tathehāpīti svamataṃ vyavasthāpitamiti //
body.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>, however, has stated this meaning as follows: 'Through repeated observation, with the aid of the mind assisted by repeated observation, [one apprehends] the connection of those of the same class...'

body.text:
(#Nibandh 47#)
vācaspatināpīdamuktam - abhijātamaṇibhedatattvavad bhūyodarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāyamindriyameva dhūmādīnā vahnyādibhiḥ svābhāvikasaṃbandhagrāhīti yuktamiti //
body.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s> too has said this: 'Just as one [discerns] the true nature of the varieties of excellent gems, the cognition aided by the impressions generated by repeated observation...'

body.text: atrocyate / bhede sati tadutpatteranyaḥ svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandhaḥ śabdāsphālanamātramevedam / na khalu nirūpyamāṇaḥ prāpyate / tathā hi svābhāvikastu dhūmādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ saṃbandhaḥ tadupādheranupalabhyamānatvāt / kvacid vyabhicārasyādarśanāditi tvayaivāsya lakṣaṇamuktam / etaccāsiddham / yataḥ, upādhiśabdena svato 'rthāntaramevāpekṣaṇīyamabhidhātavyam / na cārthāntaraṃ dṛśyatāniyatam, adṛśyasyāpi deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭasya saṃbhavāt / tataśca dhūmasyāpi hutāśena saha sambandhe syādupādhiḥ, na copalakṣyata iti kathamadarśanānnāstyeva yataḥ svābhāvikasaṃbandhasiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: To this we reply: Given that there is difference [between instances], 'natural connection' despite the production from that [different instance] — this is merely an empty phrase. For indeed...

body.text: atha yadyathāntaramapekṣaṇīyaṃ syāt / kathaṃ dhūma ityeva pāvakasatāniyama iti cet / nanvidameva cintyate / tadutpatterasvīkāre sahasraśo darśane 'pi kiṃ sarvatra dhūme satyavaśyamagniḥ sambhavī na veti kadācidarthāntaramupādhimapekṣya dhūmo 'pi syānnāgniriti kimatra niṣṭaṅkakāraṇam / tadupādheranupalabhyamānatvāt / kvacid vyabhicārasyādarśanāditi tu yaduktaṃ tatpratyuktameva / adṛśyasyāpyupādheḥ saṃbhāvyamānatvāt / vyabhicārasya ca pratyayāntaravaikalyenāhatyādarśane 'pi niṣeddhamaśakyatvāt / ata eva tayorbādhakābhāve 'pi sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvāt śaṅkā saṃbhavatyeva / na punastavāmunā viklavavikrośitamātreṇa vyāvartate / na caitāvatā prāmāṇikalokayātrātikramaḥ / prāmāṇikaireva sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāve nyāyaprāptasya saṃśayasya vihitatvāt / na ca sarvatrāpravṛttiprasaṅgaḥ, pramāṇādarthasaṃśayācca pravṛtterupapatteḥ / na cānarthasandehaḥ sarvatra va rtuṃ śakyate, kvacidarthonmukhatāyā eva darśanāt //
body.translated_text: Now, if some other factor were to be considered — [objection:] 'How is it that the invariable concomitance of fire with smoke [is established]?' [Reply:] But this is precisely what is being investigated. If the origination from that [cause] is not accepted, then even when [the concomitance] is observed a thousand times, the [question remains]: whenever there is smoke, must fire necessarily exist, or might smoke sometimes exist without fire, depending on some other factor (<s>upādhi</s>, adventitious condition)? What is the ground for certainty here? [Answer:] Because that adventitious condition is not apprehended. But as for the statement 'because deviation is not observed anywhere' — that has already been answered, since even an imperceptible adventitious condition can be conceived as possible, and because deviation, even when not observed due to the absence of another condition, cannot be negated. For this very reason, even in the absence of a sublating [cognition] of those two, since there is no proving or sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), doubt can indeed arise. Nor is it dispelled merely by your feeble clamoring. Nor does this violate the conduct of those who follow <s>pramāṇas</s>, for in the absence of a proving or sublating <s>pramāṇa</s>, doubt — which is the natural consequence according to logic — has been prescribed by those very experts in <s>pramāṇa</s>. Nor is there the consequence of non-activity everywhere, since activity is possible both from a <s>pramāṇa</s> [that establishes the object] and from doubt about the object. Nor can doubt about harm be raised everywhere, since in some cases one observes an inclination toward the object itself.

body.text: yaccānyatvāviśeṣe 'pi kiñcideva kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ ca kiñciditi svabhāvo yathā na paryanuyojyastathaiṣa svabhāvānanuyogo 'kāryakāraṇabhūtānāmapi svabhāvapratibandhe tulya eveti grāmyajanadhandhīkaraṇaṃ prativandīkaraṇamatilāghavamāviskaroti vācaspateḥ / tathā hi vastutvāviśeṣe 'pyagnirdahati nākāśamityatra yathā nātiprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ pramāṇasiddhatvādasyārthasya, tathā bhedāviśeṣe 'pi kiñcideva kasyacitkāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ ca kiñcidityatrāpi nātiprasaṅgāvatāraḥ / bhede sati tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānalakṣaṇasya kāryakāraṇabhāvasya pramāṇasiddhatvādeva / na caivaṃ svābhāvikasaṃbandhaśabdavācyo 'rthaḥ pramāṇasiddhaḥ kaścidasti, tallakṣaṇasyāsiddhatvāduktatvāt / na ca pratijñāsiddhe vastunyatiprasaṅgo nābhidhātavyaḥ, sarveṣāṃ sarvatra tadrūpābhyupagamamātreṇa vijetṛtvaprasaṅgāt / yadāhālaṅkārakāraḥ -
body.translated_text: And the [argument] 'Just as the nature [of things] — that only some particular [thing] is the cause despite there being no difference in otherness, and only some particular [thing] is the effect — is not to be questioned, so too this natural non-questionability is equally [applicable] to the natural connection of things that are not in a cause-effect relation' — this [argument] of <s>Vācaspati</s> [<s>Miśra</s>] exhibits excessive levity, like a street-juggler's trick to befuddle village folk. For just as, even though there is no difference in being a real entity, 'fire burns but space does not' — here the over-extension [objection] is not applicable because this fact is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> — so too, even though there is no difference in being distinct, 'only some particular [thing] is the cause of some particular [thing], and only some particular [thing] is the effect' — here too there is no entry for the over-extension [objection], precisely because the cause-effect relation, characterized by the following of positive and negative concomitance upon the distinction, is established by <s>pramāṇa</s>. But here, no meaning denoted by the phrase 'natural connection' is established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, since it has been stated that its definition is unestablished. Nor should over-extension not be stated against something whose reality is merely assumed [without proof], since there would be the absurd consequence that anyone could claim victory over everyone everywhere merely by assuming that form. As the author of the <s>Alaṅkāra</s> says:

children.translated_text: 'Having established whatever is pleasing to oneself, he who is rendered answerless by the opponent
(Nibandh 48)
should say "by the intrinsic nature of things" — in that way, the reply would follow, and everyone would be victorious.' Thus.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: kiṃ ca svābhāvikasaṃbandha iti ko 'rthaḥ / kiṃ svato bhūtaḥ svahetuto bhūto 'hetuko veti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ / na tāvadādyaḥ pakṣaḥ, svātmani kāritravirodhāt / dvitīyapakṣe tu tadutpattireva saṃbandho mukhāntareṇa svīkṛta iti na kaścidvivādaḥ / ahetukatve tu deśakālasvabhāvaniyamābhāvaprasaṅgādityasaṅgataḥ svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, what is the meaning of 'natural connection'? [Is it] arisen from itself, arisen from its own cause, or causeless? These are the three alternatives. The first alternative is untenable,

body.text: etena yaduktam - na sapakṣāsapakṣayordarśanādarśanābhyāṃ kāryatvasya gamakatvamapitu svābhāvikasaṃbandhabalāditi brūmaḥ, sa eva tu sapakṣāsapakṣayordarśanādarśanābhyāṃ vakṣyamāṇena krameṇa pratīyata iti, tadiṣṭakāmatāmātrāviṣkaraṇamiti mantavyam / svābhāvikasaṃbandhasya hyupādhinirapekṣaniyatatvaṃ lakṣaṇamuktam / tasya coktanyāyenāsiddhau bhūyodarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāye carame cetasi manasi vā tathābhūtaṃ niyatatvaṃ parisphuratīti sadayena vaktumaśakyatvāt /
body.translated_text: By this, the statement 'We do not say that the indicative capacity of being an effect [is established] through observation and non-observation in <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances) and <s>asapakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances), but rather through the force of the natural connection' — [this] is also [refuted]. Because:

body.text: yacca śabdatattvamiva brāhmaṇatvamiveti dṛṣṭāntīkṛtaṃ taddvayamapyasmān pratyasiddhamiti dṛṣṭāntayitumanucitam / abhijātamaṇibhedatattvaṃ tu parisphuratīti yuktam / tasya hyupadeśaparamparāto māṇikyavattenāpi kaṣṭenendradhanurākārajyotirādikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ niścitam / na caivaṃ svābhāvikasaṃbandhalakṣaṇaṃ tvayā svakapolaracitamapi pramāṇena niścitam / yenāsyāpi tādṛśī vyavasthā syāditi yatkiñcidetat //
body.translated_text: And the two examples adduced — 'like the reality of sound' and 'like brahmin-hood' — both of these are unestablished for us, and hence it is inappropriate to use them as examples. Noble born [status] and the like [are equally questionable].

body.text: kiṃ ca bhavatu tāvadayamanavadhāritarūpaḥ svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, tathāpi darśanādarśanābhyāmasya grahaṇamatidurlabham / tathā hi yadi prācīnānekadarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāyena caramacetasā dhūmasyāgniniyatatvaṃ grāhyaṃ tadā sapakṣāsapakṣayoḥ koṭiśaḥ pravṛttadarśanādarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāyena caramacetasā pārthivatvasyāpi lohalekhyatvaniyatatvaṃ gṛhyata iti pārthivatvādapi lohalekhyatvasiddhirastu / atha pārthivatvasya lohalekhyatvaniyatatvameva nāsti vajre vyābhicāradaerśanāt / tat kathaṃ pratyakṣeṇa niyatatvagrahaḥ / tarhi dhūmasya vahniniyatatvameva nāsti, vyabhicārābhāvasya darśayitumaśakyatvāt / tatkathaṃ caramacittena niyamagraha ityapi tulyam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, let this natural connection, whose nature has not been determined, be [granted] for the sake of argument. Even so, the apprehension of this [connection] through observation and non-observation is exceedingly difficult to obtain.

body.text: vyabhicārādarśanādavyabhicāra iti cet / nanu vyabhicārādarśanādavyabhicāra iti ko 'rthaḥ / kiṃ vyabhicārādarśanādavyabhicāraḥ, vyabhicārābhāvāt vā / prathame pakṣe vyabhicāro bhavatu mā vā vyabhicārādarśanādevāvyabhicāra iti niṣṇātaṃ pāṇḍityam / atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ / tadā vyabhicārābhāvaḥ kuto jñātaḥ / adarśanāditi cet / tat kimadarśanamātraṃ dṛśyādarśanaṃ vā / prathamamaśaktam / na hyadarśane 'pi vyabhicāro nāstītyabhidhātuṃ śakyate, cirakālanaṣṭabrāhmaṇīvyabhicāravat / āhatyādarśane (#Nibandh 49#) 'pyaticirakālavyavadhānena vyabhicāradarśanāt / dvitīyaṃ cāsambhavi, kvacit kadācit kenacid vyabhicāradarśanasāmagryāṃ satyāṃ vyabhicāradarśanāt / darśanasāmagryabhāve tu pratyayāntaravaikalyāt deśakālāntaravartitvād vā vyabhicārasya sa(rvaṃ) pratyupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatvābhāvāt / tasmāt satyapi vyabhicāre tadupalambhasāmagryabhāvād vyabhicārānupalambhaḥ / prakārāntareṇa vā tadutpattilakṣaṇenāvyabhicāre vyabhicārānupalambha ityubhayathāpi vyabhicāropalambhanivṛttirastu / tvayā tu yadavyabhicārapratipattinibandhanaṃ darśanādarśanamupavarṇitaṃ tatpārthivatvādau vyabhicārād dhūme 'pi nāvyabhicāranibandhanamiti dhūmo 'pi tvanmate nāśvāsabhājanamiti prasaktam /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] From the non-observation of deviation, [there follows] non-deviation. [Reply:] But what is the meaning of 'from non-observation of deviation, non-deviation'? Is it that from the non-observation of deviation, non-deviation [is established]?

body.text: asmanmate tu pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāmekatra kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau na vyabhicāraśaṅkāsaṃbhavaḥ / tadabhāve tu
body.translated_text: In our own view, however, when the cause-effect relation is established in one [instance] through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension), there is no possibility of doubt about deviation. But in the absence of that,

body.text: hetumattāṃ vilaṅghayediti
body.translated_text: [the reason] would transgress [the boundary of] being connected to a cause —

body.text: nyāyāt na saṃśayapiśācāvasaraḥ / tadevaṃ bhūyodarśanādarśanābhyāmapi na vyāptisiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: by this principle, there is no occasion for the specter of doubt. Thus, even through repeated observation and non-observation, <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is not established.

body.text: tarhi sakṛt sapakṣāsapakṣayodarśanārdanābhyāṃ vyāpterniścaya iti caturtha eva pakṣo 'stu / tathā hi kāryatvasya buddhimanmātrapūrvakatvenānvayo ghaṭādau dṛṣṭaḥ, ākāśādau buddhimatkāraṇanivṛttau kāryatvasya vyatirekaḥ / tataśca sakṛdanvayavyātireka siddhau vyāpteḥ siddhatvāt kuto 'naikāntikatā /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Then let the fourth alternative be [adopted]: certainty of <s>vyāpti</s> from a single observation and non-observation in <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>asapakṣa</s>. For the connection between being an effect and having an intelligent cause, [cognized] in a single [instance] through a mind [that grasps it]...

body.text: atrābhidhīyate / yadi buddhimatkāraṇakāryatvayorekatra pratibandhaḥ pramāṇapratītaḥ syāttadā ākāśādau buddhimannivṛttau kāryatvasya nivṛttiriti yuktam / sa ca pratibandhaḥ tādātmyaṃ tadutpattiḥ svābhāviko 'nyo vā na sidhyati sādhakapramāṇābhāvādityanantaramevāveditam / tataścākāśādau buddhimannivṛttirapi syāt / na ca kāryatvasya nivṛttiriti sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvādanaikāntikaṃ kāryatvam /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: If the connection between being an effect and having an intelligent cause were cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s> in a single [instance], then, when an intelligent [cause] is absent in space and the like, the [absence of] being-an-effect...

body.text: nanvākāśasyāsmanmate nityatvaṃ tvanmate cāsattvam / tatkathamataḥ kāryatvavyatirekaḥ sandigdha iti cet / ucyate / nahyākāśe kāryavyāvṛttimātraṃ vyatirekaḥ / kintu sādhyābhāvaprayuktaḥ sādhanābhāvo vyatirekaḥ / sa cākāśe grahītumaśakyaḥ / yathā tatra buddhimatkāraṇanivṛttistathā kāraṇamātrasyāpi nivṛttiḥ / tat kasyābhāvaprayuktaḥ kāryābhāvaḥ pratīyatāṃ yena vyatirekaḥ sidhyati//
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But space, in our view, is eternal; and in your view, it is non-existent. So how can the exclusion of being-an-effect from that be doubtful? [Reply:] It is said: It is not [the case] that space...

body.text: nanu satyamevaitat / yathākāśe buddhimatkāraṇanivṛttistathā kāraṇamātrasyāpi tatra nivṛttirna buddhimatkāraṇavyatirekānuvidhāyitvaṃ kāryatvasya niścetuṃ śakyate / tathāpi ghaṭādau kāryatvasya buddhimatānyayadarśanādākāśe 'pi buddhimadabhāvaprayuktaḥ kāryatvābhāvaḥ pratīyate / tatkathaṃ vyatirekāsiddhiriti cet / hanta ghaṭādāvapi na kāryatvasya sattāmātramanvayaḥ / kiṃ tu sādhyasadbhāvaprayuktaḥ sādhanasadbhāvaḥ / sa ca ghaṭe grahītumaśakyaḥ / yathā hi tatra buddhimadbhāvastathā kaṭakuḍyādibhāvo 'pi / tat (#Nibandh 50#) ka evaṃ jānātu kiṃ buddhimadbhāve kāryatvasya bhāvo yadvā kaṭakuḍyādibhāve bhāva iti / tasmādatra viśiṣṭānvayavyatirekagrahaṇapravaṇaviśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhāvanusartavyau yad dṛśyayoreva kāryakāraṇayostadutpattisiddhāvanvayavyatirekau sidhyataḥ //
body.translated_text: [Objection:] This is indeed true: just as there is the absence of an intelligent cause in space, so too there is the absence of cause in general there; [therefore] from the exclusion of an intelligent cause... [Reply:] No, because...

body.text: na ca pratibandhasādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ svapne 'pyastīti caturtho 'pi pakṣaḥ kṣataḥ / tadevaṃ buddhimatkāryamātrayorvyāpterasiddhāvadhikaraṇasiddhānta nyāyādyupādānādyabhijñaḥ sarvajñaḥ puruṣaviśeṣaḥ sidhyatīti pratyāśā durāśaiva //
body.translated_text: Nor is there any <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing the connection, even in dream. Thus the fourth alternative too is defeated. In this way, since the <s>vyāpti</s> between merely being an effect and having an intelligent [cause] is not [established]...

body.text: yacca kriyāsāmānyasya pakṣadharmatāvaśāccakṣurlakṣaṇakaraṇaviśeṣasiddhiriti dṛṣṭānto darśitaḥ so 'pi sādhyā(bhi)nnaḥ / tatra hi rūpajñānānyathānupapattyā siddhasya kāraṇāntarasyaiva cakṣurindriyamiti nāmakaraṇāt / rūpajñānajanakatvātiriktasya cakṣurlakṣaṇaviśeṣasyāsiddhatvāt / atha rūpajñānajanakatvameva cakṣuṣṭvamucyate / bhavatu ko doṣaḥ / etadevāsmābhi kāraṇāntaramucyate / tathaiva yadi tvayāpi buddhimatsāmānyāśrayamātrasya puruṣaviśeṣaḥ iti nāma kriyate, tadā nāsmākaṃ kācidvipratipattiḥ / paramārthato buddhimatsāmānyāśraye sarvajñatvādiviśeṣaścakṣurādiviśeṣavat sidhyatīti tatra vivadāmahe / ubhayorapi dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayorviśeṣasādhanasāmarthyābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: And the example adduced — that the specific instrument characterized as the eye is established by virtue of the <s>pakṣa-dharmatā</s> (being-a-property-of-the-subject) of action in general — that too is [a case of] non-differentiation from the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved). Because...

body.text: tadayaṃ saṃkṣepārthaḥ -
body.translated_text: This then is the summary meaning:

children.text: dṛśye tu sādhye vyabhicāra eva dṛśyaṃ na cenna vyabhicārasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the <s>sādhya</s> is perceptible, there is indeed deviation; and if it is not perceptible, the establishment of deviation [does not follow];

children.text: sādhāraṇatvādatha vā vipakṣasandehataḥ sādhyamato na sidhyati //
children.translated_text: or because of being common [to both <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>vipakṣa</s>], or because of doubt about the <s>vipakṣa</s>, the <s>sādhya</s> is therefore not established.

body.text: itīśvaro dattajalāñjaliḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) has been given a water-oblation [i.e., refuted and dismissed].

body.text: idānīṃ sādhanasvarūpaṃ nirūpyate / yadetanmerumandaramedinīghaṭapaṭādisādhāraṇaṃ kāryamātraṃ sādhanamupanyastam yāvadasya buddhimadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānamekatra nāvadhāryate tāvad gamakatvamayuktam / na ca tat svapne 'pi pratyetuṃ śakyam / tathā hi kumbhakāravyāpāre sati mṛtpiṇḍād ghaṭalakṣaṇaṃ kāryamupalabhyatāṃ nāma / na tu vyāpārāt pūrvaṃ ghaṭavatkāryamātrasya vyatirekaḥ pratyetuṃ śakyaḥ, kumbhakāravyatireke 'pi śoṣabhaṅgādilakṣaṇasya kāryasya mṛtpiṇḍe darśanāt / na ca yadvinābhūtaṃ yadupalabhyate tattasya kāryamatiprasaṅgāt / tṛṇādivanmṛtpiṇḍasya śoṣabhaṅgādikāryamātramapi pakṣīkṛtamiti cet / kriyatāṃ buddhimadvyatireke kāryamātravyatirekastvekatrāpi pratipādyatāṃ yena vyāptisiddhau tṛṇādiriva śoṣabhaṅgāderapi buddhimadanumānaṃ syāt / (#Nibandh 51#) ākāśādivaidharmyadṛṣṭāntastu pūrvaṃ pratihataḥ, buddhimatpūrvakatvasyeva kāraṇamātrapūrvakatvasyāpi tatra saṃbhavāt kiṃprayuktaḥ kāryatvābhāva ityaparijñānāt //
body.translated_text: Now the nature of the proof is examined. That which has been presented as proof — namely, mere effect-ness (<s>kāryatva</s>), common to <s>Meru</s>, <s>Mandara</s>, the earth, pots, cloths, and so forth — so long as its invariable concomitance (positive and negative) with an intelligent [cause] is not ascertained even in a single instance, its probative force is untenable. And that [concomitance] cannot be cognized even in a dream. For thus: given the potter's activity, an effect in the form of a pot may indeed be observed from a lump of clay. But before that activity, the negative concomitance of mere effect-ness — as with a pot — cannot be cognized, since even in the absence of a potter, effects characterized by drying, breaking, and so forth are observed in a lump of clay. And if [one argues] that whatever is found in the absence of something is the effect of that [absent thing], there would be an absurd over-extension. If [the opponent says] that, like grass and so forth, the mere effects of drying and breaking in a lump of clay are also included in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) — let the negative concomitance of mere effect-ness in the absence of an intelligent [cause] be demonstrated even in a single instance, by which, with the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) established, there would be an inference of an intelligent [cause] even from drying and breaking, as from grass and so forth. (#Nibandh 51#) The dissimilar example of space and so forth has already been refuted, since the possibility of being preceded merely by a cause — just as by an intelligent cause — obtains there as well, and hence it remains undetermined what grounds the absence of effect-ness.

body.text: etena yaduktam - na vyabhicāropalambhātprātisvikaviśeṣaparityāgena ghaṭādīnāmabhūtvābhavanādanyarūpaṃ viśeṣamupalakṣayāmo yanniṣṭhaṃ puruṣapūrvakatvaṃ vyavasthāpayāma iti tadapi prativyūḍham / kumbhakārādyabhāve 'pi mṛtpiṇḍādau śoṣabhaṅgādikāryadarśanādabhūtvā bhāvalakṣaṇasya kāryamātrasya vyatirekāsiddhervyāpterabhāvāt //
body.translated_text: By this, what was stated — 'Since no deviation is observed, by abandoning the specific individual [qualities], we discern in pots and so forth a distinctive feature characterized by coming-into-being-after-not-having-been, and on the basis of that we establish precedence by a person (<s>puruṣa</s>)' — that too is refuted. For even in the absence of a potter and so forth, since effects such as drying, breaking, and so forth are observed in a lump of clay, the negative concomitance of mere effect-ness — characterized by coming-into-being — is unestablished, and hence the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is absent.

body.text: nanu yadi kāryatvamātrasya na buddhimatā pratyakṣato vyāptigrahaḥ vyatirekābhāvāt, tvayāpi tarhi kathaṃ kṛtakatvasyānityatvena vyāptiravadhāryata iti cet / anapekṣālakṣaṇaviparyayabādhakapramāṇabalāditi brūmaḥ / taccātadrūpaparāvṛttasyaiva kṛtakatvasya vipakṣād vyatirekaṃ sādhayati / na ca tvayā viparyayabādhakapramāṇamabhidhātuṃ śakyata iti prāgeva pratipāditam / sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikatvādanaikāntikamidaṃ kāryatvamātram //
body.translated_text: Objection: If mere effect-ness has no perceptual apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> with an intelligent [cause], due to the absence of negative concomitance, then how have you yourself ascertained the <s>vyāpti</s> of 'being produced' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) with impermanence? We reply: by the force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that sublates the contrary, which is characterized by non-dependence [on observation]. And that [sublating <s>pramāṇa</s>] establishes the negative concomitance of 'being produced' — which is itself excluded from what is not of that nature — from the <s>vipakṣa</s> (counter-instance). And that you are unable to produce a <s>pramāṇa</s> sublating the contrary has already been demonstrated. Since the exclusion from the <s>vipakṣa</s> is doubtful, this mere effect-ness is <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive).

body.text: etena yadetat naiyāyikānāmākṣepaparihāraviḍambanam / iha khalu dve kāryatve / kāryamātram / viśiṣṭaṃ ca / tatrādyasya pratibandhāsiddheranaikāntikatvam / viśiṣṭasya bhūdharādiṣvasaṃbhavādasiddhatvamiti / tadasaṅgatam / kāryatvamātrasyaiva pratibandhopapādanāt //
body.translated_text: By this, the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>' mockery of objection and rebuttal [is also addressed]. Here indeed there are two kinds of effect-ness: mere effect-ness, and qualified [effect-ness]. Of these, the first is <s>anaikāntika</s> due to the non-establishment of invariable connection; the second is <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished) because it does not obtain in mountains and so forth. But that [distinction] is incoherent, since the invariable connection of mere effect-ness alone can be demonstrated.

body.text: yaccoktaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ kāryatvamiti / kīdṛśaṃ punastaditi vaktavyam / atha yatkāryaṃ ṣuruṣānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyitayā tatpūrvakamupalabdham / yaddṛṣṭerakriyādarśino 'pi kṝtabuddhirutpadyate tatkāryaṃ sakalaprāsādādyanugataṃ bhūdharādivyāvṛttaṃ viśiṣṭamityabhidhīyate / tadasundaram / vikalpānupapatteḥ //
body.translated_text: As for the claim of 'qualified effect-ness' — what exactly is its nature? It must be stated. If [you say] it is an effect that is observed to be preceded by a person through conformity with the positive and negative concomitance of an intelligent [agent]; or if [you say] it is that on seeing which the cognition 'this is made' arises even in one who has not observed the making — that [qualified] effect which follows palaces and such but is excluded from mountains and so forth is called 'qualified' — that is not sound, because the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual distinction) is untenable.

body.text: tathā cāha śaṅkaraḥ - kṛtabuddhiḥ kiṃ sādhyabuddhiḥ kiṃ vā sādhanabuddhiḥ / sādhyabuddhirapi yadi gṛhītavyāptikasya, sā bhavatyeva / athāgṛhītavyāptikasya, kimanyatrāpi sā bhavantī dṛṣṭā / atha sādhanabuddhiḥ / tarhi svopagamavirodhaḥ, sarvasya bhāvasya kṛtakatvopagamāditi //
body.translated_text: And thus <s>Śaṅkara</s> says: Is the cognition 'this is made' (<s>kṛtabuddhi</s>) a cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum)? Or is it a cognition of the <s>sādhana</s> (proof)? If it is even a cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>, for one who has grasped the <s>vyāpti</s>, that [cognition] already exists. But if for one who has not grasped the <s>vyāpti</s> — has it been observed to arise elsewhere [without <s>vyāpti</s>]? If, on the other hand, it is a cognition of the <s>sādhana</s> — then there is a contradiction with your own admission, since [you hold that] the 'made-ness' of everything that exists is admitted.

body.text: vācaspatiḥ punaratrāha - idamatra nipuṇataraṃ nirūpayatu bhavān kiṃ buddhimadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānaṃ viśeṣaḥ / āhosvit taddarśanaṃ yatparvatādiṣu nāstītyabhidhīyate / yadi pūrvakaḥ kalpaḥ, sa buddhimaddhetukatvaṃ tanubhuvanādīnāmātiṣṭhamānairabhyupeyata eva / na hi kāraṇaṃ kāryānanuvihitabhāvābhāvamanyo vaktyahrīkāt / atha taddarśanamiti caramaḥ kalpaḥ / na tarhi akriyādarśinaḥ kṛtabuddhisaṃbhavaḥ / ya eva hi ghaṭo 'nena buddhimadanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyī dṛṣṭaḥ, sa eva kāryo na tu vipaṇivartī / tajjātīyasya (#Nibandh 52#) tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānadarśanādadṛṣṭānvayavyatirekānuvidhānamapi tajjātīyaṃ tatheti cet / hantotpattimadghaṭādi buddhimadanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyīti anyadapitanubhuvanādikaṃ tathā bhavanna daṇḍena parāṇudyate ghaṭajātīyamutpattimadbuddhimatpūrvakamiti cet / nanu prāsādādi taddhetukaṃ na bhavet / aghaṭajātīyatvāt / atha yajjātīyamanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyi dṛṣṭam, tajjātīyamevādṛṣṭānvayavyatirekamapi taddhetukam / tat kiṃ kāryajātīyaṃ prāsādādi buddhimaddhetukaṃ na dṛṣṭam yenotpattimattanubhuvanādi tathā na syāt / na khalu tajjātīyatve kaścidviśeṣa iti //
body.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s>, however, says here: Let the honorable [opponent] examine this more closely: Is the distinguishing feature the conformity of positive and negative concomitance with an intelligent [agent]? Or is it the observation thereof, which is said to be absent in mountains and so forth? If the first alternative — then those who maintain the causal agency of an intelligent being for bodies, worlds, and so forth must accept it [as already established]. For no one, without shamelessness, can say that a cause does not conform in its presence and absence to its effect. If, however, the second alternative — that it is the observation [of conformity] — then the arising of the cognition 'this is made' in one who has not observed the making is impossible. For the very pot that has been observed by someone to conform to the positive and negative concomitance of an intelligent [agent] is the [same] effect — not one encountered in the marketplace. If [one replies] that because conformity with the positive and negative concomitance of an intelligent [agent] is observed in things of the same class, even those of the same class whose conformity has not been observed are also such — well then! A pot and so forth, being possessed of arising, conform to the positive and negative concomitance of an intelligent [agent]; therefore other things too, such as bodies, worlds, and so forth, being such [i.e., possessing arising], would not be forcibly excluded [from the same inference]. If [the opponent says]: But things of the pot-class, possessing arising, are preceded by an intelligent [agent]; yet palaces and such would not be [so preceded], being not of the pot-class — [we reply:] Well, if whatever class has been observed [to show] conformity with positive and negative concomitance, and only things of that same class, even those whose conformity has not been observed, are caused by that — then why should palaces and such, being of the class of effects, not have been observed as caused by an intelligent [agent], such that bodies, worlds, and so forth, being of that same class, would not be so? For there is no particular distinction in being 'of the same class.'

body.text: vittokastvāha - bhavatu vā kaścidanirūpitarūpo viśeṣaḥ / kiṃ punaranena viśeṣaṃ pratipādayatābhipretam / kiṃ kāryatvasāmānyasyāsiddhatvam / atha kāryaviśeṣasya / atha kāryamātrasya buddhimatkartṛvyabhicāraḥ / atha sādhyadṛṣṭāntayorvaidharmyamātram / kiṃ cātaḥ yadi tāvat kāryasāmānyasyāsiddhatvam / tannāsti / viśvambharādiṣvapi kāraṇavyāpārajanyatvasyobhayasiddhatvāt / atha kāryaviśeṣasya kumbhādivartinaḥ pakṣe 'siddhirabhidhīyate / tadā na kācidatra kṣatirviśeṣasya hetutvenānupādānāt / yadi kāryasāmānyasya kartṛvyabhicāraḥ pratipādayitumiṣṭaḥ / sa na śakyo vipakṣe 'darśanāt / tṛṇādeśca pakṣīkṛtatvāt / śaṅkāmātrasya sarvathāniṣiddhatvāt / sandigdhavyatirekitvaṃ naiyāyikānāṃ niranuyojyānuyogo bauddhānāmadoṣodbhāvanaṃ nigrahasthānamiti tu pratipāditam / tathāpi bādhakapramāṇānyabhihitānyeva / tasmānna pratibandhāsiddheḥ sarvatra vyabhicārāśaṅkā / atha sādhyadṛṣṭāntayorvaidharmyodbhāvanam / tanna / tasya sarvatra sulabhatvāt / yadi sādhyadṛṣṭāntayorvaidharmyamātrāt sādhyāsiddhiḥ nirvṛttedānīmanumānavārtāpi nikuñjamahānasayorapi dhūmavattve 'pi kathañcid vaidharmyopapatteriti sakalaṃ yatkiñcidetaditi /
body.translated_text: <s>Vittoka</s>, however, says: Let there be some distinguishing feature whose nature has not been determined. But what does the one propounding this distinction intend? Is it the non-establishment of effect-ness in general? Or of a specific kind of effect? Or the deviation of mere effect-ness from an intelligent maker? Or merely the dissimilarity between the <s>sādhya</s> and the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>? And what of it? If it is the non-establishment of effect-ness in general — that is not so, since the property of being produced by the operation of a cause is accepted by both parties even for the earth and so forth. If the non-establishment of the specific effect-ness present in pots and such in the <s>pakṣa</s> is meant — then no harm is done, since the specific [effect-ness] is not employed as the <s>hetu</s>. If the intention is to demonstrate the deviation of general effect-ness from a maker — that cannot be done, since it is not observed in the <s>vipakṣa</s>, and since grass and such have been included in the <s>pakṣa</s>, and since mere doubt is not prohibited in any case. As for the Naiyāyikas' [charge of] doubtful negative concomitance — [it has been shown that] it is a groundless quibble, while the Buddhists' [similar argument] fails to demonstrate any fault, and [the charge itself] constitutes a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>). Nevertheless, sublating <s>pramāṇas</s> have been stated. Therefore, from the non-establishment of invariable connection, there is no ground for suspecting deviation everywhere. If [the intention is merely] to bring out the dissimilarity between <s>sādhya</s> and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> — that is not [significant], since such dissimilarity is easily found everywhere. If the mere dissimilarity between <s>sādhya</s> and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> were to establish the non-proof of the <s>sādhya</s>, then even the business of inference would now be destroyed — for even between a thicket and a kitchen, though both possess smoke, some dissimilarity can be found. Thus, all of this is of no consequence.

body.text: tadayamatra saṃkṣepārthaḥ / yattāvat kāryatvamātraṃ tadevoktena krameṇa pratibandhasiddherbhūdharādiṣu dṛṣṭaṃ puruṣamanumāpayatītyasmākamabhimatasādhyamasiddhirupapannaiveti kimasmākamadhikacintayetyaṅgīkṛtyāpyuktaṃ viśiṣṭakāryatvam / tadeva tu nāstīti punarvistareṇa pratipāditamiti tadapi sarvamanavadheyameva / tathā hi kāryatvamātrasya tāvaduktena krameṇa vyāpterasiddhatvādanaikāntikatvamanivāryam / yacca viśiṣṭakāryatvaṃ vikalpya dūṣitaṃ tasyāsmābhiranabhyupagatatvāt taddūṣaṇāya prabandhaḥ prayāsaikaphalaḥ / na hi kāryatvaṃ dvividhamabhimatam / ekaṃ sarvakāryānugatam, aparaṃ parvatādivyāvṛttaṃ ghaṭapaṭaprāsādādyanuyāyīti / kiṃ tu kāryamanekajātīyakam / tatra yadi nāma paṭasya prāsādādibhiḥ saha vastutvasaṃsthānaviśeṣayogitvakāryatvādibhirdharmaiḥ sajātīyatvamasti tathāpi na tān dharmān buddhimatpūrvakānadhigacchati vyāvahārikaṃ pratyakṣam, kāryatvādīnāṃ buddhimadvyatirekānuvidhānābhāvāt / tatkathaṃ prāsādaparvatādiṣu kāryatvādidarśanād buddhimadanumānamastu / kiṃ tu yasyaiva ghaṭajātīya kāryaṃcakrasya vyatirekasiddhistasya buddhimadvyāptatvaṃ pratyakṣataḥ sidhyatītyuktam / (#Nibandh 53#) tena deśakālāntare ghaṭajātīyādeva buddhimadanumānam / yadā tu prāsādajātīyakamapi buddhimaddhetukamekatra pṛthagavadhāryate tadā tajjātīyādapi buddhimatsiddhiḥ / evaṃ tattajjātīyasarābodañcanaśakaṭapaṭakeyūraprabhṛteḥ kāryacakrād buddhimatpūrvakatvena pṛthak pṛthagavadhāritād buddhimadanumānamanavadyam /
body.translated_text: Here, then, is the summary of the matter. As for mere effect-ness — that very thing, through the establishment of invariable connection by the method stated, is observed in mountains and so forth to infer an intelligent [maker]. Our intended <s>sādhya</s> is properly established — so what need is there for us to think further? Having accepted this, the 'qualified effect-ness' was also stated. But [the argument that] even that does not exist has now been demonstrated at length — so all of that too is not to be heeded. For mere effect-ness, to begin with, since its <s>vyāpti</s> is unestablished by the stated method, its being <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive) cannot be prevented. And the 'qualified effect-ness' that was hypothesized and then refuted — since it is not accepted by us, the elaborate refutation of it is labor whose only fruit is exertion. For effect-ness is not regarded as twofold — one common to all effects, and another excluded from mountains and so forth but following pots, cloths, palaces, and such. Rather, effects are of many different classes. Therein, even if a cloth has, together with palaces and such, a shared class-membership through properties such as thingness, possessing a particular configuration, and effect-ness — still, the practical <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) does not apprehend those properties as preceded by an intelligent [agent], because effect-ness and so forth do not conform to the negative concomitance of an intelligent [agent]. Then how can the inference of an intelligent [agent] be made from observing effect-ness and so forth in palaces, mountains, and such? Rather, only for that specific class of effects — the pot-class — for which the negative concomitance has been established (as with a potter's wheel), is the pervasion by an intelligent [agent] established through perception. (#Nibandh 53#) Hence, from the pot-class alone, in another place and time, there is an inference of an intelligent [agent]. But when, for the palace-class too, a separate apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> is made in a single instance, then from the palace-class too, the inference of an intelligent [agent] may be made. Thus, from each respective class of effects — chariots, ships, wagons, cloths, bracelets, and so forth — separately ascertained as preceded by an intelligent [agent], the inference of an intelligent [agent] is flawless.

body.text: amumevārthamabhisandhāyācāryapādairabhihitam-
body.translated_text: With this very meaning in mind, the revered teacher has stated:

children.translated_text: "That whose arrangement and so forth is established as conforming to the presence and absence of a controller of such-and-such a kind —
From that, what is inferred is well-founded."

body.text: iti / evaṃ ghaṭapaṭaparvatādīnāṃ kāryatvavastutvādibhirdharmaiḥ sajātīyatve 'pi avāntaraṃ ghaṭapaṭaparvatatvādijātibhedamādāya lokasya vyāptigrāhakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ pravartataṃ iti darśayituṃ saṃvyavahārapragalbhapuruṣabuddhyapekṣayā yaddarśanādakriyādarśino 'pi kṛtabuddhirbhavatītyuktam / na tu śāstraparavaśabuddhipuruṣāpekṣayā / tathā hi śāstrasaṃskārarahitasya vyavahārapragalbhasya puruṣasya devakulajātīyakaṃ puruṣapūrvakatayāvadhāritavato nagarādvanaṃ praviṣṭasya parvatadevakulayordarśane tayordvayorapyakriyādarśino 'pi devakule kṛtabuddhirbhavati na parvate / tadanayordevakulaparvatayoḥ kāryatvādinā ekajātitve 'pi kṛtabuddhibhāvābhāvau na tayoḥ parvatadevakulatvalakṣaṇāvāntarajātibhedamanavasthāpya sthātuṃ prabhavataḥ / jātibhede ca siddhe devakulajātīye vyāptergrahaṇāt na parvatajātīyasya, na ca prāsādajātīyasya vyāptisiddhiriti na tato buddhimadanumānam / yadā tu prāsādasyāpi pṛthag vyāptigrahaḥ tadā tajjātīyādapi buddhimadanumānamastu / na kṣitidharādijātīyasya svapne 'pi vyāptigrahaḥ krīḍāparvatādernāmamātrābhede 'pi parvatādibhirekāntato bhinnasvarūpatvāt / yacca pṛṣṭaṃ keyaṃ kṛtabuddhirityādi / tatra kāmaṃ sādhyabuddhireveti brūmaḥ / yaccātroktaṃ sādhyabuddhirapi yadi gṛhītavyāptikasya sā bhavatyeva / athāgṛhītavyāptikasya kimanyatrāpi sā bhavantī dṛṣṭeti //
body.translated_text: Thus, even though pots, cloths, mountains, and so forth share the properties of effect-ness, thingness, and so forth — in order to show that ordinary <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), taking into account the sub-class distinction of pot-ness, cloth-ness, mountain-ness, and so forth, operates as the apprehender of <s>vyāpti</s> — the statement 'upon seeing which, even one who has not observed the making, the cognition "this is made" arises' was made with reference to a person of practical common-sense intelligence, not with reference to a person whose intelligence is dependent upon treatises. For a person skilled in practical affairs but lacking training in treatises, having ascertained that temple-class [structures] are preceded by a person, when he enters a forest from a city and sees both a mountain and a temple, the cognition 'this is made' arises regarding the temple but not regarding the mountain — even though he has not observed the making of either. In this case, despite the shared class-membership of temple and mountain through effect-ness and so forth, the presence and absence of the cognition 'this is made' cannot stand without positing the sub-class distinction characterized by temple-ness and mountain-ness. And when the class-distinction is established — since <s>vyāpti</s> is grasped for the temple-class but not for the mountain-class or the palace-class — the inference of an intelligent [agent] cannot be made from those [classes whose <s>vyāpti</s> has not been grasped]. But when, for the palace-class too, a separate apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> is made, then from the palace-class too, let the inference of an intelligent [agent] be made. But the <s>vyāpti</s> for the mountain-class or the earth-class cannot be grasped even in a dream — since play-mountains and the like, despite having merely the same name, are entirely different in nature from actual mountains and so forth. As for the question 'What is this cognition of being-made?' and so forth — there we willingly say: it is indeed a cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>. And as for what was said here — 'If the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> is that of one who has grasped the <s>vyāpti</s>, it already exists; if of one who has not grasped the <s>vyāpti</s>, has it been observed to arise elsewhere?'

body.text: atrocyate / gṛhītavyāptikasyānumānaṃ bhavati, agṛhītavyāptikasya na bhavatītyatrāsmākaṃ na kācidvipratipattiḥ / kevalaṃ gṛhītavyāptikosmin viṣaye na saṃbhavatīti brūmaḥ / uktakrameṇa vyatirekāsiddhervyāvahārikapratyakṣeṇa kāryatvasya vyāptatvāniścayāt / tasmādavāntarajātibhedaprasiddhyarthaṃ vyāvahārikapuruṣāpekṣayaivāsyā buddherbhāvābhāvāvuktau / jātibhede ca prayojanaṃ pūrvameva pratipāditam /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: That inference belongs to one who has grasped the <s>vyāpti</s>, and does not belong to one who has not grasped it — on this point we have no disagreement whatsoever. We merely say that the grasping of <s>vyāpti</s> is not possible in this domain, since the negative concomitance of effect-ness is unestablished by the method stated, and hence through practical <s>pratyakṣa</s> there is no certainty of effect-ness being pervaded [by an intelligent cause]. Therefore, the presence and absence of this cognition [of being-made] have been stated with reference to a person of practical common sense, for the purpose of establishing the sub-class distinction. And the purpose of the class-distinction has already been explained.

body.text: yadapyatra nipuṇammanyena vācaspatinā kathitaṃ tat kiṃ kāryajātīyaṃ prāsādādi buddhimaddhetukaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ yenotpattimattanubhuvanādi tathā na syāt, na khalu tajjātīyakatve kaścidviśeṣa iti / tadasaṅgatam / tathā hi bhavatu prāsādaparvatādīnāṃ kāryatvādinā sajātīyatvam / tattu na vyāvahārikapratyakṣeṇa buddhimadvyāptaṃ pratyetuṃ śakyam, vyāptigrahaṇasamaye dṛṣṭānte buddhimadabhāvaprayuktasya kāryamātravyatirekasya darśayitumaśakyatvāt /
body.translated_text: As for what was said here by <s>Vācaspati</s>, who considers himself clever — namely, 'It is not observed that things of the effect-class, such as palaces and the like, are caused by an intelligent being, such that things that come into being, such as the body and the world, would not be so' — and 'when they are of the same class, there is surely no distinguishing feature' — that is incoherent. For, even granted that palaces, mountains, and the like share the same class through being effects and so forth, nevertheless this [shared class] cannot be cognized as pervaded by an intelligent being through conventional perception, since at the time of apprehending the pervasion, it is impossible to show the absence of the mere effect in the absence of an intelligent being in the example.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 54#)
tadayaṃ saṃkṣepārthaḥ / kāryatvamātrasyāvyatirekādavyāptasyāgamakatvam / avāntaraṃ tu ghaṭaprāsādādisādhāraṇaṃ kāryatvamātramasmābhirapi na svīkṛtameva / yathā tu ghaṭatvapaṭatvādiprātisvikānekajātipuraskāreṇa prasiddhānumānavyavasthā sā cānavadyamavasthāpiteti /
body.translated_text:
(Nibandh 54)
This is the summary of the argument: Since mere effectness does not exhibit negative concomitance, being unpervasive, it cannot serve as a proof. As for the subordinate [property] — mere effectness that is common to pots, palaces, and the like — we too do not accept it. Rather, just as the well-known establishment of inference is through the presupposition of many specific universals such as pot-ness, cloth-ness, and so forth — that [establishment] has been flawlessly demonstrated.
