body.text: saṃprati sādhyātmā vicāryate / nanu vādinā sādhane samupanyaste taddūṣaṇopanyāsamapāsya sādhyasvarūpavikalpanaṃ nāma naiyāyikamate niranuyojyānuyogaḥ, saugatamate tvadoṣodbhāvanaṃ nigrahasthānamiti cet / tadetajjālmajalpitam / tathā hi sādhyasvarūpe 'pariniṣṭhite tadanusāriṇī pakṣasapakṣavipakṣavyavasthā kutaḥ / tadasiddhau cāsiddhatādayo doṣāḥ pakṣadharmatādayaśca guṇā na vyavasthitā ityuktam / nedānīṃ hetordoṣa guṇakatheti mūkena prativādinā sthātavyam / tasmāddhetudoṣopanyāsāyaiveyaṃ sādhyaniruktirityayameva vādī svamate niranuyojyānuyogadūṣaṇena nigrahasthānena nigṛhyata iti kimatra nirbandhena /
body.translated_text: Now the nature of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is examined. If [the objection is raised:] 'When the proponent has presented the proof, to set aside the presentation of refutation and instead speculate on the nature of the probandum is, according to the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (logician's) view, an irrelevant objection; and according to the Buddhist view, to raise a non-existent fault is a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>)' — this is contemptible chatter. For when the nature of the probandum has not been established, how can the determination of <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis), <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologous instance), and <s>vipakṣa</s> (heterologous instance) that follows it [be established]? And when those are not established, the faults such as non-establishment and the virtues such as being a property of the thesis are not fixed either — thus it has been said. [If this is so,] the respondent should not sit silent, [thinking:] 'Now there is no talk of the faults or merits of the reason.' Therefore, this elucidation of the probandum is precisely for the purpose of presenting faults in the reason — and thus this very proponent is defeated by the refutation of 'irrelevant objection' according to his own system. So why insist further?

body.text: yadetat kāryatvaṃ sādhanaṃ kimanena viśvasya buddhimanmātrapūrvakatvaṃ sādhyate / āhosvidekatvavibhutvasarvajñatvanityatvādiguṇaviśiṣṭabuddhimatpūrvakatvam / prathamapakṣe siddhasādhanam / dvitīye tu vyāpterabhāvādanaikāntikatā /
body.translated_text: This effectness being the proof (<s>sādhana</s>) — does it prove merely that the universe is preceded by an intelligent being? Or [does it prove] that it is preceded by an intelligent being qualified by the attributes of oneness, omnipresence, omniscience, eternality, and the like? In the first alternative, it is the proving of what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). In the second, there is inconclusive reasoning (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>) due to the absence of pervasion.

body.text: nanu sāmānyena vyāptau pratītāyāmapi pakṣadharmatābalād viśeṣasiddhiḥ / yathāgneḥ parvatāyogavyavacchedādisiddhiḥ / anyathā sarvānumānocchedaḥ / anumānadveṣī hyevaṃ jalpati -
body.translated_text: If [the objection is:] 'Even when the pervasion is cognized only in general, the specific [conclusion] is established by the force of the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) — just as the specific presence of fire on the mountain, its exclusion from conjunction [with water], and so forth are established. Otherwise, all inference would be destroyed. For one who hates inference speaks thus':—

children.translated_text: 'In this mire of the demolition of inference, the elephants of debaters are sunk.
In the specific, there is no positive concomitance; in the general, there is the proving of what is already established.'

body.text: atrocyate / sidhyatyeva pakṣadharmatābalato viśeṣaḥ / na tu sarvaḥ / yena hi vinā pakṣasthaṃ sādhanaṃ nopapadyate sa viśeṣaḥ sidhyatu / yathā vahnereva parvatavartitvādiviśeṣo na pañcavarṇaśikhākalāpakamanīyaḥ / na ca girīṇāṃ tarūṇāṃ kāryatvaṃ karturekatvavibhutvasarvajñatvādikamantareṇa nopapadyate, taditareṣvapi darśanāt / tasmāt
body.translated_text: To this we reply: The specific is indeed established by the force of the property of the thesis. But not every [specific]. That specific without which the proof residing in the thesis cannot be accounted for — let that be established. Just as the specific [property] of fire's presence on the mountain and the like [is established], but not [the property of fire] being beautiful with a crest of five-colored flames. And the effectness of mountains and trees is not unaccountable without the maker's oneness, omnipresence, omniscience, and the like.

children.translated_text: 'When there is mere exclusion from disjunction with the thesis — that is not a fault.
But when there is no positive concomitance with the desired [probandum] in the additional [attributes] — that is a fault.'

body.text: yadyevaṃ svasvarūpopādānopakaraṇasaṃpradānaprayojanābhijña eva kartā sādhyate / svarūpamiha ca dvayaṇukaṃ kāryam / upādānamiha paramāṇujāticatuṣṭayam / upakaraṇaṃ samastakṣetrajñasamavāyidharmādharmau / sampradānaṃ kṣetrajñāḥ, yānayaṃ bhagavān svakarmabhirabhipraiti / (#Nibandh 55#) prayojanaṃ sukhaduḥkhopabhogaḥ kṣetrajñānām / evaṃ bhūte buddhimati sādhye kutaḥ siddhasādhanam / na cāvyāptiḥ / kulāladṛṣṭāntena udāpānadyabhijñatvasya saṃbhavāt /
body.translated_text: If so, then what is proved is only a maker who knows the specific material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), instrument (<s>upakaraṇa</s>), recipient (<s>sampradāna</s>), and purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) of his own domain. The specific form here is the dyad (<s>dvayaṇuka</s>, binary atom) as the effect. The material cause here is the four classes of atoms. The instrument is the <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) inhering in all <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (individual souls) together. The recipient is the <s>kṣetrajñas</s>, whom this Lord directs according to their respective <s>karmas</s>. (Nibandh 55) The purpose is pleasure

body.text: tathā ca vācaspatiḥ pramāṇayati -
body.translated_text: And thus <s>Vācaspati</s> establishes [the argument]:

body.text: vivādādhyāsitāstanugirisāgarādayaḥ upādānādyabhijñakartṛkāḥ / kāryatvāt /
body.translated_text: 'The bodies, mountains, oceans, and the like that are the subject of dispute are produced by a maker who knows the material cause and the like. Because they are effects.

body.text: yadyatkārya tattadupādānādyabhijñakartṛkam / yathā prāsādādi /
body.translated_text: Whatever is an effect, that is produced by a maker who knows the material cause and the like — like a palace and the like.

body.text: tathā ca vivādādhyāsitāstanvādayaḥ /
body.translated_text: And likewise the bodies and the like that are the subject of dispute.

body.text: tasmāttatheti /
body.translated_text: Therefore, they are so.' — thus.

body.text: evamataḥ sādhanādupādānādyabhijñakartṛmātraṃ prasādhya tasya sarvajñatvasādhanāya vācaspatireva punarapīdamāha - bhavatu tāvadupādānādyabhijñakartṛmātrasiddhiḥ / pāriśeṣyāt tu vyatirekidvitīyanāmno 'numānādviśeṣasiddhiḥ / tathā hi
body.translated_text: Thus, having proved from the proof merely that there is a maker who knows the material cause and the like, to establish his omniscience, <s>Vācaspati</s> himself again says: 'Granted, for now, the establishment of merely a maker who knows the material cause and the like. But through the method of residues (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), through an inference of the second kind called exclusion (<s>vyatireki</s>), the specific [attributes] are established. That is:—

body.text: tanubhuvanādyupādānadyabhijñaḥ kartā nānityāsarvaviṣayabuddhimān /
body.translated_text: 'The maker who knows the material cause and the like of bodies, worlds, and so forth is not one whose intellect is non-eternal and not directed at all objects.',

body.text: tatkartustadupādānādyanabhijñatvaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: 'Because otherwise that maker would not know the material cause and the like of those [effects].',

body.text: na hyevaṃvidhastadupādānādyabhijño yathāsmadādiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'For one of this sort [with limited intellect] does not know the material cause and the like of those — just as we [ordinary persons] do not.'

body.text: tadupādānādyabhijñaścāyam /
body.translated_text: 'And this one does know the material cause and the like of those.',

body.text: tasmāttatheti /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore he is so.' — thus.

body.text: no khalu paramāṇubhedān kṣetrajñasamavāyinaśca karmāśayabhedānaparimeyānanyaḥ śakto jñātumṛte tādṛgīśvarāditi /
body.translated_text: 'For no one other than such a Lord is capable of knowing the innumerable distinctions of atoms, the distinctions of <s>karma</s>-deposits (<s>karmāśaya</s>) inhering in the individual souls — distinctions that are immeasurable.'

body.text: atrocyate / yāvanti dvayaṇukāni bhinnadeśakālasvabhāvāni kāryāṇi santi teṣu sarveṣveva kimeka eva buddhimān vyāpriyate / aneko vā / yadvā svasvaviṣayamātropādānādivedinaḥ parasparavyāpārānabhijñā bhinnadeśakālasvabhāvāḥ pratidvayaṇukamanya eva buddhimanto vyāpriyante iti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: Among all the dyads that differ in place, time, and nature, which are effects — does a single intelligent being operate in all of them? Or many? Or rather, intelligent beings who know only the material cause and the like of their own respective domains, who are ignorant of each other's operations, who differ in place, time, and nature — do different intelligent beings operate for each dyad? — thus there are three alternatives.

body.text: na tāvat prathamapakṣaḥ / deśakālasvabhāvabhinnānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dvayaṇukānāṃ karturekatvāsiddheḥ / yaccaikatvasādhanāya kāryaliṅgāviśeṣādityādyapi sādhanamupanyastaṃ tadasaṅgatam / dhūmaliṅgāviśeṣe 'pi hyagneranekatvavat tatrāpi tacchaṅkāsaṃbhavāt / saditi liṅgāviśeṣāditi tu dṛṣṭānto 'smān pratyasiddha eva, tasmād yathā mayā nānātvasādhanāya pramāṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ tathā tvayāpyekatvasādhanāya sādhanamabhidhānīyam /
body.translated_text: The first alternative is not [viable]. Because the oneness of the maker of all dyads differing in place, time, and nature is not established. And the proof adduced for establishing oneness — such as 'from the non-distinction of the effect-mark' and so forth — is incoherent. For just as there can be multiplicity of fire even when the smoke-mark is non-distinct, so too the suspicion [of multiplicity] is possible in that case as well. And the example 'from the non-distinction of the mark of existence' is unestablished for us.

body.text: atha manyate anekatvasādhanābhāvādekatvasiddhiriti / yadyevamekatvasādhanābhāvādanekatvameva kiṃ nāvagacchasi /
body.translated_text: If [you] think that oneness is established from the absence of a proof for multiplicity — then, in the same way, since there is no proof for oneness, why do you not accept multiplicity itself?

body.text: yadapyuktam - ekatve tu na pramāṇāntaramanveṣṭavyamekasya karturabhāve bahūnāṃ vyāhatamanasāmityādi / tadapi cintyatām / bahubhiḥ karaṇe yugapatkāryānutpattiriti kiṃ (#Nibandh 56#) bhinnadeśakālānāṃ kāryāṇāmanutpattirvivakṣitā / ekasyaiva vā mahāvayavinaḥ / kṣitighaṭādirūpasya / tatra ekasminnapi kārye bahubhiḥ karaṇe utpattivirodhi (naṃ) na paśyāmaḥ / bahūnāṃ parasparaṃ vaimatyaniyamābhāvāt / parasparāvyāghātapuruṣatvayordvividhasyāpi virodhasyāsaṃbhavāt / puruṣatvaṃ hi apuruṣatvena viruddham / na tu parasparāvyāghātena /
body.translated_text: As for what was said — 'If there is oneness, no other means of knowledge need be sought, since in the absence of a single maker, multiple [makers] with conflicting intentions...' and so forth — consider this too: When multiple [makers] are producing, is the non-production of simultaneous effects (Nibandh 56) intended with regard to effects at different times and places? Or of a single great composite — having the form of earth, pot, and the like? In the case of a single [composite] too, what

body.text: ye tvanantadeśakālasvabhāvabhedabhinnāsteṣu sutarāmevānekavyāpāraniṣedho 'sambhavīti dvitīyopi pakṣo vyudastaḥ / na ca karturekatvena dṛṣṭā vyāptisiddhiḥ / anekenāpi svatantreṇa svasvaprayojanārthinā grāmapraviṣṭahariṇādimāraṇaikakāryadarśanāt / tasyāpi pakṣīkaraṇe ekakartṛpūrvakābhimatasyāpi pakṣīkaraṇe ātmakartṛpūrvakatvamastu / tadevaṃ na sarvadvayaṇukānāṃ karturekatvasiddhiḥ / tathā coktam
body.translated_text: Those [effects] that are differentiated by infinite distinctions of place, time, and nature — for them, all the more so, the denial of multiple operations is impossible. Thus the second alternative too is refuted. Nor is the pervasion established that [implies] the maker's oneness. For even by many [agents], each independent and seeking their own respective purposes, there is observed a single effect such as the killing of a deer that has entered the village. And if that [deer-killing] too were made into a thesis [requiring a single agent], then even what you desire — [the universe] having a single maker — would become a thesis [requiring proof].

body.text: ekakarturna siddhau tu sarvajñatvaṃ kimāśrayam /
body.translated_text: 'If the oneness of the maker is not established, then on what basis [is established] omniscience?'

body.text: ata eva dvitīyo 'pi pakṣaḥ kṣīṇaḥ / sarveṣu dvayaṇukeṣvekasyāpi karturapravṛttau bahūnāṃ sutarāmapravṛtteḥ /
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the second alternative too is exhausted. If even a single maker does not operate in all dyads, then all the more so, many [makers do not operate in all of them].

body.text: tṛtīyastu pakṣo yadi bhaved tadā svasvavyāpāraviṣayamātropādānādyabhijñatve 'pi naikaḥ kaścit sarvajñaḥ sidhyati / na ca jñānaṃ sattāmātreṇa katipayātīndriyadarśanavat sarvārthagrahaṇaṃ yena tadabhedāt prastutaparamāṇūvat sarvasyaivāviśeṣeṇa grahaṇāt sarvajñatā syāt / anumānato hi katipayātīndriyadarśane siddhe 'pīśvarasya tatkāraṇayogitvaṃ niścīyate / na tu jñānasattāmātreṇa prakārāntareṇeti niścaya iti kutaḥ sarvajñatā /
body.translated_text: If the third alternative were to hold, then — even though each [maker] knows the material cause and the like of only their own respective domain of operation — no single being is proved to be omniscient. Nor does cognition, by mere existence, grasp all objects — like the perception of a few supra-sensory [objects] — since, due to its non-differentiation, it would grasp everything without distinction, including the atoms under consideration; and thus there would be omniscience [for everyone]. For the perception of a few supra-sensory [objects] is [known] through inference.

body.text: nanvatīndriyaṃ paramāṇvādikaṃ jānato na kathaṃ sārvajñyamiti cet / tat kimidānīmasarvadarśitveṣvatīndriyadarśanamātreṇa sarvajñatāpratyāśā / evameveti cet / hanta yadi nāma nyāyavihastena tvayā īdṛśo hastasamāracitaḥ sarvajñaḥ paribhāvitastathāpyanyeṣāmapāradūradeśakālavartināṃ dvayaṇukādīnāmupādānādiṣu januṣāndhaprakhyasya paramapuruṣārthāvedino vā lokaiḥ prāmāṇikaiśca nāsya sārvajñyamanumanyate //
body.translated_text: If [the objection is:] 'How is one who knows the supra-sensory — atoms and the like — not omniscient?' — then: Why now do you expect omniscience merely from the perception of supra-sensory [objects], when [the perception] does not reveal everything? 'That is exactly so!' [you say]. Well then, if this is the omniscient being fashioned with such sleight of hand by you who are bereft of logic — even so, the material causes and the like of other dyads and so forth that exist at immeasurably distant places and times are not

body.text: asmākantu nātīndriyadarśimātre pradveṣaḥ / evaṃ ca karturekatvāsiddhau vyatirekyapi heturasamarthaḥ viśveṣāmekasya karturasiddhau tadupādānādyabhijñabhāvasyā siddhatvāt / yaśca yanmātrakāraḥ sa tanmātropādānādyabhijño bhavanna sarvajñaḥ / anekāśrayeṇāpi upādānādyabhijñasāmānyasya caritārthatvāt / tadevamupādānādyabhijñapuruṣamātrasiddhāvapi naikatvasarvajñatvādiviśiṣṭapuruṣaviśeṣasiddhiḥ / puruṣamātre ca siddhasādhanamuktam / buddhimanmātrapūrvakatāmicchatāmupādānādyabhijñabuddhimatpūrvakatve sādhye kathaṃ siddhasādhanamiti cet / na tadapekṣayā siddhasādhyatāyā janitatvāt (#Nibandh 57#) kevalamasiddhoddhāre 'bhimate viśeṣe siddhe 'pi naiyāyikasyāpi nābhimatasiddhiriti brūmaḥ //
body.translated_text: We, however, have no hostility toward one who merely sees the supra-sensory. And thus, since the oneness of the maker is not established, the exclusionary reason (<s>vyatireki hetu</s>) too is powerless — because, when the single maker of the universe is not established, the statement that he knows the material cause and the like is also unestablished. And whoever is the maker of only that much is one who knows the material cause and the like of only that much, and is not omniscient — since the general property of knowing the material cause and the like is fully accounted for even by multiple substrata. Therefore

body.text: saugatasya tāvadaniṣṭasiddhiriti cet, na, svābhimatasādhyasādhanenaiva hi parasyāniṣṭamapi sādhanīyam / anyathā mātṛśokasmaraṇādināpi tadaniṣṭasiddhiḥ syāditi / asya saṃgrahaḥ
body.translated_text: If [the objection is:] 'This would at least be the proving of what is undesirable for the Buddhist' — no, for even what is undesirable for the opponent is to be proved by the very proof and probandum accepted [by the proponent] himself. Otherwise, even the recollection of a mother's death and the like would prove what is undesirable for him. Here is the summary:

children.translated_text: 'The establishment of what is desired by the opponent does not refute what is desired by the opponent — in the proof and in mere effort of reasoning.
In proving the desired specific [conclusion], let the proof tolerate the doubt regarding the counter-instance — when there is no positive concomitance [with the specific].'

body.text: sādhyacintādhikārastṛtīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The third chapter on the examination of the probandum is concluded.

body.text: evamanye 'pi hetavo yathāyogamabhyuhya dūṣaṇīyāḥ / tadevaṃ tāvadīśvarasya sadvyavahāro niṣiddhaḥ / asadvyavahārārthantu tallakṣaṇavilakṣaṇakṣaṇabhaṅgasādhakaṃ sattādisādhanameva draṣṭavyamiti //
body.translated_text: In the same way, other reasons too should be taken up and refuted as appropriate. Thus, in this manner, the valid conventional usage of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) has been refuted. But for the purpose of establishing invalid usage, one should see the very proofs such as 'existence' and the like as establishing momentariness — which is contrary to the definition of that [God].

children.translated_text: May this [work] — pervading the erroneous fabrication of a creator by the ignorant, obstructing the darkness of delusion —
the light [that is] the beautiful, stainless composition of <s>Ratnakīrti</s> — remain long, unobstructed!

body.text:
(#Nibandh 58#)
// 3 // apohasiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text:
(Nibandh 58)
[End of treatise] 3. The <s>Apohasiddhi</s> (Establishment of Exclusion).

body.text: // namastārāyai //
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Tārā</s>!

body.text: apohaḥ śabdārtho nirucyate / nanu ko 'yamapoho nāma / kimidamanyasmādapohyate / asmād vānyadapohyate / asmin vānyadapohyata iti vyutpattyā vijātivyāvṛttaṃ bāhyameva vivakṣitam / buddhyākāro vā / yadi vā apohanamapoha ityanyavyāvṛttimātram iti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is explained as the meaning of words. Now, what is this <s>apoha</s>? Is it that 'this is excluded from another'? Or 'another is excluded from this'? Or 'another is excluded in this'? — by these etymologies, [some say] the intended meaning is the external [object] distinguished from what is of a different class (<s>vijāti</s>). Or the form of cognition. Or, [by the derivation] 'exclusion is <s>apoha</s>,' [it means] mere exclusion of the other — thus there are three alternatives.

body.text: na tāvadādimau pakṣau / apohanāmnā vidhereva vivakṣitatvāt / antimo 'pyasaṃgataḥ, pratītibādhitatvāt / tathā hi parvatoddeśe vahnirastīti śābdī pratītirvidhirūpamevollikhantī lakṣyate / nānagnirna bhavatīti nitrṛttimātramāmukhayantī / yacca pratyakṣabādhitaṃ na tatra sādhanāntarāvakāśaḥ ityatiprasiddham //
body.translated_text: To begin with, the first two options are not [viable], because by the word '<s>apoha</s>' (exclusion) it is precisely the positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>) that is intended to be expressed. The last [option] too is incoherent, because it is contradicted by cognition. For indeed, the verbal cognition 'There is fire on the mountain' is observed as delineating precisely a positive form, not as indicating mere negation in the form 'It is not the case that there is no fire.' And it is extremely well-known that where there is contradiction by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), there is no room for another means of proof.

body.text: atha yadyapi nivṛttimahaṃ pratyemīti na vikalpaḥ tathāpi nivṛttapadārthollekha eva nivṛttyullekhaḥ / na hyanantarbhāvitaviśeṣaṇapratītirviśiṣṭapratītiḥ / tato yathā sāmānyamahaṃ pratyemīti vikalpābhāve 'pi sādhāraṇākāraparisphuraṇād vikalpabuddhiḥ sāmānyabuddhiḥ pareṣām, tathā nivṛttapratyayākṣiptā nivṛtibuddhirapohapratītivyavahāramātanotīti cet /
body.translated_text: Now, if [one says:] even though there is no conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>) of the form 'I cognize negation,' nevertheless the delineation of the negated referent is itself the delineation of the negation. For a cognition of the qualified cannot occur without the cognition of the qualifier being included within it. Therefore, just as for the opponents, even in the absence of a conceptual thought 'I cognize a universal,' the conceptual cognition is a cognition of the universal due to the manifestation of a common form — in the same way, the negation-cognition, implied by the cognition of the negated [referent], extends the convention of <s>apoha</s> (exclusion)-cognition —

body.text: nanu sādhāraṇākāraparisphuraṇe vidhirūpatayā yadi sāmānyabodhavyavasthā, tat kimāyātamasphuradabhāvākāre cetasi nivṛttipratītivyavasthāyāḥ / tato nivṛttimahaṃ pratyemītyevamākārābhāve 'pi nivṛttyākārasphuraṇaṃ yadi syāt ko nāma nivṛttipratītisthitimapalapet / anyathā asati pratibhāse tatpratītivyavahṛtiriti gavākāre 'pi cetasi turagabodha ityastu /
body.translated_text: Objection: If the determination of universal-cognition is established by virtue of the positive form when the common form manifests, then what follows from the non-manifestation of the absence-form in the mind for the determination of negation-cognition? Therefore, if the manifestation of a negation-form were to occur even in the absence of a mental form 'I cognize negation,' who indeed would deny the establishment of negation-cognition? Otherwise, if there were the convention of cognizing X when X does not appear, then even when a cow-form is in the mind, there would be cognition of a horse — let that be so!

body.text: atha viśeṣaṇatayā antarbhūtā nivṛttipratītirityuktam / tathāpi yadyagavāpoḍha itīdṛśākāro vikalpastadā viśeṣaṇatayā tadanupraveśo bhavatu kiṃ tu gauriti pratītiḥ / tadā ca sato 'pi nivṛttilakṣaṇasya viśeṣaṇasya tatrānutkalanāt kathaṃ tatpratītivyavasthā /
body.translated_text: If it is said that the negation-cognition is included as a qualifier — even so, if the conceptual thought has the form 'excluded from non-cow,' then let its inclusion as a qualifier be granted; but the cognition is [simply] 'cow.' And in that case, since the qualifier characterized by negation, even though present, is not made salient therein, how can the determination of that [negation-]cognition be established?

body.text: athaivaṃ matiḥ - yad vidhirūpaṃ sphurati tasya parāpoho 'pyastīti tatpratītirucyate / tadāpi sambandhamātramapohasya / vidhireva sākṣānnirbhāsī / api (#Nibandh 59#) caivamadhyakṣasyāpyapohaviṣayatvamanivāryam viśeṣato vikalpādekavyāvṛttollekhino 'khilānyavyāvṛttamīkṣamāṇasya / tasmādvidhyākārāvagrahādadhyakṣavad vikalpasyāpi vidhiviṣayatvameva nānyāpohaviṣayatvamiti kathamapohaḥ śabdārtho ghuṣyate /
body.translated_text: Now if the view is this: 'What manifests as positive form — the exclusion of the other also belongs to it, and so it is called the cognition of that' — even then, <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) has merely a relation [to the positive]. It is the positive entity alone that directly appears. Moreover, in this way it would be unavoidable that even perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) has <s>apoha</s> as its object — especially since perception, delineating exclusion from one [thing], observes exclusion from all others. Therefore, since from the apprehension of the positive form, conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>), just like perception, has precisely the positive entity as its object and not the exclusion of others — how can <s>apoha</s> be proclaimed as the meaning of words?

body.text: atrābhidhīyate / nāsmābhirapohaśabdena vidhireva kevalo 'bhipretaḥ / nāpyanyavyāvṛttimātram / kintvanyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhiḥ śabdānāmarthaḥ / tataśca na pratyekapakṣopanipātidoṣāvakāśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here we reply: By the word '<s>apoha</s>' (exclusion) we do not intend merely the positive entity alone, nor merely the exclusion of others. Rather, the meaning of words is the positive entity qualified by the exclusion of others (<s>anyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhiḥ</s>). Therefore there is no room for the faults that befall each individual position.

body.text: yattu goḥ pratītau na tadātmāparātmeti sāmarthyādapohaḥ paścānniścīyata iti vidhivādināṃ matam, anyāpohapratītau vā sāmarthyādanyāpoḍho 'vadhāryate iti pratiṣedhavādināṃ matam / tadasundaram / prāthamikasyāpi pratipatti kramādarśanāt / na hi vidhiṃ pratipadya kaścidarthāpattitaḥ paścādapohamavagacchati / apohaṃ vā pratipadyānyāpoḍham / tasmād goḥ pratipattirityanyāpoḍhapratipattirucyate / yadyapi cānyāpoḍhaśabdānullekha uktastathāpi nāpratipattireva viśeṣaṇabhūtasyānyāpohasya / agavāpoḍha eva gośabdasya niveśitatvāt / yathā nīlotpale niveśitādindīvaraśabdānnīlotpalapratītau tatkāla eva nīlimasphuraṇamanivāryaṃ tathā gośabdādapyagavāpoḍhe niveśitād gopratītau tulyakālameva viśeṣaṇatvādago 'pohasphuraṇamanivāryam / yathā pratyakṣasya prasajyarūpābhāvāgrahaṇamabhāvavikalpotpādanaśaktireva tathā vidhivikalpānāmapi tadanurūpānuṣṭhānadānaśaktirevābhāvagrahaṇamabhidhīyate / paryudāsarūpābhāvagrahaṇaṃ tu niyatasvarūpasaṃvedanamubhayoraviśiṣṭam / anyathā yadi śabdādarthapratipattikāle kalito na parāpohaḥ kathamanyaparihāreṇa pravṛttiḥ / tato gāṃ badhāneti codito 'śvādīnapi badhnīyāt //
body.translated_text: Now, the view of the proponents of the positive (<s>vidhivādin</s>) is that in the cognition of a cow, <s>apoha</s> is subsequently ascertained through implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>), since [the cow] is 'not of other-nature, not of non-self-nature.' And the view of the proponents of negation (<s>pratiṣedhavādin</s>) is that in the cognition of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of others), the excluded-from-others is determined through implication. That is not sound, because even the primary apprehension does not admit of sequential order. For no one, having apprehended the positive, subsequently understands the exclusion through implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>); nor, having apprehended the exclusion, [subsequently understands] the excluded-from-others. Therefore, the cognition of a cow is called the cognition of the excluded-from-others. And even though it was said that the word '<s>anyāpoḍha</s>' (excluded-from-others) is not delineated [in the cognition], nevertheless the cognition of <s>anyāpoha</s> as a qualifier is not absent — because the word 'cow' (<s>go-śabda</s>) is assigned precisely to what is excluded from non-cows (<s>agavāpoḍha</s>). Just as, when the word '<s>indīvara</s>' (blue lotus) is assigned to a blue lotus, in the cognition of a blue lotus from that word, the manifestation of blueness at that very time is unavoidable — so too, from the word 'cow,' which is assigned to what is excluded from non-cows, in the cognition of a cow, the manifestation of exclusion from non-cows is unavoidable, simultaneously, by virtue of being a qualifier. Just as perception's non-apprehension of absence in the form of simple negation (<s>prasajyarūpa</s>) is called precisely the power to generate a conceptual thought of absence — so too, for positive conceptual thoughts, the power to induce corresponding action is called the apprehension of absence. But the apprehension of absence in the form of nominative exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) is the awareness of a determinate intrinsic nature, which is the same for both. Otherwise, if the exclusion of others is not discerned at the time of understanding the object from the word, how would there be activity excluding others? Then one commanded 'Tie the cow' would tie horses and the like as well.

body.text: yadapyavocad vācaspatiḥ jātimatyo vyaktayo vikalpānāṃ śabdānāṃ ca gocaraḥ / tāsāṃ ca tadvatīnāṃ rūpamatajjātīyaparāvṛttamityatastadavagaterna gāṃ badhāneti codito 'śvādīn badhnāti / tadapyanenaiva nirastam / yato jāteradhikāyāḥ prakṣepe 'pi vyaktīnāṃ rūpamatajjātīyaparāvṛttameva cet, tadā tenaiva rūpeṇa śabdavikalpayorviṣayībhavantīnāṃ kathamatadvayāvṛttiparihāraḥ //
body.translated_text: And what <s>Vācaspati</s> said — that individuals possessing universals are the domain of conceptual thoughts and words, and their form, as possessing them, is 'turned away from what is not of that class,' and therefore from that understanding one commanded 'Tie the cow' does not tie horses and the like — that too is refuted by this very [argument]. For even if an additional universal is introduced, if the form of the individuals is precisely 'turned away from what is not of that class,' then how is the exclusion from non-that avoided for those [individuals] that become the object of word and conceptual thought precisely through that form?

body.text: atha na vijātīyavyāvṝttaṃ vyaktirūpaṃ tathāpratītaṃ vā tadā jātiprasāda eṣa iti kathamarthato 'pi tadavagatirityuktaprāyam /
body.translated_text: If the individual-form is not excluded from what is of a different class, or is not cognized as such, then this is merely the grace of the universal — and how can there be understanding of that even in substance? This is essentially what has been said.

body.text: atha jātibalādevānyatovyāvṛtam / bhavatu jātibalāt svahetuparamparābalād vānyavyāvṛtam / ubhayathāpi vyāvṛttapratipatau vyāvṛttipratipattirastyeva /
body.translated_text: If [the exclusion is] by the power of the universal alone, or excluded from others by the power of the universal, or by the power of the succession of one's own causes — in either case, in the cognition of what is excluded, there is indeed the cognition of exclusion.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 60#)
na cāgavāpoḍhe gośabdasaṅketavidhāvanyīnyāśrayadoṣaḥ / sāmānye tadvati vā saṃkete 'pi taddoṣāvakāśāt / na hi sāmānyaṃ nāma sāmānyamātramabhipretam, turage 'pi gośabdasaṃketaprasaṅgāt / kiṃ tu gotvam / tāvatā ca sa eva doṣaḥ / gavādiparijñāne gotvasāmānyāparijñānāt / gotvasāmānyāparijñāne gośabdavācyā parijñānāt /
body.translated_text:
(Nibandhāvalī 60)
Nor is there the fault of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>) in the convention of the word 'cow' being established for what is excluded from non-cows. For even in the convention based on the universal or what possesses it, there is room for that fault. For what is meant by 'universal' is not merely universality in general — since there would be the absurd consequence of the word 'cow' being conventionally assigned even to a horse. Rather, it is cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>). And with just that, the same fault [arises]: because cow-ness as a universal is not known without knowing cows and the like, and because the referent of the word 'cow' is not known without knowing the universal of cow-ness.

body.text: tasmādekapiṇḍadarśanapūrvako yaḥ sarvavyaktisādhāraṇa iva bahiraghyasto vikalpabuddhyākāraḥ tatrāyaṃ gauriti saṃketakaraṇe netaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, the conceptual cognition-form, which appears externally as if common to all individuals, preceded by seeing a single lump [i.e., one instance] — when the convention 'This is a cow' is made with respect to that, there is no fault of mutual dependence.

body.text: abhimate ca gośabdapravṛttāvagośabdena śeṣasyāpyabhidhānamucitam / na cānyāpoḍhānyāpohayorvirodho viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvakṣatirvā, parasparavyavacchedābhāvāt / sāmānādhikaraṇyasadbhāvāt / bhūtalaghaṭābhāvavat / svābhāvena hi virodho na parābhāvenetyābālaprasiddham / eṣa panthāḥ śrughnamupatiṣṭhata ityatrāpyapoho gamyata eva / aprakṛtapathāntarāpekṣayā eṣa eva śrudhnapratyanīkāniṣṭasthānāpekṣayā śrughnameva / araṇyamārgavad vicchedābhāvādupatiṣṭhata eva / sārthadūtādivyavacchedena panthā eveti pratipadaṃ vyavacchedasya sulabhatvāt / tasmādapohadharmaṇo vidhirūpasya śabdādavagatiḥ puṇḍarīkaśabdādiva śvetimaviśiṣṭasya padmasya //
body.translated_text: And in the accepted usage of the word 'cow,' it is appropriate that the remainder is also denoted by the word 'non-cow.' And there is no contradiction between the excluded-from-others (<s>anyāpoḍha</s>) and the exclusion-of-others (<s>anyāpoha</s>), nor any damage to the relation of qualified and qualifier, because of the absence of mutual exclusion, because of the presence of co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) — like the absence of a pot on a ground-surface. For contradiction is through one's own absence, not through the absence of another — this is well-known even to a child. In the [statement] 'This path leads to <s>Shrughna</s>' too, exclusion is indeed understood — with reference to other paths that are not relevant, this one alone [leads to] <s>Shrughna</s> itself, with reference to undesired destinations opposed to <s>Shrughna</s>. Like a forest path, [it] indeed leads [there] due to the absence of interruption. 'It is a path' through exclusion from caravans, messengers, and the like — because exclusion is easily available at every word. Therefore, the understanding from words is of the positive entity possessing the property of exclusion — just as from the word '<s>puṇḍarīka</s>' (white lotus), [one understands] a lotus qualified by whiteness.

body.text: yadyevaṃ vidhireva śabdārtho vaktumucitaḥ, kathamapoho gīyata iti cet / uktamatrāpohaśabdenānyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhirucyate / tatra vidhau pratīyamāne viśeṣaṇatayā tulyakālamanyāpohapratītiriti /
body.translated_text: If so, it would be appropriate to say that the positive entity alone is the meaning of words — why is <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) spoken of? It has been stated: by the word '<s>apoha</s>' is meant the positive entity qualified by the exclusion of others. And therein, when the positive is cognized, the cognition of the exclusion of others [occurs] simultaneously as a qualifier.

body.text: na caiva pratyakṣasyāpyapohaviṣayatvavyavasthā kartamucitā / tasya śābdapratyayasyeva vastuviṣayatve vivādābhāvāt / vidhiśabdena ca yathādhyavasāyamatadrūpaparāvṛtto bāhyo 'rthobhimataḥ, yathāpratibhāsaṃ buddhyākāraśca / tatra bāhyo 'rtho 'dhyavasāyādeva śabdavācyo vyavasthāpyate / na svalakṣaṇaparisphūrtyā / pratyakṣavaddeśakālāvasthāniyatapravyaktasvalakṣaṇāsphuraṇāt / yacchāstram
body.translated_text: And it is not appropriate to establish that even perception has <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) as its object. For there is no dispute that verbal cognition, like [perception], has a real object (<s>vastu</s>) as its domain. And by the word 'positive entity' (<s>vidhi</s>), what is intended is the external object turned away from what is not of that form, as determined, and the cognitive form (<s>buddhyākāra</s>) as it appears. Of these, the external object is established as expressible by words only through determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), not through the manifestation of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) — because, unlike perception, the particular, delimited by specific place, time, and state, does not vividly manifest [in verbal cognition]. As the treatise states:

body.text: śabdenāvyāpṛtākṣasya buddhāvapratibhāsanāt /
body.translated_text: Because the object does not appear in the cognition of one whose sense faculty is not engaged with the word,

body.text: arthasya dṛṣṭāviva
body.translated_text: as in the case of seeing the object —

body.text:
iti / indriyaśabdasvabhāvopāyabhedādekasyaivārthasya pratibhāsabheda iti cet /
atrāpyuktam -
body.translated_text:
If [one objects:] due to the difference of means — sense faculty, word, and intrinsic nature — there is a difference in appearance of one and the same object.
To this too it has been said:

children.translated_text: What other basis has indeed arisen for cognitions of that [object] in reality?
How can there be a form of one and the same [thing] that appears with different aspects?

body.text: na hi spaṣṭāspaṣṭe dve rūpe parasparaviruddhe ekasya vastunaḥ staḥ / yata ekenendriyabuddhau pratibhāsetānyena vikalpe / tathā sati vastuna eva bhedaprāpteḥ / (#Nibandh 61#) na hi svarūpabhedādaparo vastubhedaḥ / na ca pratibhāsabhedādaparaḥ svarūpabhedaḥ / anyathā trailokyamekameva vastu syāt //
body.translated_text: For there are not two forms — clear and unclear — mutually contradictory, belonging to one and the same real object. Such that by one [form] it appears in sense-cognition and by the other in conceptual thought. In that case, a difference in the object itself would follow. (Nibandhāvalī 61) For there is no other difference of the object apart from the difference of intrinsic nature. Nor is there another difference of intrinsic nature apart from the difference of appearance. Otherwise, the three worlds would be one single object.

body.text: dūrāsannadeśavartinoḥ puruṣayorekatra śākhini spaṣṭāspaṣṭapratibhāsabhede 'pi na śākhibheda iti cet / na brūmaḥ pratibhāsabhedo bhinnavastuniyataḥ, kiṃ tvekaviṣayatvābhāvaniyata iti / tato yatrārthakriyābhedādisacivaḥ pratibhāsabhedastatra vastubhedaḥ, ghaṭavat / anyatra punarniyamenaikaviṣayatāṃ pariharatītyekapratibhāso bhrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] for two persons situated at far and near locations, even though there is a difference of clear and unclear appearance regarding a single tree, there is no difference of the tree — [we reply:] We do not say that a difference of appearance is determined by a different object, but rather that it is determined by the absence of having a single object. Therefore, where the difference of appearance is accompanied by a difference in causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) and the like, there is a difference of object, like a pot. But otherwise, [the difference of appearance] invariably precludes having a single object — and so the one appearance [that is single] is erroneous.

body.text: etena yadāha vācaspatiḥ - na ca śābdapratyakṣayorvastugocaratve pratyayābhedaḥ kāraṇabhedena pārokṣyāpārokṣyabhedopapatteriti, tannopayogi / parokṣapratyayasya vastugocaratvāsamarthatāt / parokṣatāśrayastu kāraṇabheda indriyagocaragrahaṇaviraheṇaiva kṛtārthaḥ / tanna / śābde pratyaye svalakṣaṇaṃ parisphurati / kiṃ ca svalakṣaṇātmani vastuni vācye sarvātmanā pratipatteḥ vidhiniṣedhayorayogaḥ / tasya hi sadbhāve 'stīti vyartham, nāstītyasamartham / asadbhāve tu nāstīti vyartham, astītyasamartham / asti cāstyādipadaprayogaḥ / tasmāt śābdapratibhāsasya bāhyārthabhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyaṃ na tadviṣayatāṃ kṣamate //
body.translated_text: By this, what <s>Vācaspati</s> says — 'There is no difference of cognition when both verbal and perceptual [cognitions] have a real object as their domain, because the difference of mediate and immediate is explained by the difference of cause' — that is not useful. Because mediate cognition is incapable of having a real object as its domain. The difference of cause, which is the basis for mediacy, accomplishes its purpose precisely through the absence of apprehension of the domain of the sense faculty. [If one objects:] 'No, the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) manifests in verbal cognition.' Moreover, if the real object in its particular nature is what is expressed [by words], then both affirmation and negation regarding it in its entirety would be impossible. For if it exists, 'it exists' is pointless; 'it does not exist' is groundless. And if it does not exist, 'it does not exist' is pointless; 'it exists' is groundless. Yet there is the use of words like 'exists' and 'does not exist.' Therefore the verbal appearance's being common to both the existence and non-existence of the external object does not permit [the claim of] its being the object [of the word].

body.text: yacca vācaspatinā jātimadvyaktivācyatāṃ svavācaiva prastutyāntarameva na ca śabdārthasya jāterbhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyaṃ nopapadyate / sā hi svarūpato nityāpi deśakālaviprakīrṇānekavyaktyāśrayatayā bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇībhavantyastināstisaṃbandhayogyā / vartamānavyaktisaṃbandhitā hi jāterastitā / atītānāgatavyaktisaṃbandhitā ca nāstiteti sandigdhavyatirekitvādanaikāntikaṃ bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyam, anyathāsiddhaṃ veti vikalpitam / tadaprastutam / tāvatā tāvanna prakṛtakṣatiḥ / jātau bharaṃ nyasyatā svalakṣaṇavācyatvasya svayaṃ svīkārāt / kiṃ ca sarvatra padārthasyasvalakṣaṇasvarūpeṇaivāstitvādikaṃ cintyate / jātestu vartamānādivyaktisaṃvadhī 'stitvādikamiti tu bālapratāraṇam / evaṃ jātimadvyaktivacane 'pi doṣaḥ / vyakteścet pratītisiddhiḥ jātiradhikā pratīyatāṃ mā vā, na tu vyaktipratītidoṣānmuktiḥ /
body.translated_text: And what <s>Vācaspati</s> said — that individuals possessing universals are expressible [by words], having introduced it with his own words — [we reply:] is it not also impossible that the universal, which is the meaning of words, should be common to existence and non-existence? For although it is eternal in its intrinsic nature, by being the substrate of multiple individuals scattered across place and time, it becomes common to existence and non-existence and is fit for the relations 'exists' and 'does not exist.' For the existence of the universal is its relation to present individuals; and its non-existence is its relation to past and future individuals — [but this argument is] inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) due to doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>), or [the proof is] based on an irrelevant factor — this has been considered. But that is beside the point. By so much, there is no damage to the present [thesis]. For the one who places the burden on the universal has himself accepted the expressibility of the particular. Moreover, everywhere, the existence and the like of an entity is considered precisely with respect to the intrinsic nature of the particular. But [to say that] the existence and the like of the universal is [determined by] its relation to present and other individuals — that is a deception of the naive. Thus even in the doctrine that words denote individuals possessing universals, the fault [remains]. If the establishment of cognition comes from the individual, let the universal additionally be cognized or not — but there is no escape from the faults pertaining to the cognition of the individual.

body.text: etena yaducyate kaumārilaiḥ sabhāgatvādeva vastuno na sādhāraṇyadoṣaḥ / vṛkṣatvaṃ hyanirdhāritabhāvābhāvaṃ śabdādavagamyate / tayoranyatareṇa śabdāntarāvagatena saṃbadhyata iti / tadapyasaṅgatam / sāmānyasya nityasya pratipattābanirdhāritabhāvābhāvatvāyogāt /
body.translated_text: By this, what is said by the followers of <s>Kumārila</s> — 'Because of the homogeneity of the object itself, there is no fault of commonality; for cow-ness is understood from the word as having undetermined existence and non-existence, and it is connected with one or the other [existence or non-existence] known through another word' — that too is incoherent. Because it is impossible for the universal, being eternal, to have undetermined existence and non-existence when apprehended.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 62#)
yaccedam - na ca pratyakṣasyeva śabdānāmarthapratyāyanaprakāro yena taddṛṣṭa ivāstyādiśabdāpekṣā na syāt, vicitraśaktitvāt pramāṇānāmiti / tadapyaindriyakaśābdapratibhāsayorekasvarūpagrāhitve bhinnāvabhāsadūṣaṇena dūṣitam / vicitraśaktitvaṃ ca pramāṇānāṃ sākṣātkārādhyavasāyābhyāmapi caritārtham / tato yadi pratyakṣārthapratipādanaṃ śābdena tadvadevāvabhāsaḥ syāt / abhavaṃśva na tadviṣayakhyāpanaṃ kṣamate //
body.translated_text: As for the [objection]: 'The manner of conveying meaning by words is not like that of perception, so that, as in its case, there would be no need for words like “exists” and so forth, because the pramāṇas have diverse capacities' — that too has been refuted by the objection of different appearances, given that the sensory and verbal appearances have one and the same form as their object. And the diverse capacity of pramāṇas is also fulfilled by direct apprehension and determination (adhyavasāya). Therefore, if verbal conveyance of the object of perception were [of the same nature], the appearance would be just like that [of perception]. If it does not exist [in that manner], it cannot reveal the domain of that [perception].

body.text: nanu vṛkṣaśabdena vṛkṣatvāṃśe codite sattvādyaṃśaniścayanārthamastyādipadaprayoga iti cet /
body.translated_text: If it is objected that, when the word '<s>vṛkṣa</s>' (tree) has indicated the tree-aspect, the words 'exists' and the like are employed for the purpose of determining the aspect of existence and so forth —

body.text: niraṃśatvena pratyakṣasamadhigatasya svalakṣaṇasya ko 'vakāśaḥ padāntareṇa / dharmāntaravidhiniṣedhayoḥ pramāṇāntareṇa vā / pratyakṣe 'pi pramāṇāntarāpekṣā dṛṣṭeti cet / bhavatu tasyāniścayātmakatvādanabhyastasvarūpaviṣaye / vikalpastu svayaṃ niścayātmako yatra grāhī tatra kimapareṇa / asti ca śabdaliṅgāntarāpekṣā / tato na vastusvarūpagrahaḥ //
body.translated_text: what scope is there for another word with respect to the <s>svalaḵṣaṇa</s> (particular) that has been apprehended by perception as partless? Or for another <s>pramāṇa</s> with respect to the assertion or negation of another property? If it is said that even in perception there is observed dependence on another <s>pramāṇa</s> — let it be so, since [perception] is of the nature of non-determination regarding an object whose form has not been familiarized. But <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), being itself of the nature of determination, where it apprehends, what need is there of another? And there is dependence on other words and inferential marks. Therefore, [vikalpa] does not apprehend the true nature of the object.

body.text: nanu bhinnā jātyādayo dharmāḥ parasparaṃ dharmiṇaśceti jātilakṣaṇaikadharmadvāreṇa pratīte 'pi śākhini dharmāntaravattayā na pratītiriti kiṃ na bhinnābhidhānādhīno dharmāntarasya nīlacaloccaistaratvāderavabodhaḥ / tadetadasaṅgatam / akhaṇḍātmanaḥ svalakṣaṇasya pratyakṣe 'pi pratibhāsāt / dṛśyasya dharmadharmibhedasya pratyakṣapratikṣiptatvāt / anyathā sarvaṃ sarvatra syādityatiprasaṅgaḥ / kālpanikabhedāśrayastu dharmadharmivyavahāra iti prasādhitaṃ śāstre /
body.translated_text: If it is objected that <s>jāti</s> (genus) and the like are properties distinct from each other and from the property-bearer, and therefore even when a tree is cognized through a single property characterized by genus, it is not cognized as possessing other properties — so why should the cognition of other properties such as being blue, moving, and tall not depend on different expressions? — that is incoherent, because even in perception the <s>svalaḵṣaṇa</s> (particular) appears as having an undivided nature; because the perceived distinction of property and property-bearer is rejected by perception; otherwise, everything would be everywhere — which is an absurd over-extension. But the practical distinction of property and property-bearer rests on a fictitious division — this has been established in the [Buddhist] treatise.

body.text: bhavatu vā pāramārthiko 'pi dharmadharmibhedaḥ / tathāpyanayoḥ samavāyāderdūṣitatvādupakāralakṣaṇaiva pratyāsattireṣitavyā / evaṃ ca yathendriyapratyāsattyā pratyakṣeṇa dharmipratipattau sakalataddharmapratipattistathā śabdaliṅgābhyāmapi vācyavācakādisaṃbandhapratibaddhābhyāṃ dharmipratipattau niravaśeṣataddharmapratipattirbhavet / pratyāsatimātrasyāviśeṣāt //
body.translated_text: Or let the distinction of property and property-bearer be ultimately real as well. Even so, since <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) and the like have been refuted, the proximity [between them] must be understood as characterized by beneficial relation (<s>upakāra</s>). And thus, just as through the proximity of the sense faculty, when the property-bearer is apprehended by perception, all its properties are apprehended, so too through words and inferential marks — which are bound by the relation of signifier and signified and so forth — when the property-bearer is apprehended, all its properties without remainder would be apprehended, since there is no distinction in mere proximity.

body.text: yacca vācaspati, na caikopādhinā sattvena viśiṣṭe tasmin gṛhīte upādhyantaraviśiṣṭastadgrahaḥ / svabhāvo hi dravyasyopādhibhirviśiṣyate / na tūpādhayo vā viśeṣyatvaṃ vā tasya svabhāva iti / tadapi plavata eva / na hyabhedādupādhyantaragrahaṇamāsañjitam / bhedaṃ puraskṛtyaivopakārakagrahaṇe upakāryagrahaṇaprasañjanāt / na cāgnidhūmayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāva iva svabhāvata eva dharmadharmiṇoḥ pratipattiniyamakalpanamucitam / (#Nibandh 63#) tayorapi pramāṇāsiddhatvāt / pramāṇasiddhe ca svabhāvopavarṇanamiti nyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: And as for what <s>Vācaspati</s> [says] — 'When that [object] qualified by one <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct), namely existence, is apprehended, the apprehension of it as qualified by another limiting adjunct [does not follow], for the upādhis qualify the nature of the substance, but the upādhis or their being qualifiable are not its nature' — that too is afloat [i.e., groundless]. For it is not the case that the apprehension of another upādhi is entailed by non-difference; rather, it is precisely on the basis of difference that, when the beneficial factor is apprehended, the apprehension of the beneficiary follows. Nor is it appropriate to fabricate an inherent restriction of cognition between property and property-bearer, as in the cause-effect relation between fire and smoke, because even those two [fire and smoke] are not established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> [as having such a natural restriction]. And the principle is: only what is established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> can be described as natural.

body.text: yaccātra nyāyabhūṣaṇena sūryādigrahaṇe tadupakāryāśeṣavasturāśigrahaṇaprasañjanamuktam, tadabhiprāyānavagāhanaphalam / tathā hi tvanmate dharmadharmiṇorbhedaḥ, upakāralakṣaṇaiva ca pratyāsattistadopakārakagrahaṇe samānadeśasyaiva dharmarūpasyaiva copakāryasya grahaṇamāsañjitam / tatkathaṃ sūryopakāryasya bhinnadeśasya dravyāntarasya vā dṛṣṭavyabhicārasya grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ / tasmādekadharmadvāreṇāpi vastusvarūpapratipattau sarvātmapratīteḥ kva śabdāntareṇa vidhiniṣedhāvakāśaḥ / asti ca / tasmānna svalakṣaṇasya śabdavikalpaliṅgapratibhāsitvamiti sthitam //
body.translated_text: And as for what <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> has said here — that in the apprehension of the sun and the like, there would follow the apprehension of the entire mass of objects that are benefited by it — that results from a failure to understand the intended meaning. For in your view there is a distinction between property and property-bearer, and the proximity is characterized as beneficial relation. In the apprehension of that beneficial factor, only that which is the beneficiary — being of the nature of a property in the same location — is entailed [in the apprehension]. So how is the absurd consequence of apprehending the beneficiary of the sun, which is in a different location and is a different substance, and for which deviation [from the rule] is observed, coherent? Therefore, even through a single property, when the true nature of the object is apprehended, [there follows] the cognition of [its] entire nature — so where is there scope for assertion and negation by another word? And yet there is [such dependence on other words]. Therefore, it is established that the <s>svalaḵṣaṇa</s> (particular) does not appear in verbal cognition, <s>vikalpa</s>, or inferential marks.

body.text: nāpi sāmānyaṃ śābdapratyayapratibhāsi / saritaḥ pāre gāvaścarantīti gavādiśabdāt sāsnāśṛṅgalāṅgūlādayo 'kṣarākāraparikaritāḥ sajātīyabhedāparāmarśanāt sampiṇḍitaprāyāḥ pratibhāsante / na ca tadeva sāmānyam /
body.translated_text: Nor does <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) appear in verbal cognition. From the word '<s>gāvaḥ</s>' (cows) in [a sentence like] 'Cows are grazing on the other bank of the river,' there appear dewlap, horns, tail, and the like — accompanied by letter-shapes and without the awareness of differences among members of the same class — as if condensed together. But that is not the universal itself.

body.text: varṇākṛtyakṣarākāraśūnyaṃ gotvaṃ hi kathyate /
body.translated_text: For <s>gotva</s> (cowness) is said to be devoid of color, shape, and letter-form.

body.text: tadeva ca sāsnāśṛṅgādimātramakhilavyaktāvatyantavilakṣaṇamapi svalakṣaṇenaikīkriyamāṇaṃ sāmānyamityucyate tādṛśasya bāhyasyāprāpterbhrāntirevāsau keśapratibhāsavat / tasmād vāsanāvaśād buddhereva tadātmanā vivarto 'yamastu / asadeva vā tadrūpaṃ khyātu / vyaktaya eva vā svajātīyabhedatiraskāreṇānyathā bhāsantāmanubhavavyavadhānāt smṛtipramoṣo vābhidhīyatām / sarvathā nirviṣayaḥ khalvayaṃ sāmānyapratyayaḥ / kva sāmānyavārtā /
body.translated_text: And that very [appearance of] mere dewlap, horns, and the like — though utterly unlike every individual — when unified with the <s>svalaḵṣaṇa</s> (particular), is called '<s>sāmānya</s>' (universal). But since such an external [entity] is never reached, that [cognition] is nothing but an error, like the appearance of hair [before one with an eye-disease]. Therefore, let this be a transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of the intellect itself in that form, due to <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions); or let a non-existent form appear as that; or let the individuals themselves, by concealing the differences among their own kind, appear differently — [which amounts to] a lapse of memory due to intervening experiences. In every case, this cognition of a universal is truly without an [external] object. Where is there any talk of a universal?

body.text: yat punaḥ sāmānyābhāve sāmānyapratyayasyākasmikatvamuktaṃ tadayuktam / yataḥ pūrvapiṇḍadarśanasmaraṇasahakāriṇātiricyamānaviśeṣapratyayajanikā sāmagrī nirviṣayaṃ sāmānyavikalpamutpādayati / tadevaṃ na śābde pratyaye jātiḥ pratibhāti / nāpi pratyakṣe / na cānumānato 'pi siddhiḥ / adṛśyatve pratibaddhaliṅgādarśanāt / nāpondriyavadasyāḥ siddhiḥ jñānakāryataḥ kādācitkasyaiva nimittāntarasya siddheḥ / yadā piṇḍāntare antarāle vā gobuddherabhāvaṃ darśayet tadā śāvaleyādisakalagopiṇḍānāmevābhāvādabhāvo gobuddherupapadyamānaḥ kathamarthāntaramākṣipet / atha gotvādeva gopiṇḍaḥ / anyathā turago 'pi gopiṇḍaḥ syāt / yadyevaṃ gopiṇḍādeva gotvamanyathā turagatvamapi gotvaṃ syāt / tasmāt kāraṇaparamparāta eva (#Nibandh 64#) gopiṇḍo gotvaṃ tu bhavatu mā vā / nanu sāmānyapratyayajananasāmarthyaṃ yadyekasmāt piṇḍādabhinnaṃ tadā vijātīyavyāvṝttaṃ piṇḍāntaramasamartham / atha bhinnam, tadā tadeva sāmānyam, nāmni paraṃ vivāda iti cet / abhinnaiva sā śaktiḥ prativastu / yathā tvekaḥ śaktasvabhāvo bhāvastathānyo 'pi bhavan kīdṛśaṃ doṣamāvahati / yathā bhavatāṃ jātirekāpi samānadhvaniprasavahetuḥ, anyāpi svarūpeṇaiva jātyantaranirapekṣā, tathāsmākaṃ vyaktirapi jātinirapekṣā svarūpeṇaiva bhinnā hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: As for what was further said — that in the absence of the universal, the cognition of a universal would be uncaused — that is incorrect. Because the causal aggregate — which includes the perception of a prior individual, its recollection as a cooperating factor, and the surplus particular cognition — produces the objectless <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) of a universal. Thus, <s>jāti</s> (genus) does not appear in verbal cognition. Nor in perception. Nor is it established through inference either, because no inferential mark bound to it is observed when it is invisible. Nor is its establishment from a cognitive effect [valid], like that of the water-sense-faculty, because only a contingent other cause is established [as the explanation]. When one would show the absence of the cow-cognition in another individual or in an interval [between individuals], then, since that absence of cow-cognition is explained simply by the absence of all those individual cows such as puppies and so forth, how could it point to something else [i.e., a universal]? If [it is said that] the cow-individual is [so] precisely because of cowness — otherwise a horse too would be a cow-individual — then by the same token, cowness [exists] precisely because of the cow-individual — otherwise horse-ness too would be cowness. Therefore, from the causal chain itself the cow-individual [is explained]; cowness may or may not exist. If it is objected that the capacity to produce the cognition of a universal, if not different from a single individual, would mean that another individual excluded from a different class would lack that capacity; and if different, then that itself is the universal — the dispute is merely about the name — [we reply:] that capacity is indeed non-different in each individual. Just as one entity has the nature of that capacity, so too does another; what fault does this bring? Just as in your view a single <s>jāti</s> (genus) is the cause of producing the same sound, and another [jāti] too, by its own nature alone and independent of another genus, [so too] in our view, the individual too, independent of genus, is by its own nature alone the distinct cause.

body.text: yattu trilocanaḥ - aśvatvagotvādīnāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣāṇāṃ svāśraye samavāyaḥ sāmānyaṃ sāmānyamityabhidhānapratyayayornimittamiti / yadyevaṃ vyaktiṣvapyayameva tathābhidhānapratyayaheturastu, kiṃ sāmānyasvīkārapramādena / na ca samavāyaḥ saṃbhavī /
body.translated_text: As for what <s>Trilocana</s> [says] — that the <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) of universals and particulars such as horse-ness, cow-ness, and the like in their substratum is the cause of the expression and cognition 'sāmānya, sāmānya' (universal, universal) — if so, let this very [capacity] in the individuals themselves be the cause of that expression and cognition; what is the use of the error of accepting a universal? And <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is not possible:

children.translated_text: The establishment of <s>samavāya</s> [depends on] the cognition 'here [it is],' and the cognition 'here' [depends on] the perception of two [distinct things].

children.text: na ca kvacit tadviṣaye tvapekṣā svakalpanāmātramato 'bhyupāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: But nowhere is there a need for that [samavāya] with respect to its domain — therefore, the acceptance [of it] is merely one's own fabrication.

body.text: etena seyaṃ pratyayānuvṛttiranuvṛttavastvanuyāyinī kathamatyantabhedinīṣu vyaktiṣu vyāvṛttaviṣayapratyayabhāvānupātinīṣu bhavitumarhatītyūhāpravartanamasya pratyākhyātam / jātiṣveva parasparavyāvṛttatayā vyaktīyamānāsvanuvṛttapratyayena vyabhicārāt /
body.translated_text: By this, the conjecture that asks 'how can this recurrent cognition, which follows a recurrent object, occur in individuals that are utterly different and whose cognitions follow objects that are mutually exclusive?' — is rejected, because even in the jātis (genera) themselves, which are manifested as mutually exclusive, there is deviation from the recurrent cognition.

body.text: yat punaranena viparyaye bādhakamuktam, abhidhānapratyayānuvṛttiḥ kutaścinnivṛttya kvacideva bhavantī nimittavatī, na cānyannimittamityādi / tanna samyak / anuvṛttamantareṇāpyabhidhānapratyayānuvṛtteratadrūpaparāvṛttasvarūpaviśeṣādavaśyaṃ svīkārasya sādhitatvāt / tasmāt -
body.translated_text: And as for the defeater stated by him [<s>Trilocana</s>] for the contrary [position] — 'the recurrence of expression and cognition, occurring only in certain [things] while ceasing with respect to others, must have a basis (nimitta), and there is no other basis,' and so forth — that is not correct, because even without [positing] a recurrent [entity], it has been established that the recurrence of expression and cognition must be accepted as [arising] from a specific nature that is turned away from what is not of that form.

children.text: tulye bhede yayā jātiḥ pratyāsattyā prasarpati /
children.translated_text: The very proximity by which <s>jāti</s> (genus) extends to certain [things] and not to others —
let that itself be the basis of word and cognition.

body.text: yat punaratra nyāyabhūṣaṇoktaṃ na hyevaṃ bhavati, yayā pratyāsattyā daṇḍasūtrādikaṃ prasarpati kvacinnānyatra saiva pratyāsattiḥ puruṣasphaṭikādiṣu daṇḍisūtritvādivyavahāranibandhanamastu, kiṃ daṇḍasūtrādineti / tadasaṅgatam / daṇḍasūtrayorhi puruṣasphaṭikapratyāsannayoḥ dṛṣṭayo daṇḍisūtritva pratyayahetutvaṃ nāpalapyate / sāmānyaṃ tu svapne 'pi na dṛṣṭam / tad yadīdaṃ parikalpanīyaṃ tadā varaṃ pratyāsattireva sāmānyapratyayahetuḥ parikalpyatām, kiṃ gurvyā parikalpanayetyabhiprāyāparijñānāt /
body.translated_text: And as for what <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> says here — 'It is not the case that the very proximity by which the staff, thread, and the like extend to certain [things] and not to others — that very proximity in persons, crystals, and the like should be the basis of the usage one-who-has-a-staff, one-who-has-a-thread, and so forth — what need of a staff, thread, and so forth?' — that is incoherent. For it is not denied that the proximity of the staff and thread to the person and crystal, when perceived, is the cause of the cognition of one-who-has-a-staff and one-who-has-a-thread. But the universal has never been perceived even in a dream. If this [universal] is to be posited, then it would be better to posit proximity itself as the cause of the cognition of a universal — what need of a weighty fabrication? — [this objection arises] from a failure to understand the intended meaning.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 65#)
athedaṃ jātiprasādhakamanumānamabhidhīyate / yadviśiṣṭajñānaṃ tadviśeṣaṇagrahaṇanāntarīyakam / yathā daṇḍijñānam / viśiṣṭajñānaṃ cedaṃ gaurayamityarthataḥ kāryahetuḥ / viśeṣaṇānubhavakāryaṃ hi dṛṣṭānte viśiṣṭabuddhiḥ siddheti / atrānuyogaḥ / viśiṣṭabuddherbhinnaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇanāntarīyakatvaṃ vā sādhyaṃ viśeṣaṇamātrānubhavanāntarīyakatvaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: Now, this inference for establishing <s>jāti</s> (genus) is stated: Whatever is a qualified cognition necessarily involves the apprehension of a qualifier — like the cognition 'one who has a staff.' And this cognition 'this is a cow' is a qualified cognition — this is essentially a reason based on effect (<s>kārya-hetu</s>). For in the example, the qualified cognition is established as an effect of the experience of a qualifier. Here is the challenge: Is what is to be established the entailment of the qualified cognition with the apprehension of a distinct qualifier, or the entailment with the experience of a qualifier in general?

body.text: prathamapakṣe pakṣasya pratyakṣabādhā sādhanāvadhānamanavakāśayati, vastugrāhiṇaḥ pratyakṣasyobhayapratibhāsābhāvāt / viśiṣṭabuddhitvaṃ ca sāmānyaheturanaikāntikaḥ, bhinnaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇamantareṇāpi darśanāt / yathā svarūpavān ghaṭaḥ, gotvaṃ sāmānyamiti vā /
body.translated_text: In the first alternative, perceptual contradiction of the thesis prevents the proof from gaining a foothold, because perception, which apprehends the real object, has no appearance of both [a distinct qualifier and qualified]. And the reason 'being a qualified cognition' is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) with respect to [the probandum of apprehending] a distinct qualifier, because [qualified cognition] is observed even without the apprehension of a distinct qualifier — as in [the cognitions] 'the pot possesses its own form' or 'cowness is a universal.'

body.text: dvitīyapakṣe tu siddhasādhanam / svarūpavān ghaṭa ityādivat gotvajātimān piṇḍa iti parikalpitaṃ bhedamupādāya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasyeṣṭatvādagovyāvṛttānubhavabhāvitvād gaurayamiti vyavahārasya / tadevaṃ na sāmānyasiddhiḥ / bādhakaṃ ca sāmānyaguṇakarmādyupādhicakrasya kevalavyaktigrāhakaṃ paṭupratyakṣaṃ dṛśyānupalambho vā prasiddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the second alternative, it is [a case of] proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). For, just as in 'the pot possesses its own form,' so too in 'the individual possesses cow-genus' — the relation of qualifier and qualified is accepted [by us] based on a fictitious distinction; and the usage 'this is a cow' arises from experiencing the exclusion of non-cow. Thus, <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) is not established. And the well-known defeater [against it] is acute perception that apprehends only individuals, setting aside the entire wheel of <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts) such as universals, qualities, actions, and the like — or the non-apprehension of the visible.

body.text: tadevaṃ vidhireva śabdārthaḥ / sa ca bāhyo 'rtho buddhyākāraśca vivakṣitaḥ / tatra na buddhyākārasya tattvataḥ saṃvṛtyā vā vidhiniṣedhau, svasaṃvedanapratyakṣagamyatvāt / anadhyavasāyācca / nāpi tattvato bāhyasyāpi vidhiniṣedhau, tasya śābde pratyayepratibhāsanāt / ata eva sarvadharmāṇāṃ tattvato 'nabhilāpyatvaṃ pratibhāsādhyavasāyābhāvāt / tasmād bāhyasyaiva sāṃvṛtau vidhiniṣedhau / anyathā saṃvyavahārahāniprasaṅgāt / tadevaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus, the meaning of words is positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>) alone. And that is intended as both an external object and an aspect of cognition (<s>buddhyākāra</s>). Of these, the aspect of cognition is neither ultimately nor conventionally subject to assertion or negation, because it is known through the perception of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), and because there is no determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) [regarding it by words]. Nor are assertion and negation of the external [object] ultimate, because that [external object] does not appear in verbal cognition. For this very reason, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are ultimately inexpressible (<s>anabhilāpya</s>), because they are not objects of appearance and determination [by words]. Therefore, assertion and negation are of the external [object] in conventional [discourse] alone; otherwise, there would follow the destruction of all practical transactions. Thus:

children.translated_text: Neither of the [mental] aspect nor of the external [object] is positive assertion established ultimately;

children.text: bahireva hi saṃvṛtyā saṃvṛtyāpi tu nākṛteḥ //
children.translated_text: it is only of the external conventionally — and even conventionally, not of the [mental] form.

body.text: etena yad dharmottaraḥ āropitasya bāhyatvasya vidhiniṣedhāvityalaukikamanāgamamatārkikīyaṃ kathayati, tadapyapahastitam /
body.translated_text: By this, what <s>Dharmottara</s> says — that assertion and negation pertain to externality as superimposed — which is an extra-ordinary, non-scriptural, and merely speculative statement — is also refuted.

body.text: nanvavyavasāye yadyadhyavaseyaṃ vastu na sphurati tadā tadadhyavasitamiti ko 'rthaḥ / apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtamiti yo 'rthaḥ / apratibhāsāviśeṣe viṣayāntaraparihāreṇa kathaṃ niyataviṣayā pravṛttiriti cet / ucyate / yadyapi viśvamagṛhītaṃ tathāpi vikalpasya niyatasāmagrīprasūtatvena niyatākāratayā, niyataśaktitvāt niyataiva jalādau pravṛttiḥ / dhūmasya parokṣāgnijñānajananavat /
body.translated_text: But [you object:] in the conceptual determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), when the particular thing that is to be determined does not appear [directly], what does it mean [to say] 'that is determined'? [Reply:] The meaning is that even without appearing [directly], it is made the object of purposive activity. [Objection:] In the absence of any difference in non-appearance [between objects], how can there be purposive activity directed at a specific object, with the exclusion of other objects? [Reply:] We say: although the particular is not apprehended [by the conceptual cognition], nevertheless, since the conceptual cognition is produced from a determinate assemblage [of causes], it has a determinate form and, due to having a determinate capacity, the purposive activity toward water and such is necessarily determinate — just as smoke generates knowledge of fire that is not directly perceived.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 66#)
niyataviṣayā hi bhāvāḥ pramāṇapariniṣṭhitasvabhāvā na śaktisāṃkaryaparyanuyogabhājaḥ / tasmāt tadadhyavasāyitva mākāraviśeṣayogāt tatpravṛttijanakatvam / na ca sādṛśyādāropeṇa pravṛttiṃ brūmaḥ, yenākāre bāhyasya bāhye vā ākārasyāropadvāreṇa dūṣaṇābakāśaḥ / kiṃ tarhi svavāsanāvipākavaśādupajāyamānaiva buddhirapaśyantyapi bāhyaṃ bāhye pravṛttimātanotīti viplutaiva / tadevamanyābhāvaviśiṣṭo vijātivyāvṛtto 'rtho vidhiḥ / sa eva cāpohaśabdavācyaḥ śabdānāmarthaḥ pravṛttinivṛttiviṣayaśceti sthitam /
body.translated_text: [Nibandh 66] For entities that have a fixed object-domain and whose own nature is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) are not susceptible to the charge of confusion of capacities. Therefore, [a cognition's] being a determination of that [object] — due to possessing a particular form — is [the same as its being] a generator of purposive activity toward that [object]. And we do not say that purposive activity [occurs] through superimposition based on resemblance — such that there would be room for the objection of superimposing the external onto the form or the form onto the external. Rather, the cognition, arising solely through the ripening of its own latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), even though not perceiving the external [object], extends purposive activity toward the external [object] — it is thus 'deluded' [by nature]. Thus, an object that is distinguished by the absence of what is other — excluded from what is of a different kind — is the positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>). And it is precisely this that is referred to by the word <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) [as] the meaning of words, and [as] the object of purposive activity and cessation — this is established.

body.text: atra prayogaḥ / yad vācakaṃ tatsarvamadhyavasitātadrūpaparāvṛtavastumātragocaram / yatheha kūpe jalamiti vacanam / vācakaṃ cedaṃ gavādiśabdarūpamiti svabhāvahetuḥ / nāyamasiddhaḥ / pūrvoktena nyāyena pāramārthikavācyavācakabhāvasyābhāve 'pyadhyavasāyakṛtasyaiva sarvavyavahāribhiravaśyaṃ svīkarttavyatvāt / anyathā sarvavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgāt / nāpi viruddhaḥ / sapakṣe bhāvāt / na cānaikāntikaḥ / tathā hi śabdānāmadhyavasitavijātivyāvṛttavastumātraviṣayatvamanicchadbhiḥ paraiḥ paramārthato
body.translated_text: Here is the formal proof: Whatever is an expressive word, all of that has as its object merely a thing that is excluded from what is not of that nature — [a thing that is] the content of determination. Just as the statement 'there is water in this well.' And this, in the form of [words like] 'cow' and such, is indeed an expressive word — this is a reason based on essential nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). This [reason] is not unestablished, because although there is no real expressor-expressed relation in the ultimate sense, the one [merely] established through determination must necessarily be accepted by all who engage in [verbal] transactions, by the reasoning stated above. Otherwise, the absurd consequence of the annihilation of all transactions would follow. Nor is it contradictory, since it obtains in the positive instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>). Nor is it inconclusive. For those opponents who do not wish [to accept] that words have as their object merely a thing excluded from what is of a different kind, [must hold that] in the ultimate sense [the expressed meaning is one of the following]:

body.text: vācyaṃ svalakṣaṇamupādhirupādhiyogaḥ sopādhirastu yadi vā kṛtirastu buddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'The expressed [meaning] is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), or a qualifying property (<s>upādhi</s>), or the connection with a qualifying property, or the qualified [entity], or alternatively the [mental] construction, or the <s>Buddha</s> [himself] —'

body.text: gatyantarābhāvāt / aviṣayatve ca vācakatvāyogāt /
body.translated_text: Due to the absence of any other alternative. And in the absence of [any] object, the status of being an expressive [word] is impossible.

body.text: tatra ādyantayorna samayaḥ phalaśaktihānermadhye 'pyupādhivirahāt tritayena yuktaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Of these, the first and last [options] have no conventional agreement, [because they suffer from] the loss of [the capacity to produce] a fruit. In the middle [options] too, due to the absence of the qualifying property, [the objection applies] to [all] three [together].'

body.text: tadevaṃ vācyāntarasyābhāvāt viṣayavattvalakṣaṇasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau vipakṣato nivarttamānaṃ vācakatvamadhyavasitabāhyaviṣayatvena vyāpyata iti vyāptisiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, since there is no other [viable] expressed meaning, and since the pervader — namely, having an object-domain — ceases in the counter-instance, the property of being an expressive word, which withdraws from the counter-instance, is pervaded by having a determined external object — thus the establishment of the pervasion [is achieved].

body.text: mahāpaṇḍitaratnakīrtipādavira(ci) tamapohaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Apoha-prakaraṇa</s> (Treatise on Exclusion) composed by the great scholar <s>Ratnakīrti</s> is concluded.
[Nibandh 67]

body.text: // kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s> (Proof of Momentariness)

body.text: / anvayātmikā //
body.translated_text: The positive form (<s>anvayātmikā</s>).

body.text: ṃamastārāyai //
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Tārā</s>!

children.translated_text: The pervasion that has the positive form, which implies the negative [concomitance], is here stated for the reason of existence (<s>sattva</s>) in a positive example (<s>sādharmyavat dṛṣṭānta</s>).
Whatever exists is momentary — like a pot. And the objects in dispute are existent — thus [the proof].

body.text: yat sat tat kṣaṇikam / yathā ghaṭaḥ / santaśvāmī vivādāspadībhūtā padarthā iti /
body.translated_text: The capacity of the reason to establish a non-evident object cannot be demonstrated without removing the suspicion of it being a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>). And pseudo-reasons are threefold in division: unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

body.text: hetoḥ parokṣārthapratipādakatvaṃ hetvābhāsatvaśaṅkānirākaraṇamantareṇa na śakyate pratipādayitum / hetvābhāsāśca aśiddhaviruddhānaikāntikaprabhedena trividhāḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, this reason [of existence] is not unestablished. For although in different philosophical systems various definitions of the characteristic of existence have been stated — such as 'being capable of causal efficacy' (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), 'inherence with universal existence' (<s>sattāsamavāya</s>), 'having one's own nature' (<s>svarūpasattva</s>), 'possessing origination, destruction, and permanence' (<s>utpādavyayadhrauvyayogitva</s>), 'being an object of a <s>pramāṇa</s>' (<s>pramāṇaviṣayatva</s>), 'being within the range of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that apprehends it,' 'being an object of designation,' and so forth — nevertheless, what use is this irrelevant matter, now pinned [to the discussion]? Whatever definition of the existence of things will prove tenable when examined by <s>pramāṇa</s>, that very one we too shall accept. Only this — causal efficacy — is well-known to all people, and it is precisely this that, intended by the word 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>), has been taken up as the reason. And that [causal efficacy], as cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s> such as perception or inference in entities whose existence is established by such <s>pramāṇas</s> and which are made the subjects [of the proof] — thus there is not even the possibility of the [reason being] unestablished either in its own nature or through the locus.

body.text: tatra na tāvadayamasiddho hetuḥ / yadi nāma darśane darśane nānāprakāraṃ sattvalakṣaṇamuktamāste, arthakriyākārittvaṃ, sattāsamavāyaḥ, svarūpasattvam, utpādavyayadhrauvyayogitvaṃ, pramāṇaviṣayattvaṃ tadupalambhakapramāṇagocaratvaṃ, vyapadeśaviṣayatvamityādi, tathāpi kimanenāprastutenedānīmeva niṣṭaṅkitena / yadeva hi pramāṇato nirūpyamāṇaṃ kadārthānāṃ sattvamupapannaṃ bhaviṣyati tadeva vayamapi svīkariṣyāmaḥ / kevalaṃ tadetadarthakriyākāritvaṃ sarvajanaprasiddhamāste tat khalvatra sattvaśabdenābhisandhāya sādhanatvenopāttam / tacca yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣānumānapramāṇaprasiddhasadbhāveṣu bhāveṣu pakṣikṛteṣu pratyakṣādinā pramāṇena pratītamiti na svarūpeṇāśrayadvāreṇa bāsiddhisaṃbhāvanāpi //
body.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction, since [the reason] obtains in the pot, which is made the positive instance. [Objection:] But how can [the pot] be a positive instance, since momentariness is [equally] unestablished in it, just as in the subject? For its momentariness is not established through perception, since there is no certainty of it as such. Nor through the inference from existence, since if another example were required [for that inference], there would be an infinite regress. And there is no other inference. Or if there is, then by that very [inference] momentariness would be established in the subject itself, making the existence-inference superfluous.

body.text: nāpi viruddhatā,sapakṣīkṛte ghaṭe sadbhāvāt / nanu kathamasya sapakṣatvam, pakṣavadatrāpi kṣaṇabhaṅgāsiddheḥ / na hyasya pratyakṣataḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ, tathātvenāniścayāt / nāpi sattvānumānataḥ,punarnidarśanāntarāpekṣāyāmanavasthānaprasaṅgāt / na cānyadanumānamasti / saṃbhave vā tenaiva pakṣe 'pi kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddheralaṃ sattvānumāneneti cet /
body.translated_text: [We] reply: There is indeed another inference — in the form of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio ad absurdum) and <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> (reversal of the reductio) — which is an additional <s>pramāṇa</s> proving the momentariness of the pot. For consider: the pot, at the present moment, performs one causal action. [The question is:] At past and future moments too, would it perform that same causal action, or a different one, or no action at all? — these are three positions.

body.text: ucyate / anumānāntarameva prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayātmakaṃ ghaṭasya kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhakaṃ pramāṇāntaramasti / tathā hi ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇe tāvadekāmarthakriyāṃ (#Nibandh 68#) karoti / atītānāgatakṣaṇayorapi ki tāmevārthakriyāṃ kuryāt, anyāṃ vā, na vā kāmapi kriyāmiti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: The first position is not tenable here, because what has [already] been done cannot be done [again].

body.text: nātra prathamaḥ pakṣo yuktaḥ, kṛtasya karaṇāyogāt /
body.translated_text: If the second is accepted, then let this be examined: when the pot performs an effect occurring at the present moment, is it also capable of [producing] an effect occurring at past and future moments, or not? If it is capable, then just as with the effect at the present moment, it should produce the effect at past and future moments at that very [present] time — since it is [equally] capable with respect to those too, and since there can be no delay for one that is capable. Otherwise, even the effect at the present moment would absurdly fail to be produced — since there is no difference [in the pot's nature] between the earlier and later times. And for one that is [fully] capable, dependence on auxiliary causes is impossible. If it is not capable, then since contradictory properties of being capable and not capable with respect to one [and the same] effect are superimposed [on the pot], its momentary destruction becomes an unstoppable conclusion.
