body.text: atha dvitīyo 'bhyupagamyate, tadidamatra vicāryatām / yadā ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇabhāvi kāryaṃ karoti tadā kimatītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvinyapi kārye śakto 'śakto vā / yadi śaktastadā vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryavadatītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvyapi kāryaṃ tadaiva kuryāt / tatrāpi śaktatvāt / śaktasya ca kṣepāyogāt / anyathā varttamānakṣaṇabhāvino 'pi kāryasyākaraṇaprasaṅgāt / pūrvāparakālayorapi śaktatvenāviśeṣāt / samarthasya ca sahakāryapekṣāyā ayogāt / athāśaktaḥ, tadaikatra kārye śaktāśaktatvaviruddhadharmādhyāsāt kṣaṇavidhvaṃso ghaṭasya durvāraprasaraḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: Nor does the third position work, because the nature of being capable persists [as such]. For when even a delay is intolerable for a capable entity, non-production is all the more excluded. Otherwise, as stated, even the present effect would fail to be produced.

body.text: nāpi tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ saṅgacchate, śaktasvabhāvānuvṛttereva / yadā hi śaktasya padārthasya vilambo 'pyasahyastadā dūrotsāritamakaraṇam / anyathā vārtamānikasyāpi kāryasyākaraṇaṃ syādityuktam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, whatever, whenever, is a legitimate object of the convention 'it produces [that],' it produces that at that time. And if it does not produce [it], it is not a legitimate object of the convention of production. Thus, since the pot differs at every moment by having the nature of being capable with respect to one effect and otherwise [incapable with respect to others], its positive-instance status is intact.

body.text: tasmād yad yadā yajjananavyavahārapātraṃ tattadā tat kuryāt / akurvacca na jananavyavahārabhājanam / tadevamekatra kārye samarthetarasvabhāvatayā pratikṣaṇaṃ bhedād ghaṭasya sapakṣatvamakṣatam //
body.translated_text: Here is the formal proof: Whatever, whenever, is fit for the convention of producing something, that produces that at that time — just as the final assemblage of causes [produces] its own effect.

body.text: atra prayogaḥ / yad yadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tat tadā tajjanayatyeva / yathā antyā kāraṇasāmagrī svakāryam /
body.translated_text: And this pot, which is fit for the convention of producing effects at past and future moments, [should produce them] at the time of producing the present-moment effect — and at the time of the lapse of all [other] causal activity — this is the <s>prasaṅga</s> based on a reason of essential nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). And this [property of] being an object of the convention of producing effects at the second and subsequent moments — [used as] the <s>prasaṅga</s>-reason — is established in the pot (the subject) merely through the opponent's own admission, both at the time of producing the present-moment effect and at the time of the lapse of all causal activity — thus unestablishedness is out of the question.

body.text: atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryajananavyavahārayogyaścāyaṃ ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle 'pīti svabhāvahetuprasaṅgaḥ / asya ca dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇavyavahāragocaratvasya prasaṅgasādhanasya vārtamānikakāryakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle ca ghaṭe dharmiṇi parābhyupagamamātrataḥ siddhatvādasiddhistāvadasaṃbhavinī /
body.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction, since it is possible for [the reason] to obtain in the positive instance of the final causal assemblage.

body.text: nāpi viruddhatā, sapakṣe 'ntyakāraṇasāmagryāṃ sadbhāvasaṃbhavāt /
body.translated_text: But [you object:] this reason is commonly inconclusive (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), because the [property used as the] reason — namely, being an object of the convention of being capable — is observed even in the counter-instance, i.e., a seed stored in a granary, which does not directly produce [anything]. [Reply:] No, because the convention of being capable is of two kinds: ultimate and figurative. Here, what is taken as the reason is the being-an-object-of-the-convention-of-production that is ultimate, i.e., connected with actual production. And since that is impossible in a seed stored in a granary and the like — which is an object of merely figurative convention of production, due to being the cause of a cause — how can there be common inconclusiveness?

body.text: nanvayaṃ sādhāraṇānaikāntiko hetuḥ / sākṣādajanake 'pi kuśūlādyavasthitavījādau vipakṣe samarthavyavahāragocaratvasya sādhanasya darśanāditi cet / na / dvividho hi samarthavyavahāraḥ - pāramārthika aupacārikaśca / tatra yatpāramārthikaṃ jananaprayuktaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ tadiha sādhanatvenopāttam / tasya ca kuśūlādyavasthitabījādau kāraṇakāraṇatvādaupacārikajananavyavahāraviṣayabhūte saṃbhavābhāvāt kutaḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntikatā /
body.translated_text: [Nibandh 69] Nor does this [reason] have doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatirekitā</s>), because a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> exists for the contrary. For it is well-known from universal experience that this being-an-object-of-the-convention-of-production is pervaded by having a fixed object-domain. And this [fixed domain] is not without a cause, because otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of no restriction of place, time, and nature. And no cause other than production is perceived, due to the observation that [the convention] follows the positive and negative [concomitance] of that [production].

body.text:
(#Nibandh 69#)
na cāsya sandigdhavyatirekitā, viparyaye bādhakapramāṇasadbhāvāt / tathā hīdaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ niyataviṣayatvena vyāptamiti sarvajanānubhavaprasiddham / na cedaṃ nirnimittam, deśakālasvabhāvaniyamābhāvaprasaṅgāt / na ca jananādanyannimittamupalabhyate, tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: And if being an object of the convention of production could exist even without production, then everyone would have the convention of producing everything everywhere — and there would be no restriction. But this [restriction] is perceived as fixed. Therefore, when in the counter-instance — where production is absent — the pervader, namely having a fixed object-domain, ceases, the being-an-object-of-the-convention-of-production, which withdraws [with it], comes to rest in production alone — thus, since the pervasion is established, the reason is faultless. And this pot does not produce an effect occurring at past and future moments at the time of producing the present-moment effect, nor at the time when all causal activity has elapsed. Therefore, it is not fit for the convention of production [of those effects] — [all this follows from] the principle that every <s>prasaṅga</s> terminates in its <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s>.

body.text: yadi ca jananamantareṇāpi jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ syāt tadā sarvasya sarvatra jananavyavahāra ityaniyamaḥ syāt / niyataścāyaṃ pratītaḥ / tato jananābhāve vipakṣe niyataviṣayatvasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau nivartamānaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ janana eva viśrāmyatīti vyāptisiddheranavadyo hetuḥ / na caiṣa ghaṭo varttamānakāryakaraṇakṣaṇe sakalakriyātikramaṇe cātītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvi kārya janayati / tato na jananavyavahārayogyaḥ, sarvaḥ prasaṅgaḥ prasaṅgaviparyayaniṣṭha iti nyāyāt //
body.translated_text: Here too is the formal proof: Whatever, whenever, does not produce something, that is not, at that time, fit for the convention of being capable with respect to that [thing] — just as a <s>kodrava</s> (weed) grain, which does not produce a rice sprout, [is not fit for the convention of being capable] with respect to a rice sprout. And this pot does not produce an effect occurring at past and future moments at the time of producing the present-moment effect and at the time of the lapse of all causal activity — this is a non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) that separates the capable moment from the incapable moment.

body.text: atrāpi prayogaḥ / yad yadā yanna karoti na tattadā tatra samarthavyavahārayogyam / yathā śālyaṅkuramakurvan kodravaḥ śālyaṅkure / na karoti caiṣā ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle cātītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvi kāryamitivyāpakānupalabdhirbhinatti samarthakṣaṇādasamarthakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: Here too there is no unestablishedness, since it is impossible for the pot to produce an effect at past and future moments at the time of producing the present-moment effect and at the time when all causal activity has elapsed.

body.text: atrāpyasiddhirnāsti, vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle cātītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇasyāyogāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction, since [the reason] obtains in the positive instance.

body.text: nāpi virodhaḥ, sapakṣe bhāvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there inconclusiveness, because the pervasion — complete in its universal scope — between being-an-object-of-the-convention-of-being-capable and production, both being positive entities, has been established by the reasoning stated above.

body.text: na cānaikāntikatā, pūrvoktena nyāyena samarthavyavahāragocaratvajanakatvayorvidhibhūtayoḥ sarvopasaṃhāravatyā vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt //
body.translated_text: Now, as to the objection raised here — 'in the statement "whatever, whenever, does not produce something, that is not at that time capable with respect to it," what is the meaning of "produces"? Is it causality, or the completeness of the assemblage of cooperating conditions conducive to the arising of the effect, or unfailing [connection with] the effect, or connection with the effect?' — Of these, the meaning of 'produces' is precisely causality. Therefore, the faults arising from the other alternatives are thwarted by non-acceptance.

body.text: yat punaratroktam, yad yadā yanna karoti na tattadā tatra samarthamityatra kaḥ karotyarthaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇatvam / uta kāryotpādānuguṇasahakārisākalyam / ahosvit kāryāvyabhicāraḥ / kāryasaṃbandho veti / tatra kāraṇatvameva karotyarthaḥ / tataḥ pakṣāntarabhāvino doṣā anabhyupagamapratihatāḥ /
body.translated_text: And it is not proper to say here that the non-apprehension of the pervader is not different from the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) on the grounds that causality and capacity are synonymous in this subject, since what is to be proved is the absence of being-an-object-of-the-convention-of-being-capable. And between causality and being-an-object-of-the-convention-of-being-capable, there is a difference in exclusion, like between 'tree' and '<s>śiṃśapā</s>' (a type of tree) — thus there is no occasion for this kind of petty babble.

body.text: na cātra pakṣe kāraṇatvasāmarthyayoḥ paryāyatvena vyāpakānupalambhasya sādhyāviśiṣṭatvamabhidhātumucitam, samarthavyavahāragocaratvābhāvasya sādhyatvāt / kāraṇatvasamarthavyavahāragocaratvayośca vṛkṣaśiṃśapayoriva vyāvṛttibhedo 'stītyanavasara evaivaṃvidhasya kṣudrapralāpasya /
body.translated_text: Thus, through the force of the pair of reasons — <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> — momentariness is established in the pot as an example. How then can it be said that there is no inference other than [that from] existence that proves momentariness in the example? And there is no superfluity of the existence-reason [in the main proof], since the <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> [merely] establish momentariness in the example alone.

body.text: tadevaṃ prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayahetudvayabalato ghaṭe dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ siddhaḥ / tat kathaṃ sattvādanyadanumānaṃ dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhakaṃ nāstītyucyate / na caivaṃ sattvahetorvaiyarthyam, dṛṣṭāntamātra eva prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayābhyāṃ kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhanāt //
body.translated_text: Thus, through the force of the pair of reasons — <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> — momentariness is established in the pot as an example. How then can it be said that there is no inference other than [that from] existence that proves momentariness in the example? And there is no superfluity of the existence-reason [in the main proof], since the <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅga-viparyaya</s> [merely] establish momentariness in the example alone.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 70#)
nanvābhyāmeva pakṣe 'pi kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhirastviti cet / astu, ko doṣaḥ / yo hi pratipattā prativastu yad yadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tattadā tajjanayati ityādikamupanyasitumanalasastasya tata eva kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ / yastu prativastu tannyāyopanyāsaprayāsabhīruḥ sa khalvekatra dharmiṇi yad yadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tattadā tajjanayati ityādinyāyena sattvamātramasthairyavyāptamavadhārya sattvādevānyatra kṣaṇikatvamavagacchatīti, kathamapramato vaiyarthyamasyācakṣīta / tadevamekakāryakāriṇo ghaṭasya dvitīyādikṣaṇa bhāvikāryāpekṣayā samarthetarasvabhāvaviruddhadharmādhyāsād bheda eveti kṣaṇabhaṅgitayā sapakṣatāmāvahati ghaṭe sattvaheturupalabhyamāno na viruddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: Let momentariness be established even through these two [i.e., positive and negative concomitance] in the thesis itself. Reply: So be it — what is the fault? For one who is not too lazy to present the reasoning 'whatever is fit for the conventional usage of producing such-and-such at such-and-such a time produces that at that time' with respect to each entity — for that person, momentariness is established from that very reasoning. But one who is reluctant to undertake the labor of presenting this reasoning for each entity — he, having ascertained through the reasoning 'whatever is fit for the conventional usage of producing such-and-such at such-and-such a time produces that at that time' in one case that mere existence (<s>sattva</s>) is pervaded by impermanence, then understands momentariness elsewhere from existence alone. How would an attentive person declare this to be futile? Thus, since a pot that produces a single effect, by the superimposition of contradictory properties — namely, having a nature that is more capable [at the first moment] compared to effects that arise in the second and subsequent moments — is indeed different [at each moment], the reason of existence, being observed in the case of the pot, which thereby serves as a concordant instance by virtue of its momentariness, is not contradictory.

body.text: na cāyamanaikāntikaḥ, atraiva sādharmyavati dṛṣṭānte sarvopasaṃhāravatyā vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt / nanu viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalād vyāptisiddhiḥ / tasya copanyāsavārtāpi nāsti / tatkathaṃ vyāptiḥ prasādhiteti cet / tadetat taralabuddhivilasitam / tathā hi uktametad vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle 'tītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikārye 'pi ghaṭasya śaktisaṃbhave tadānīmeva tatkaraṇam / akaraṇe ca śaktāśaktasvabhāvatayā pratikṣaṇaṃ bheda iti kṣaṇikatvena vyāptaiva sā arthakriyāśaktiḥ //
body.translated_text: Nor is this reason inconclusive, since the pervasion with a comprehensive induction is established in this very concordant example. Objection: The establishment of pervasion is through the force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means) that contradicts the counter-thesis. But there is not even a mention of its presentation. So how is the pervasion established? Reply: This is the play of a fickle intellect. For it has been stated: at the time of producing the effect that exists at the present moment, if the pot also has the capacity for producing the effects existing at past and future moments, it would produce them at that very time. And if it does not produce them, then, by virtue of being of a capable and incapable nature [respectively], there is difference at each moment — thus the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāśakti</s>) is indeed pervaded by momentariness.

body.text: nanvevamanvayamātramastu / vipakṣāt punarekāntena vyāvṛttiriti kuto labhyata iti cet / vyāptisiddhereva / vyatirekasandehe vyāptisiddhireva kathamiti cet / na / dvividhā hi vyāptisiddhiḥ / anvayarūpā ca kartṛdharmaḥ sādhanadharmavati dharmiṇi sādhyadharmasyāvaśyambhāvo yaḥ, vyatirekarūpā ca karmadharmaḥ sādhyābhāve sādhanasyāvaśyambhāvoyaḥ / enayoścaikatarapratītirniyamena dvitīyapratītimākṣipati / anyathaikasyā evāsiddheḥ / tasmād yathā viparyaye bādhakapramāṇabalāt niyamavati vyatireke siddhe 'nvayaviṣayaḥ saṃśayaḥ pūrvaṃ sthito 'pi paścāt parigalati tato 'nvayaprasādhanārthaṃ na pṛthak sādhanamucyate tathā prasaṅgatadviparyayahetudvayabalato niyamavatyanvaye siddhe vyatirekaviṣaye pūrvaṃ sthito 'pi sandehaḥ paścāt parigalatyeva /
body.translated_text: Objection: Let there be mere positive concomitance in this way. But how is the definite exclusion from the counter-instance obtained? Reply: From the very establishment of pervasion. Objection: How can there be establishment of pervasion when there is doubt about the negative concomitance? Reply: No. For the establishment of pervasion is twofold: the positive form, which is the agent's property — namely, the necessary presence of the property to be proved in the subject possessing the proving property; and the negative form, which is the object's property — namely, the necessary absence of the proving property in the absence of what is to be proved. Of these two, the cognition of either one necessarily entails the cognition of the other; otherwise, neither one alone would be established. Therefore, just as when the negative concomitance is established — through the force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that contradicts the counter-thesis — in a determinate form, any doubt previously existing regarding the positive concomitance dissolves, and hence no separate proof is stated for establishing the positive concomitance; similarly, when the determinate positive concomitance is established through the force of the twin reasons of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its reversal, any doubt previously existing regarding the negative concomitance also dissolves.

body.text: na ca vyatirekaprasādhakamanyat pramāṇaṃ vaktavyam / tataśca sādhyābhāve sādhanasyaikāntiko vyatirekaḥ / sādhane sati sādhyasyāvaśyamanvayo veti na kaścidarthabhedaḥ / tadevaṃ viparyayabādhakapramāṇamantareṇāpi prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayahetudvayabalādanvayarūpavyāptisiddho sattvahetoranaikāntikatvasyābhāvādataḥ sādhanāt kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiranavadyeti //
body.translated_text: And no other <s>pramāṇa</s> need be stated for establishing the negative concomitance. Thus, the definite exclusion of the proving property in the absence of what is to be proved, and the necessary positive concomitance of what is to be proved when the proving property is present — there is no difference in meaning. Therefore, even without a <s>pramāṇa</s> that contradicts the counter-thesis, because the non-inconclusiveness of the reason of existence is established through the force of the twin reasons of <s>prasaṅga</s> and reversal-of-<s>prasaṅga</s>, the proof of momentariness from this reason is faultless.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 71#)
nanu ca sādhanamidamasiddham / na hi kāraṇabuddhyā kārya gṛhyate, tasya bhāvitvāt / na ca kāryabuddhyākāraṇam, tasyātītatvāt / na ca vartamānagrāhiṇā jñānenātītānāgatayorgrahaṇam, atiprasaṅgāt / na ca pūrvāparayoḥ kālayorekaḥ pratisandhātā asti, kṣaṇabhaṅgabhaṅgaprasaṅgāt / kāraṇābhāve tu kāryābhāvapratītiḥ svasaṃvedanavādino manorathasyāpyaviṣayaḥ / nanu ca pūrvottarakālayoḥ saṃvitto, tābhyāṃ vāsanā, tayā ca hetūphalāvasāyo vikalpa iti cet tadayuktam /
body.translated_text: Objection: This proof is unestablished. For an effect is not grasped through a cognition of the cause, since the effect is future. Nor is a cause grasped through a cognition of the effect, since the cause is past. Nor can a cognition that grasps the present grasp the past and future, since that would lead to absurd overextension. Nor is there a single entity that connects the earlier and later moments, since that would contradict momentariness. But the cognition of the absence of an effect upon the absence of its cause is beyond even the fantasy of one who advocates self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>). Objection: There is awareness of the earlier and later moments, from those two arise impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), and from those arises the conceptual judgment determining cause and effect. Reply: That is improper.

body.text: sa hi vikalpo gṛhītānusandhāyako 'tadrūpasamāropako vā / na prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ / ekasya pratisandhāturabhāve pūrvāparagrahaṇayorayogāt /vikalpavāsanāyā evābhāvāt / nāpi dvitīyaḥ / marīcikāyāmapi jalavijñānasya prāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt / tadevamanvayavyatirekayorapratipatterarthakriyālakṣaṇaṃ sattvamasiddhamiti //
body.translated_text: For that conceptual judgment is either one that connects what has already been grasped, or one that superimposes what is not of that nature. The first alternative does not hold, because in the absence of a single connecting entity, the grasping of the earlier and later is impossible — since there would be no impression-for-conceptual-judgment at all. Nor does the second hold, because then the water-cognition in a mirage would also turn out to be a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore, since positive and negative concomitance are not apprehended, existence (<s>sattva</s>) defined as causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is unestablished.

body.text: kiṃ ca prakārāntarādapīdaṃ sādhanamasiddham / tathā hi bījādīnāṃ sāmarthyaṃ bījādijñānāt tatkāryādaṅkurādervā niścetavyam / kāryatvaṃ ca vastutvasiddhau sidhyati / vastutvaṃ ca kāryāntarāt / kāryāntarasyāpi kāryatvaṃ vastutvasiddhau / tadvastutvaṃ ca tadaparakāryāntarādityanavasthā /
body.translated_text: Moreover, this proof is unestablished from another angle as well. For the capacity of seeds and the like must be ascertained either from the cognition of seeds and the like, or from their effect, namely sprouts and the like. And effecthood is established only when reality (<s>vastutva</s>) is established. And reality is established from another effect. And the effecthood of that other effect too depends on the establishment of reality. And that reality again depends on yet another effect — thus there is infinite regress.

body.text: athānavasthābhayāt paryante kāryāntaraṃ nāpekṣate, tadā tenaiva pūrveṣāmasattvaprasaṅgānnaikasyāpyarthasāmarthya sidhyati /
body.translated_text: If, out of fear of infinite regress, the last member does not require a further effect, then by that very reasoning, since the non-reality of the prior members would follow, the capacity of not even a single entity would be established.

body.text: nanu kāryatvasattvayorbhinnavyāvṛttikatvāt sattāsiddhāvapi kāryatvasiddhau kā kṣatiriti cet / tadasaṅgatam / satyapi kāryatvasattvayorvyāvṛttibhede sattāsiddho kutaḥ kāryatvasiddhiḥ / kāryatvaṃ hyabhūtvābhāvitvam / bhavanaṃ ca sattā / sattā ca saugatānāṃ sāmarthyameva / tataśca sāmarthyasandehe bhavatītyeva vaktumaśakyam / kathamabhūtvābhāvitvaṃ kāryatvaṃ setsyati / apekṣitaparavyāpāratvaṃ kāryatvamityapi nāsato dharmaḥ / sattvaṃ ca sāmarthyam / tacca sandigdhamiti kutaḥ kāryatvasiddhiḥ / tadasiddhau pūrvasya sāmarthyaṃ na sidhyatīti sandigdhāsiddho hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: Objection: Since effecthood and existence have different exclusions (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), even if existence is not established, what harm is there if effecthood is established? Reply: That is incoherent. Even granting a difference in the exclusions of effecthood and existence, how is effecthood established without the establishment of existence? For effecthood is the state of coming-to-be after not having been. And coming-to-be is existence. And existence, for the Buddhists, is nothing but causal capacity. Therefore, when there is doubt about causal capacity, it is impossible even to say 'it exists.' How then will effecthood — the state of coming-to-be after not having been — be established? Nor is the definition of effecthood as 'being dependent on the operation of another' a property of what is non-existent. And existence is causal capacity. And that is in doubt. So how is effecthood established? And without its establishment, the capacity of the prior member is not established — hence the reason suffers from doubtful non-establishment.

body.text: tathā viruddho 'pyayam / tathā hi kṣaṇikatve sati na tāvadajātasyānanvayaniruddhasya vā kāryārambhakatvaṃ saṃbhavati / na ca niṣpannasya tāvān kṣaṇo 'sti yamupādāya kasmaicit kāryāya vyāpāryeti / ataḥ kṣaṇikapakṣa evārthakriyānupapatterviruddhatā / atha vā vikalpena yadupanīyate tat sarvamavastu / tataśca yastvātmake kṣaṇikatve sādhye 'vastūpasthāpayannanumānavikalpo viruddhaḥ / yadvā sarvasyaiva hetoḥ kṣaṇikatve sādhye viruddhatvaṃ deśakālāntarānanugame sādhyasādhanabhāvābhāvāt / anugame ca nānākālamekamakṣaṇikaṃ kṣaṇikatvena virudhyata iti //
body.translated_text: Likewise, this reason is also contradictory. For, given momentariness, neither what has not yet arisen, nor what has already ceased without a subsequent connection, can have the capacity to initiate an effect. Nor does what has already come into being have a moment long enough during which it could be employed for some effect. Therefore, since causal efficacy is impossible on the thesis of momentariness itself, the reason is contradictory. Alternatively, whatever is presented by a conceptual judgment is entirely unreal. Therefore, the inferential conceptual judgment, which presents an unreal entity while what is to be proved is momentariness — which is the nature of a real entity — is contradictory. Or again, every reason whatsoever is contradictory when momentariness is what is to be proved, because the relation of proving-property and property-to-be-proved is absent when there is no persistence through different places and times. And if there is persistence, then a single thing existing at different times, being non-momentary, contradicts momentariness.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 72#)
anaikāntiko 'pyayam, sattvasthairyayorvirodhābhāvāditi /
body.translated_text: This reason is also inconclusive, since there is no contradiction between existence and permanence.

body.text: atrocyate / yattāvaduktaṃ sāmarthyaṃ na pratīyata iti, tat kiṃ sarvathaiva na pratīyate, kṣaṇabhaṅgapakṣe vā /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: As for the first objection that capacity is not cognized — does it mean that it is not cognized at all, or that it is not cognized on the thesis of momentariness?

body.text: prathamapakṣe sakalakārakajñāpakahetucakrocchedānmukhaspandanamātrasyāpyakaraṇaprasaṅgaḥ / anyathā yenaiva vacanena sāmarthyaṃ nāstīti pratipādyate tasyaiva tatpratipādanasāmarthyamavyāhatamāyātam / tasmāt paramapuruṣārthasamīhayā vastutattvanirūpaṇapravṛttasya śaktisvīkārapūrvikaiva pravṛttiḥ / tadasvīkāre tu na kaścit kvacit pravarteteti nirīhaṃ jagajjāyeta /
body.translated_text: On the first alternative, the destruction of the entire wheel of indicating reasons and all causal agents would lead to the absurd consequence that not even the movement of the lips could be accomplished. Otherwise, the very statement by which it is maintained that 'capacity does not exist' would itself arrive with its capacity to convey that meaning unimpaired. Therefore, for one who, motivated by the aspiration for the highest human goal, engages in determining the true nature of things, the engagement is necessarily preceded by the acceptance of capacity. But if that acceptance is refused, no one would engage in anything, and the world would become inert.

body.text: atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ / tadāsti tāvat sāmarthyapratītiḥ / sā ca kṣaṇikatve yadi nopapadyate tadā viruddhaṃ vaktumucitam / asiddhamiti tu nyāyabhūṣaṇīyaḥ pāpo vilāpaḥ / na ca satyapi kṣaṇikatve sāmarthyapratītivyāghātaḥ / tathā hi kāraṇagrāhijñānopādeyabhūtena kāryagrāhiṇā jñānena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa asya bhāve asya bhāva ityanvayaniścayo janyate / tathā kāraṇāpekṣayā bhūtalakaivalyagrāhijñānopādeyabhūtena kāryāpekṣayā bhūtalakaivalyagrāhiṇā jñānena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa asyābhāve asyābhāva iti vyatirekaniścayo janyate / yadāhurguravaḥ -
body.translated_text: Now for the second alternative: in that case, the cognition of capacity does exist. And if it cannot be justified under momentariness, then it would be proper to declare the reason contradictory. But to call it unestablished is a wretched lamentation befitting one who merely adorns the <s>Nyāya</s> system. And even given momentariness, there is no conflict with the cognition of capacity. For the cognition of positive concomitance — 'when this exists, that exists' — is generated by means of a cognition that grasps the effect, which is the subservient member of a cognition that grasps the cause, imbued with the impressions deposited by it. Likewise, the cognition of negative concomitance — 'when this is absent, that is absent' — is generated by means of a cognition, with respect to the cause, that grasps the ground-surface alone, which is the subservient member of a cognition, with respect to the effect, that grasps the ground-surface alone, imbued with the impressions deposited by it. As the masters say:

children.translated_text: "A second cognition, born immediately after a single determination, furnishes the reflective judgment of positive concomitance.

Likewise, another cognition, born from the experience of the absence of that single [cause], produces the reflective judgment of negative concomitance — thus the understanding of negative concomitance."

body.text: evaṃ sati gṛhītānusandhāyaka evāyaṃ vikalpaḥ, upādānopādeyabhūtakramipratyakṣadvayagṛhītānusandhānāt / yadāhālaṅkāraḥ-
body.translated_text: This being so, this conceptual judgment is indeed one that connects what has already been grasped, since it connects what has been grasped by the pair of sequential perceptions that stand in the relation of subservient and dominant. As the <s>Alaṅkāra</s> (the author of the <s>Pramāṇaviniścayālaṅkāra</s>) says:

children.translated_text: "Even though a single perception does not apprehend the earlier and later,
when there exist two perceptions, how is the awareness of the earlier and the later [impossible]?"

body.text: nāpi dvitīyo 'siddhaprabhedaḥ / sāmarthyaṃ hi sattvamiti saugatānāṃ sthitireṣā / na caitatprasādhanārthamasmākamidānīmeva prārambhaḥ / kiṃ tu yatra pramāṇapratītebījādau vastubhūte dharmiṇi pramāṇapratītaṃ sāmarthyaṃ tatra kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhanāya / tataścāṅkurādīnāṃ kāryādarśanādāhatya sāmarthyasandehe 'pi paṭupratyakṣaprasiddhamasatparāvṛttaṃ sanmātratvamavāryameva / anyathāṅkurādau sattāmātrānabhyupagame pratidarśanaṃ lakṣaṇabhedapraṇayanāyogāt / sarvatra sadvyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgācca / tasmācchāstrīyasattvalakṣaṇasandehe (#Nibandh 73#) 'pi paṭupratyakṣabalāvalambitavastubhāve 'ṅkurādau kāryatvamupalabhyamānaṃ bījādeḥ sāmarthyamupasthāpayatīti nāsiddhidoṣāvakāśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Nor does the second sub-type of non-establishment apply. For the settled position of the Buddhists is that capacity is existence (<s>sattva</s>). And our present endeavor is not for the purpose of establishing that. Rather, with respect to the subject — the seed and the like, which is a real entity cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s> — the capacity cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s> is used for establishing momentariness. Therefore, even when there is doubt about capacity due to the non-observation of the effects such as sprouts and the like, the mere existence-as-distinct-from-the-non-existent, which is well-established through sharp perception, cannot be denied. Otherwise, if mere existence of sprouts and the like were not accepted, there would be no possibility of formulating different definitions for each observation, and the absurd consequence would be the absence of all positive usage. Therefore, even when there is doubt about the technical definition of existence in the treatises, effecthood — being observed in [entities like] sprouts and the like whose real-entity status rests on the strength of sharp perception — presents the capacity of the seed and the like. Hence there is no room for the fault of non-establishment.

body.text: nāpi kṣaṇikatve sāmarthyakṣatiḥ, yato viruddhatā syāt / kṣaṇikatvaniyataprāgbhāvitvalakṣaṇakāraṇatvayorvirodhābhāvāt kṣaṇamātrasthāyino 'pi sāmarthyasaṃbhavāditi nādimo virodhaḥ / nāpi dvitīyo virodhaprabhedaḥ / avastuno vastuno vā svākārasya grāhyatvepi adhyavaseyavastvapekṣayaiva sarvatra prāmāṇyapratipādanād vastusvabhāvasyaiva kṣaṇikatvasya siddhiriti kva virodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is there any impairment of capacity given momentariness, such that the reason would be contradictory. Because there is no contradiction between momentariness-determined prior-existence — which characterizes causality — and [the cause's capacity], since even something lasting only a moment can have capacity — hence the first type of contradiction does not apply. Nor does the second type of contradiction apply. For even though the conceptual judgment grasps either an unreal or a real own-form, validity is everywhere established with reference to the real entity that is the object of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), and thus it is momentariness — which is the nature of a real entity — that is established. So where is the contradiction?

body.text: yacca gṛhyate yaccādhyavasīyate te dve apyanyanivṛttī na vastunī, svalakṣaṇāvagāhitve 'bhilāpasaṃsargānupapatteriti cet / na / adhyavasāyasvarūpāparijñānāt / agṛhīte 'pi vastuni mānasyādipravṛttikārakatvaṃ vikalpasyādhyavasāyitvam / apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtatvamadhyavaseyatvam / etaccādhyavaseyatvaṃ svalakṣaṇasyaiva yujyate, nānyasya / arthakriyārthitvādarthipravṛtteḥ / evaṃ cādhyavasāye svalakṣaṇasyāsphuraṇameva / na ca tasyāsphuraṇai 'pi sarvatrāviśeṣeṇa pravṛttyākṣepaprasaṅgaḥ, pratiniyatasāmagrīprasūtāt, pratiniyatasvākārāt, pratiniyataśaktiyogāt, pratiniyataevātadrūpaparāvṛtte 'pratīte 'pi pravṛttisāmarthyadarśanāt, yathā sarvasyāsattve 'pi bījādaṅkurasyaivotpattiḥ, dṛṣṭasya niyatahetuphalabhāvasya pratikṣeptumaśakyatvāt / paraṃ bāhyenārthena sati pratibandhe prāmāṇyam / anyathā tvaprāmāṇyamiti viśeṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Objection: Both what is grasped and what is determined are exclusions-from-other (<s>anyāpoha</s>), not real entities, since if they apprehended unique particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), the connection with verbal expression would be impossible. Reply: No. Because of the failure to understand the true nature of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). Determination by a conceptual judgment means its capacity to cause engagement toward action even with respect to an ungrasped real entity. Being the object of determination means being made the object of engagement even without appearing directly. And this status of being the object of determination belongs only to the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), not to anything else, since the engagement of the agent is motivated by the desire for causal efficacy. Thus, in determination, the unique particular indeed does not appear directly. Yet there is no absurd consequence of indiscriminate engagement everywhere despite its non-appearance, because the conceptual judgment arises from a determinate aggregate of conditions, has a determinate own-form, possesses a determinate capacity-connection, and because, even without the cognition of the determinate exclusion-from-what-is-not-of-that-nature, the capacity for engagement is observed — just as, even though all [seeds] are non-existent [at the time of the sprout's arising], a sprout arises from the seed alone, since the observed determinate cause-effect relation cannot be denied. The difference is this: when there is a connection with an external object, there is validity; otherwise, there is invalidity.

body.text: tathā tṛtīyo 'pi pakṣaḥ prayāsaphalaḥ / nānākālasyaikasya vastuno vastuto 'saṃbhave 'pi sarvadeśakālavartinoratadrūpaparāvṛttayoreva sādhyasādhanayoḥ pratyakṣeṇa vyāptigrahaṇāt / dvividho hi pratyakṣasya viṣayaḥ grāhyo 'dhyavaseyaśca / sakalātadrūpaparāvṛttaṃ vastumātraṃ sākṣādasphuraṇāt pratyakṣasya grāhyo viṣayo mā bhūt, tadekadeśagrahaṇe tu tanmātrayorvyāptiniścāyakavikalpajananādadhyavaseyo viṣayo bhavatyeva / kṣaṇagrahaṇe santānaniścayavat / rūpamātragrahaṇe rūparasagandhasparśātmakaghaṭaniścayavacca / anyathā sarvānumānocchedaprasaṅgāt //
body.translated_text: Likewise, the third thesis too bears fruit. Even though the real existence of a single entity across different times is impossible, the pervasion is grasped by perception with respect to the provable and the prover that are excluded from what is not of that nature and that exist in all places and times. For the object of perception is of two kinds: the directly apprehended and the determinately cognised. The entirety of what is excluded from everything not of that nature may not be a directly apprehended object of perception, since it does not appear directly. But when a part of it is apprehended, then, since it generates a determinate cognition that ascertains the pervasion of merely those two [properties], it is indeed a determinately cognised object — like the ascertainment of a continuum upon the apprehension of a single moment, and like the ascertainment of the pot consisting of form, taste, smell, and touch upon the apprehension of mere form. Otherwise, the absurd consequence of the destruction of all inference would follow.

body.text: tathā hi vyāptigrahaḥ sāmānyayoḥ, viśeṣayoḥ, sāmānyaviśiṣṭasvalakṣaṇayoḥ svalakṣaṇa viśiṣṭasāmānyayorveti vikalpāḥ /
body.translated_text: For the alternatives regarding the apprehension of pervasion are as follows: [it may be] between two universals, between two particulars, between a particular qualified by a universal, or between a universal qualified by a particular.

body.text: nādyo vikalpaḥ, sāmānyasya bādhyatvāt / abādhyatve 'pyadṛśyatvāt / dṛśyatve 'pi puruṣārthānupayogitayā tasyānumeyatvāyogāt / nāpyanumitāt sāmānyād viśeṣānumānam / sāmānyasarvasvalakṣaṇayorvakṣyamāṇanyāyena pratibandhapratipatterayogāt /
body.translated_text: The first alternative does not hold, because the universal is subject to refutation. Even if it is not refuted, because it is invisible. Even if visible, because, being useless for human purposes, it is not fit to be inferred. Nor can the particular be inferred from an inferred universal, because the apprehension of the invariable connection between the universal and all the particulars is impossible, by the reasoning to be stated.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 74#)
nāpi dvitīyaḥ, viśeṣasyānanugāmitvāt /
body.translated_text: (Nibandh 74) Nor does the second alternative hold, because the particular is non-recurrent.

body.text: antime tu vikalpadvaye sāmānyādhāratayā dṛṣṭa eva viśeṣaḥ sāmānyasya viśeṣyo viśeṣaṇaṃ vā karttavyaḥ / adṛṣṭa eva vā deśakālāntaravartī / yadvā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭātmako deśakālāntarvarttyatadrūpaparāvṛttaḥ sarvo viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: But in the last two alternatives, the particular, being seen as the substratum of the universal, must be made either the qualificand or the qualifier of the universal. Or it is precisely unseen, being situated in another place and time. Or else, the particular — comprising both seen and unseen, being excluded from what is not of that nature, and situated across all places and times — is all the particulars.

body.text: na prathamaḥ pakṣo 'nanugāmitvāt / nāpi dvitīyaḥ, adṛṣṭatvāt / na ca tṛtīyaḥ, prastutaikaviśeṣadarśane 'pi deśakālāntaravartināṃ viśeṣāṇāmadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: The first option does not hold, because of non-recurrence. Nor the second, because of being unseen. Nor the third, because even upon seeing one particular under discussion, the particulars existing at other places and times are not seen.

body.text: atha teṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva viśeṣāṇāṃ sadṛśatvāt, sadṛśasāmagrīprasūtatvāt, sadṛśakāryakāritvāditi pratyāsattyā ekaviśeṣagrāhakaṃ pratyakṣamatadrūpaparāvṛttamātre niścayaṃ janayadatadrūpaparāvṛttaviśeṣamātrasya vyavasthāpakam / yathaikasāmagrīpratibaddharūpamātragrāhakaṃ pratyakṣaṃṃ ghaṭe niścayaṃ janayad ghaṭagrāhakaṃ vyavasthāpyate / anyathā ghaṭo 'pi ghaṭasantāno 'pi pratyakṣato na sidhyate, sarvātmanā grahaṇābhāvāt / tadekadeśagrahaṇaṃ tvatadrūpaparāvṛtte 'pyaviśiṣṭam / yadyevamanenaiva krameṇa sarvasya viśeṣasya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvavat vyāptipratipattirapyastu / tat kimarthaṃ nānākālamekamakṣaṇikamabhyupagantavyaṃ yena kṣaṇikatva sādhanasya viruddhatvaṃ syāditi na kaścidvirodha prabhedaprasaṅgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Objection: Since all those particulars are similar, since they are produced from similar aggregates of conditions, and since they produce similar effects — therefore, by virtue of this proximity, the perception that grasps one particular, generating a determinate cognition regarding what is merely excluded from what is not of that nature, is established as determining merely the particular that is excluded from what is not of that nature. Just as the perception that grasps mere form, which is connected with a single aggregate of conditions, when generating a determinate cognition regarding a pot, is established as grasping the pot. Otherwise, neither the pot nor the continuum of the pot would be established through perception, since it is not apprehended in its entirety. But the apprehension of a part of it is no different even in the case of what is excluded from what is not of that nature. If that is so, then by this very procedure, just as the relation of qualifier and qualificand is apprehended for every particular, so too let the apprehension of pervasion be [achieved]. What need is there then to postulate a single non-momentary entity existing across different times, such that the proof of momentariness would involve the fallacy of contradiction? Thus, no division of contradiction arises.

body.text: na cāyamanaikāntiko 'pi hetuḥ, pūrvoktakrameṇa sādharmyadṛṣṭānte prasaṅgaviparyayahetubhyāmanvayarūpavyāpteḥ prasādhanāt / nanu yadi prasaṅgaviparyayahetudvayabalato ghaṭedṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ sidhyet tadā sattvasya niyamena kṣaṇikatvena vyāptisiddheranaikāntikatvaṃ nasyāditi yuktam / kevalamidamevāsambhavi / tathā hi śakto 'pi ghaṭaḥ kramikasahakāryapekṣayā kramikāryaṃ kariṣyati /
body.translated_text: Nor is this reason inconclusive, because the pervasion in the form of positive concomitance is established through the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio ad absurdum) and <s>viparyaya</s> (contraposition) arguments in the concordant example, by the method previously stated. Objection: If, by the force of the two arguments — <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>viparyaya</s> — momentary destruction were established in the example of a pot, then, since the pervasion of existence necessarily with momentariness would be established, inconclusiveness would indeed be destroyed — this is proper. However, this very thing is impossible. For a pot, even though capable, will produce a successive effect in dependence on a successive co-operative condition.

body.text: na caitad vaktavyam / samartho 'rthaḥ svarūpeṇa karoti / svarūpaṃ ca sarvadāstītyanupakāriṇī sahakāriṇyapekṣā na yujyata iti / satyapi svarūpeṇa kārakatve sāmarthyābhāvāt kathaṃ karotu / sahakārisākalyaṃ hi sāmarthyam / tadvaikalyaṃ cāsāmarthyam / na ca tayorāvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyāṃ tadvataḥ kācit kṣatiḥ, tasya tābhyāmanyatvāt / tasmādarthaḥ samartho 'pi syāt, na ca karotīti sandigdhavyatirekaḥ prasaṅgahetuḥ //
body.translated_text: And this should not be said: 'A capable entity produces by its own nature; and its own nature exists at all times; therefore the expectation of a non-contributing co-operative condition is improper.' For even though causality by its own nature exists, how can it produce [an effect] in the absence of capacity? For capacity is the totality of co-operative conditions, and the absence of any of them is incapacity. And by the appearance and disappearance of those [conditions], the possessor of them suffers no change, since it is different from them. Therefore, an entity may be capable and yet not produce — hence the reductio argument has doubtful negative concomitance.

body.text: atrocyate / bhavatu tāvat sahakārisākalyameva sāmarthyam / tathāpi so 'pi tāvad bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa kārakaḥ / tasya ca yādṛśaścaramakṣaṇe 'kṣepakriyādharmā svabhāvastādṛśa eva cet prathamakṣaṇe tadā tadāpi prasahya kurvāṇo brahmaṇāpyanivāryaḥ / na ca so 'pyakṣepakriyādharmā svabhāvaḥ sākalye sati jāto bhāvād bhinna evābhidhātuṃ (#Nibandh 75#) śakyaḥ, bhāvasyākartṛtvaprasaṅgāt / evaṃ yāvad dharmāntaraparikalpastāvattāvadudāsīno bhāvaḥ / tasmād yadrūpamādāya svarūpeṇāpi janayatītyucyate tasya prāgapi bhāve kathamajaniḥ kadācit / akṣepakriyāpratyanīkasvabhāvasya vā prācyasya paścādanuvṛttau kathaṃ kadācidapi kāryasaṃbhavaḥ //
body.translated_text: To this we reply: Let it be that the totality of co-operative conditions is indeed the capacity. Even so, that entity is still a cause by its own nature. And if its nature at the final moment — characterised by the property of projecting the effect — is exactly the same at the first moment, then even at that time it would produce forcefully, unstoppable even by <s>Brahman</s>. And that nature characterised by the property of projecting the effect, which arises when the totality [of conditions] is present, cannot be said to be other than the entity itself, because there would be the absurd consequence that the entity is not a cause. (Nibandh 75) Thus, as long as one postulates additional properties, the entity remains that much indifferent. Therefore, whatever nature it is by virtue of which it is said to produce even by its own nature — how could there be non-production at some time, given that nature existed before as well? Or if its prior nature, which is opposed to the property of projecting the effect, continues later, how could there ever be production of the effect?

body.text: nanu yadi sa evaikaḥ kartā syād yuktametat / kiṃ tu sāmagrī janikā / tataḥ sahakāryantaravirahavelāyāṃ balīyaso 'pi na kāryaprasava iti kimatra viruddham / na hi bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa karotīti svarūpeṇaiva karoti, sahakārisahitādeva tataḥ kāryotpattidarśanāt / tasmād vyāptivat kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pyekatrānyayogavyavacchedenānyatrāyogavyacchedenāvaboddhavyaḥ, tathaiva laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ saṃpratipatteriti //
body.translated_text: Objection: If that single entity alone were the cause, this argument would be valid. But the aggregate of conditions is the cause. Therefore, in the absence of another co-operative condition, even something very powerful does not give rise to the effect — what is contradictory in this? For it is not the case that when we say 'the entity produces by its own nature' it means it produces by its own nature alone, since we observe that the effect arises only from the entity together with its co-operative conditions. Therefore, like pervasion, the causal relation too should be understood through the determination of exclusive co-occurrence in one case and exclusive non-co-occurrence in the other — for this is precisely the understanding of worldly investigators.

body.text: atrocyate / yadā militāḥ santaḥ kāryaṃ kurvate tadaikārthakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvameṣāmastu, ko niṣeddhā / militaireva tu tat kāryaṃ karttavyamiti kuto labhyate / pūrvāparayoarekasvabhāvatvād bhāvasya sarvadā jananājananayoranyataraniyamaprasaṅgasya durvāratvāt / tasmāt sāmagrī janikā, naikaṃ janakamiti sthiravādināṃ manorathasyāpyaviṣayaḥ /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: When, having come together, they produce an effect — let this co-operative condition-hood, characterised by jointly producing one thing, belong to them; who would deny it? But from where is it obtained that the effect must be produced only by them together? Because the entity has the same nature at the earlier and later times, the inevitable consequence — that it must be invariably determined as either always producing or never producing — is irresistible. Therefore, that the aggregate produces and not a single entity — this is not even within the range of the eternal-theorists' wishful thinking.

body.text: dṛśyate tāvadidamiti cet / dṛśyatām / kiṃ tu pūrvasthitādeva sāmagrīmadhyapraviṣṭād bhāvāt kāryotpattiranyasmādeva vā viśiṣṭād bhāvādutpannāditi vivādapadam / tatra prāgapi saṃbhave sarvadaiva kāryotpattirna vā kadācidapīti virodhamasamādhāya cakṣuṣī nimīlya tata eva kāryotpattidarśanāditi sādhyānuvādamātrapravṛttaḥ kṛpāmarhatīti /
body.translated_text: If [objected]: 'But this is what is observed!' — let it be observed. However, the point of dispute is precisely this: does the effect arise from the very same entity that existed before and has entered the aggregate of conditions, or from an altogether different and distinctive entity that has arisen? There, if it is possible even before [the aggregate], then either the effect always arises or never arises at all — without resolving this contradiction, merely closing one's eyes and saying 'We see the effect arising from that very thing' amounts to nothing more than restating the thesis, and deserves compassion.

body.text: na ca pratyabhijñādibalādekatvasiddhiḥ / tat pauruṣasya lūnapunarjātakeśanakhādāvapyupalambhato nirdalanāt / lakṣaṇabhedasya ca darśayitumaśakyatvāt / sthirasiddhadūṣaṇe cāsmābhiḥ prapañcato nirastatvāt / tasmāt sākṣāt kāryakāraṇabhāvāpekṣayobhayatrāpyanyayogavyavacchedaḥ / vyāptau tu sākṣāt paramparayā kāraṇamātrāpekṣayā kāraṇe vyāpake 'yogavyavacchedaḥ / kārye vyāpye 'nyayogavyavacchedaḥ / tathā tadatatsvabhāve vyāpake 'yogavyavacchedaḥ / tatsvabhāve ca vyāpye 'nyayogavyavacchedaḥ / vikalpārūḍharūpāpekṣayā vyāptau dvividhamavadhāraṇam /
body.translated_text: Nor is the identity [of the entity at different times] established by the force of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) and the like. For that [recognition] is of personal [judgment] and is refuted by its being observed even in the case of hair, nails, and the like that have been cut and grown again. And because the distinguishing marks of difference cannot be shown [to be absent]. And because in the refutation of the permanent, this has been rejected by us in detail. Therefore, with respect to the causal relation directly, there is the determination of exclusive co-occurrence and exclusive non-co-occurrence in both [cases]. But with respect to pervasion — directly or indirectly, relative to a mere cause — in the pervading cause there is the determination of exclusive non-co-occurrence; in the pervaded effect there is the determination of exclusive co-occurrence. Likewise, in the pervading 'non-being-of-that-nature' there is the determination of exclusive non-co-occurrence; and in the pervaded 'being-of-that-nature' there is the determination of exclusive co-occurrence. With respect to the form mounted upon conceptual cognition, there is a twofold determination in pervasion.

body.text: nanu yadi pūrvāparakālayorekasvabhāvo bhāvaḥ sarvadā janakatvenājanakatvena vā vyāpta upalabdhaḥ syāt, tadāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ saṃgacchate / na ca kṣaṇabhaṅgavādinā pūrvāparakālayorekaḥ (#Nibandh 76#) kaścidupalabdha iti cet / tadetadatigrāmyam / tathā hi pūrvāparakālayorekasvabhāvatve satītyasyāyamarthaḥ / parakālabhāvī janako yaḥ svabhāvo bhāvasya sa eva yadi pūrvakālabhāvī, pūrvakālabhāvī vā yo 'janakaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa eva yadi parakālabhāvī tadopalabdhameva jananamajananaṃ vā syāt / tathā ca sati siddhayoreva svabhāvayorekatvārope siddhameva jananamajananaṃ vāsajyata iti /
body.translated_text: Objection: If the entity, having the same nature at the earlier and later times, were observed as invariably pervaded by either always being a cause or never being a cause, then this consequence would follow. But a proponent of momentary destruction has not observed any single [entity] at the earlier and later times. Reply: This is extremely crude. For the meaning of 'if the entity has the same nature at the earlier and later times' is this: if the nature of the entity that produces at the later time is the very same as that which exists at the earlier time, or if the non-producing nature at the earlier time is the very same at the later time, then the observed production or non-production would simply be [invariably determined]. And when identity is superimposed upon two natures that are [already] established, the already-established production or non-production is simply entailed.

body.text: nanu kāryameva sahakāriṇamamekṣate, na tu kāryotpattihetuḥ / yasmād dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijamāgantukaṃ na sahakāryantaram, tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavat sahakārinānātvādapi kramavat kāryanānātvopapatteraśakyaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratikṣaṇamanyānyatvamupapādayitumiti cet / ucyate / bhavatu tāvannijāgantukabhedena dvividhaṃ sāmarthyam / tathāpi yat prātisvikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇamarthakriyādharmakamavaśya mabhyupagantavyam, tat kiṃ prāgapi paścādeva veti vikalpya yaddūṣaṇamudīritaṃ tatra kimuktamaneneti na pratīmaḥ / yattu kāryeṇaiva sahakāriṇo 'pekṣyanta ityupaskṛtaṃ tadapi nirupayogam / yadi hi kāryameva svajanmani svatantraṃ syād yuktametat / kevalamevaṃ sati sahakārisākalyasāmarthyakalpanamaphalam / svatantrādeva hi kāryaṃ kādācitkaṃ bhaviṣyati / tathā ca sati santo hetavaḥ sarvathāsamarthāḥ / asadetat kāryaṃ svatantramiti viśuddhā buddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: It is the effect that requires the co-operative condition, not the cause of the effect's production. For capacity is of two kinds — intrinsic and extrinsic — and is not an additional co-operative condition. Therefore, since even for a non-momentary [entity], diversity of effects is accounted for by the diversity of co-operative conditions, just as it is accounted for by sequential [production], it is impossible to demonstrate that entities are different at every moment. Reply: Let capacity be of two kinds — intrinsic and extrinsic. Even so, that particular real entity (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), with the property of causal efficacy, which must necessarily be accepted — we do not understand what has been said in response to the objection raised by analysing whether it exists before or only later. And as for the claim that the co-operative conditions are required by the effect itself — that too is useless. For if the effect were self-determining in its own production, this claim would be valid. But in that case, the postulation that capacity consists of the totality of co-operative conditions would be fruitless. For the effect, being occasional, would arise from the self-determining [entity] itself. And in that case, the causes, existing [at all times], would be entirely incapable. The pure understanding is: 'This effect is not self-determining.'

body.text: atha kāryasyaivāyamaparādho yadidaṃ samarthe kāraṇe satyapi kadācinnopapadyata iti cet / na tattarhi tatkāryaṃ svātantryāt / yadbhāṣyam
body.translated_text: Objection: If it is the effect's own fault that it sometimes fails to arise even when the cause is fully capable — then that is not its effect. As stated in the verse:

children.translated_text: If, even when the cause is the same in all conditions, there is no effect,

children.text: svatantraṃ kāryamevaṃ syānna tatkāryaṃ tathā sati //
children.translated_text: then the effect would be self-determining — and in that case, it would not be its effect.

body.text: atha na tadbhāve bhavatīti tatkāryamucyate / kiṃtu tadabhāve na bhavatyeveti, vyatirekaprādhānyāditi cet / na / yadi hi svayaṃ bhavan bhāvayedeva hetuḥ svakāryam, tadā tadabhāvaprayukto 'syābhāva iti pratītiḥ syāt / no ced yathā kāraṇe satyapi kārya svātantryānna bhavati, tathā tadabhāve 'pi svātantryādeva na bhūtamiti śaṅkā kena nivāryeta / yad bhāṣyam
body.translated_text: Objection: [The relation is called 'its effect'] not because it arises in its presence, but because it does not arise in its absence — thus the negative concomitance is primary. Reply: No. For if the cause, being present, were to invariably bring about its own effect, then the cognition 'its absence is caused by the absence of that [cause]' would arise. But if it is the case that even when the cause is present, the effect does not arise due to its self-determination, then the suspicion that even in the absence of [the cause], it simply did not arise due to its own self-determination — by what can this be averted? As stated in the verse:

body.text:
tadbhāve 'pi na bhāvaścedabhāve 'bhāvitā kutaḥ /
tadabhāvaprayukto 'sya so 'bhāva iti tat kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: If there is no arising even in the presence of that [cause], how [can we assert] non-existence in [its] absence? How then [can we say] 'its absence is caused by the absence of that'?

body.text: tasmād yathaiva tadabhāve niyamena na bhavati tathaiva tadbhāve niyamena bhavedeva / abhavacca na tatkāraṇatāmātmanaḥ kṣamate /
body.translated_text: Therefore, just as in its absence the [effect] invariably does not arise, so too in its presence it must invariably arise. And the fact that it did not [invariably arise] cannot accommodate [the claim of] its being the cause.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 77#)
yaccoktaṃ prathamakāryotpādanakāle hi uttarakāryotpādanasvabhāvaḥ, ataḥ prathamakāla evāśeṣāṇi kāryāṇi kuryāditi / tadidaṃ mātā me bandhyetyādivat svavacanavirodhādayuktam / yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ sa kathamādau kāryaṃ kuryāt / na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ / na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikamapi karotīti /
body.translated_text: (Nibandh 77) As for what was said — 'At the time of producing the first effect, it has the nature of producing the later effect; therefore it would produce all effects at the very first moment' — this, like saying 'My mother is barren,' is improper due to self-contradiction. For how can that which has the nature of producing the later effect produce an effect at the outset? It does not then have the nature of producing that [first] effect. For that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and so forth.

body.text: atrocyate / sthirasvabhāvatve hi bhāvasyottarakālamevedaṃ kāryaṃ na pūrvakālamiti kuta etat / tadabhāvācca kāraṇamapyutarakāryakaraṇasvabhāvamityapi kutaḥ / kiṃ kurmaḥ / uttarakālameva tasya janmeti cet / astu sthiratve tadanupapadyamānamasthiratāmādiśatu /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: If the entity has a permanent nature, then from where comes this — that this effect belongs to the later time and not to the earlier? And since that [temporal restriction] is absent, from where also comes the claim that the cause has the nature of producing only the later effect? 'What can we do? It is simply born at the later time.' If [so said]: Let that very non-accounting, which does not hold in the case of permanence, point toward impermanence.

body.text: sthiratve 'pyeṣa eva svabhāvastasya yaduttarakṣaṇa eva karotīti cet / hatedānīṃ pramāṇapratyāśā / dhūmādatrāgnirityatrāpi svabhāva evāsya yadidānīmatra niragnirapi dhūma iti vaktuṃ śakyatvāt / tasmāt pramāṇaprasiddhe svabhāvālambanam / na tu svabhāvāvalambanena pramāṇavyālopaḥ / tasmād yadi kāraṇasyottarakāryakārakatvamabhyupagamya kāryasya prathamakṣaṇabhāvitvamāsajyate, syāt svavacanavirodhaḥ / yadā tu kāraṇasya sthiratve kāryasyottarakālatvamevāsaṅgatamataḥ kāraṇasyāpyuttarakāryajanakatvaṃ vastuto 'sambhavi tadā prasaṅgasādhanamidam / jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ hi jananena vyāptamiti prasādhitam / uttarakāryajananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ ca tvadabhyupagamāt prathamakāryakaraṇakāla eva ghaṭe dharmiṇi siddham / atastanmātrānubandhina uttarābhimatasta karyasya prathame kṣaṇe 'saṃbhavā deva prasaṅgaḥ kriyate / na hi nīlakārake 'pi pītakārakatvārope pītasaṃbhavaprasaṅgaḥ svavacanavirodho nāma / tadevaṃ śaktaḥ sahakāryanapekṣitatvād jananena vyāptaḥ / ajanaryaśca śaktāśaktatvaviruddhadharmādhyāsād bhinna eva //
body.translated_text: Objection: Even granting permanence, this alone is its nature—that it acts only at the subsequent moment. Reply: Then abandon the hope for a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge)! For even in the [inference] 'There is fire here, because of smoke,' one could say: 'This is just its nature—that even now, here where there is no fire, there is smoke,' since [on your view] such an assertion would be possible. Therefore, [valid inference] depends on the established nature [of things as known by] <s>pramāṇa</s>; but one should not overturn <s>pramāṇa</s> by relying on [arbitrary claims about] natures. Therefore, if one accepts that the cause produces the subsequent effect and then imposes upon the effect the property of existing at the first moment, there would be self-contradiction. But when—given the permanence of the cause—the posteriority of the effect is itself incoherent, and hence the cause's producing of a subsequent effect is in reality impossible—then this is a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio ad absurdum) argument. For it has been established that being the object of the conventional usage 'generating' is pervaded by [actual] generation. And 'being the object of the conventional usage of generating a subsequent effect' is established in the <s>dharmin</s> (subject), namely the pot, at the very time of producing the first effect—due to your own concession. Therefore, since the so-called subsequent effect is bound exclusively to that [first-moment generating capacity], a reductio is drawn regarding the impossibility of its [arising at] a later moment. For when one who produces blue is also [falsely] attributed with producing yellow, the reductio that yellow should arise is not a 'self-contradiction.' Thus, one that is capable (<s>śakta</s>)—because it does not require an auxiliary—is pervaded by [actual] generating. And the non-generator—because of the superimposition of the contradictory properties of being capable and incapable—is necessarily different [from the generator].

body.text: nanu bhavatu prasaṅgaviparyayabalādekakāryaṃ prati śaktāśaktatvalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ / tathāpi na tato bhedaḥ sidhyati / tathā hi bījamaṅkurādikaṃkurvad yadi yenaiva svabhāvenāṅkurādikaṃ karoti tenaiva kṣityādikaṃ tadā kṣityādīnāmapyaṅkurasvābhāvyāpattiḥ / nānāsvabhāvatvena tu kārakatve svabhāvānāmanyonyābhāvāvyabhicāritvādekatra bhāvābhavau parasparaviruddhau syātāmityekamapi bījaṃ bhidyeta / evaṃ pradīpo 'pi tailakṣayavarttidāhādikam / tathā pūrvarūpamapyuttararūparasagandhādikamanaikaiḥ svabhāvaiḥ parikalitaṃ karoti / teṣāṃ ca svabhāvānāmanyo 'nyābhāvāvyabhicārādviruddhānāṃ yoge pradīpādikaṃ bhidyeta / na ca bhidyate /
body.translated_text: Objection: Let there be, by the force of the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its converse, a superimposition of contradictory properties—being capable and incapable—with respect to a single effect. Even so, difference does not follow from that. For consider: a seed, while producing a sprout and so forth—if it produces earth and the like by the very same nature by which it produces the sprout, then earth and the like would also have the nature of a sprout. But if it produces by multiple natures, then since those natures do not deviate from mutual absence, the presence and absence [of different natures] in one [entity]—being mutually contradictory—would split even a single seed. Likewise a lamp too [produces] the consumption of oil, burning of the wick, and so forth. Similarly, a prior form too produces a subsequent form, taste, smell, and so forth through multiple natures. And since those natures do not deviate from mutual absence—being contradictory—their conjunction would split the lamp and the like. But it is not split.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 78#)
tanna viruddhadharmādhyāso bhedakaḥ / tathā bījasyāṅkuraṃ prati kārakatvaṃ gardabhādikaṃ pratyakārakatvamiti kārakatvākārakatve api viruddho dharmau / na ca tadyoge 'pi bījabhedaḥ / tadevamekatra bīje pradīpe rūpe ca vipakṣe paridṛśyamānaḥ śaktāśaktatvādirviruddhadharmādhyāso na ghaṭāderbhedaka iti /
body.translated_text: [<s>Nibandh</s> 78] Therefore, the superimposition of contradictory properties does not establish difference. For the seed's capacity to produce a sprout and its incapacity with respect to a donkey and the like—these too are contradictory properties, namely capacity and incapacity. Yet there is no splitting of the seed from their conjunction. Thus, the superimposition of contradictory properties such as being capable and incapable—observed in the counter-examples of a single seed, lamp, and form—does not establish difference in the pot and so forth.

body.text: atra brūmaḥ / bhavatu tāvad bījādīnāmanekakāryakāritvāddharmabhūtānekasvabhāvabhedaḥ, tathāpi kaḥ prastāvo viruddhadharmādhyāsasya / svabhāvānāṃ hyanyonyābhāvāvyabhicāre bhedaḥ prāptāvasaro na virodhaḥ / virodhastu yadvidhāne yanniṣedho yanniṣedhe ca yadvidhānaṃ tayorekatra dharmiṇi parasparaparihārasthitatayā syāt / tadatraikaḥ svabhāvaḥ svābhāvena viruddho yukto bhāvābhāvavat / na tu svabhāvāntareṇa ghaṭatvavastutvavat / evamaṅkurādikāritvaṃ tadakāritvena viruddhaṃ na punarvastvantarakāritvena / pratyakṣavyāpāraścātra yathā nānādharmairadhyāsitaṃ bhāvamabhinnaṃ vyavasthāpayati tathā tatkāryakāriṇaṃ kāryāntarākāriṇaṃ ca / tad yadi pratiyogitvābhāvādanyonyābhāvāvyabhiocāriṇāvapi svabhāvāvaviruddhau tatkārakatvānyākārakatve vāviṣayabhedādaviruddhe tat kimāyātamekakāryaṃ prati śaktāśaktatvayoḥ parasparapratiyoginorviruddhayordharmayīḥ / etayorapi punaravirodhe virodho nāma dattajalāñjaliḥ //
body.translated_text: To this we reply: Let there be, for the seed and so forth, a multiplicity of natures qua dharmas, owing to [their] producing multiple effects. Even so, what occasion is there for the superimposition of contradictory properties? For when natures do not deviate from mutual absence, what obtains is difference, not contradiction. Contradiction, however, would occur when the negation of one entails the affirmation of the other, and vice versa—[that is,] when the two exist in a single <s>dharmin</s> (subject) by way of mutual exclusion. Here, one nature is opposed to its own [specific] absence—like existence and non-existence—but not to another nature—like pot-ness and thing-ness. Likewise, being the producer of a sprout is contradictory with not producing that [sprout]—but not with producing another thing. And the function of perception here is such that, just as it establishes as undifferentiated an entity to which diverse properties are attributed, so too [it establishes] a thing as both producing one effect and not producing another. Therefore, if—because of the absence of a counter-correlate—even natures that do not deviate from mutual absence are not contradictory, and [if likewise] capacity-to-produce-one-thing and incapacity-to-produce-another are not contradictory because of difference in domain—then what follows regarding the capability and incapability with respect to a single effect, which are indeed mutually counter-correlative and contradictory? If even these two were not contradictory, then contradiction itself would be bid farewell.

body.text: bhavatu tarhyekakāryāpekṣayaiva sāmarthyāsāmarthyayorvirodhaḥ / kevalaṃ yathā tadeva kāryaṃ prati kvaciddeśe śaktirdeśāntare cāśaktiriti deśabhedādaviruddhe śaktyaśaktī tathaikatraiva kāryakālabhedādapyaviruddhe / yathā pūrvaṃ niṣkriyaḥ sphaṭikaḥ sa eva paścāt sakriya iti cet / ucyate / na hi vayaṃ paribhāṣāmātrādekatra kārye deśabhedādaviruddhe śaktyaśaktī brūmaḥ, kiṃ tu virodhābhāvāt / taddeśakāryakāritvaṃ hi taddeśakāryākāritvena viruddham / na punardeśāntare tatkāryākāritvenānyakāryakāritvena vā //
body.translated_text: Objection: Let the contradiction between capability and incapability be only with reference to a single effect. But just as there is capability with respect to that very effect in one place and incapability in another place—and capability and incapability are non-contradictory because of spatial difference—so too [they should be] non-contradictory even in a single [entity] because of temporal difference; just as a crystal that was previously inactive becomes active thereafter. Reply: We do not say that capability and incapability regarding a single effect are non-contradictory in different places merely by stipulation; rather, [we say so] because there is no contradiction. For the capacity to produce an effect at that place is contradictory with not producing that effect at that place—but not with not producing that effect elsewhere, or with producing another effect.

body.text: yadyevaṃ tatkālakāryakāritvaṃ tatkālakāryākāritvena viruddham / na punaḥ kālāntare tatkāryākāritvenānyakāryakāritvena vā / tatkathaṃ kālabhede 'pi virodha iti cet / ucyate / dvayorhi dharmayorekatra dharmiṇyanavasthitiniyamaḥ parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇo virodhaḥ / sa ca sākṣātparasparapratyanīkatayā bhāvābhāvavad vā bhavet, ekasya vā niyamena pramāṇāntareṇa bādhanānnityatvasattvavad vā bhavediti na kaścidarthabhedaḥ / tadatraikadharmiṇi tatkālatat kāryakāritvādhāre kālāntare tatkāryākāritvasyānyakāryakāritvasya vā niyamena pramāṇāntareṇa bādhanādvirodhaḥ / tathā hio yatraiva dharmiṇi tatkālakāryakāritvamupalabdhaṃ na tatraiva kālāntare (#Nibandh 79#) tatkāryākāritvamanyakāryakāritvaṃ vā brahmaṇāpyupasaṃhartuṃ śakyate, yenānayoravirodhaḥ syāt / kṣaṇāntare kathitaprasaṅgaviparyayahetubhyāmavaśyaṃbhāvena dharmibhedaprasādhanāt //
body.translated_text: Objection: If so, the capacity to produce an effect at that time is contradictory with not producing that effect at that time—but not with not producing that effect at another time, or with producing another effect. So how is there contradiction even with temporal difference? Reply: Contradiction is the rule of non-co-existence of two properties in a single <s>dharmin</s> (subject), characterized by mutual exclusion. And this may be either directly through mutual opposition—like existence and non-existence—or through one being invariably refuted by another <s>pramāṇa</s>—like permanence and thing-ness. Now, here in a single <s>dharmin</s>, which is the locus of 'capacity to produce that effect at that time'—[the property of] 'not producing that effect at another time' or 'producing another effect [at another time]' is contradictory because it is invariably refuted by another <s>pramāṇa</s>. For in the very <s>dharmin</s> in which the capacity to produce that effect at that time is observed, [<s>Nibandh</s> 79] neither 'not producing that effect at another time' nor 'producing another effect [later]' can be brought together [with it] even by <s>Brahmā</s>—such that there would be non-contradiction between them—because the reductio and its converse, as explained for the subsequent moment, necessarily establish difference of the <s>dharmin</s>.

body.text: na ca pratyabhijñānādekatvasiddhiḥ, tatpauruṣasya nirmūlitatvāt / ata eva vajro 'pi pakṣakukṣau nikṣiptaḥ / kathamasau sphaṭiko barākaḥ kālabhedenābhedaprasādhanāya dṛṣṭāntībhavitumarhati / na caivaṃ samānakālakāryāṇāṃ deśabhede 'pi dharmibhedo yukto bhedaprasādhakapramāṇābhāvāt / indriyapratyakṣeṇa nirastavibhramāśaṅkenābhedaprasādhanācceti na kālabhede 'pi śaktyaśaktyorvirodhaḥ svasamayamātrādapahastayituṃ śakyaḥ, samayapramāṇayorapravṛtteriti //
body.translated_text: Nor is unity established by recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), since that [recognition] has been uprooted as [merely] conventional (<s>pauruṣa</s>). For this very reason, the <s>vajra</s> (diamond[-like argument]) has been placed in the belly of the thesis. How can that crystal—[the example of something being] a non-agent [at one time and an agent at another]—serve as an instance for establishing non-difference through temporal difference? Nor in this way is there difference of the <s>dharmin</s> even with spatial difference for effects [produced] at the same time—because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing difference; [rather, there is] establishment of non-difference by sensory perception that is free from suspicion of error. Therefore, the contradiction between capability and incapability even in temporal difference cannot be waved away by mere [assertion of one's own] doctrine, since doctrine and <s>pramāṇa</s> do not [both] operate [when they conflict].

children.translated_text: Therefore, in all cases, the establishment of the superimposition of contradictory properties is itself the establishment of difference.

children.text: vipratipannaṃ prati tu viruddhadharmādhyāsād bhedavyavahāraḥ sādhyate //
children.translated_text: But for one who disputes [the thesis], the conventional usage of difference is established through the superimposition of contradictory properties.

body.text: nanu tathāpi sattvamidamanaikāntikamevāsādhāraṇatvāt sandigdhavyatirekitvād vā / yathā hīdaṃ kramākramanivṛttāvakṣaṇikānnivṛttaṃ tathā sāpekṣatvānapekṣatvayorekatvānekatvayorapi vyāpakayornivṛttau kṣaṇikādapi / tathā hi upasarpaṇapratyayena devadattakarapallavādinā sahacaro bījakṣaṇaḥ pūrvasmādeva puñjāt samartho jāto 'napekṣa ādyātiśayasya janaka iṣyate / tatra ca samānakuśūlajanmasu bahuṣu bījasantāneṣu kasmāt kiñcideva bījaṃ paramparayāṅkurotpādānuguṇamupajanayati vījakṣaṇaṃ nānye bījakṣaṇā bhinnasantānāntaḥ pātinaḥ / na hi upasarpaṇapratyayāt prāgeva teṣāṃ samānāsamānasantānavartināṃ bījakṣaṇānāṃ kaścit paramparātiśayaḥ / athopasarpaṇapratyayāt prāṅ na tatsantānavartino 'pi janayanti, paramparayāpyaṅkurotpādānuguṇaṃ bījakṣaṇaṃ bījamātrajananāt teṣām / kasyacideva bījakṣaṇasyopasarpaṇa pratyayasahabhuva ādyātiśayotpādaḥ / hanta tarhi tadabhāve satyutpanno 'pi na janayedeva / tathā ca kevalānāṃ vyabhicārasaṃbhavādādyātiśayotpādakamaṅkuraṃ vā pratikṣityādīnāṃ parasparāpekṣāṇāmevotpādakatvamakāmenāpi svīkarttavyam / ato na tāvadanapekṣā kṣaṇikasya sambhavinī / nāpyapekṣā yujyate, samasamayakṣaṇayoḥ savyetaragoviṣāṇayorivopakāryopakārakabhāvāyogāt iti nāsiddhaḥ prathamo vyāpakābhāvaḥ / api cāntyo bījakṣaṇo 'napekṣāṅkurādikaṃ kurvan yadi yenaiva rūpeṇāṅkuraṃ karoti tenaiva kṣityādikaṃ tadā kṣityādīnāmapyaṅkurasvābhāvyāpattirabhinnakāraṇatvāditi na tāvadekatvasaṃbhavaḥ //
body.translated_text: Objection: Even so, this 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>) [as a reason for momentariness] is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), either because it is uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) or because [its] negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is doubtful. For just as this [existence] is excluded from what is excluded from both sequential and non-sequential [production], [and hence] from the non-momentary; so too it should be excluded from the momentary as well—[since it should be] excluded from what is excluded from both dependence and independence, and from both unity and multiplicity—these being its pervaders. For the seed-moment that arises as capable from the very same aggregate as its predecessor—in association with the auxiliary condition of approaching [water, etc.]—is held [by you] to be independent, the generator of the initial surplus, without requiring [anything further]. But among the many seed-continua born in the same granary, why does only a particular seed produce—through a series—a seed-moment conducive to sprout-production, while other seed-moments belonging to different continua do not? For prior to the auxiliary condition of approaching [water], there is no serial surplus whatsoever among those seed-moments, whether belonging to the same or different continua. If, then, even prior to the approaching-condition those within that [particular] continuum do not generate—even in a series—a seed-moment conducive to sprout-production (since they are merely generators of [the next] seed), [then] the initial surplus arises only in that particular seed-moment which co-exists with the approaching-condition. But then, in its absence, even when produced it would not generate at all! And thus, since deviation is possible for isolated [factors], the production of the initial surplus—or [rather] earth and the like with respect to the sprout—must be accepted even unwillingly as [requiring] mutual dependence. Therefore, independence is not possible for the momentary. Nor is dependence appropriate, since for two things existing at the same moment—like the right and left horns of a cow—the relation of helper and helped is impossible. Thus, the first exclusion of the pervader [viz. 'either dependent or independent'] is not unestablished. Moreover, the final seed-moment, independently producing sprout and so forth—if it produces the sprout by the very same form by which it produces earth and the like—then earth and the like would have the nature of sprout, because they would have an undifferentiated cause. Thus unity [of nature] is not possible.

body.text: nanu rūpāntareṇa karoti / tathā hi bījasyāṅkuraṃ pratyupādānatvam / kṣityādikaṃ tu prati sahakāritvam / yadyevaṃ sahakāritvopādānatve kimekaṃ tattvaṃ nānā vā / (#Nibandh 80#) ekaṃ cet kathaṃ rūpāntareṇa janakam / nānātve tvanayorbījādbhedo 'bhedo vā / bhede kathaṃ bījasya janakatvaṃ tābhyāmevāṅkurādīnāmutpatteḥ / abhede vā kathaṃ bījasya na nānātvaṃ bhinnatādātmyāt, etayorvaikatvamekatādātmyāt /
body.translated_text: Objection: It produces by a different form. Namely, the seed has the role of material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) with respect to the sprout, but is an auxiliary cause (<s>sahakārin</s>) with respect to earth and the like. Reply: If so, are the auxiliary-nature and material-cause-nature one reality or many? [<s>Nibandh</s> 80] If one, how does it generate by a different form? If many, are these different from or identical with the seed? If different, how does the seed have generative power—since the sprout and the like would arise from those [natures] alone? If identical, how is the seed not a multiplicity—since its identity would be with what is different [from itself], and [those natures'] unity would arise from their being identical [with the seed]?

body.text: yadyucyeta kṣityādau janayitavye tadupādānaṃ pūrvameva kṣityādibījasya rūpāntaramiti / na tarhi bījaṃ tadanapekṣaṃ kṣityādīnāṃ janakam / tadanapekṣatve teṣāmaṅkurādbhedānupapatteḥ / na cānupakārakāṇyapekṣanta iti tvayaivoktam / na ca kṣaṇasyopakārasaṃbhavo 'nyatra jananāt, tasyābhedyatvādityanekatvamapi nāstīti dvitīyo 'pi vyāpakābhāvo nāsiddhaḥ / tasmādasādhāraṇānaikāntikatvaṃ gandhavattvavaditi /
body.translated_text: If one says: 'The material cause of earth and the like, when they are to be generated, is itself another form of the seed that already existed previously'—then the seed is not, independently of those [forms], the generator of earth and the like. For if [the seed were] independent of them, the difference of those [earth, etc.] from the sprout could not be accounted for. And it is you yourself who have said that non-helpers are not depended upon. Nor is there any possibility of a moment's helping [another moment] apart from generating it—since [a moment] is indivisible. Thus multiplicity too does not exist. Therefore, the second exclusion of the pervader [viz. 'either one or many'] is also not unestablished. Hence the inconclusiveness is [only of the] uncommon type, like smell-possession [which proves nothing specific].

body.text: yadi manyetānupakārakā api bhavanti sahakāriṇo 'pekṣaṇīyāśca kāryeṇānuvihitabhāvābhāvācca sahakaraṇācca /
body.translated_text: If one thinks: 'Non-helpers too are auxiliaries, and are required [by the effect], because the effect's presence and absence follows theirs, and because of [their] auxiliary [role]'—

body.text: nanvanena krameṇākṣaṇiko 'pi bhāvo 'nupakārakānapi sahakāriṇaḥ kramavataḥ kramavatkāryeṇānukṛtānvayavyatirekānapekṣiṣyate / kariṣyate ca kramavatsahakārivaśaḥ krameṇa kāryāṇīti vyāpakānupalabdherasiddheḥ sandigdhavyatirekamanaikāntikaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇikatva siddhāviti /
body.translated_text: Objection: By this same reasoning, even a non-momentary entity will require non-helping auxiliaries that are sequential—because the effect, whose presence and absence follows theirs, [also operates] sequentially; and it will produce effects sequentially under the influence of sequential auxiliaries. Therefore, since the non-apprehension of the pervader [argument against permanence] is unestablished, the [reason] 'existence' is inconclusive with doubtful negative concomitance in [the proof of] momentariness.

body.text: atra brūmaḥ / kīdṛśaṃ punarapekṣārthamādāya kṣaṇike sāpekṣānapekṣatvanivṛttirucyate / kiṃ sahakāriṇamapekṣata iti sahakāriṇāsyopakāraḥ karttavyaḥ / atha pūrvāvasthitasyaiva bījādeḥ sahakāriṇā saha saṃbhūyakaraṇam / yadvā pūrvāvasthitasyetyanapekṣyamilitāvasthasya karaṇamātramapekṣārthaḥ / atra prathamapakṣasyāsaṃbhavādanapekṣaiva kṣaṇikasya, kathamubhayavyāvṛttiḥ / yadyanapekṣaḥ kimityupasarpaṇapratyayābhāve 'pi na karoti / karotyeva yadi syāt / svayamasaṃbhavī tu kathaṃ karotu / atha tadvā tādṛgvāsīditi na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
