body.translated_text: To this we reply: What meaning of 'dependence' is being adopted when you say that the exclusion from both dependence and independence applies to the momentary? Does 'dependence' mean: 'depending on an auxiliary, it must be helped by that auxiliary'? Or: 'the seed and the like, which have existed previously, act together with the auxiliary'? Or is the meaning of 'dependence' merely the action of what has existed previously—without requiring [another's help]—in a combined state? In the first alternative, since it is impossible [for a momentary entity], independence alone belongs to the momentary—so how is there exclusion from both? If [you say] it is independent, why does it not produce even in the absence of the approaching-condition? It does produce, if it exists [at that moment]. But how can what is itself impossible produce? If [you respond:] 'That [particular seed-moment] was such, or was of such a kind'—then there is no distinction [from our position].

body.text: tatastādṛksvabhāvasaṃbhave 'yakaraṇaṃ sahakāriṇi nirapekṣatāṃ na kṣamata iti cet / asaṃbaddhametat, varṇasaṃsthānasāmye 'pyakartṛṃstatsvabhāvatāyā virahāt / sa cādyātiśayajanakatvalakṣaṇaḥ svabhāvaviśeṣo na samānāsamānasantānavartiṣu bījakṣaṇeṣu sarveṣveva saṃbhavī / kiṃ tu keṣucideva karmakarakarapallavasahacareṣu /
body.translated_text: If it is objected that when such a nature arises, the non-production [of effect] does not tolerate independence from cooperative conditions — this is incoherent, because even when there is sameness of phoneme-configuration, the nature of being its [specific] producer is absent. And that special nature characterized by being the generator of the initial excellence does not occur in all seed-moments residing in similar or dissimilar continua; rather, it occurs only in certain ones accompanied by action, agent, and sprout.

body.text: nanvekatra kṣetre niṣpattilavanādipūrvakamānīyaikatra kuśūle kṣiptāni sarvāṇyeva bījāni sādhāraṇarūpāṇyeva pratīyante / tat kutastyo 'yamekabījasaṃbhavī viśeṣo 'nyeṣāmiti cet / ucyate / kāraṇaṃ khalu sarvatra kārye dvividham - dṛṣṭamadṛṣṭaṃ (#Nibandh 81#) ceti sarvāstikaprasiddhametat / tataḥ pratyakṣaparokṣasahakāriapratyayasākalyamasarvavidā pratyakṣato na śakyaṃ pratipattum / tato bhavedapi kāraṇasāmagrīśaktibhedāttādṛśaḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ keṣāñcideva bījakṣaṇānāṃ yena ta eva bījakṣaṇā ādyātiśayamaṅkuraṃ vā paramparayā janayeyuḥ / nānye ca bījakṣaṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: When seeds planted in one field, having been preceded by crushing, salt, and so forth, and gathered into one granary, are all perceived as having a common form — whence then is this distinction arising from one seed but not from others? Reply: Indeed, the cause everywhere is twofold with respect to its effect — visible and invisible (#Nibandh 81#) — this is accepted by all <s>āstikas</s> (those who affirm [valid means of knowledge]). Therefore, the totality of perceptible and imperceptible cooperative conditions cannot be ascertained through perception alone by one who is not omniscient. Hence, through difference in the capacity of the causal aggregate, such a difference of nature may well exist in certain seed-moments alone, by virtue of which those very seed-moments would generate the initial excellence or sprout in succession — and not other seed-moments.

body.text: nanu yeṣūpasarpaṇapratyayasahacareṣu svakāraṇaśaktibhedādādyātiśayajanakatvalakṣaṇo viśeṣaḥ saṃbhāvyate sa tatrāvaśyamastīti kuto labhyamiti cet / aṅkurotpādādanumitādādyātiśayalakṣaṇāt kāryāditi brūmaḥ /kāraṇānupalabdhestarhi tadabhāva eva bhaviṣyatīti cet / na / dṛśyādṛśyasamudāyasya kāraṇasyādarśane 'pyabhāvāsiddheḥ kāraṇānupalabdheḥ sandigdhāsiddhatvāt / tadayamarthaḥ
body.translated_text: Objection: In those [seed-moments] accompanied by the cooperative condition of approach, where the distinction characterized by being the generator of initial excellence is hypothesized due to the difference in the capacity of their own causes — how is it obtained that it necessarily exists there? Reply: We say: from the effect characterized by initial excellence, inferred from the production of the sprout. Objection: Then from the non-apprehension of the cause, its very absence would follow. Reply: No, because even when the cause — which is an aggregate of visible and invisible [factors] — is not seen, its absence is not established, since the non-apprehension of the cause is of doubtful establishment. This is the meaning:

children.translated_text: Of a moment possessing hand-contact, there is no difference from [another moment] distinguished by a different time —

children.text: bhedo veti matadvaye mitibalaṃ yasyāstvasau jitvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: or there is difference — in these two views, the strength of cognition belongs to whichever is victorious.
In the former [view], the strength [of the argument] is the absence of a reason [for difference]; in the latter, [the strength is] the component of the effect, or

children.text: sāmagrī tu na sarvathekṣaṇasahā kāryaṃ tu mānānugam // iti //
children.translated_text: the [causal] aggregate is not in every case amenable to observation — but the effect accords with the means of valid cognition. Thus.

body.text: tadevaṃ nopakāro 'pekṣārtha ityanapekṣaiva kṣaṇikasya sahakāriṣu nobhayavyāvṛtiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, assistance is not the meaning of dependence — thus, for the momentary entity, there is independence from cooperative conditions, and [yet] exclusion from both [production and non-production] does not [follow].

body.text: atha saṃbhūyakaraṇamapekṣārthaḥ, tadā yadi pūrvasthitasyeti viśeṣaṇāpekṣā tadā kṣaṇikasya naivaṃ kadācidityanapekṣaivākṣīṇā /
body.translated_text: Now, if combined action is the meaning of dependence, then if the qualification 'of what previously existed' is required, then for the momentary entity this is never the case — thus independence is undiminished.

body.text: atha pūrvasthitasyetyanapekṣya militāvasthitasyaiva karaṇamapekṣārthastadā sāpekṣataiva, nānapekṣā / tathā ca nobhayavyāvṛttirityasiddhaḥ prathamo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / tathaikatvānekatvayorapi vyāpakayoḥ kṣaṇikād vyāvṛttirasiddhā / tattadvyāvṛttibhedamāśrityopādānatvādikālpanikasvabhāvabhede 'pi paramārthata ekenaiva svarūpeṇānekakāryaniṣpādanādubhayavyāvṛtterabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: But if, without requiring [the qualification] 'of what previously existed,' the action only of what exists in a combined state is the meaning of dependence, then there is indeed dependence, not independence. And thus the exclusion from both is unestablished — [hence] the first <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader) is unestablished. Likewise, the exclusion of unity and multiplicity — which are also pervaders — from the momentary is unestablished. Because, even when there is a constructed distinction of essential nature based on different exclusions [from unity and multiplicity], in ultimate reality, since multiple effects are accomplished by a single own-form alone, the exclusion from both does not hold.

body.text: yacca bījasyaikenaiva svabhāvena kārakatve kṣityādīnāmaṅkurasvābhāvyāpattiranyathā kāraṇābhede 'pi kāryabhede 'pi kāryasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgādityuktam tadasaṅgatam / kāraṇaikatvasya kāryabhedasya ca paṭunendriyapratyakṣeṇa prasādhanāt / ekakāraṇajanyatvaikatvayorvyāpteḥ pratihatatvāt / prasaṅgasyānupadatvāt /
body.translated_text: And as for what was said — that if the seed has causal efficacy by one nature alone, then earth and the like would have the nature of the sprout, since otherwise, even with no difference in cause, if there is difference in effect, the effect would be without a cause — that is incoherent. Because the unity of cause and the difference of effect are established by keen sensory perception. Because the pervasion between being produced by a single cause and being unitary is refuted. Because the unwanted consequence does not follow.

body.text: yacca kāraṇābhede kāryābheda ityuktaṃ tatra sāmagrīsvarūpaṃ kāraṇamabhipretam / sāmagrīsajātīyatve na kāryavijātīyatetyarthaḥ / na punaḥ sāmagrīmadhyagatenaikenānekaṃ kāryaṃ na kartavyaṃ nāma, ekasmādanekotpatteḥ pratyakṣasiddhatvāt / na caivaṃ pratyabhijñānāt kālabhede 'pyabhedasiddhirityuktaprāyam / na cendriyapratyakṣaṃ bhinnadeśaṃ sapratighaṃ (#Nibandh 82#) dṛśyamarthadvayamekamevopalambhayatīti kvacidupalabdham yena tatrāpi bhede śaṅkā syāt / śaṅkāyāṃ vā paṭupratyakṣasyāpyapalāpe sarvapramāṇocchedaprasaṅgāditi /
body.translated_text: And as for what was said that 'given no difference in cause there is no difference in effect' — there the aggregate-form is intended as the cause. The meaning is: there is no dissimilarity of effect when there is similarity of the aggregate. But it is not the case that one [factor] within the aggregate cannot produce multiple effects — since the production of many from one is established by perception. Nor is it the case that through recognition, identity is established even across temporal difference — this has been mostly stated already. And sensory perception does not cause the apprehension of two visible objects occupying different spatial locations (#Nibandh 82#) and having resistance as one and the same — this has never been observed. Hence there would be no doubt about difference even there. Or if there is doubt, then since even keen perception would be rejected, the unwanted consequence of the destruction of all means of valid cognition [would follow].

body.text: nāpi sattvahetoḥ sandigdhavyatirekitvam, kṣityāderdravyāntarasya bījasvabhāvatvenāsmābhirasvīkṛtatvāt / anupakāriṇyapekṣāyāḥ pratyākhyātatvāt vyāpakānupalambhasyāsiddhatvāyogāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is the <s>sattva</s>-reason (existence-reason) one of doubtful negative concomitance, because earth and other substances are not accepted by us as being of the nature of the seed. Because dependence without assistance has been rejected. Because the non-establishment of the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader) is inadmissible.

body.text: tadetau dvāvapi vyāpakānupalambhāvasiddhau na kṣaṇikāt sattvaṃ nivartayata iti nāyamasādhāraṇo hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus these two <s>vyāpakānupalambhas</s> (non-apprehensions of the pervader) are both unestablished and do not remove <s>sattva</s> (existence) from the momentary — therefore this is not an inconclusive reason.

body.text: api ca vidyamāno bhāvaḥ sādhyetarayoraniścitānvayavyatireko gandhavattādivadasādhāraṇo yuktaḥ / prakṛtavyāpakānupalambhācca sarvathārthakriyaivāsatī ubhābhyāṃ vādibhyāmubhayasmādvinivartitatvena nirāśrayatvāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, an existing entity whose positive and negative concomitance with either the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) or the other [i.e., its absence] is undetermined — like the property of having smell — is rightly [called] inconclusive. But due to the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> under discussion, <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) itself is entirely absent [in the non-momentary], since it is excluded from both [alternatives] by both disputants — hence it is without a locus.

body.text: tat kathamasādhāraṇānaikāntiko bhaviṣyatītyalaṃ pralāpini nirbandhena /
body.translated_text: Therefore, how could [this reason] become an inconclusive <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (exclusively inconclusive) one? — enough with insistence from the prattler!

body.text: tadevaṃ śaktasya kṣepāyogāt samarthavyavahāragocaratvaṃ jananena vyāptamiti prasaṅgaviparyayayoḥ satve hetorapi nānaikāntikatvam / ataḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiritisthitam //
body.translated_text: Thus, since there is no impediment to what is capable, and since being the object of the conventional usage of 'capable' is pervaded by productive activity — through both <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>viparyaya</s> (contraposition), even when existence is the reason, there is no inconclusiveness. Therefore, the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) stands established.

body.text: iti sādharmyadṛṣṭānte 'nvayarūpavyāptyā
body.translated_text: Thus, through the pervasion in the form of positive concomitance in the example of similarity (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>),

body.text: kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ samāptā //
body.translated_text: the proof of momentariness (<s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) is concluded.

body.text: kṛtiriyaṃ mahāpaṇḍitaratnakīrtipādānāmiti //
body.translated_text: This is the composition of the feet of the great <s>paṇḍita</s> <s>Ratnakīrti</s>.

(#Nibandh 83#)
Section 5.

body.text: // kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Proof of Momentariness (<s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>)

body.text: // vyatirekātmikā //
body.translated_text: through the method of dissimilarity (<s>vyatirekātmikā</s>).

body.text: // namastārāyai //
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Tārā</s>.

children.translated_text: The pervasion in the form of dissimilarity, which implies the form of positive concomitance,
is here stated for the reason of <s>sattva</s> (existence) in the example of dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>).

body.text: yat sat tat kṣaṇikam / yathā ghaṭaḥ / santaścāmī vivādāspadībhūtāḥ padārthā iti svabhāvahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Whatever exists is momentary — like a pot. And these entities that are the subject of dispute do exist — thus [this is] a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (reason based on essential nature).

body.text: na tāvadasyāsiddhiḥ saṃbhavati, yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣānumānapramāṇapratīte dharmiṇi sattvaśabdenābhipretasyārthakriyākāritvalakṣaṇasya sādhanasya pramāṇasamadhigatatvāt /
body.translated_text: First, non-establishment [of the reason] is not possible, because the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) — namely, that which is intended by the word '<s>sattva</s>' (existence), characterized as having causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) — is ascertained by a means of valid cognition in the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) which is cognized by perception or inference as appropriate.

body.text: na ca viruddhānaikāntikate, vyāpakānupalambhātmanā viparyaye bādhakapramāṇena vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt / yasya kramākramau na vidyete na tasyārthakriyāsāmarthyam / yathā śaśaviṣāṇasya / na vidyete cākṣaṇikasya kramākramāviti vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / na tāvadayamasiddho hetuḥ, akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramasadbhāvāyogāt / tathā hi prāptāparakālayorekatve nityatvam / tasya kramākramayoge kṣaṇadvaye 'pyavaśyaṃ bhedaḥ / bhedābhedayośca parasparavirodhāt kuto 'kṣaṇike kramākramasaṃbhavaḥ / kṣaṇadvaye 'pi bhede kramākramayogaḥ / abhede hi prathama eva kṣaṇe śaktatvād bhāvino 'pi kāryasya karaṇaprasaṅge kathaṃ kāryāntarakaraṇe kramāntarāvakāśaḥ / na cākṣaṇikasyākrameṇaiva sakalasvakāryaṃ kṛtvā svāsthyam / kṣaṇāntare 'pi śaktatvāt punastatkāryakaraṇaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction or inconclusiveness, since the pervasion is established by a sublating cognition (<s>bādhakapramāṇa</s>) regarding the counter-thesis, in the form of a <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader). That which has neither succession nor simultaneity has no capacity for causal efficacy — like the horn of a hare. And the non-momentary has neither succession nor simultaneity — this is the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>. Now, this reason is not unestablished, because succession and simultaneity cannot co-exist in a non-momentary <s>dharmin</s>. For if that which has attained the subsequent time is identical [with what existed before], there is permanence. If succession and simultaneity are [both] present, then in both moments there must necessarily be difference. And since difference and non-difference are mutually contradictory, how can succession and simultaneity be possible in the non-momentary? When there is difference in both moments, [then] succession and simultaneity are possible. For if [the entity is] non-momentary, since it is capable in the very first moment, there would be the unwanted consequence of producing even the future effect [immediately] — so how is there room for another succession of effects? Nor can the non-momentary, having performed all its effects simultaneously, remain at rest — since being capable in the next moment too, there would be the unwanted consequence of producing that effect again.

body.text: tasmādakṣaṇikamiti pūrvāparakālayorabhedaḥ / kramākramayoga iti pūrvāparakālayorbhedaḥ / anayośca parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇo virodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, 'non-momentary' means non-difference between the prior and subsequent times. 'Having succession and simultaneity' means difference between the prior and subsequent times. And between these two there is a contradiction characterized by mutual exclusion.

body.text: tadayamakṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramābhāvalakṣaṇo heturnāsiddho vaktavyaḥ / kramākramayogitvākṣaṇikatvayorvirodhādeva /
body.translated_text: Thus this reason — the absence of succession and simultaneity in the non-momentary <s>dharmin</s> — should not be called unestablished, precisely because of the contradiction between possessing succession-and-simultaneity and being non-momentary.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 84#)
nāpi viruddhaḥ, sapakṣe bhāvāt /
body.translated_text:
(#Nibandh 84#)
Nor is it contradictory, because it is present in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue).

body.text: na cānaikāntikaḥ, kramākramābhāvasyārthakriyāsāmarthyābhāvena vyāptatvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is it inconclusive, because the absence of succession and simultaneity is pervaded by the absence of capacity for causal efficacy.

body.text: yenaiva hi pratyakṣātmanā pramāṇenāparaprakārābhāvādvidhibhūtābhyāṃ kramākramābhyāṃ vidhibhūtasyārthakriyāsāmarthyasya vyāptiḥ prasādhitā, tenaivārthakriyāsāmarthyābhāvena kramākramābhāvasya vyāptiḥ prasādhiteti svīkarttavyam / na hi dahanādinā dhūmādervyāptisādhakapramāṇādaparaṃ dhūmādyabhāvena dahanādyabhāvasya vyāptisādhakaṃ kiñcit pramāṇaṃ śaraṇabhūtamasti / tasmādvidhyoreva vyāptisādhakaṃ pramāṇamabhāvayorapi vyāptisādhakamiti nyāyasya duratikramatvāt sattvābhāvena kramākramābhāvo vyāpta eveti nānaikāntika ityanavadyo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / tadayamakṣaṇikād vinivartamānaḥ svavyāpyaṃ sattvaṃ nivartyaṃ kṣaṇike viśrāmayatīti sattvahetoḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhirapyanavadyā /
body.translated_text: For by the very same perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) by which the pervasion of the positive entity — causal efficacy — by the positive entities succession and simultaneity (which are [established] in the absence of any other form) is established — by that very [pramāṇa], the pervasion of the absence of succession and simultaneity by the absence of causal efficacy must be accepted. For there is no other refuge-pramāṇa that establishes the pervasion of the absence of smoke and the like by the absence of fire and the like, apart from the pramāṇa that establishes the pervasion of smoke and the like by fire and the like. Therefore, since the principle that the very pramāṇa establishing pervasion between positive entities also establishes pervasion between their absences is inviolable — the absence of succession and simultaneity is pervaded by the absence of <s>sattva</s> (existence) — hence [the reason] is not inconclusive. Thus this is a faultless <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>. This [vyāpakānupalambha], turning away from the non-momentary, causes its pervaded [property] — sattva — which is to be negated, to rest in the momentary. Thus the proof of momentariness through the sattva-reason is also faultless.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 85#)
nanu vyāpakānupalambhataḥ sattvasya kathaṃ svasādhyapratibandhasiddhiḥ, asyāpyanekadoṣaduṣṭatvāt / tathā hi na tāvadayaṃ prasaṅgo hetuḥ, sādhyadharmiṇi pramāṇasiddhatvāt, parābhyupagamasiddhatvābhāvāt, viparyayaparyavasānābhāvācca / atha svatantraḥ, tadāśrayāsiddhaḥ / akṣaṇikasyāśrayasyāsaṃbhavāt / apratītatvādvā / pratītarhi pratyakṣeṇānumānena vikalpamātreṇa vā syāt /
body.translated_text:
(#Nibandh 85#)
Objection: How is the establishment of the connection of <s>sattva</s> (the reason) with its own <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) achieved through the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>, since that too is vitiated by many faults? For this [vyāpakānupalambha] is not a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) reason — because it is established by a pramāṇa in the dharmin of the sādhya, because it is not established merely by the opponent's concession, and because it does not culminate in the counter-thesis. If it is an independent [reason], then it has the fault of an unestablished locus — because the non-momentary locus is impossible. Or [it is] unapprehended. If apprehended, it would be either by perception, inference, or mere conceptual construction.

body.text: prathamapakṣadvaye sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa vā svapratītilakṣaṇārthakāritve maulasādhāraṇo hetuḥ vyāpakānulambhaśca svarūpāsiddhaḥ syāt / arthakriyākāritve kramākramayoranyatarasyā vaśyaṃbhāvāt / antimapakṣe tu na kaściddheturanāśrayaḥ syāt / vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sulabhatvāt /
body.translated_text: In the first two alternatives, directly or indirectly, the original inconclusive reason and the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> would be unestablished in their own nature — since if [the locus] has causal efficacy as its object of apprehension, succession or simultaneity necessarily follows. In the last alternative, no reason whatsoever would be without a locus — since a <s>dharmin</s> established by mere conceptual construction is easily available everywhere.

body.text: api ca, tat kalpanājñānaṃ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvi vā syāt, liṅgajanma vā, saṃskārajaṃ vā, sandigdhavastukaṃ vā, avastukaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: Moreover, that conceptual cognition would be either: (1) following upon perception, (2) born from a logical mark, (3) born from residual impressions, (4) of doubtful objective reference, or (5) without objective reference.

body.text: tatrādyapakṣadvaye 'kṣaṇikasya sattaivāvyāhatā / kathaṃ bādhakāvatāraḥ / tṛtīye tu na sarvadākṣaṇikasattāniṣedhaḥ, tadarpitasaṃskārābhāve tatsmaraṇāyogāt / caturthe tu sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ hetudoṣaḥ / pañcame ca tadviṣayasyābhāvo na tāvat pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati, akṣaṇikātmanaḥ sarvadaiva tvanmate 'pratyakṣatvāt / na cānumānatastadabhāvastatpratibaddhaliṅgānupalambhādityāśrayāsiddhistāvaduddhatā / evaṃ dṛṣṭānto 'pi pratihantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the first two alternatives, the existence of the non-momentary remains uncontradicted — how can the sublating cognition enter? In the third, the negation of the existence of the non-momentary is not [possible] at all times, since without the residual impression deposited by it, the memory of it would be impossible. In the fourth, the fault of the reason is having a doubtful locus. In the fifth, the non-existence of its object cannot be established through perception — since in your view the non-momentary is never perceptible. Nor through inference — [which would require] the non-apprehension of a mark connected with it — and thus the non-establishment of the locus has been raised. The example too should be challenged in the same way.

body.text: svarūpāsiddho 'pyayaṃ hetuḥ, sthirasyāpi kramākramisahakāryapekṣayā kramākramābhyāmarthakriyopapatteḥ / nāpi kramayaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ / tathā hi kramisahakāryapekṣayā kramikāryakāritvaṃ tāvadaviruddham /
body.translated_text: This reason is also unestablished in its own nature, because even for what is permanent, causal efficacy through succession and simultaneity is possible through dependence on successive and simultaneous cooperative conditions. Nor does the fault stated in the succession-and-simultaneity alternative follow. For causal activity producing successive effects through dependence on successive cooperative conditions is not contradictory.

body.text: tathā ca śaṅkarasya saṃkṣipto 'yamabhiprāyaḥ / sahakārisākalyaṃ hi sāmarthyam / tadvaikalyaṃ cāsāmarthyam / na ca tayorāvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyāṃ tadvataḥ kācit kṣatiḥ, tasya tābhyāmanyatvāt / tatkathaṃ sahakāriṇo 'napekṣya kāryakaraṇaprasaṅga iti /
body.translated_text: And this is the condensed purport of <s>Śaṅkara</s>: Capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is indeed the totality of cooperative conditions. And incapacity is their incompleteness. And by the appearance and disappearance of those [conditions], no damage is done to their possessor, since it is different from them. Therefore, how is there the unwanted consequence of producing effects without regard to cooperative conditions?

body.text: trilocanasyāpyayaṃ saṃkṣiptārthaḥ / kāryameva hi sahakāriṇamapekṣate / na kāryotpattihetuḥ / yasmāt dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijamāgantukaṃ ca sahakāryantaram, tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavatsahakārinānātvādapi kramavatkāryanānātvopapatteraśakyaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratikṣaṇamanyānyatvamupapādayitumiti /
body.translated_text: And this is the condensed meaning of <s>Trilocana</s> as well: It is the effect that depends on the cooperative condition, not the cause of the effect's production. Since capacity is twofold — intrinsic and adventitious (i.e., another cooperative condition) — therefore, even for the non-momentary, since there is diversity of effects due to the diversity of successive cooperative conditions, it is impossible to demonstrate that entities are different at every moment.

body.text: nyāyabhūṣaṇo 'pi lapati / prathamakāryotpādanakāle hi uttarakāryotpādanasvabhāvaḥ / ataḥ prathamakāla evāśeṣāṇi kāryāṇi kuryāditi cet / tadidaṃ mātā me bandhyetyādivat svavacanavirodhādayuktam / yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ sa (#Nibandh 86#) kathamādau tat kāryaṃ kuryāt / (atha kuryāt) na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāva / nahi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikamapi karotīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> also argues: 'At the time of producing the first effect, [the cause] has the nature of producing the subsequent effect. Therefore, it should produce all effects at the very first moment.' This, like [saying] 'My mother is barren,' is untenable because of self-contradiction. For that which has the nature of generating the subsequent effect— [<s>Nibandh</s> 86] how could it produce that effect at the beginning? If it were to produce [it at the beginning], then it would not have the nature of producing that [particular later] effect. For that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and so forth.

body.text: vācaspatirapi paṭhati / nanvayamakṣaṇikaḥ svarūpeṇa kāryaṃ janayati / taccāsya svarūpaṃ tṛtīyādiṣviva kṣaṇeṣu dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe saditi tadāpi janayet / akurvan vā tṛtīyādiṣvapi na kurvīta, tasya tādavasthyāt / atādavasthye vā tadevāsya kṣaṇikatvam //
body.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s> also writes: 'Now, this non-momentary [entity] generates the effect by its own nature. And that nature of its exists in the second moment just as in the third and subsequent moments—so it should generate then too. Or, if it does not generate [in the second moment], it should not generate in the third and subsequent moments either, since its condition remains unchanged. But if its condition changes—that itself would be its momentariness.'

body.text: atrocyate / satyaṃ svarūpeṇa kāryaṃ janayati na tu tenaiva / sahakārisahitādeva tataḥ kāryotpattidarśanāt / tasmād vyāptivatkāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pyekatrānyayogavyavacchedena / anyatrāyogavyavacchedenāvavoddhavyaḥ / tathaiva laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ saṃpratipatteriti na kramikāryakāritvapakṣoktadoṣāvasaraḥ //
body.translated_text: To this we reply: It is true that it generates the effect by its own nature, but not by that alone; for the generation of the effect is observed only from [the cause] together with its auxiliaries. Therefore, the causal relation, like pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), should be understood through the exclusion of co-occurrence elsewhere in one case (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>), and through the exclusion of non-co-occurrence (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>) in the other. For this is also the consensus of ordinary investigators. Therefore, there is no occasion for the fault stated in the position [advocating] sequential effect-production.

body.text: nāpyakṣaṇike yaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣāvakāśaḥ / ye hi kāryamutpāditavanto dravyaviśeṣāsteṣāṃ vyāpārasya niyatakāryotpādanasamarthasya niṣpādite kārye 'nuvartamāneṣvapi teṣu dravyeṣu nivṛttārthādūnā sāmagrī jāyate / tatkathaṃ niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayiṣyati / na hi daṇḍādayaḥ svabhāvenaiva kartāro yenāmī niṣpatterārabhya kāryaṃ vidadhyuḥ / kiṃ tarhi vyāpārāveśinaḥ / na ceyatā svarūpeṇa na kartāraḥ, svarūpakārakatvanirvāhaparatayā vyāpārasamāveśāditi //
body.translated_text: Nor is there scope for the fault stated in the position of simultaneity for the non-momentary [entity]. For those particular substances that have produced an effect—when their operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>), which was capable of producing a determinate effect, [has accomplished its task]—once the effect is accomplished, even though those substances continue to exist, the aggregate becomes diminished in its completed function. So how could [they] produce again what has [already] been produced? For sticks and the like are not producers by their mere nature—such that they would make the effect starting from [the moment of] completion. Rather, [they are producers] through the entry of their operation. And it is not that [the entity] is not a producer by its own nature [at all]—[rather,] the entry of the operation serves to fulfill the role of [its] own-nature as causal agent.

body.text: kiṃ ca kramākramābhāvaśca bhaviṣyati na ca sattvābhāva iti sandigdhavyatireko 'pyayaṃ vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / na hi kramākramābhyāmanyasya prakārasyābhāvaḥ siddhaḥ, viśeṣaniṣedhasya śeṣābhyanujñāviṣayatvāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, there will be [a case where] the absence of both sequence and simultaneity [obtains], and yet the absence of existence (<s>sattva</s>) does not [follow]—so this non-apprehension of the pervader has doubtful negative concomitance. For the absence of any mode other than sequence and simultaneity is not established—since a particular negation has the domain of permitting the remainder.

body.text: kiṃ ca prakārāntarasya dṛśyatve nātyantaniṣedhaḥ / adṛśyatve tu nāsattāniścayo viprakarṣiṇāmiti na kramākramābhyāmarthakriyāsāmarthyasya vyāptisiddhiḥ / ataḥ sandigdhavyatireko 'pi vyāpakānupalambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if the other mode is visible, there is no absolute negation [of it]; and if it is invisible, there is no certainty of its non-existence for those who take a detached view—so there is no establishment of the pervasion of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>) by sequence and simultaneity. Therefore, even the non-apprehension of the pervader has doubtful negative concomitance.

body.text: kiṃ ca dṛśyādṛśyasahakāripratyayasākalyavataḥ kramayaugapadyasyātyantaparokṣatvāt tena vyāptaṃ sattvamapi parokṣameveti na tāvatpratibandhaḥ pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati / nāpyanumānataḥ, tatpratibaddhaliṅgābhāvāditi /
body.translated_text: Moreover, since sequence and simultaneity—for [an entity] that has the totality of visible and invisible auxiliary conditions—are utterly beyond perception, even existence (<s>sattva</s>), which is pervaded by them, is itself beyond perception. Therefore, in the first place, the connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is not established through perception. Nor through inference, because there is no inferential mark that is connected with that [connection].

body.text: api ca kramākramābhyāmarthakriyākāritvaṃ vyāptamityatisubhāṣitam / yadi krameṇa vyāptaṃ kathamakrameṇa / athākrameṇa na tarhi krameṇa / kramākramābhyāṃ vyāptamiti tu bruvatā vyāpterevābhāvaḥ pradarśito bhavati / na hi bhavati dhūmo vahnibhāvābhāvābhyāṃ vyāpta iti / ato vyāpteranaikāntikatvam /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, [the claim that] causal efficacy is pervaded by sequence and simultaneity is most eloquently [stated indeed]! If pervaded by sequence, how also by non-sequence? If by non-sequence, then not by sequence. But one who says 'pervaded by both sequence and non-sequence' has thereby demonstrated the very absence of pervasion. For one never [validly] says 'smoke is pervaded by both the existence and non-existence of fire.' Therefore, the pervasion [itself] is inconclusive.

body.text: api ca kimidaṃ bādhakamakṣaṇikānāmasattāṃ sādhayati, utasvidakṣaṇikāt sattvasya vyatirekam, atha sattvakṣaṇikatvayoḥ pratibandham / na pūrvo vikalpaḥ, (#Nibandh 87#) uktakrameṇa hetorāśrayāsiddhatvāt / na ca dvitīyaḥ / yato vyāpakanivṛttisahitā vyāpyanivṛttirvyatirekaśabdasyārthaḥ / sā ca yadi pratyakṣeṇa pratīyate tadā taddhetuḥ syāditi sattvamanaikāntikam / vyāpakānupalambhaḥ svarūpāsiddhaḥ / atha sā vikalpyate tadā pūrvoktakrameṇa pañcadhā vikalpya vikalpo dūṣaṇīyaḥ / ata eva na tṛtīyo 'pi vikalpaḥ, vyatirekāsiddhau sambandhāsiddheḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, does this 'refuter' (<s>bādhaka</s>, the non-apprehension of the pervader) establish the non-existence of the non-momentary, or the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) of existence from the non-momentary, or the connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) between existence and momentariness? Not the first alternative, [<s>Nibandh</s> 87] because of the unestablished substratum of the reason (<s>hetu</s>), as explained above. Nor the second. For the meaning of the word <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) is: the absence of the pervaded together with the absence of the pervader. And if that is cognized through perception, then the reason 'existence' would be [merely] the cause of that [perception]—so existence would be inconclusive; [and] the non-apprehension of the pervader would be essentially unestablished. But if it is conceived through conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>), then—analyzing the conceptual cognition in five ways as described earlier—the concept should be refuted. For this very reason, nor [does] the third alternative [hold], since in the absence of established negative concomitance, the connection is unestablished.

body.text: kiṃ ca na bhūtalavadatrākṣaṇiko dharmī dṛśyate / na ca svabhāvānupalambhe vyāpakānupalambhaḥ kasyacit dṛśyasya pratipattimantareṇāntarbhāvayituṃ śakyata iti /
body.translated_text: Moreover, a non-momentary <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is not observed here, unlike an atom. Nor can the non-apprehension of the pervader, [used] in the non-perception of own-nature (<s>svabhāvānupalambha</s>), be subsumed [under another proof] without the cognition of some visible [entity].

body.text: kiṃ cāsyābhāvadharmatve āśrayāsiddhatvamitaretarāśrayatvaṃ ca / bhāvadharmatve viruddhatvaṃ ca / ubhayadharmatve cānaikāntikatvamiti na trayīṃ doṣajātimatipatati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if [the reason] has absence as its property, there is [the fault of] unestablished substratum and mutual dependence; if it has existence as its property, [the fault of] contradiction; and if it has both as its property, inconclusiveness—so it does not escape the threefold class of faults.

body.text: yat punaruktamakṣaṇikatve kramayaugapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhāditi / tatra virodhasiddhimanusaratā virodhyapi pratipattavyaḥ / tatpratītināntarīyakatvād virodhasiddheḥ / yathā tuhinadahanayoḥ sāpekṣadhrūvabhāvayośca / pratiyogī cākṣaṇikaḥ pratīyamānaḥ pratītikāritvāt sanneva syāt, ajanakasyāprameyatvāt /
body.translated_text: Now, as for what was said—that if [an entity were] non-momentary, there would be a contradiction with causal efficacy through both sequence and simultaneity—in that case, one who investigates the establishment of contradiction must also cognize the contradictory counter-correlate. For the establishment of contradiction is inseparable from its cognition—just as with frost and fire, or with that which is conditional and that which is permanent. And the counter-correlate—the non-momentary—being cognized, should exist, since it is productive of cognition; for what is not a generator cannot be a <s>prameya</s> (object of valid knowledge).

body.text: saṃvṛtisiddhenākṣaṇikatvena virodhasiddhiriti cet / saṃvṛtisiddhamapi vāstavaṃ kālpanikaṃ vā syāt /
body.translated_text: Objection: The contradiction is established through the non-momentary as established conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtisiddha</s>). Reply: The conventionally established [non-momentary] would be either real (<s>vāstava</s>) or imaginary (<s>kālpanika</s>).

body.text: yadi vāstavaṃ kathaṃ tasyāsattvam / kathaṃ cārthakriyākāritvavirodhaḥ / arthakriyāṃ kurvaddhi vāstavamucyate /
body.translated_text: If real—how is there non-existence (<s>asattva</s>) for it? And how is there contradiction with causal efficacy? For what performs causal efficacy is said to be 'real.'

body.text: atha kālpanikam / tatra kiṃ virodho vāstavaḥ, kālpaniko vā / na tāvad vāstavaḥ, kalpitavirodhivirodhatvāt, bandhyāputravirodhavat / atha virodho 'pi kālpanikaḥ na tarhi sattvasya vyatirekaḥ pāramārthika iti kṣaṇabhaṅgo dattajalāñjaliriti /
body.translated_text: If imaginary—is the contradiction [with it] real or imaginary? It is not real, because the contradictory is [itself merely] imagined—like a contradiction with a barren woman's son. If the contradiction too is imaginary, then the negative concomitance of existence [from the non-momentary] is not ultimate—and so momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) can be bid farewell.

body.text: ayameva codyaprabandho 'smadgurubhiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ
body.translated_text: This very chain of objections was summarized by our teachers [in verse]:

children.translated_text: The permanent does not exist, or is not the object of cognition—hence the unestablished substratum

children.text: hetoḥ svānubhavasya ca kṣatirataḥ kṣiptaḥ sapakṣo 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: of the reason; and there is damage to one's own experience; therefore, the concordant instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) too is displaced;

children.text: śūnyaśca dvitayena sidhyati na cāsattāpi sattā yathā
children.translated_text: and [the substratum] is empty with respect to both [existence and non-existence]; and non-existence is not established, just as existence [is not];

children.text: no nityena virodhasiddhirasatā śakyā kramāderapi // iti //
children.translated_text: nor can the establishment of contradiction with the permanent or with the non-existent [be accomplished], even from sequence and the rest. //

body.text: atrocyate / iha vastunyapi dharmidharmavyavahāro dṛṣṭo yathā gavi gotvam, paṭe śuklatvam, turage gamanamityādi / avastunyapi dharmidharmavyavahāro dṛṣṭo yathā śaśaviṣāṇe tīkṣṇatvābhāvo bandhyāputre vaktṛtvābhāvo gaganāravinde gandhābhāva (#Nibandh 88#) ityādi / tatrāvastuni dharmitvaṃ nāstīti kiṃ vastudharmeṇa dharmitvaṃ nāsti, āhosvidavastudharmeṇāpi /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: Here, the conventional usage of property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) and property (<s>dharma</s>) is observed even in real entities—as cow-ness in a cow, whiteness in a cloth, movement in a horse, and so forth. And the conventional usage of property-bearer and property is also observed in non-entities—as the absence of sharpness in a hare's horn, the absence of speaking in a barren woman's son, the absence of fragrance in a sky-lotus, [<s>Nibandh</s> 88] and so forth. Now, when [one says] 'a non-entity does not have the status of property-bearer'—does this mean it does not have property-bearer-status with respect to a real property, or not even with respect to a non-real property?

body.text: prathamapakṣe siddhasādhanam / dvitīyapakṣe tu svavacanavirodhaḥ / yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: In the first alternative, the conclusion is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). But in the second alternative, there is self-contradiction. As the teachers say:

children.text: dharmasya kasyacidavastuni mānasiddhā bādhāvidhivyavahṛtiḥ kimihāsti no vā /
children.translated_text: 'Is there or is there not, regarding a non-entity, a conventionally established usage of refutation or affirmation of some property, established by <s>pramāṇa</s>?

children.text: kvāpyasti cet kathamiyanti na dūṣaṇāni nāstyeva cet svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: If there is [such usage] somewhere—how can these objections arise? If there is not—then [your very statement achieves] the establishment of self-contradiction.'

body.text: avastuno dharmitvasvīkārapūrvakatvasya vyāpakasyābhāvādā śrayāsiddhidūṣaṇasyānupanyāsaprasaṅga ityarthaḥ / yenaiva hi vacanenāvastuno dharmitvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, tenaivāvastuno dharmitvābhāvena dharmeṇa dharmitvamabhyupagatam / parantu pratiṣidhyata iti vyaktamidamīśvaraceṣṭitam / tathā hyavastuno dharmitvaṃ nāstīti vacanena dharmitvābhāvaḥ kimavastuni vidhīyate, anyatra vā, na vā kvacidapīti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning is: since the pervader—namely, the prior acceptance of property-bearer-status of a non-entity—is absent, the objection of 'unestablished substratum' should not even be raised. For by the very statement by which property-bearer-status is denied to a non-entity, by that very [statement] the property-bearer-status of the non-entity—[namely,] having the property 'absence of property-bearer-status'—is accepted. Yet it is denied! This is clearly a divine sport (<s>īśvaraceṣṭita</s>). For when the statement 'a non-entity does not have property-bearer-status' [is made]—is the absence-of-property-bearer-status predicated of the non-entity, or of something else, or of nothing at all? These are three alternatives.

body.text: prathamapakṣe 'vastuno na dharmitvaniṣedhaḥ, dharmitvābhāvasya dharmasya tatraiva vidhānāt / dvitīye 'vastuni kimāyātam anyatra dharmitvābhāvavidhānāt / tṛtīyastu pakṣo vyartha eva nirāśrayatvāditi kathamavastuno dharmitvaniṣedhaḥ / tasmādyathā pramāṇopanyāsaḥ prameyasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptaḥ, vācakaśabdopanyāso vā vācyasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptastathāvastuno dharmitvaṃ nāstīti vacanopanyāso 'vastuno dharmitvasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptaḥ / anyathā tadvacanopanyāsasya vyarthatvāt / tad yadi vacanopanyāso vyāpyadharmastadāvastuno dharmitvasvīkāro 'pi vyāpakadharmo durvāraḥ / atha na vyāpakadharmaḥ tadā vyāpyasyāpi vacanopanyāsasyāsaṃbhava iti mūkataivātra balādāyāteti kathaṃ na svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: In the first alternative, there is no denial of property-bearer-status to the non-entity—since the property 'absence-of-property-bearer-status' is predicated of that very [non-entity]. In the second, what does it matter to the non-entity that absence-of-property-bearer-status is predicated of something else? The third alternative is utterly pointless, being without a substratum. So how is property-bearer-status denied to a non-entity? Therefore, just as the presentation of a <s>pramāṇa</s> is pervaded by the prior acceptance of a <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge), and just as the presentation of a signifying word is pervaded by the prior acceptance of a signified [meaning]—so too the presentation of the statement 'a non-entity does not have property-bearer-status' is pervaded by the prior acceptance of the non-entity's property-bearer-status. Otherwise, the presentation of that statement would be pointless. If, then, the presentation of the statement is the pervaded property, then the acceptance of the non-entity's property-bearer-status is also the pervading property, which is unavoidable. But if [you say] it is not the pervading property, then even the presentation of the statement—being the pervaded—is impossible; and thus silence forcibly arrives here. So how is there not establishment of self-contradiction?

body.text: yadāhācāryaḥ - na hyabruvan paraṃ bodhayitumīśaḥ / bruvan vā doṣamimaṃ parihartumiti mahati saṃkaṭe praveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: As the <s>ācārya</s> (master) says: 'For one who does not speak is unable to instruct another; and one who speaks cannot avoid this fault—so [the opponent] enters a great predicament.'

body.text: avastuprastāve sahṛdayānāṃ mūkataiva yujyata iti cet / aho mahadvaidagdhyam / avastuprastāve svayameva yathāśakti valgitvā bhagno mūkataiva nyāyaprāpteti paribhāṣayā niḥsartumicchati / na cāvastuprastāvo rājadaṇḍena vinā caraṇamardanādināniṣṭimātreṇa vā pratiṣeddhaṃ śakyate / tataśvātrāpi kramākramabhāvasya sādhanatve sattvābhāvasya ca sādhyatve sandigdhavastubhāvasyāvastvātmano vā kṣaṇikasya dharmitvaṃ kena pratiṣidhyate /
body.translated_text: Objection: In the context of non-entities, the appropriate [response] for the sensitive is simply silence. Reply: Oh, what great cleverness! Having yourself pranced about as best you could in the context of non-entities, and having been defeated, [you now] wish to escape by the stipulation that silence alone is appropriate! But the context of non-entities cannot be prohibited except by royal punishment or merely by some unpleasantness such as foot-pressing. Therefore, here too—when the existence of both sequence and non-sequence is what is to be proved, and the absence of existence is what is to be established, [and] the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is the momentary whose reality is doubtful or whose nature is non-real—by what [means] is [its] property-bearer-status denied?

body.text:
(#Nibandh 89#)
trividho hi dharmo dṛṣṭaḥ / kaścit vastuniyato nīlādiḥ / kaścidavastuniyato yathā sarvopākhyāvirahaḥ / kaścidubhayasādhāraṇo yathānupalabdhimātram / tatra vastudharmeṇāvastuno dharmitvaniṣedha iti yuktam / na tvavastudharmeṇa, vastvavastudharmeṇa vā, svavacanasyānupanyāsaprasaṅgādityakṣaṇikasyābhāve sandehe 'pi vā vastudharmeṇa dharmitvamavyāhatamiti nāyamāśrayāsiddho vyāpakānupalambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: [<s>Nibandh</s> 89] For a threefold [classification of] property is observed: some [property] is confined to real entities, such as blue and the like; some is confined to non-entities, such as the absence of all designation; and some is common to both, such as mere non-apprehension. Now, denying the property-bearer-status of a non-entity with respect to a real property is appropriate. But not with respect to a non-real property, or a property common to both real and non-real—because there would follow the impossibility of presenting one's own statement. Therefore, even when the non-momentary is absent or doubtful, its property-bearer-status with respect to a real property is unobstructed. Thus, this non-apprehension of the pervader does not have an unestablished substratum.

body.text: akṣaṇikāpratītā vāśrayāsiddho heturiti yuktamuktam, tadapratītau tadvyavahārāyogāt / kevalamasau vyavahārāṅgabhūtā pratītirvastvavastunorekarūpā na bhavati / sākṣātpāramparyeṇa vastusāmarthyabhāvino hi vastupratītiḥ / yathā pratyakṣamanumānaṃ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvī ca vikalpaḥ / avastunastu sāmarthyābhāvādvikalpamātrameva pratītiḥ / vastuno hi vastubalabhāvinī pratītiryathā sākṣātpratyakṣam, paramparayā tatpṛṣṭhabhāvī vikalpo 'numānaṃ ca / avastunastu na vastubalabhāvinī pratītistatkārakatvenāvastutvahāniprasaṅgāt / tasmādvikalpamātramevāvastunaḥ pratītiḥ / na hyabhāvaḥ kaścidvigrahavān yaḥ sākṣātkartavyo 'pi tu vyavahartavyaḥ / sa ca vyavahāro vikalpādapi sidhyatyeva / anyathā sarvajanaprasiddho 'vastuvyavahāro na syāt / iṣyate ca taddharmitvapratiṣedhānubandhādityakāmakenāpi vikalpamātrasiddho 'kṣaṇika svīkartavya iti nāyamapratītatvādapyāśrayāsiddho heturvaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The statement that the reason is 'substratum-unestablished because the non-momentary is not cognized' was said appropriately—because in the absence of its cognition, conventional usage regarding it is impossible. However, that cognition, which is a component of conventional usage, is not of a single form for real and non-real [entities]. For the cognition of a real [entity] arises from the power of the real thing itself—either directly or through a chain; as [for example] perception, inference, and the conceptual cognition that follows in the wake of perception. But for a non-entity, since it lacks [causal] power, mere conceptual cognition alone constitutes its cognition. For a real entity's cognition arises from the force of the real thing—directly, as perception; through a chain, as the subsequent conceptual cognition and inference. But for a non-entity, the cognition does not arise from the force of a real thing—since [if it did], the non-entity would lose its non-entity status by being a cause. Therefore, mere conceptual cognition alone is the cognition of a non-entity. For absence is not something embodied that can be directly perceived—rather, it is [merely] something to be conventionally used. And that conventional usage is accomplished even through conceptual cognition alone. Otherwise, the universally acknowledged conventional usage regarding non-entities would not be possible. And that [usage] is admitted—[as seen from] its invariable connection with the denial of [its] property-bearer-status. Therefore, even unwillingly, the non-momentary—established through mere conceptual cognition—must be accepted [as a subject], and hence this reason should not be called 'substratum-unestablished' even on account of [the non-momentary's] not being [directly] cognized.

body.text: tataścākṣaṇikasya vikalpamātrasiddhatve yaduktam, na kaściddheturanāśrayaḥ vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sulabhatvāditi tadasaṅgatam / vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra saṃbhave 'pi vastudharmeṇa dharmitvāyogāt / vastudharmahetutvāpekṣayā āśrayāsiddhasyāpi hetoḥ saṃbhavāt / yathātmano vibhutvasādhanārthamupanyastaṃ sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvāditi sādhanam / vikalpaścāyaṃ hetūpanyāsāt pūrvaṃ sandigdhavastukaḥ / samarthite tu hetāvavastuka iti brūmaḥ /
body.translated_text: And then, regarding what was said against the establishment of the non-momentary through mere conceptual construction — namely, 'No reason is without a locus, since a <s>dharmin</s> (subject) established through mere conceptual construction is easily available everywhere' — that is incoherent. For even though a <s>dharmin</s> established through mere conceptual construction may be available everywhere, it cannot serve as a <s>dharmin</s> with respect to a real property (<s>vastudharma</s>). And a reason that is unestablished in its locus is indeed possible when one considers that the reason pertains to a real property. For example, the proof adduced for the purpose of establishing the ubiquity of the self: 'because it possesses qualities that are apprehended everywhere.' And this conceptual construction, prior to the presentation of the reason, has a doubtful real referent. But when the reason has been validated, we say it is devoid of a real referent.

body.text: na cātra sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ nāma hetudoṣaḥ / āstāṃ tāvat / sandigdhasyāvastuno 'pi vikalpamātrasiddhasyāvastudharmāpekṣayā dharmitvaprasādhanāt / vastudharmahetvapekṣayaiva sandigdhāśrayasya hetvābhāsasya vyavasthāpanāt / yatheha nikuñje mayūraḥ kekāyitāditi / avastukavikalpaviṣayasyāsattvaṃ tu vyāpakānupalambhādeva prasādhitam / evaṃ dṛṣṭāntasyāpi vyomotpalāderdharmitva vikalpamātreṇa pratītiścāvagantavyā / tadeva mavastudharmāpekṣayāvastuno dharmitvasya vikalpamātreṇa pratīteścāpahnotumaśakyatvānnāyamāśrayāsiddho hetuḥ / na ca dṛṣṭāntakṣatiḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is the fault of 'doubtful locus' (<s>sandigdhāśrayatva</s>) here a defect of the reason. Let that be for now. For even what is doubtful and unreal, being established through mere conceptual construction, can be shown to be a <s>dharmin</s> with respect to a non-real property. And the pseudo-reason of doubtful locus is determined only with respect to reasons pertaining to real properties — as in: 'Here in the thicket there is a peacock, because of the cry.' The unreality of what is the object of a conceptual construction of an unreal thing has been established precisely through the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> (non-perception of the pervader). Likewise, even for the example — a sky-lotus and the like — the status of being a <s>dharmin</s> and its apprehension through mere conceptual construction should be understood. Since the <s>dharmin</s>-hood of the unreal with respect to a non-real property and its apprehension through mere conceptual construction cannot be denied, this reason is not one whose locus is unestablished. Nor is there any deficiency in the example.

body.text: na caiṣa svarūpāsiddhaḥ, akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramayorvyāpakayorayogāt / tathā hi yadi tasya prathame kṣaṇe dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇasāmarthyamasti tadā (#Nibandh 90#) prathamakṣaṇabhāvikāryavat dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvyapi kāryaṃ kuryāt, samarthasya kṣepāyogāt / atha tadā sahakārisākalyalakṣaṇasāmarththaṃ nāsti, tadvaikalyalakṣaṇasyāsāmarthyasya saṃbhavāt / na hi bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa karotīti svarūpeṇaiva karoti, sahakārisahitādeva tataḥ kāryotpattidarśanāditi cet / yadā tāvadamī militāḥ santaḥ kāryaṃ kurvate tadaikārthakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvameṣāmastu, ko niṣeddhāḥ / militaireva tu tatkāryaṃ karttavyamiti kuto labhyate / pūrvāparakālayorekasvabhāvatvād bhāvasya sarvadā jananājananayoranyataraniyamaprasaṅgasya durvāratvāt / tasmāt sāmagrī janikā, naikaṃ janakamiti sthiravādināṃ manorājyasyāpyaviṣayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is this [reason] unestablished in its own nature (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), because in a non-momentary <s>dharmin</s>, both sequential (<s>krama</s>) and simultaneous (<s>akrama</s>) [causal efficacy], which are the pervaders, are impossible. For consider: if in the first moment it has the capacity to produce the effect that belongs to the second and subsequent moments, then (#Nibandh 90#) just as it produces the effect belonging to the first moment, it should also produce the effect belonging to the second and subsequent moments, since what is capable cannot be delayed. If, however, at that time it lacks the capacity characterized by the completeness of auxiliary conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>), then there is the possibility of incapacity characterized by the deficiency of those [auxiliary conditions]. [Objection:] 'It is not that an entity produces by its own nature alone; rather, the effect is seen to arise only from [the cause] together with auxiliary conditions.' [Reply:] When these, being assembled together, produce an effect, let their status as auxiliary conditions — characterized by joint operation toward a single result — stand; who would deny it? But whence is it obtained that the effect must be produced only by the assembled [conditions]? Since the entity has one and the same nature at earlier and later times, the undesirable consequence of a necessary determination toward either perpetual production or perpetual non-production is unavoidable. Therefore, the claim of the permanentists that 'the aggregate is the producer, not a single [entity]' is not even within the domain of their fantasy.

body.text: kiṃ kurmo dṛśyate tāvadevamiti cet / dṛśyatām, kiṃ tu pūrvasthitādeva paścāt sāmagrīmadhyapraviṣṭād bhāvāt kāryotpattiranyasmādeva viśiṣṭasāmagrīsamutpannāt kṣaṇāditi vivādapadametat / tatra prāgapi saṃbhave sarvadaiva kāryotpattirna vā kadācidapīti virodhamasamādhāya tata eva kāryotpattiriti sādhyānuvādamātrapravṛttaḥ kṛpāmarhati /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'What can we do? It is simply observed to be so.' [Reply:] Let it be observed, but this is precisely the point of dispute: whether the effect arises from the very same entity that existed before and later entered the aggregate of conditions, or from an entirely different moment produced by the distinctive aggregate. In that case, without resolving the contradiction — that if [the cause] is capable even before [the aggregate is complete], the effect should arise at all times, or not at all — one who proceeds by merely restating the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), saying 'the effect arises from that very [permanent entity],' deserves compassion.

body.text: na ca pratyabhijñānādevaikatvasiddhiḥ, tatpauruṣasya lūnapunarjātakeśakuśakadalīstambādau nirdalanāt / vistareṇa ca pratyabhijñādūṣaṇamasmābhiḥ sthirasiddhidūṣaṇe pratipāditamiti tata evāvadhāryam /
body.translated_text: Nor is the unity [of a permanent entity] established through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), since the validity of such [recognition] is demolished in cases like hair that has been cut and regrown, <s>kuśa</s> grass, plantain stems, and the like. And the refutation of recognition has been set forth by us in detail in the <s>Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇa</s> (Refutation of Permanence); therefore, it should be ascertained from that very [work].

body.text: nanu kāryameva sahakāriṇamapekṣate / na tu kāryotpattihetuḥ / yasmād dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijamāgantukaṃ ca sahakāryantarama, tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavatsahakārinānātvādapi kramavatkāryanānātvamiti cet / bhavatu tāvat nijāgantukabhedena dvividhaṃ sāmarthyam / tathāpi tat prātisvikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇaṃ sadyaḥ kriyādharmakamavaśyābhyupagantavyam / tadyadi prāgapi, prāgapi kāryaprasaṅgaḥ / atha paścādeva, na tadā sthiro bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] It is the effect alone that requires an auxiliary condition, not the cause of the effect's production. For capacity is twofold — intrinsic and adventitious — due to the auxiliary conditions. Therefore, even for a non-momentary [entity], the diversity of effects in sequence is due to the diversity of auxiliary conditions in sequence. [Reply:] Let capacity be twofold — intrinsic and adventitious. Still, that [capacity] must necessarily be accepted as a particular real entity (<s>vastusvalakṣaṇa</s>), belonging to the individual, and characterized by immediate activity. If it exists even before [the auxiliary conditions are complete], then the undesirable consequence of the effect arising before [its time] follows. If it exists only afterwards, then the entity is not permanent.

body.text: na ca kāryaṃ sahakāriṇo 'pekṣata iti yuktam, tasyāsattvāt / hetuśca sannapi yadi svakāryaṃ na karoti, tadā tatkāryameva tanna syāt, svātantryāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is it correct [to say] that the effect requires auxiliary conditions, since [the effect before its production] is non-existent. And if a cause, even though existent, does not produce its own effect, then that would simply not be its effect, due to [the cause's] independence.

body.text: yaccoktam - yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ sa kathamādau kāryaṃ kuryāt, (atha kuryāt) na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ, na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikamapi karotīti tadasaṅgatam / sthirasvabhāvatve bhāvasyottarakālamevedaṃ na pūrvakālamiti kuta etat / tadabhāvācca kāraṇamapyuttarakāryasvabhāvamityapi kutaḥ /
body.translated_text: And the statement — 'That which has the nature of producing a subsequent effect, how could it produce an effect at the beginning? And if it did, it would not then have the nature of producing that [subsequent] effect; for what has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and the like' — that is incoherent. If the entity has a permanent nature, whence comes the [determination] that 'this [effect arises] only at a later time, not at an earlier time'? And in the absence of that [determination], whence [comes the claim] that the cause too has the nature of [producing] a later effect?

body.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ, uttarakālameva tasya janmeti cet / sthiratve tadanupapadyamānamasthiratāmādiśatu / sthiratve 'pyeṣa eva svabhāvastasya yaduttarakṣaṇa eva kāryaṃ karotīti (#Nibandh 91#) cet / na / pramāṇabādhite svabhāvābhyupagamāyogāditi na tāvadakṣaṇikasya kramikāryakāritvamasti / nāpyakramikāryakāritvasaṃbhavaḥ, dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe kārakasvarūpasadbhāve punarapi kāryakaraṇaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'What can we do? Its production simply occurs at a later time.' [Reply:] Let that which is inexplicable under [the hypothesis of] permanence point to impermanence. [Objection:] 'Even under permanence, this is simply its nature — that it produces the effect only at a later moment.' (#Nibandh 91#) [Reply:] No, because it is impossible to accept a nature that is contradicted by valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Thus, first of all, sequential causal efficacy does not belong to a non-momentary [entity]. Nor is simultaneous causal efficacy possible, because if the entity's causal nature persists even in the second moment, the undesirable consequence of producing the effect again [would follow].

body.text: kāryeniṣpanne tadviṣayavyāpārābhāvādūnā sāmagrī na niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayediti cet / na / sāmagrīsaṃbhavāsaṃbhavayorapi sadyaḥ kriyākārakasvarūpasaṃbhave janakatvamavāryamiti prāgeva pratipādanāt / kāryasya hi niṣpāditatvāt punaḥ kartumaśakyatvameva kāraṇamasamarthamāvedayati / tadayamakṣaṇike kramākramikāryakāritvābhāvo na siddhaḥ / na ca kramākramābhyāmaparaprakārasaṃbhavo yena tābhyāmavyāptau sandigdhavyatireko hetuḥ syāt / prakārāntaraśaṅkāyāṃ tasyāpi dṛśyatvādṝśyatva prakāradvayadūṣaṇe 'pi svapakṣe 'pyanāśvāsaprasaṅgāt / tasmādanyonyavyavacchedasthitayornāparaḥ prakāraḥ saṃbhavati / svarūpāpraviṣṭasya vastuno 'vastuno vātatsvabhāvatvāt / prakārāntarasyāpi kramasvarūpāpraviṣṭatvāt / tathātīndriyasya sahakāriṇo 'dṛśyatve 'pyayogavyavacchedena dṛśyasahakārisahitasya dṛśyasyaiva sattvasya dṛśyakramākramābhyāṃ vyāptiḥ pratyakṣādeva sidhyati / evaṃ kramākramābhyāmarthakriyākāritvaṃ vyāptamiti kramākramayoranyonyavyavacchedena sthitatvādetatprakāradvayaparihāreṇārthakriyākāritvamanyatra na gatamityarthaḥ / ata evaitayorvinivṛttau nivartate //
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'Once the effect has been accomplished, the absence of activity directed toward that [effect] means the aggregate is incomplete, and an incomplete aggregate would not produce what has already been produced.' [Reply:] No, because it has already been demonstrated that when the entity's causal nature characterized by immediate activity is present — regardless of whether the aggregate obtains or not — its productive capacity cannot be blocked. For the very fact that, the effect having been accomplished, it cannot be produced again, itself reveals the cause as incapable. Thus, the absence of sequential or simultaneous causal efficacy in a non-momentary [entity] has not been established [by the opponent]. Nor is there any third mode besides the sequential and simultaneous, such that, were the pervasion to fail with respect to those two, the reason would have doubtful negative concomitance. If a third mode is suspected, that too [would fall under] the two modes of visible and invisible; and since in refuting both modes, the same doubt would arise even in one's own position — therefore, for [sequential and simultaneous], which stand in mutual exclusion, no third mode is possible. For anything not included in an entity's own nature — whether real or unreal — is not of that nature. And the third mode too would not be included in the nature of either sequential or simultaneous. Moreover, even if a super-sensory auxiliary condition is invisible, the pervasion of real existence — which is visible — by visible sequential and simultaneous [modes], when combined with visible auxiliary conditions, is established through perception alone, by the method of agreement-and-difference. Thus, causal efficacy is pervaded by [either] the sequential or the simultaneous; and since these two stand in mutual exclusion, when this twofold mode is eliminated, causal efficacy does not go elsewhere — that is the meaning. And precisely when both are eliminated, [causal efficacy] ceases.

body.text: trilocanasyāpi vikalpatraye prathamadūṣaṇamāśrayāsiddhidoṣaparihārato nirastam / dvitīyaṃ cāsaṅgatam, vikalpajñānena vyatirekasya pratītatvāt / na hyabhāvaḥ kaścidvigrahavān yaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ, api tu vikalpādeva vyavahartavyaḥ / na hyabhāvasya vikalpādanyā pratipattirapratipattirvā sarvathā / ubhayathāpi tadvyavahārahāniprasaṅgāt / evaṃ vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntasya hetuvyatirekasya ca vikalpādeva pratipattiḥ / tṛtīyamapi dūṣaṇamasaṅgatam / vyāpakānupalambhena nirdoṣeṇa sattvasya kṣaṇikatvena vyāpteravyāhatatvāt / tadayaṃ vyāpakānupalambho 'kṣaṇikasyāsattvam sattvasya tato vyatirekaṃ kṣaṇikatvena vyāptiṃ va sādhayatyekavyāpārātmakatvāditi sthitam //
body.translated_text: Even <s>Trilocana</s>'s three objections [are answered]: the first objection has been refuted through the resolution of the defect of unestablished locus. The second is also incoherent, since the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is apprehended through conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpajñāna</s>). For absence is not some embodied entity that must be directly perceived; rather, it is to be dealt with through conceptual construction alone. For there is no apprehension or non-apprehension of absence other than through conceptual construction in any way whatsoever; for in either case, the undesirable consequence of the loss of discourse about it [would follow]. Likewise, the apprehension of the dissimilar example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) and of the negative concomitance of the reason is through conceptual construction alone. The third objection is also incoherent, because the pervasion of existence by momentariness through the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> (non-perception of the pervader), which is faultless, remains uncontradicted. Thus, this <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> establishes the unreality of the non-momentary, the negative concomitance of existence therefrom, or the pervasion [of existence] by momentariness — all through a single operation. This is established.

body.text: nanu vyāpakānupalabdhiriti yadyanupalabdhimātraṃ tadā na tasya sādhyabuddhijanakatvamavastutvāt / na cānyopalabdhirvyāpakānupalabdhirabhidhātuṃ śakyā bhūtalādivadanyasya kasyacidanupalabdheriti cet / tadasaṅgatam / dharmyupalabdherevānyatrānupalabdhitayā vyavasthāpanāt / yathā hi neha śiṃśapā vṛkṣābhāvādityatra vṛkṣāpekṣayākevalapradeśasya dharmiṇa upalabdhirvṛkṣānupalabdhiḥ / śiṃśapāpekṣayā ca kevalapradeśasya dharmiṇa upalabdhireva rśiśapāyā abhāvopalabdhiriti svabhāvahetuparyavasāyivyāpāro (#Nibandh 92#) vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / tathā nityasya dharmiṇo vikalpabuddhyavasitasya kramikāritvākramikāritvāpekṣayā kevalagrahaṇādeva kramikāritvākramikāritvānupalambhaḥ / artha kriyāpekṣayā ca kevalapratītirevārthakriyāyogapratītiriti vyāpakānupalambhāntarādasya na kaścidviśeṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-perception of the pervader) is mere non-perception, then it cannot generate the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved), being insubstantial. Nor can the perception of something else be called <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>, since, like [the perception of] ground and the like, the non-perception is of something other [than what is perceived]. [Reply:] That is incoherent. For it is precisely the perception of the <s>dharmin</s> that is established as the non-perception of something else. Just as in 'There is no <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree here, because of the absence of trees' — here, with respect to trees, the perception of the bare location as <s>dharmin</s> is the non-perception of trees; and with respect to <s>śiṃśapā</s>, the very perception of the bare location as <s>dharmin</s> is the perception of the absence of <s>śiṃśapā</s> — thus the <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s> has an operation that culminates in a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (reason based on essential nature). (#Nibandh 92#) Likewise, with respect to sequential and simultaneous causal efficacy, the mere bare apprehension of the permanent <s>dharmin</s> as determined by conceptual cognition is itself the non-perception of sequential and simultaneous causal efficacy. And with respect to causal efficacy [in general], the mere bare apprehension is itself the apprehension of the impossibility of causal efficacy. Therefore, this [argument] has no difference from any other <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>.

body.text: adhyavasāyāpekṣayā va bāhye 'kṣaṇike vastuni vyāpakābhāvād vyāpyābhāvasiddhivyavahāraḥ / adhyavasāyaśca samanantarapratyayabalāyātākāraviśeṣayogādagṛhīte 'pi pravartanaśaktirboddhavyaḥ / īdṛśaścādhyavasāyo 'smaccitrādvaitasiddhau nirvāhitaḥ / sa cāvisaṃvādī vyavahāraḥ parihartumaśakyaḥ / yad vyāpakaśūnyaṃ tadvayāpyaśūnyamiti / etasyaivārthasyānenāpi krameṇa pratipādanāt / ayaṃ ca nyāyo yathā vastubhūte dharmiṇi tathāvastubhūte 'pīti ko viśeṣaḥ / tathā hyekajñānasaṃsargyatra vikalpya eva / yathā ca hariṇaśirasi tenaikajñānasaṃsargi śṛṅgamupalabdhaṃ śaśaśirasyapi tena sahaikajñānasaṃsargitvasaṃbhāvanayaiva śṛṅgaṃ niṣidhyate, tathā nīlādāvapariniṣṭhitanityānityabhāve kramākramau svadharmiṇā sārdhamekajñānasaṃsargiṇau dṛṣṭau, yadi nitye bhavataḥ, nityagrāhijñāne svadharmiṇā nityena sahaiva gṛhyeyātāmiti saṃbhāvanayā ekajñānasaṃsargadvārakameva pratiṣidhyate / kathaṃ punaretasminnityajñāne kramākramayorasphuraṇamiti yāvatā kramākramakroḍīkṛtameva nityaṃ vikalpayāma iti cet / ata eva bādhakāvatāro viparītāropa mantareṇa tasya vaiyarthyāt / kālāntare 'pyekarūpatayā nityatvam / kramākramau ca kṣaṇadvaye bhinnarūpatayā / tato nityatvasya kramākramikāryaśakteśca parasparaparihārasthiti lakṣaṇatayā durvāro virodha iti kathaṃ nitye kramākramayorantarbhāvaḥ anantarbhāvācca śuddhanityavikalpena dūrīkṛtakramākramasamāropeṇa kathamullekhaḥ / tataśca pratiyogini nitye 'pi vikalpyamāne ekajñāna saṃsargilakṣaṇaprāpte nityopalabdhireva nityaviruddhasyānupalabhyamānasya kramākramasyānupalabdhiḥ / tata eva cārthakriyāśakteranupalabdhiḥ / tasmād vyāpakavivekidharmyupalabdhitayā na vyāpakānupalambhāntarādasya viśeṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Or, with respect to the external non-momentary entity, through the determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) [that operates] upon it, the establishment and discourse of the absence of the pervaded follows from the absence of the pervader. And <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) should be understood as the power of engaging [with an object] even when [the object] is not [directly] apprehended, due to the specific form that has come about through the force of the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>). Such <s>adhyavasāya</s> has been explained in our <s>Citrādvaitasiddhi</s> (Establishment of Variegated Non-Duality). And that non-deceptive conventional practice cannot be denied: 'Whatever is devoid of the pervader is devoid of the pervaded.' For this very meaning is demonstrated through this procedure as well. And what difference is there in this reasoning, whether the <s>dharmin</s> is a real entity or an unreal entity? For certainly, co-occurrence in a single cognition applies only to what is conceptually constructed. And just as a horn, co-occurring in a single cognition with [the head of] a deer, is perceived on a deer's head — and on a hare's head, by the very possibility of its co-occurrence in a single cognition with [the hare's head], the horn is negated — so too, in blue and the like, where the permanent and impermanent nature is not finally determined, the sequential and simultaneous [modes], observed in a single cognition together with their <s>dharmin</s>: if they were to exist in the permanent, they should be apprehended in the very cognition that grasps the permanent, together with the permanent <s>dharmin</s> — and it is by the possibility of co-occurrence in a single cognition that [their absence] is negated. [Objection:] 'But how is the non-appearance of sequential and simultaneous [modes] in this cognition of the permanent [established], inasmuch as we conceptualize the permanent as encompassing the sequential and simultaneous?' [Reply:] Precisely for this reason does the invalidating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>) descend — for without a superimposition of the contrary, it would be purposeless. Permanence means having one and the same form even at different times. The sequential and simultaneous, however, involve different forms at [different] pairs of moments. Therefore, since permanence and the capacity for sequential-or-simultaneous causal efficacy stand in a relation of mutual exclusion, the contradiction is unavoidable — so how can the sequential and simultaneous be included in the permanent? And without such inclusion, how can there be manifestation through a pure conceptual construction of permanence, in which the superimposition of sequential and simultaneous has been removed? Thus, even when the permanent is conceptualized as the counter-positive, having attained the characteristic of co-occurrence in a single cognition, the very perception of the permanent is the non-perception of the sequential and simultaneous, which are contradictory to the permanent and are not being perceived. And from that very [non-perception follows] the non-perception of the capacity for causal efficacy. Therefore, as a perception of the <s>dharmin</s> that discriminates the pervader, this [argument] has no difference from any other <s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>.

body.text: na tvetadavastu dharmitvopayogivastva dhiṣṭhānatvāt pramāṇavyavasthāyā iti cet / kimidaṃ vastvadhiṣṭhānatvaṃ nāma / kiṃ paramparayāpi vastunaḥ sakāśādāgatatvam, atha vastuni kenacidākāreṇa vyavahārakāraṇatvam, vastubhūtadharmipratibaddhatvaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'But this [<s>dharmin</s>] is not a real entity, [so it cannot serve as] a locus for the <s>dharmin</s>-hood that is useful [for the proof], because the validity of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) is grounded in real entities.' [Reply:] What exactly is this 'being grounded in a real entity'? Is it [the <s>dharmin</s>] having come, even indirectly, from a real entity? Or is it being a cause of practical usage with respect to a real entity through some aspect? Or is it being dependent on a real <s>dharmin</s>?

body.text:
(#Nibandh 93#)
yadyādyaḥ pakṣastadā kramākramasyārthakriyāyāśca vyāptigrahaṇagocaravastupratibaddhatvamasyāpi na kṣīṇam / na dvitīye 'pi pakṣe doṣaḥ saṃbhavati, kṣaṇabhaṅgivastusādhanopāyatvādasya / na cāntimo 'pi vikalpaḥ kalpyate, tasyaiva nityavikalpasya vastuno dharmibhūtasya kramākramavadbāhyanityopādānaśūnyatvenārthakriyāvad bāhyanityopādānaśūnyatve prasādhanāt / paryudāsavṛttyā buddhisvabhāvabhūtākṣaṇikākāre vastubhūte dharmiṇi pratibaddhatvasaṃbhavāt //
body.translated_text: If the first alternative [holds], then the invariable connection of successive-and-simultaneous [efficacy] with causal efficacy — [i.e.,] this [reason's] being bound to a real object within the scope of the apprehension of pervasion — is also not undermined. Nor does a defect arise in the second alternative, because this [reason] serves as a means of establishing momentary reality. Nor is the last alternative to be imagined, because that very permanent conceptual object, which is the <s>dharmin</s> (subject), being devoid of an external permanent substrate just like [it is devoid of] successive-and-simultaneous [efficacy], the proof of its being devoid of an external permanent substrate — like [its lack of] causal efficacy — is established. [This is] because the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is possible with respect to the real <s>dharmin</s>, which is the non-permanent image of the nature of cognition, established through the exclusion-denoting (<s>paryudāsa</s>) usage.

body.text: ayameva nyāyo na vaktā bandhyāsutaścaitanyābhāvādityādau yojyaḥ / etena yathā vṛkṣābhāvādirantarbhāvayituṃ śakyate na tathāyamiti trilocano 'pi nirastaḥ //
body.translated_text: This same logic should be applied in [the argument] 'A barren woman's son is not a speaker, because of the absence of consciousness,' and so forth. By this, <s>Trilocana</s>'s [objection] too — that 'this [case] cannot be subsumed under [the category of] the absence of a tree and so forth' — is also refuted.

body.text: na ca kramādyabhāvastrayīṃ doṣajātiṃ nātikrāmati, abhāvadharmatve 'pi āśrayāsiddhidoṣaparihārāt / yattvanena pramāṇāntarānnityānāmasattvasiddhau kramādivirahasyābhāvadharmatā sidhyatītyuktam, tadvālasyāpi durabhidhānam / nityo hi dharmī / asattvaṃ sādhyam / kramikāryakāritvākramikāryakāritvaviraho hetuḥ / asya cābhāvadharmatvaṃ nāma asattvalakṣaṇasvasādhyāvinābhāvitvamucyate / tacca kramākrameṇa sattvasya vyāptisiddhau sattvasya vyāpyasyābhāvena kramākramasya vyāpakasya viraho vyāptaḥ sidhyatītyabhāvadharmatvaṃ prāgeva vidhyorvyāptisādhanāt pratyakṣādanumānādekasmādvā pramāṇāntarāt siddhamiti netaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor does the absence of succession and the rest fail to transcend the three categories of defects, because even when it is a property of an absence, the defect of unestablished substratum (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) is avoided. As for what [<s>Trilocana</s>] said — that 'the absence-property-nature of the absence of succession and the rest is established when the non-existence (<s>asattva</s>) of permanent things is established through another <s>pramāṇa</s>' — that is something even a child would have difficulty saying. For the <s>dharmin</s> is permanent; the <s>sādhya</s> is non-existence; the absence of successive-effect-producing and simultaneous-effect-producing is the reason. And its being an absence-property means: it is said to be inseparable from its own <s>sādhya</s>, characterized as non-existence. And that is established — once the pervasion of existence with succession-and-simultaneity is established, the absence of the pervader, succession-and-simultaneity, is pervaded by the absence of the pervaded, existence — thus, the absence-property-nature is established even prior to [the establishment of] the pervasion of the two positive [concomitances], from perception, or from inference, or from a single other <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therefore there is no defect of mutual dependence.

body.text: na ca sattāyāmivāsattāyāmapi tulyaḥ prasaṅgo bhinnanyāyatvāt / vastubhūtaṃ hi tatra sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca / tayordharmyapi vastveva yujyate / vastunastu pratyakṣānumānābhyāmeva siddhiḥ / tayorabhāve niyamenāśrayāsiddhiriti yuktam / asattāsādhane tvavastudharmo heturavastu vikalpamātrasiddhe dharmiṇi nāśrayāsiddhidoṣeṇa dūṣayituṃ śakyaḥ / tathā akṣaṇikasya kramayaugapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhaḥ sidhyatyeva / tathā vikalpādevākṣaṇiko virodhī siddhaḥ / vikalpollikhita ścāsya svabhāvo nāpara ityapi vyavahartavyam / anyathā tadanuvādena kramākramādirahitatvādiniṣedhādikamayuktam, tatsvarūpasyānullekhādanyasyollekhā dityakṣaṇikaśaśaviṣāṇādiśabdānuccāraṇaprasaṅgaḥ / asti ca / ato yathā pramāṇābhāve 'pi vikalpasiddhasya (#Nibandh 94#) bandhyāsutādeḥ saundaryādiniṣedho 'nurūpastathā vikalpopanītasyaivākṣaṇikarūpasya tata eva pratyanīkākāreṇa saha virodhavyavasthāyāṃ kīdṛśo doṣaḥ syāt / yadi cākṣaṇikānubhavābhāvād virodhapratiṣedhastarhi bandhyāputrādyanubhavābhāvādeva saundaryādiniṣedho 'pi mā bhūt //
body.translated_text: Nor is the same difficulty applicable to non-existence as it is to existence, because the logical principles are different. For there, the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> are real entities (<s>vastu</s>). For those, the <s>dharmin</s> too must properly be a real entity. And the establishment of a real entity is only through perception and inference. In their absence, it is proper that there is necessarily an unestablished substratum. But in proving non-existence, the reason is a property of a non-entity, and the <s>dharmin</s>, which is merely established through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), cannot be faulted with the defect of unestablished substratum. Thus, the contradiction of causal efficacy with the permanent through succession and simultaneity is indeed established. Likewise, the permanent as a contradictory [of the momentary] is established through conceptual construction alone. And it must be maintained that its nature as delineated by conceptual construction is [its nature], and no other. Otherwise, the negation of being devoid of succession-and-simultaneity and so forth through the restatement of that [permanent] would be unjustified, because its own nature is not delineated and something else is delineated — resulting in the undesirable consequence that words like 'non-momentary' and 'hare's horn' could never be uttered. But they are [uttered]. Therefore, just as the negation of beauty and so forth is appropriate for a barren woman's son that is established merely through conceptual construction even in the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, so too, when the non-momentary form, presented through conceptual construction alone, is established as contradictory with [its] opposing form from that very [conceptual construction], what defect could there be?
