And if the contradiction is denied because there is no experience of the non-momentary, then, because there is no experience of a barren woman's son either, the negation of beauty and so forth should also not hold.

body.text: nanvevaṃ virodhasyāpāramārthikatvam / taddvāreṇa kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhirapyapāramārthikī syāditi cet / na hi virodho nāma vastvantaraṃ kiñcidubhayakoṭidattapādasaṃbandhābhidhānamiṣyate asmābhirūpapadyate vā yenaikasaṃbandhino vastutvābhāve 'pāramārthikaṃ syāt / yathā tviṣyate tathā pāramārthika eva / viruddhābhimatayoranyo 'nyasvarūparihāramātraṃ virodhārthaḥ / sa ca bhāvābhāvayoḥ pāramārthika eva / na bhāvo 'bhāvarūpamāviśati, nāpyabhāvo bhāvarūpaṃ praviśatīti yo 'yamanayorasaṃkaraniyamaḥ sa eva pāramārthiko virodhaḥ / kālāntaraikarūpatayā hi nityatvam / kramākramau kṣaṇadvaye 'pi bhinnarūpatayā / tato nityatvakramākramikāryakāritvayorbhāvābhāvavad virodho 'styeva //
body.translated_text: Objection: In that case, the contradiction would be non-ultimate (<s>apāramārthika</s>); and through that, the proof of momentariness would also be non-ultimate. Reply: We neither hold nor does it follow that contradiction is some separate real entity with both its feet placed in a relationship with both extremes, such that when one relatum is not a real entity, [the contradiction] would be non-ultimate. As it is held [by us], it is entirely ultimate. The meaning of contradiction is nothing but the mutual exclusion of each other's nature among [the two things] held to be contradictory. And that, between existence and non-existence, is entirely ultimate. Existence does not enter the form of non-existence, nor does non-existence enter the form of existence — this principle of non-mixing between the two is itself the ultimate contradiction. For permanence consists in being of one form across different times; succession and simultaneity consist in being of different forms even across two moments. Therefore, the contradiction between permanence and successive-and-simultaneous-effect-production, like that between existence and non-existence, certainly holds.

body.text: nanu nityatvaṃ kramayaugapadyavattvaṃ ca viruddhau dharmau vidhūya nāparo virodho nāma, kasya bāstavatvamiti cet / na / na hi dharmāntarasya saṃbhavena virodhasya pāramārthikatvaṃ brūmaḥ / kiṃ tu viruddhayordharmayoḥ sadbhāve / anyathā virodhanāmadharmāntarasaṃbhave 'pi yadi na viruddhau dharmau kva pāramārthikavirodhasaṃbhavaḥ / viruddhauceddhamau tāvataiva tāttviko virodhavyavahāraḥ kimapareṇa pratijñāmātrasiddhena virodhanāmnā vastvantareṇa /
body.translated_text: Objection: Having removed permanence and the possession of succession-and-simultaneity as contradictory properties, there is no further contradiction — whose reality [is there]? Reply: No. We do not assert the ultimate reality of contradiction through the existence of some other property. Rather, [it consists] in the existence of the two contradictory properties themselves. Otherwise, even if the [additional] property called 'contradiction' were possible, if the two properties are not contradictory, where is the possibility of ultimate contradiction? And if the two properties are contradictory, then by that alone there is a genuine usage of 'contradiction' — what need is there for yet another real entity called 'contradiction,' established by mere assertion?

body.text: tadayaṃ pūrvapakṣasaṃkṣepaḥ
body.translated_text: This is the summary of the prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>):

children.translated_text: 'The permanent does not exist, or is not within the scope of cognition; hence there is unestablished substratum of the reason;

children.text: hetoḥ svānubhavasya ca kṣatirataḥ kṣiptaḥ sapakṣo 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: and one's own experience is undermined — therefore the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) too is dismissed;

children.text: śanyaśya dvitayena sidhyati na cāsattāpi sattā yathā
children.translated_text: of the empty [concept], nothing is established by either [method]; nor does non-existence [function like] existence;

children.text: no nityena virodhasiddhirasatā śakyā kramāderapi // iti //
children.translated_text: through non-existence, the establishment of contradiction is not possible with succession and the rest [either].' Thus.

body.text: atra siddhāntasaṃkṣepaḥ
body.translated_text: Here is the summary of the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.translated_text: 'With respect to some property of a non-entity, the [following] usage of prohibition and injunction, established by <s>pramāṇa</s>, through the mental [cognition] —
does this exist here or not?
If it exists somewhere, how do these objections not [fail to] apply?
And if it does not exist at all, then the refutation of one's own statement is established.'

body.text:
(#Nibandh 95#)
tadevaṃ nityaṃ na kramikāryakāritvākramikāryakāritvayogīti paramārthaḥ / tataśca sattāyuktamapi naiveti paramārthaḥ / tataśca kṣaṇikākṣaṇikaparihāreṇa rāśyantarābhāvādakṣaṇikānnivartamānamidaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇika eva viśrāmyattena vyāptaṃ sidhyatīti sattvāt kṣaṇikatvasiddhiravirodhinī //
body.translated_text: Thus, the ultimate meaning is: the permanent does not possess successive-effect-producing and simultaneous-effect-producing. And therefore, the ultimate meaning is: it does not even possess existence. And therefore, since there is no third category besides the momentary and non-momentary, this existence, which departs from the non-momentary, rests in the momentary alone, and is pervaded by it — thus, the establishment of momentariness from existence is non-contradictory.

children.translated_text: The nature of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), from the realization of which liberation is held [to follow] —
that very [nature], the churner of the <s>tīrthyas</s> (non-Buddhist opponents), momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>), has been established.

body.text: iti kṛtiriyaṃ ratnakīrteḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the work of <s>Ratnakīrti</s>.

(Nibandh 96)
// 6 //

body.text: // pramāṇāntarbhāvaprakaraṇam //
body.translated_text: <s>Pramāṇāntarbhāvaprakaraṇam</s> (Chapter on the Inclusion of [All] Means of Valid Knowledge).

children.translated_text: The refutation of the class of <s>pramāṇas</s> other than the two [i.e., perception and inference]
is not unprecedented; but here it is sealed by [a fresh] application.

body.text: iha khalu pramāṇamātre na kecid vipratipadyante / antataścārvākasyāpi saṃpratipatteḥ / pramāṇamātrocchedavādī ca tattadāṅśakya pratividhānādasmadgurubhiravajñātaḥ
body.translated_text: In this [matter], no one disputes the existence of <s>pramāṇa</s> as such — since even the <s>Cārvāka</s> (materialist) ultimately concedes [it]. And the proponent of the total destruction of all <s>pramāṇa</s> has been dismissed by our teachers through the remedy of [showing] the partial [acceptance in his own position]:

children.translated_text: 'If <s>pramāṇa</s> is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then the occasion for inquiry is destroyed;

children.text: bruvatā niyataṃ kiñcit sādhyaṃ vā bādhyameva vā //
children.translated_text: by saying [anything at all], one necessarily [admits] something to be proved or something to be refuted.'
'For one who speaks what is illogical, what kind of reputation is there in an assembly?
Without inference, how is the other's illogicality [shown]? What is established if it is disregarded?'
'If it is accepted by him, then [if you argue that] by his own view there is refutation —
if there is no refutation of it, [then] out of fear of it, how can there be refutation?'

children.text: sādhyaṃ na kiñciditi ced bādhāyā api sādhyatā /
children.translated_text: 'If nothing is to be proved, then [even] refutation too is something to be proved;

children.text: sāpi neti vaco vyarthaṃ praśnamātre 'pi kiṃ phalam //
children.translated_text: if that too is not [something to be proved], the words are futile — what fruit is there even in asking the question?'
'If the words have fruit somewhere, it is nothing other than causing understanding;
if words are capable of communicating, then perception, smoke, etc. are [even more] excellent [means].'
'If <s>pramāṇa</s> is accepted in the conventional [realm] (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), then this inquiry too is conventional;

children.text: saṃvṛtāvapi neṣṭaṃ ced vadan jetā yathā tathā //
children.translated_text: if it is not accepted even conventionally, then let the speaker be the victor however he pleases.'

children.text: saṃvṛtiśca vinā mānaṃ vāṅmātreṇa na sidhyati /
children.translated_text: 'And the conventional is not established by mere speech without <s>pramāṇa</s>;
if from <s>pramāṇa</s> [itself], the acceptance of <s>pramāṇa</s> is unavoidable.'

body.text: ācāryopyāha -
body.translated_text: The teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) too has said:

children.translated_text: 'If it is undesired — <s>pramāṇa</s> is indeed the basis of all desires;

children.text: bhāvābhāvavyavasthāṃ kaḥ kartuṃ tena vinā prabhuḥ //
children.translated_text: who is capable of establishing the determination of existence and non-existence without it?'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tadevaṃ pramāṇamātrāpratikṣepe pratyakṣaṃ tāvadādau gaṇanīyam, tanmūlatvādaparapramāṇopapatteḥ / na ca cārvāko 'pyanumānamanavasthāpya sthātuṃ prabhavati, vyāpāratrayakaraṇāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, given that <s>pramāṇa</s> as such is not rejected, <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) should first be counted, because the justification of other <s>pramāṇas</s> depends on it as their foundation. And even the <s>Cārvāka</s> is unable to take his stand without accepting inference, because he performs the three operations [of the inferential process].

body.text:
(#Nibandh 97#)
tacchāstre hi pratyakṣetarasāmānyayoḥ pramāṇetaravidhānaṃ lakṣaṇapraṇayanato vidhātavyam / tacca lakṣaṇaṃ pratyakṣe dharmiṇi lakṣye prāmāṇye pratyetavye svabhāvo hetuḥ / parabuddhipratipattau ca kāyādivyāpāraḥ kāryahetuḥ / paralokapratiṣedhe ca dṛśyānupalambho 'ṅgīkartavya iti kathamanumānāpalāpaḥ / yadācāryaḥ
body.translated_text: For in that system, the determination of '<s>pramāṇa</s>-or-other' regarding the general [categories of] perception and non-perception must be made by formulating a definition. And that definition — when the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) is perception and the <s>lakṣya</s> (definiendum) is to be understood as valid — the natural nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is the reason. And for communicating [one's] understanding to another, bodily and other activity is the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>). And for denying the next world, the non-perception of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>) must be accepted — so how can inference be denied? As the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) [says]:

children.translated_text: 'From the existence of the general [categories of] <s>pramāṇa</s>-and-other, [and] from the occurrence of a different cognition;
and from the denial of the existence of any other <s>pramāṇa</s> —'

body.text: api ca
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: 'When the object is impossible [to perceive], from its absence, even perception has the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s>;
for [a cognition] whose nature is invariably connected [with its object], with respect to its being a cause of that [knowledge], both [perception and inference] are equal.'

body.text: ityanumānamapi pramāṇam / prāmāṇyaṃ ca pramāṇāntarāgṛhītaniścitapravṛttiviṣayārthatayā tatprāpaṇe śaktiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus inference too is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) consists in the capacity to bring about an object that is a definite object of activity, not grasped by another <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text: nanvastu prāpaṇe śaktiḥ prāmāṇyam, paramasaunārthādutpatteḥ, api tvarthadarśanādi(ti) cet / kimidamarthadarśanam / arthasya dharmo dṛśyatvam / jñānasya dharmo draṣṭṛtvam / prathamapakṣe nīlatvavad dṛśyatvasyāpi sādhāraṇatvādekagocaro 'rthaḥ sarvagocaraḥ syāt / na hi pratipuruṣamarthānāṃ bhedo nairātmyaprasaṅgāt / dvitīyapakṣe tu kathamanyasmin jñānasvabhāve draṣṭṛtve satyanyasyāsamba(ddha)syārthasya pratyāśā syāt / draṣṭṛtvaṃ dṛśyatvamantareṇānupapadyamānaṃ tadākṣipatīti cet / nanu jñānārthayorutpattisārūpyabalato draṣṭṛdṛśyatvavyavasthā(pa)nametat / anabhyupagame draṣṭṛtvaṃ dṛśyatvaṃ ca na saṃbhavatīti kiṃ kenākṣipyatām / bhavatu vā prakārāntareṇāpi draṣṭṛdṛśyabhāvastathāpi bhede satyavyabhicārastadutpattireva prāptinimittam / sā ca prāpaṇaśaktiḥ pratyakṣānumānayoraviśiṣṭeti pramāṇe eva /
body.translated_text: Objection: Let validity be the capacity to bring about the object — since [cognition] arises from a supreme, beneficial object — or rather, 'seeing the object' and so forth. Reply: What is this 'seeing the object'? If it is a property of the object — visibility (<s>dṛśyatva</s>) — or if it is a property of cognition — being a seer (<s>draṣṭṛtva</s>)? In the first case, since visibility too, like blueness, would be common [to all objects], an object grasped in one domain would be [grasped] in all domains. For there is no difference among objects for each person, because [otherwise] there would be the undesirable consequence of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>). In the second case, how, when the seer-nature belongs to one cognitive nature, could there be expectation of an unrelated object? If [objected:] 'Seer-hood, being impossible without visibility, entails it' — well, the establishment of the seer-and-visible relation is [precisely] from the arising-similarity (<s>utpattisārūpya</s>) between cognition and object. Without accepting that, neither seer-hood nor visibility is possible — so what entails what? Or even if the seer-visible relation exists through some other means, given that they are different, there is deviation [from the invariable connection]; their very arising is the cause of attainment. And that capacity for attainment is not different for perception and inference — hence both are indeed <s>pramāṇas</s>.

body.text: nanvanyadapi śābdopamānādikaṃ pramāṇamasti / tathā hi śabdāccodanārūpādasannikṛṣṭe 'rthe svargādau yajjñānamutpadyate tadapi śābdaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇameva / pratyayitoditavākyaprasūtaṃ ca jñānaṃ pramāṇam / yadāha kumārilaḥ
body.translated_text: Objection: There is yet another <s>pramāṇa</s>, namely verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), and so forth. For the cognition that arises from a verbal statement of the nature of an injunction (<s>codanā</s>) regarding a non-proximate object such as heaven — that too, being verbal cognition, is indeed a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And the cognition born from the statement of a trustworthy person is also a <s>pramāṇa</s>. As <s>Kumārila</s> says:

body.text: taccākartṛkato vākyādanyādvā pratyayito (?) ditāt / iti /
body.translated_text: 'And that [cognition arises] either from an authorless statement, or from [the statement of] someone known to be trustworthy.' Thus.

body.text: tatra yadā śabdasamutthaṃ jñānaṃ pramāṇaṃ tadopādānādibuddhiḥ phalam / yadā tu śabdastadā tadālambanaṃ jñānaṃ phalamiti / naiyāyikasya punaḥ
body.translated_text: In that [system], when the cognition arising from words is the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the cognition of the referent and so forth is the result (<s>phala</s>). But when the word [itself is the pramāṇa], the cognition that takes it as its object is the result. For the <s>Naiyāyika</s>, however:

body.text: āptopadeśaḥ śabdaḥ
body.translated_text: 'The instruction of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>)' —

body.text: iti śabdapramāṇalakṣaṇasūtram / tatra śabda iti lakṣyapadam / āptopadeśa iti lakṣaṇapadam / asyāyaṃ saṃkṣepārthaḥ / āptopadiṣṭaḥ śabdaḥ pramāṇamiti / āptaśca (#Nibandh 98#) sākṣātkṛtaheyopādeyatattvo yathādṛṣṭasya cārthasyācikhyāsayā prayukta upadeṣṭā abhidhīyate / pramāṇaphalavyavasthā ca pūrvavad draṣṭavyeti /
body.translated_text: this is the <s>sūtra</s> defining the verbal-testimony <s>pramāṇa</s>. Therein, '<s>śabda</s>' is the term for the <s>lakṣya</s> (definiendum); 'instruction of a trustworthy person' is the defining term. The summary meaning is: the word instructed by a trustworthy person is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is defined as a teacher who has directly realized the reality of what is to be abandoned and adopted, and who is motivated by the desire to communicate the object as [he has] seen [it]. The determination of <s>pramāṇa</s> and result should be understood as before.

body.text: tathā mīmāṃsakānāmupamānaṃ pramāṇam / yaduktaṃ śabarasvāminā upamānamapi sādṛśyamasannikṛṣṭe 'rthe buddhimutpādayati / yathā gavayadarśanaṃ goḥ smaraṇasyeti /
body.translated_text: Similarly, for the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. As <s>Śabarasvāmin</s> has said: 'Analogy too — [that is,] similarity — produces cognition regarding a non-proximate object. For example, the perception of a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) [produces] the recollection of a cow.'

body.text: asyāyamarthaḥ / ekatra dṛśyamānaṃ sādṛśyaṃ kartṛ / pratiyogyantare dṛśyamānapratiyogisādṛśyaviśiṣṭatayaitatsādṛśyaviśiṣṭo 'sau ityasannikṛṣṭe 'rthe yāṃ buddhimutpādayati tadupamānaṃ pramāṇamiti / yattadoradhyāhāra iti / tasmāt smaratīti smaraṇaṃ puruṣaḥ / tenāyamarthaḥ - yathā gavaye dṛśyamānaṃ sādṛśyaṃ gāṃ smarato manuṣyasya etatsādṛśyaviśiṣṭo 'sau gauriti buddhimutpādayatīti /
body.translated_text: The meaning of this is: Similarity, perceived in one entity, is the productive factor. <s>Upamāna</s> (comparison) is the <s>pramāṇa</s> that, through the entity being qualified by the similarity perceived in the counterpart, produces the cognition 'That is similar to this' regarding an object not [currently] in contact [with the senses]. The word 'remembers' [in the definition] implies the person. Thus the meaning is: just as the similarity perceived in a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox), for a person remembering the cow, produces the cognition 'That is qualified by this similarity—that is a cow.'

body.text: na cedamupamānaṃ smaraṇaṃ kartavyam, gavayasādṛśyaviśiṣṭasya gorgoviśiṣṭasya ca sādṛśyasya prameyatvāt / gosādṛśyayorviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasyopamānapramāṇaviṣayasya gogrāhiṇā gavayagrāhiṇā vā pratyakṣeṇa kenacidagrahaṇāt / yadāha bhaṭṭaḥ
body.translated_text: But this <s>upamāna</s> should not be made [into a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> based on mere] recollection, since the similarity qualifying the <s>gavaya</s> and the similarity qualifying the cow are both objects of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>). For the qualifier-qualified relationship between the cow and its similarity, which is the domain of the <s>upamāna pramāṇa</s>, is not apprehended by any perception—neither by the perception that grasps the cow nor by that which grasps the <s>gavaya</s>. As <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [<s>Kumārila</s>] says:

children.text: pratyakṣe 'pi yathā deśe smaryamāṇe ca pāvake /
children.translated_text: Just as, when the place is perceived and the fire remembered,
the validity of inference lies in the establishment of the qualified [fire-in-that-place] from another [source];

children.text: pratyakṣeṇāvabuddhe ca sādṛśye gavi ca smṛte /
children.translated_text: so too, when the similarity is apprehended by perception and the cow is remembered,
the validity of <s>upamāna</s> lies in the establishment of the qualified [cow-with-that-similarity] from another [source].

body.text: na ca grahaṇamantareṇa smaraṇamasti / tasmānnopamānaṃ smaraṇamataḥ pramāṇamiti / naiyāyikādīnāṃ tūpamānasūtram,
body.translated_text: And there is no recollection without prior apprehension. Therefore <s>upamāna</s> is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> based on mere recollection. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s>' <s>sūtra</s> on <s>upamāna</s>, however, is:

body.text: prasiddhasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanamupamānam iti /
body.translated_text: '<s>Upamāna</s> is the means of establishing the <s>sādhya</s> (thing to be proved) from the well-known similarity.'

body.text: asyāyamarthaḥ / prasiddhaṃ sādharmyaṃ yasya tasmād gavayādeḥ sādhyasya saṃjñāsaṃjñisambandhasya sādhanaṃ siddhistadupamānaphalam / samākhyāsambandhapratipattiheturupamānamityarthaḥ / ayamasya prapañcaḥ / yaḥ pratipattā gāṃ jānāti na gavayam, ādiṣṭaśca svāminā gacchāraṇyam gavayamānayāsmāditi, gavayaśabdavācyamarthama jānāno vanecaramanyaṃ vā tajjñaṃ pṛṣṭavān, bhrātaḥ kīdṛśo gavaya iti / tena cādiṣṭaṃ yathā gaustathā gavaya iti / tasya śrutātideśavākyasya kasyāñcidaraṇyānyāmupagatasyātideśavākyārthasmaraṇasahakāri yad gavayasārūpyajñānaṃ tatprathamata evāsau gavayaśabdavācyo 'rtha iti pratipattiṃ prastuvānamupamānaṃ pramāṇamiti /
body.translated_text: The meaning of this is: From a <s>gavaya</s> etc. that possesses well-known similarity, the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s>—namely the relation between name and named (<s>saṃjñā-saṃjñi-sambandha</s>)—is the result of <s>upamāna</s>. The meaning is: <s>upamāna</s> is the cause of apprehending the relation of designation. Here is the elaboration: A person who knows the cow but not the <s>gavaya</s>, instructed by his master 'Go to the forest and bring a <s>gavaya</s>'—not knowing the object denoted by the word '<s>gavaya</s>'—asks a forest-dweller or someone else who knows: 'Brother, what does a <s>gavaya</s> look like?' He is told: 'A <s>gavaya</s> is like a cow.' When that person, having heard the statement of transfer, arrives at some forest, the cognition of resemblance to a <s>gavaya</s>, cooperating with the recollection of the meaning of the transfer-statement, is the <s>upamāna pramāṇa</s> that initiates the apprehension: 'This is the object denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>.'

body.text:
(#Nibandh 99#)
tathārthāpattisaṃjñaṃ pramāṇaṃ mīmāṃsakasya / arthāpattirapi dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vārtho 'nyathā nopadyamāno yadarthāntaraṃ parikalpayati / sārthāpattiḥ / yathā jīvati devadatte gṛhābhāvadarśanena bahirbhāvasyārthasya parikalpanā / asyāyamarthaḥ / pratyakṣādibhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pramāṇaiḥ prasiddhoḥ yo 'rthaḥ sa yena vinā na yujyate tasyārthasya kalpanamarthāpattiriti / sā ca ṣaṭpramāṇapūrvikā ṣaṭprakāraiveti //
body.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇa</s> called <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) belongs to the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>. <s>Arthāpatti</s> is when an object that is seen or heard, being otherwise inexplicable, posits another fact. That is <s>arthāpatti</s>. For example: when <s>Devadatta</s> is alive, the observation of his absence from the house leads to the positing of his being outside. The meaning is: the postulation of an object without which a thing established by the six <s>pramāṇas</s> such as perception etc. would be unjustified—that is <s>arthāpatti</s>. And since it is preceded by six <s>pramāṇas</s>, it is of six kinds.

body.text: pratyakṣānumānādipramāṇapañcakābhāvasvabhāvamabhāvākhyaṃ pramāṇam / prameyaṃ ghaṭādyabhāvaḥ / nāstīha ghaṭādīti jñānaṃ ghaṭādyabhāvālambanaṃ phalam / yadāha kumārilaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇa</s> called <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence) has as its nature the absence of the five <s>pramāṇas</s> such as perception and inference. Its object of knowledge is the non-existence of a pot etc. The result is the cognition 'There is no pot etc. here,' which has as its object the absence of pot etc. As <s>Kumārila</s> says:

children.translated_text: The non-arising of perception etc. is called the <s>pramāṇa</s> of absence;
that [non-arising] is either the non-transformation of oneself, or cognition directed at another object.
Where the five <s>pramāṇas</s> do not arise with respect to the nature of an object,
there, for the purpose of comprehending the existence of the object [i.e., its non-existence], the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of absence obtains.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: etāni ṣaṭ pramāṇāni pratyakṣādīnyasaṃkīrṇasvasvalakṣaṇayogitvādanyonyāpraviṣṭasvabhāvāni pratyetavyānīti //
body.translated_text: These six <s>pramāṇas</s>—perception and the rest—should be understood as having mutually non-overlapping natures, since each possesses its own unmixed defining characteristic.

body.text: atrocyate / codanāyāstāvad vāhye 'rthe pratibandhābhāvānna prāmāṇyam / prayogaḥ - yasya yatra pratibandho nāsti na tasya tatra prāmāṇyam / yathā dahane 'pratibaddhasya rāsabhasya / apratibaddhāśca bahirarthe vaidikāḥ śabdāḥ iti vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ / na tāvadayamasiddho hetuḥ / śabdānāṃ vastutaḥ pratibandhābhāvāt / pratibaddhasvabhāvatā hi pratibandhaḥ / na ca sā nirnibandhanā, sarveṣāṃ sarvatra pratibaddhasvabhāvatāprasaṅgāt / nibandhanaṃ cāsyāstādātmyatadutpattibhyāmanyannopalabhyate, atatsvabhāvasyātadutpatteśca tatrāpratibaddhasvabhāvatvāt / na hi śabdānāṃ vahirarthasvabhāvatāsti bhinnapratibhāsāvabodhaviṣayatvāt / nāpi śabdā bahirarthādupajāyante, arthamantareṇāpi puruṣasyecchāpratibaddhavṛtteḥ śabdasyotpādadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: First, Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) has no validity regarding external objects, because of the absence of a connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) with external objects. The formal argument: that which has no connection with something has no validity regarding it—like a donkey with respect to burning, which has no connection [with fire]. And Vedic words are unconnected with external objects—this is a case of non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). This reason is not unestablished, because words in reality lack a connection [with objects]. For a connection is the state of having a connected nature. And that is not without a basis, since otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that everything would have a connected nature with everything else. And no basis for this [connection] is observed other than identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) or causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>), since what is not of that nature and not produced from it has no connected nature with it. Words do not have the nature of external objects, since they are apprehended as distinct appearances. Nor are words produced from external objects, since the production of words is seen to depend on a person's will, even without an [external] object.

body.text: nanu yogyatayaiva kiñcat pratibaddhasvabhāvamupalabhyate / yathā cakṣurindriyaṃ rūpe / cakṣuḥ khalu vyāpāryamāṇam rūpamevopalabhbhayati / tathaivaite vaidikāḥ śabdāstādātmyatadutpattiviyuktā api yogyatāmātreṇātīndriyamarthaṃ bodhayiṣyanti tatkathaṃ tādātmyatadutpattivirahamātreṇāpratibandho yenaivaṃ vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ sidhyatīti / naiṣa doṣaḥ / yataścakṣurindriyamapi rasādiparihāreṇa rūpa eva prakāśakatvena pratiniyataṃ tatkāryatvāt / rūpaṃ hi cakṣurupakaroti / na sattāmātreṇa cakṣū rūpaṃ prakāśayati, vyavahitasyāpi rūpopalabdhiprasaṅgāt / tasmād rūpād yogyadeśasannihitāt tajjñānajananayogyatāmāsādya cakṣū rūpajñānamutpādayattatkāryamiti vyaktamavasīyate / anyathā tadupakārānapekṣasya tasyāpi tatprakāśananiyamo nopapadyate / (#Nibandh 100#) na hyanupakāryatvāviśeṣe cakṣū rūpasyaiva prakāśakam, na rasāderiti ghaṭāmupaiti niyamaḥ / ayameva tarhi niyamaḥ kuto yad rūpeṇaiva cakṣurūpakartavyam, na rasādineti / yadi vastuvaśādeva rūpamupakaroti na rasādikam, hanta tarhi yathopakāryatvaṃ prati niyamaścakṣuṣo rūpeṇa, tathā śabdānāmapi svābhāvika evāstu bahirarthapratyāyananiyama iti /
body.translated_text: Objection: 'Something is observed to have a connected nature through mere capacity (<s>yogyatā</s>) alone—for example, the eye-faculty with respect to form. The eye, when operating, apprehends form alone. Likewise, these Vedic words, even though separated from identity and causal origination, will, through mere capacity, reveal supersensory objects. So how, merely from the absence of identity and causal origination, is the absence of connection established, such that the non-apprehension of the pervader succeeds?'—This is no fault. For the eye-faculty too, to the exclusion of taste etc., is determined to be revelatory of form alone because it is an effect of form. Form assists the eye. The eye does not reveal form merely through its existence, since then it would absurdly apprehend even obstructed form. Therefore, having attained from form situated in a suitable location the capacity to generate the cognition of it, the eye produces cognition of form—[and] it is clearly ascertained that this is its effect. Otherwise, for [an eye] that does not depend on assistance from it, the restriction to revealing form alone would be inexplicable. For, given no difference in non-assistance, the restriction that the eye reveals form alone and not taste etc. does not hold. 'Then whence this very restriction that the eye is to be assisted by form alone and not by taste etc.?' If [you say] it assists form by the very nature of things and not taste etc.—well then, just as the restriction of the eye's being-assisted is with respect to form, so too let there be an intrinsic (<s>svābhāvika</s>) restriction of words to revealing external objects.

body.text: atrocyate / na cakṣuṣaḥ svābhāviko rūpopakāryatāniyamaḥ, kasyacid vastunaḥ svābhāvikatvānupapatteḥ / tathā hi svābhāvikatvaṃ vastudharmasyānujānānaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ - kiṃ svābhāvika iti svato bhavati, āhosvit parataḥ, athāhetutaḥ / yadi svato bhavati, tadasaṅgatam, svātmani kriyāvirodhāt / athāhetutaḥ tadayuktam, ahetordeśādiniyamāyogāt / tasmānna svābhāviko rūpopakāryatāpratiniyamaścakṣuṣaḥ / kiṃnibandhanastarhi svahetupratibaddha iti, brūmaḥ - cakṣūḥ khalu svahetunā janyamānaṃ tādṛśameva janitam yadrūpopakartavyameva bhavati / rūpamapi tādṛśameva svahetunā janitaṃ yattadupakārakasvabhāvam /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: The eye does not have an intrinsic restriction of being-assisted by form, because the intrinsic nature of any entity is untenable. For one who grants that intrinsic nature is a property of an entity must be asked: Does 'intrinsic' mean it arises from itself, or from another, or without a cause? If from itself—that is incoherent, because of the contradiction of an action upon oneself. If without a cause—that is unreasonable, because without a cause there can be no restriction to a particular location etc. Therefore the restriction of the eye's being-assisted by form is not intrinsic. 'What then is its basis?'—it is dependent on its own cause, we say. The eye, being produced by its own cause, is produced as such that it is to be assisted by form alone. Form too is produced by its own cause as such that it has the nature of assisting the eye.

body.text: śabdānāmapi sa svabhāvaḥ svahetupratibaddho yenaite bāhyārthāvyabhicāriṇa iti cet / na śakyamevamabhidhātum, nityatvābhyupagamādvedavākyānām / athānityatvamabhyupagamyāyamākṣepaḥ parihartumiṣyate, tadapi duṣkaram, doṣāntaraprasaṅgāt / yadi svahetunaiva te niyamārthopadarśanaśaktimanto janitāḥ, tadāvyutpannasamayasyāpi svārthamavavodhayeyuḥ / yathā cakṣuḥ svaheto rūpaprakāśakamutpannaṃ sat prakāśayatyeva rūpamasaṅketavido 'pi, na ca śabdāduccaritāt prāgapratītasamayasyāpi viśeṣāvagamaḥ samasti / tasmānna svahetupratibaddhaścakṣurāderiva śabdānāmarthapratipādananiyama iti niścayaḥ //
body.translated_text: If [it is said]: 'Words too have that nature, dependent on their own causes, by which they are non-deviating with respect to external objects'—it cannot be stated thus, because of the accepted eternality of Vedic sentences. If [you say] 'This objection is to be answered by accepting the non-eternality [of Vedic words]'—that too is difficult, because of the consequence of another fault. If they were produced by their own causes alone with the power to reveal their fixed objects, then they would convey their meaning even to one who has not learned the convention. Just as the eye, produced from its cause as revelatory of form, reveals form even to one who does not know any convention—but from a word, before it is uttered, no comprehension of a specific meaning arises even in one who has not learned the convention. Therefore the determination is: words do not have a restriction of conveying meaning that is dependent on their own causes, like the eye etc.

body.text: atha svahetubhirevāyamīdṛśasteṣāṃ svabhāvo datto yena te saṃketaviśeṣasahāyā eva kamapyarthamavabodhayanti / na tarhi saṅketaparāvṛttau padārthāntaravṛttayo bhaveyuḥ / yadi hyayamagnihotraśabdaḥ saṃketāpekṣo yāgaviśeṣapratipādakaḥ, kathaṃ saṅketānyatvenārthāntaraṃ pratipādayati / na hi kṣityādyapekṣeṇa bījena svahetoraṅkurajananasvabhāvenotpannena rāsabhaḥ śakyo janayitum, tathā śabdo 'pi yadarthapratipādananiyatastameva prakāśayet //
body.translated_text: If [it is said]: 'Their own causes have given them precisely this nature, whereby they convey some object only with the assistance of a particular convention'—then upon the change of convention, they should not operate with respect to another object. For if this word '<s>agnihotra</s>' is a designator of a particular sacrifice depending on a convention, how could it designate another object through a different convention? Just as a seed, produced from its own cause with the nature of generating a sprout depending on earth etc., cannot be made to produce a donkey—so too a word, if fixed in designating a particular object, should reveal that alone.

body.text: atha tattatsaṅketāpekṣastattadarthapratyāyanayogya evāyaṃ jāta ityucyate / tadapi na prastutopayogi / na hyevamasya prāmāṇyamavatiṣṭhate / yadā hi saṅketenāpuruṣārtha pratipādanamapi saṃbhāvyata eva, tadā na śakyamupakalpayituṃ kimayamabhimatasyaivārthasya dyotako na veti / tarhi vācyavācakalakṣaṇaḥ śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandho bhaviṣyati / tathā cāha
body.translated_text: If it is said: 'This [word] was produced as capable of conveying this or that object depending on this or that convention'—that too is of no use to the present topic. For its validity does not stand thus. For when it is conceivable that through convention it could designate even what is not a human purpose, it cannot be determined whether it reveals the intended object or not. 'Then the relation between words and meanings will be of the nature of signifier and signified (<s>vācya-vācaka</s>).' And so he says:

children.translated_text: Even if the signifier-signified relations between words and meanings are real,
unless manifested by conventions, they are not causes of the apprehension of meaning.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 101#)
iti cet / nanu tasya vāstavatve 'saṅketavido 'pyarthapratipattirbhavedityuktam, saṅketāpekṣāyāṃ cārthāntare na pravartetetyādyabhihitam / ataḥ pūrvamevāyaṃ pratyākhyāto vācyavācakalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ / tasmānna bahirarthe pratibandhaḥ śabdānāmiti nirṇayaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'But if that [relation] is real, even one who does not know the convention would apprehend the meaning'—this was already stated. And 'if it depends on convention, it would not operate with respect to other objects'—this too was already stated. Therefore this signifier-signified relation has already been refuted above. Hence the determination is: words have no connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) with external objects.

body.text: tataśca nāsiddho hetuḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore the reason [in our inference] is not unestablished.

body.text: nāpi viruddhaḥ, viparyayavyāptyabhāvāt / tadabhāvaśca sapakṣe vṛttyupadarśanāt / na hi viruddhasya sādharmyavati dharmiṇi sadbhāvo yuktaḥ, sādhyaviparyayasya tatrābhāvāt / na ca vyāpakamantareṇa vyāpyasya saṃbhavaḥ, tatpracyutiprasaṅgāt //
body.translated_text: Nor is it contradicted (<s>viruddha</s>), because of the absence of pervasion by the opposite. And that absence [of opposite pervasion is shown] by demonstrating [the reason's] occurrence in the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>). For it is not proper for a contradicted [reason] to be present in a subject that accords with the <s>sādhya</s>, since the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> is absent there. And without the pervader, the pervaded cannot exist, as that would entail its loss of that [pervaded] status.

body.text: nāpyanaikāntiko hetuḥ, viparyaye bādhakapramāṇasaṃbhavāt / prāmāṇyapratiṣedhe hi sādhye pramāṇyameva vipakṣaḥ / na ca tasmin pratibandhābhāvalakṣaṇo heturasti, svaviruddhena pratibandhena vyāptatvāt / na khalvayaṃ prādeśikaḥ pramāṇaśabdo jñāneṣu nirnibandhana eva, sarvajñāneṣu prāmāṇyavyapadeśaprasaṅgāt / nibandhanaṃ ca svaviṣayapratibandhādanyannopapadyate / tasmāt pramāṇasya pramāṇavyapadeśaviṣayatvaṃ svaviṣayapratibandhane vyāptam / ataḥ pramāṇe dharmiṇi vipakṣe prāmāṇyasya viruddhavyāptasyopalambhena vipakṣe vyavacchedasiddhernānaikāntiko hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is the reason inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because of the possibility of a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> in the case of the opposite. For when the negation of validity is the <s>sādhya</s>, validity itself is the counter-example (<s>vipakṣa</s>). And the reason characterized as absence-of-connection does not exist there [in the counter-example], because it is pervaded by a connection that is its opposite. For this term '<s>pramāṇa</s>' is not applied to cognitions arbitrarily without basis, since otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of the designation '<s>pramāṇa</s>' applying to all cognitions. And no basis for it is tenable other than connection with one's own object. Therefore, the fact of being designated '<s>pramāṇa</s>' is pervaded by connection with one's own object. Hence, since in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (validity), the [reason's] contradictory [i.e., the presence of connection] is apprehended, the exclusion from the <s>vipakṣa</s> is established, and the reason is not inconclusive.

body.text: na cānyo doṣaḥ saṃbhavī / tasmānnirastāśeṣadoṣeṇa hetunā yat prasiddhaṃ tadupādeyameva satām (iti) paṇḍitaśrījitāripādaireva vedāprāmāṇye darśitam /
body.translated_text: Nor is any other fault possible. Therefore, what is established by a reason from which all faults have been removed is to be accepted by the wise—this has been demonstrated by the venerable Paṇḍita <s>Jitāri</s> himself regarding the invalidity of the <s>Vedas</s>.

body.text: evaṃ ca vaidikaśabdānāṃ pramāṇye niraste tadutthaṃ jñānamapyapramāṇameva / āptapraṇītasya punarvacanasyārthāvyabhicāre tajjanmano jñānasyāvyabhicārasaṃbhave 'pi na prāmāṇyamupagantuṃ śakyate, paracittavṛttīnāmaśakyaniścayatvenāptatvāparijñānāt vacanasyāpi tatpraṇītatvāpratipatteḥ / prayogaścātra -
body.translated_text: And thus, when the validity of Vedic words is refuted, the knowledge arising from them is also not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Even for the words of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>), though there may be the possibility of non-deviation of the knowledge born from them when [the words] are non-deviating with respect to their objects, validity cannot be attained, because the mental states of other persons cannot be ascertained with certainty, and hence the trustworthiness [of the speaker] cannot be known, and consequently the authorship of the statement by such a trustworthy person cannot be established. And the formal argument here is—

body.text: yad yena rūpeṇa na niścitaṃ na tat tena rūpeṇa vyavahriyate / yathā rathyāpuruṣaḥ sarvajñatvena / na pratīyate cābhimatapuruṣa āptatveneti vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ //
body.translated_text: That which is not ascertained in a particular form is not used in that form — like a man on the street [is not used] as omniscient. And the person claimed [as trustworthy] is not perceived as being trustworthy (<s>āpta</s>) — [this is] a <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-perception of the pervader).

body.text: nāyamasiddhaḥ, āptābhimatasya tathātvāniścayāt / tathā hi paracittavṛttayo 'tīndriyatvānna pratyakṣasamadhigamyā iti kāyavāgvyavahārato 'numātavyāḥ / tau ca kāyavāgvyavahārau buddhipūrvamanyathāpi kartuṃ śakyete / tatastatpratibaddhatvenāniścayāt kathaṃ kāyavāgvyavahārato viśiṣṭaparacittavṛttyanumānam //
body.translated_text: This [reason] is not unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), because the trustworthiness of the person claimed as <s>āpta</s> is not ascertained. For the mental states of others, being beyond the senses (<s>atīndriya</s>), cannot be directly perceived, and must be inferred from bodily and verbal behavior. But both bodily and verbal behavior can also be deliberately performed otherwise. Therefore, since there is no certainty [that behavior] is invariably connected with [trustworthiness], how can one infer special mental states of others from bodily and verbal behavior?

body.text: nāpi viruddhaḥ, sapakṣe sadbhāvasaṃbhavāt //
body.translated_text: Nor is [this reason] contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), because of the possibility of its presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (positive instance).

body.text: nāpyanaikāntikaḥ, prāmāṇikatadrūpavyavahartavyatvaniścitatvayorvyāpyavyāpakabhūtayorvidhibhūtayorvṛkṣatvaśiṃśapātvayoriva pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ sarvopasaṃhāreṇa (#Nibandh 102#) vyāpteḥ siddhatvāt / tadataḥ sādhanād doṣatrayarahitāt sādhyaṃ siddhyadavācyameva / tadevamāptatvasya durbodhatvena tatpraṇītatvāniścayādekaprahāranihatamāptavacasaḥ prāmāṇyam /
body.translated_text: Nor is it inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) is established with universal application through perception and non-perception, for the two [properties] — being authoritative (<s>prāmāṇika</s>) and being to-be-used-in-that-form, which are ascertained — are related as pervader and pervaded, both being positive [properties], like tree-ness and <s>śiṃśapā</s>-ness. (Nibandha 102) Therefore, from this proof which is free from the three defects, the <s>sādhya</s> (thesis) is indeed established — this is beyond dispute. Thus, since trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) is difficult to ascertain, and since [one's being] composed by a trustworthy person is uncertain, the authority of the trustworthy person's words is demolished at a single stroke.

body.text: ato yadetasya prāmāṇyaprasiddhyarthaṃ vācaspatiprabhṛtīnāṃ valgitaṃ tadaprāptāvasarameva / evaṃ pratyayoditamapi bhaṭṭābhimataṃ śābdaṃ pramāṇyaṃ vyastamiti boddhavyam / tasmāt sthitametat na śābdaṃ bahirarthe pramāṇamastīti / buddhyākāre tu tatkāryaprasūtatvāttadanumānameveti /
body.translated_text: Therefore, whatever display <s>Vācaspati</s> and others have made for the purpose of establishing the authority of this [verbal testimony] is entirely without occasion. Thus it should be understood that the verbal authority as conceived by <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [<s>Kumārila</s>], though propounded with [elaborate] reasoning, has been refuted separately. Therefore this stands established: verbal testimony is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for external objects. But regarding the form in the cognition, since it is produced as an effect of that [verbal testimony], it is merely an inference from that.

body.text: mīmāṃsakoktaṃ tāvadupamānaṃ mānameva na bhavati, nirviṣayatvādasya / ihāpi prayogaḥ -
body.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> (analogy) as maintained by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> is indeed not a valid means of knowledge, because it has no object (<s>nirviṣaya</s>). Here too the argument is:

body.text: yasya na viṣayavattvaṃ na tasya prāmāṇyam / yathā keśoṇḍukajñānasya / na siddhaṃ ca viṣayavattvamupamānajñānasyeti vyāpakānupalambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: That which has no object (<s>viṣayavattva</s>) does not have validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) — like the cognition of floating hairs [seen by one with an eye disease]. And the objecthood of <s>upamāna</s>-cognition is not established — [this is] a <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>.

body.text: nāyamasiddho hetuḥ, nirviṣayatvādupamānasya / tathā hi sādṛśyaviśiṣṭaḥ piṇḍaḥ piṇḍaviśiṣṭaṃ vā sādṛśyamupamānasya viṣayo varṇyate / na sadṛśavastuvyatiriktaṃ sādṛśyaṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ śakyate, pramāṇenāpratītatvāt /
body.translated_text: This reason is not unestablished, because <s>upamāna</s> is indeed without an object. For the object of <s>upamāna</s> is described as either: a particular thing qualified by similarity, or similarity qualified by a particular thing. [But] similarity as something distinct from the similar objects cannot be established, because it is not perceived by any <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text: nanu sādṛśyaṃ vastu durvārameva / yadāha
body.translated_text: But surely similarity is an undeniable reality! As [someone] says:

children.translated_text: 'The reality of similarity cannot be denied;
it is the connection of a greater number of components [i.e., properties] with another universal (<s>jāti</s>).'

body.text: iti / atrocyate / yadi sadṛśātiriktaṃ sādṛśyaṃ vastu dṛśyaṃ syāt, tadā dṛśyānupalambhagrastameva, śāstrānāhitasaṃskāreṇāpi kenacittasyādarśanāt / tasya cāstitve sarva sarvatrāstītyapravṛttinivṛttikaṃ jagadāpadyeta / athādṛśyaṃ tatsādṛśyamupeyate, tathāpi tatra prasiddhaliṅgābhāvādasiddhameva / siddhena ca tena viṣayavattopamānasya sidhyeta / sādṛśyapratyayastu svahetostathotpannena sadṛśavastunāpi kriyamāṇoghaṭata eva iti na sādṛśyamupasthāpayituṃ prabhavati / upamānapramāṇabalādeva sādṛśyasiddhiriti cet / na / pramāṇāntarasiddhayoreva sādṛśyapiṇḍayorviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasyopamānaviṣayatvāt kathaṃ sādṛśyamātrasyopamānāt siddhiḥ / tataśca sādṛśyasyāsiddherna tadviśiṣṭaḥ piṇḍaḥ piṇḍaviśiṣṭaṃ vā sādṛśyamupamānasya viṣayaḥ / tadevamupamānasya nirviṣayatvaṃ siddhamiti nāsiddho hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: If similarity as something distinct from the similar [objects] were a visible reality, then it would be grasped by the non-perception of the visible — since no one, even without the dispositions instilled by [philosophical] treatises, perceives it. And if it existed [as a visible entity], everything would be [similar to] everything everywhere, resulting in the world being without any basis for activity or cessation [of activity]. If, on the other hand, one accepts that similarity is invisible (<s>adṛśya</s>), even then it is unestablished, because there is no well-known inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for it. And only if it were established could the objecthood of <s>upamāna</s> be established through it. But the cognition of similarity, arising from its own cause, is perfectly accomplished even by the similar object [itself] — so it is not capable of establishing [a separate entity called] similarity. If one says: 'Similarity is established precisely by the force of the <s>upamāna</s> <s>pramāṇa</s> [itself]' — no, because since the qualifier-qualificand relation between similarity and the particular thing, both established by other <s>pramāṇas</s>, is the object of <s>upamāna</s>, how can similarity alone be established from <s>upamāna</s>? And since similarity is not established, neither a particular thing qualified by it, nor similarity qualified by a particular thing, is the object of <s>upamāna</s>. Thus the objectlessness of <s>upamāna</s> is established, and the reason is not unestablished.

body.text: nāpi viruddhaḥ, sapakṣe bhāvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is [the reason] contradictory, because of its presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s>.

body.text: na cānaikāntikaḥ / tathā hi prāmāṇyābhāve sādhye pramāṇyameva vipakṣaḥ / tacca viṣayavattayā vyāptam, nirnimittatve sarvajñānaprāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt / tadayaṃ viruddhavyāptopalabdhyā vipakṣānnivartamāno viṣayavattvābhāvalakṣaṇo hetuḥ prāmāṇyābhāvalakṣaṇa eva viśrāmyatīti vyāptisiddhiḥ / ato nopamānaṃ pramāṇamiti /
body.translated_text: Nor is it inconclusive. For when the <s>sādhya</s> is the absence of validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>), validity itself is the <s>vipakṣa</s> (contrary instance). And that [validity] is pervaded by having an object (<s>viṣayavattva</s>), because otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that all cognitions would be valid. Therefore this reason, characterized by the absence of objecthood, which turns away from the <s>vipakṣa</s> through the perception of what is pervaded by the contrary, comes to rest precisely in [the property] characterized by the absence of validity — thus the <s>vyāpti</s> is established. Therefore, <s>upamāna</s> is not a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 103#)
naiyāyikaparikalpitopamānanirākaraṇāryamapyayameva prayogo draṣṭavyaḥ, tasyāpi nirviṣayatvāt / tathā hi samākhyāsaṃbandhastasya viṣayo varṇyate / sa ca paramārthato nāsti / sa hi saṃbandhaḥ saṃbandhibhyāṃ bhinno 'bhinno vā / yadi bhinnastadā tayoriti kutaḥ / na ca saṃbandhāntarāditi vaktavyam, tadapi kathaṃ teṣāmiti cintāyāmanavasthāprasaṅgaḥ / na ca yathā pradīpaḥ prakāśāntaramantareṇa prakāśate tathā saṃbandho 'pi saṃbandhāntaramantareṇa saṃbaddho bhaviṣyatīti vaktumucitam / pramāṇasiddhe hi vasturūpe 'yamasya svabhāva iti varṇyate / yathā pradīpasyaiva / saṃbandhastu na pramāṇapratītaḥ / tatka evaṃ jānātvayamasya svabhāva iti, yadvā nāstyevāyamiti / ayamanayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ saṃbaddhāvetāviti tu buddhiḥ svahetubalāt saṃbaddhavastudvayādapi saṃbhāvyamānā na saṃbandhamākṣeptuṃ prabhavati / tasmānna bhinnasaṃbandhasiddhiḥ / athābhinnaḥ tadā saṃbandhināveva kevalāviati na samākhyāsaṃbandho nāma, yaḥ kaścidupamānasya viṣayaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: (Nibandha 103) For the refutation of <s>upamāna</s> as conceived by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> too, this very same argument should be applied, since that too is without an object. For the object of that [Nyāya <s>upamāna</s>] is described as the relation between a name (<s>samākhyā</s>) and [its referent]. But that [relation] does not ultimately exist. For that relation is either different from or identical with the relata. If different, then how [does it belong] 'to those two'? And one should not say 'through another relation' — for in pondering 'how does that [other relation] belong to those [relata]?', there would be an infinite regress. Nor is it proper to say: 'Just as a lamp illuminates without another illumination, so too a relation will be related without another relation' — for this [self-illuminating] nature is described for a real entity established by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, saying 'this is its intrinsic nature' — as with the lamp itself. But the relation is not cognized by any <s>pramāṇa</s>. So who would know 'this is its intrinsic nature'? — or rather, it simply does not exist. The cognition 'this is the relation of these two' or 'these two are related' arises by the force of its own causes and is possible even from the two related objects [themselves] — it cannot conjure up a [separate] relation. Therefore, a distinct relation is not established. If, on the other hand, [the relation is] non-different [from the relata], then there are only the bare relata and nothing called the 'name-referent relation' that could be the object of <s>upamāna</s>.

body.text: nanu saṃbandhabuddhijanakatvaṃ saṃbaddhapadārthādbhinnamabhinnaṃ vā / bhede ca sa eva sambandhaḥ, nāmni paraṃ vivādaḥ / athābhinnam, tadā yathā saṃbaddhapadārthasya svabhāvaḥ sarvapadārthasādhāraṇastathā tadapi rūpaṃ tadavyatibhinnaṃ sarvapadārthasādhāraṇamiti sa padārtho 'bhimatapadārtheneva parairapi padārthaiḥ saha saṃbaddhaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: But is the capacity to generate the cognition of relation different from or identical with the related object? If different, that itself is the relation — the dispute is merely about the name. If identical, then just as the intrinsic nature of the related object is common to all objects, so too that form, being non-different from it, would be common to all objects — and so that object would be related to all other objects just as to the intended object.

body.text: nacaivam, tasmādbhinnaṃ tatsabandhabuddhijanakatvaṃ saṃbaddhapadārthādeṣṭavyamiti cet / nanvetadāśaṅkya rājakulapādaiḥ parihṛtameva / tathā hi
body.translated_text: If one says: 'It is not so, therefore the capacity to generate the cognition of relation must be accepted as different from the related object' — well, this [objection] has already been anticipated and answered by the Venerable Master (<s>Rājakulapāda</s>). For:

children.text: saṃbaddhaṃ svayameva cennanu yathā taṃ tasya saṃbandhinaṃ
children.translated_text: 'If [the object] is itself related [to its name, without a separate relation], then just as it [is related]

children.text: pratyātmā jagatīmapi prati tathā tatkena yogo 'sya na /
children.translated_text: to that particular relatum, why is there not also such a connection for it with respect to the whole world?

children.text: saṃbandhe parato 'pi tulyamakhilaṃ tenaiva cet saṃyamo
children.translated_text: If the same applies even when [a separate] relation [is posited] from another [entity], then restraint [comes] only from the cause [of the cognition];

children.text: hetuḥ kiṃ na niyāmakaḥ sa ca kathaṃ yogaḥ kvacinnāpare //
children.translated_text: and how is that cause a determining factor, and why is the connection [limited to] some [things] and not others?'

body.text: iti / tasmāt saṃbandhābhāvāt pūrvoktena nyāyena sārūpyābhāvāccāsiddhaṃ naiyāyikasyāpi nirviṣayamupamānaṃ pramāṇamato 'nantareṇaiva vyāpakānupalambhena nirākṛtam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, since relation does not exist, and since similarity also does not exist, by the reasoning stated earlier — <s>upamāna</s> as conceived by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> too is established as objectless, [and] not a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s>; it is thus refuted by the immediately preceding <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> [argument].

body.text: arthāpattirapi / yadetat sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ pratyakṣādipratīto yo 'rthaḥ sa yena vinā nopapadyate tasyārthasya parikalpanamarthāpattirityatra vicāryate / yasyārthasya darśanād yo 'rthaḥ parikalpyate tayoryadi pratibandho 'stitadārthāpattiranumānameva / arthāpattiriti nāmāntarakaraṇe nāsmākaṃ kācidvipratipattiḥ / tathā hi pramāṇaparidṛṣṭo 'rthaḥ kenacidvinā nopapadyata iti kuto labhyate, yadi paridṛśyamānaparikalpyamānayoḥ kaścit saṃbandhaḥ syāt / anyathā tena vinā nopapadyata ityahrīkādanyo na brūyāt, (#Nibandh 104#) ghaṭapaṭavat / sa ca sambandhaḥ kvacit pūrvamavaśyaṃ pratyakṣānupalambhataḥ kvacidadṛśyatve 'pi viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalādvā niścetavyaḥ / anyathā tena vinānupapattijñānasyaivānupapatteḥ / sati caivam, ekaṃ saṃbandhinaṃ dṛṣṭvā yatrasthena vinā tatrasthaṃ nopapadyate, tasya dvitīyasya saṃbandhinaḥ kalpanamanumānameva / tatra svabhāvapratibandhe svabhāvahetujaiva sārthāpattiḥ / tadutpattipratibandhe kāryāliṅgajaiva / taduktam - anyathānupapannatvamanvayavyatirekiṇyarthe bhavati yat, tasmānnārthāpattiḥ pramāṇāntaramiti / tasmāt paridṛśyamānaparikalpyamānayoḥ sati pratibandhe nārthāpattiḥ pramāṇāntaramiti / atha tayorna pratibandhaḥ, tadārthāpattiḥ pramāṇameva na bhavatīti mantavyam, sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa ca saṃbandhābhāvāt / yasya yatra pratibandho nāsti na tasya tatra prāmāṇyamityādirveda nirākaraṇārtha yaḥ pūrvamupanyastaḥ sa evāsyā api prāmāṇyanirākaraṇāya draṣṭavyaḥ / sāmānyenaivārthāpattau nirākṛtāyāṃ pratyakṣādipūrvakatvalakṣaṇastatprapañco nirasto bhavatyeveti tadarthaṃ na prabandho 'bhidhīyate, gavi nirākṛte śāvaleyanirākṛtivat / tasmānnārthāpattiḥ pramāṇāntaramiti /
body.translated_text: <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) likewise [is refuted]. The general definition of this is: 'The postulation of a thing without which a fact cognized through perception and the like would be inexplicable — that is <s>arthāpatti</s>.' This is examined here. If there is an invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) between the fact from whose observation another fact is postulated, and [that postulated fact], then <s>arthāpatti</s> is nothing but inference (<s>anumāna</s>). We have no objection to its being given another name. For how is it obtained that a fact ascertained by a <s>pramāṇa</s> is inexplicable without something else, unless there is some connection between what is observed and what is postulated? Otherwise, no one but a shameless person would say 'it is inexplicable without that' (Nibandha 104) — [it would be] like [inferring one from] a pot and a cloth. And that connection must in some cases be first ascertained from perception and non-perception; in other cases, even when [the connection is] invisible, it must be ascertained by the force of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that refutes the contrary. Otherwise, the very cognition of 'inexplicability without that' would itself be inexplicable. And this being so, having seen one relatum and postulating the second relatum without which [the first] in its locus would be inexplicable — that is nothing but inference. When the connection is one of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>), the <s>arthāpatti</s> is generated by a reason of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>); when [the connection] is one of causal origination, it is generated by an effect-sign (<s>kāryāliṅga</s>). As has been stated: 'The otherwise-inexplicability that applies in an object [characterized by] positive and negative concomitance — therefore <s>arthāpatti</s> is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>.' Therefore, when there is an invariable connection between what is observed and what is postulated, <s>arthāpatti</s> is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>. If, however, there is no such connection between them, then <s>arthāpatti</s> is simply not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all — this should be understood, because there is no connection either directly or indirectly. The [argument] that 'whatever has no invariable connection with something is not a valid means of knowledge regarding it' and so forth, which was previously adduced for the refutation of the Vedas, should be applied here too for the refutation of the authority of this [<s>arthāpatti</s>]. Since <s>arthāpatti</s> is refuted in general, the elaboration of its being preceded by perception and the like [as a defining characteristic] is also refuted — and therefore no [separate] treatise is composed for that purpose, just as when the cow is refuted, the calf is [automatically] refuted. Therefore, <s>arthāpatti</s> is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>.

body.text: tathā abhāvapramāṇasyāpi prāmāṇyaṃ nopapadyate, tasyāpi nirviṣayatvāt / tataśca mīmāṃsakopavalgitopamānanirākaraṇārthamupanyasto yo viṣayavattvābhāvalakṣaṇo 'nupalambhaḥ sa evāsyāpi nirāsārthamupanyasitavyaḥ / nanu cātrāsiddho hetuḥ / tathā hi yadi ghaṭābhāvo vāstavaḥ prameyabhūto na syāt, tadā nāstīha ghaṭa iti pratyayaḥ kathamutpadyata iti cet / kevalapradeśagrāhipratyakṣāditi brūmaḥ / nanu yadi kaivalyaṃ praveśasvarūpaṃ tattarhi saghaṭe 'pi pradeśe vidyata iti tatrāpi tasya pratyayasya sadbhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / athātiriktaḥ, mukhāntareṇābhāva evābhyupagato bhavatīti cet, na / kaivalyaṃ tadviviktatvamasaṅkīrṇatvamityādibhiḥ padaiḥ pradeśasya ghaṭaṃ pratyanāpannādhārabhāvasya svahetuta utpannasya ghaṭapradeśādanya evātmābhidhīyate / sa eva cābhāvapratyayaṃ janayatīti kimapareṇābhāvena kartavyam /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the authority of <s>abhāva</s> (absence) as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is also not tenable, since it too is without an object. Therefore, the same argument from the absence of objecthood (<s>viṣayavattvābhāva</s>) that was adduced for the refutation of <s>upamāna</s> as propounded by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> should be applied for the refutation of this [<s>abhāva</s>] as well. But the reason is not unestablished here. For if the absence of a pot were not a real entity (<s>vāstava</s>), a knowable thing, then how would the cognition 'there is no pot here' arise? — if one asks this, we say: from perception that grasps only the bare locus. But if that bare [locus] is the intrinsic nature of the [locus], then it would exist even in a locus with a pot, and so there would be the absurd consequence that this cognition [of absence] would exist there too. If [the bare locus] is something additional [beyond the locus itself], then absence is admitted under another guise — if one says this, no. By the words 'bare,' 'free from that,' 'unmixed with [that],' and so forth, what is denoted is a distinct nature of the locus — one that has not assumed the status of a substrate for the pot, that has arisen from its own causes, and that is different from the locus-of-the-pot. And that very [locus] generates the cognition of absence — so what need is there for another [entity called] 'absence'?

body.text: nanu ghaṭaṃ pratyanāpannādhārabhāvasya pradeśasyeti ghaṭābhāvayuktasya pradeśasyetyuktaṃ bhavatīti cet / tarhi ghaṭābhāvo 'pi ghaṭaṃ pratyanāpannādhārabhāvaḥ kimabhāvāntareṇa svarūpeṇaiva vā / prathamapakṣe 'navasthā / atha tadabhāvarūpatvādabhāvāntaramantareṇaiva ghaṭābhāvo ghaṭaṃ pratyanāpannādhārabhāvaḥ / yadyevamasahāyaḥ pradeśaviśeṣo 'pi paryudāsavṛttyā ghaṭābhāvarūpatvādabhāvaṃ vinaiva ghaṭaṃ pratyanāpannādhārabhāvo yukta iti kimakāṇḍamāhopuruṣikayā mithyāpralāpenābodhaviklavaṃ śiṣyapudgalamākulayasi / tasmād bhūtalātiriktasyābhāvasyāsiddhatvānnāyaṃ viṣayavattābhāvalakṣaṇo heturasiddhaḥ / pramāṇapañcakābhāvādeva tu prameyābhāvasiddhipratyāśāpi na yujyate, vipratipattiviṣayatvādasyā nenaiva prameyābhāvasiddherayogāt /
body.translated_text: But [one might object]: 'A locus that has not assumed the status of a substrate for the pot' means 'a locus conjoined with the absence of the pot' — if one says this: then is the absence of the pot too 'one that has not assumed the status of a substrate for the pot' by virtue of another absence, or by its own nature? In the first case, infinite regress. If, however, the absence of the pot, being of the nature of absence, is 'one that has not assumed the status of a substrate for the pot' without requiring another absence — then if so, a particular locus too, being unaccompanied [by the pot], can, by the method of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>), properly be 'one that has not assumed the status of a substrate for the pot' without requiring absence [as a separate entity], since it is of the nature of absence-of-the-pot. So why do you confuse your poor bewildered students with this groundless bravado of false chatter? Therefore, since absence as something additional to the ground is not established, this reason characterized by the absence of objecthood is not unestablished. But the hope of establishing the absence of a knowable through the absence of the five [means of valid knowledge] is also not proper, because this [matter] is a subject of dispute, and the establishment of the absence of the knowable is impossible by this alone.

body.text: viruddhānaikāntikatve ca pūrvameva hetoḥ parihṛte / tadataḥ siddhamabhāvapramāṇābhimatasyāprāmāṇyamiti /
body.translated_text: The contradictoriness and inconclusiveness of the reason have already been dealt with earlier. Therefore, from this, the non-authority of what is claimed as the <s>abhāva</s>-<s>pramāṇa</s> is established.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 105#)
athavābhāvapramāṇasvarūpameva nirūpyatām / kaḥpunaḥ pramāṇābhāvātmābhimato bhavatām, kiṃ prasajyavṛttyā pramāṇānutpattimātram, atha vā paryudāsavṛttyā bhāvāntaram / vastvantaramapi jaḍarūpaṃ jñānarūpaṃ vā / jñānarūpamapi jñānamātrakamekajñānasaṃsargivastujñānaṃ veti ṣaḍ vikalpāḥ /
body.translated_text:
(Nibandh 105)
Alternatively, let the very nature of <s>abhāva-pramāṇa</s> (absence as a means of valid knowledge) be examined. What, then, is the nature of <s>pramāṇābhāva</s> (absence of a means of knowledge) as intended by you? Is it, through mere negation (<s>prasajya-vṛtti</s>), simply the non-arising of a <s>pramāṇa</s>? Or, through implicative negation (<s>paryudāsa-vṛtti</s>), another positive entity? And if it is another entity, is it of an insentient nature or of the nature of cognition? And if of the nature of cognition, is it mere cognition, or cognition of an entity associated with a single cognition? — thus there are six alternatives.

body.text:
tatra na tāvannivṛttirūpo 'bhāvo yujyate / sa khalu nikhilaśaktivikalatayā na kiñcit / yacca na kiñcit tatkathamabhāvaṃ paricchindyāt, tadviṣayaṃ vā jñānaṃ janayet, pratītaṃ vā tatkathamiti sarvamandhakāranartanam /
yadāhuḥ -
body.translated_text:
Of these, first, absence in the form of mere negation is not tenable. For it, being devoid of all capacities, is nothing. And what is nothing — how could it delimit absence, or generate cognition directed at it, or [if] cognized — how [is that possible]? Thus everything is a dance in darkness.
As they say:

body.text: na hyabhāvaḥ kasyacit pratipattiḥ pratipattiheturvā tasyāpi kathaṃ pratipattiriti / nāpi vastvantaratāpakṣe jaḍarūpo 'bhāvaḥ saṅgacchate, tasyābhāvalakṣaṇaprameyaparicchedābhāvāt, paricchedasya jñānadharmatvāt / nāpi jñānamātrasvabhāvo 'bhāvo vaktavyaḥ, deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭasyāpi tato 'bhāvaprasaṅgāt, tadapekṣayāpi jñānamātratvāt tasya / athaikajñānasaṃsargivastujñānasvabhāvo 'numanyate tadāstamabhāvapramāṇapratyāśayā, pratyakṣaviśeṣasyaivābhāvanāmakaraṇāt / tasya cāsmābhirdṛśyānupalambhākhyasādhanatvena svīkṛtatvāt / ato na kācid vipratipattirnāma / tasmādabhāvapramāṇasvarūpamarpi nirūpyamāṇaṃ viśīryata eva / yadapyasya lakṣaṇamuktam
body.translated_text: 'For absence is neither the cognition of anything nor the cause of cognition — how then could there be cognition of it?' Nor does absence as another positive entity of an insentient nature hold, since there is no delimitation of the object characterized by absence for that [insentient entity], delimitation being a property of cognition. Nor can absence be said to have the nature of mere cognition, since even what is remote in place, time, and nature would then be absent from it, given that it too is of the nature of mere cognition in relation to that [absent thing]. If absence is admitted to have the nature of cognition of an entity associated with a single cognition, then abandon the hope for an <s>abhāva-pramāṇa</s> (absence as a separate means of knowledge), since it is merely a special case of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) given the name 'absence.' And since that has been accepted by us as having the nature of a proof called 'non-apprehension of the perceivable' (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>), there is no disagreement whatsoever. Therefore, even the nature of <s>abhāva-pramāṇa</s>, when examined, simply disintegrates. As for the definition given of it:

body.text: pratyakṣāderanutpattiḥ pramāṇābhāva ucyate /
body.translated_text: 'The non-arising of perception and the like is called the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge)' —

body.text: ityādi, tadapi yācitakamaṇḍanam / tasmāt sthitametat, pramāṇasya sato 'traivāntarbhāvāt pramāṇe eva //
body.translated_text: and so forth — that too is borrowed finery. Therefore, it is established that, since the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) exists, it is subsumed right here within the [established] <s>pramāṇas</s> themselves.

body.text: pramāṇāntarbhāvaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The chapter on the subsumption of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) is concluded.

(Nibandh 106)
[Treatise] 7.

body.text: // vyāptinirṇayaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Vyāptinirṇayaḥ</s> (Ascertainment of Pervasion).

body.text: iha dahanādinā dhūmāderarthāntarasya vyāptistadutpattilakṣaṇā / sā ca viśiṣṭānvayavyatirekagrahaṇapravaṇaviśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhasādhaneti nyāyaḥ / atra ca bhaṭṭaprabhṛtayo vipratipadyante / tathā hi te 'gnimati pradeśe dhūmasya bhūyodarśanaṃ tadviyukte ca tathaivādarśanamityanvayavyatirekitvaṃ kalpayāmbabhūvuḥ /
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of one thing — such as smoke and the like — by another — such as fire and the like — is characterized by the origination of the former from the latter. And the method [for establishing this] is through a specific <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension) that are inclined to apprehend the specific positive and negative concomitance. On this point, <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [Jayanta] and others disagree. For they have proposed that [pervasion amounts to] repeated observation of smoke in a region where fire is present, and likewise its non-observation in a region devoid of fire — [this being] the positive and negative concomitance.

body.text: nanu bhūyasāpi pravṛtte darśanādarśane ghaṭakulaṭādāvupalabdho vyabhicāra iti cet / kimetāvatā tatrāpyanumānamastu, tadvadvā dhūmādāvapi bhā bhūt / prathamapakṣastāvad vyabhicārādeva nirastaḥ / dvitīyo('pi) vyabhicārādeva / na hyanyasya vyabhicāre dhūmasya kiñcit / tasmādagnidhūmayoravyabhicārasyāsaṃbhave śatamapi tadupapattayaḥ tatprasādhakaviśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhā vā nānumānopayoginaḥ / saṃbhave vā kiṃ tadutpattyā tadupayoginā viśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhena, darśanādarśanābhyāmevāvyabhicārasiddheḥ / tathā ca kāśikākāraḥ prācīnānekadarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāyenacarameṇa cetasā dhūmasyāgniniyatatvaṃ gṛhyata iti //
body.translated_text: If [the objection is:] 'Even when [observation] proceeds repeatedly, deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is found in [cases like] pot, unchaste woman, and so forth' — then what of it? Either let there be inference in that case too, or let there be [deviation] in [the case of] smoke and the like as well. The first alternative is already refuted by the very fact of deviation. The second

body.text: trilocanastvāha - pratyakṣānupalambhayorviśeṣaviṣayatvāt kathaṃ tābhyāṃ sāmānyayoḥ saṃbandhapratipattiḥ / athānagnivyāvṛttenādhūmavyāvṛttasya saṃbandhaḥ pratīyata eveti / nanu so 'pi kasya pramāṇasya viṣayaḥ / na tāvatpratyakṣasya, svalakṣaṇaviṣayatvāttasya / nāpyanumānasya, tasyāpi tatpūrvakatvāt / na ca vyāvṛtyoḥ kaścitsaṃbandhaḥ / atha pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvī vikalpo dṛṣṭe bhede 'bhedamadhyavasyati, tadeva sāmānyam / evamapi vikalpānāṃ na vastvena viṣayaḥ / api tu grāhyākāraḥ / sa ca na vastu / vastu tu teṣāṃ parokṣameveti, kathaṃ tenāpi sambandhagrahaḥ / asmākaṃ tu bhūyodarśanasahāyena manasā tajjātīyānāṃ saṃbandho gṛhīto bhavati / ato dhūmo nāgniṃ vyabhicarati / tadvyabhicāre dhūma upādhirahitaṃ saṃbandhamatikrāmediti hetovipakṣaśaṅkānivartakaṃ pramāṇamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptopādhivirahaheturanupalambhākhyaṃ pratyakṣameva / tataḥ siddhaḥ svābhāvikaḥ sambandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>, however, says: 'Since <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension) have specific objects, how can the cognition of the relation between universals [be obtained] through them?' If [the reply is:] 'The relation of what is excluded from non-fire with what is excluded from non-smoke is indeed cognized' — then by which <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) is even that [cognized]?

body.text: vācaspatestu prapañcaḥ / tathā hi dhumādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandhaḥ / na tu vahnyādīnāṃ dhūmādibhiḥ / te hi vināpi dhūmādibhirupalabhyante / vahnyādayastu yadārdrendhanasaṃbandhamanubhavanti tadā dhūmādibhiḥ saṃbadhyante / vahnyādīnāṃ (#Nibandh 107#) tu sphuṭamārdrendhanādyupādhikṛtaḥ saṃbandho na tu svābhāvikaḥ / tato 'niyataḥ / svābhāvikastu dhūmādīnāṃ vahnayādibhiḥ saṃbandhaḥ, tadupādheranupalabhyamānatvāt / kvacid vyabhicārasyādarśanāt anupalabhyamānasyāpi kalpanānupapatteḥ / na cādṛśyamāno 'pi darśanānarhatayā sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvena sagdihyamāna upādhiḥ saṃbandhasya svābhāvikatvaṃ pratibadhnātīti yuktam /
body.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s>'s elaboration is as follows: The natural relation (<s>svābhāvika saṃbandha</s>) of smoke and the like with fire and the like [exists]; but not of fire and the like with smoke and the like, for fire and the like are perceived even without smoke and the like. But fire and the like, when they undergo the connection with moist fuel,

body.text: avaśyaṃ śaṅkayā bhāvyaṃ niyāmakamapaśyatām
body.translated_text: 'Those who do not see a constraining factor must necessarily entertain doubt' —

body.text: iti tu dattāvakāśā laukikamaryādātikrameṇa śaṅkāpiśācī labdhaprasarā na kvacinnāstīti nāyaṃ kvacit pravarteta / sarvatraiva kasyacidanarthasya kathañcicchaṅkāspadatvāt / anarthaśaṅkāyāśca prekṣāvatāṃ nivṛttyaṅgatvāt / antataḥ snigdhānnapānopayoge 'pi maraṇadarśanāt / tasmāt prāmāṇikalokayātrāmanupālayatā yathādarśanamevaśaṅkanīyam / na tvadṛṣṭapūrvamapi / viśeṣasmṛtyapekṣa eva hi saṃśayo nāsmṛterbhavati / na ca smṛtirananubhūtacare bhavitumarhati / taduktaṃ mīmāṃsāvārtikakṛtā -
body.translated_text: but if opportunity is given [for such reasoning], then, by transgressing the conventions of the world, the ghost of doubt, having gained free rein, would be nowhere absent — and so [a person] would never undertake any action anywhere, since everything is somehow a possible ground for suspecting some harm. And since the suspicion of harm [is a reason for]

body.text: nāśaṅkā niḥpramāṇikā iti /
body.translated_text: 'Doubt without a basis in any <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) [is groundless]' — thus.

body.text: tasmādupādhiṃ prayatnenānviṣyanto 'nupalabhamānā nāstītyavagamya svābhāvikatvaṃ saṃbandhasya niścinumaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, diligently seeking a vitiating condition (<s>upādhi</s>) and not finding one, we conclude 'it does not exist' and ascertain the natural character of the relation.

body.text: syādetat / anyasyānyena sahākāraṇena cet svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandho bhavet, sarvaṃ sarveṇa svabhāvataḥ saṃbadhyeta / sarvaṃ sarvasmād gamyeta / athānyasya cedanyat kāryaṃ kasmāt sarvaṃ sarvasmānna bhavati, anyatvāviśeṣāt / tataśca sa evātiprasaṅgaḥ / yadyucyeta na bhāvasvabhāvāḥ paryanuyojyāḥ, tasmādanyatvāviśeṣe 'pi kiñcideva kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ ca kiñciditi / nanveṣa svabhāvānāmanuyogo bhinnānāmakāryakāraṇabhūtānāmapi svabhāvapratibandhe tulya eva / tasmād yatkiñcidetadapi / kena punaḥ pramāṇenaiṣa svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandho gṛhyate / pratyakṣasaṃbandhiṣu pratyakṣeṇa / tathā hi abhijāatamaṇibhedatattvavad bhūyodarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāyamindriyameva dhūmādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ svābhāvikāsaṃbandhagrāhīti yuktamutpaśyāmaḥ / evaṃ mānāntaraviditasaṃbandheṣu mānāntarāṇyeva yathāsvaṃ bhūyodarśanasahāyāni svābhāvikasaṃbandhagrahaṇe pramāṇānyunnetavyāni / svabhāvataśca pratibaddhā hetavaḥ svasādhyena yadi (#Nibandh 108#) sādhyamantareṇa bhaveyuḥ, svabhāvādeva pracyaveranniti tarkasahāyā nirastasādhyavyatirekavṛttisandehā yatra dṛṣṭāstatra svasādhyamupasthāpayantyeveti //
body.translated_text: It may be [objected]: 'If the relation of one thing with another, without a common cause, were natural, then everything would be naturally related to everything; everything would be inferable from everything. And if one thing were the effect of another, why does not everything arise from everything?'

body.text: atrocyate / iha khalu bhede tadutpattireva vyāptiḥ / na cāsāvanyo vā svata evāvinābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ svābhāvikaḥ saṃbandho bhūyodarśanamātrataḥ sidhyati / tathā hi, kiṃ yatra bhūyodarśanapravṛttistatra niyatatvavyavasthā, yatra vā niyatatvamasti tatraiva bhūyodarśanapravṛttiḥ / prathamapakṣe ghaṭādapi kulaṭā, pārthivatvādapi lohalekhyatvaṃ sidhyet, bhūyodarśanasaṃbhave 'pi niyatatvasaṃbhavāt /
body.translated_text: To this we reply: Here, in [the case of] distinct [entities], the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is precisely the origination of one from the other. And this — or any other natural relation characterized by invariable concomitance — is not established by mere repeated observation alone. For consider: Does the invariable rule hold wherever repeated observation proceeds?

body.text: vyabhicāradarśanānnaivamiti cet / kasya punarvyabhicāradarśanam yasya kasyacit śāstrakārasya, pratipatturvā / prathamapakṣe pratipattuḥ kimāyātaṃ yato nānumānamayaṃ kuryāt / anyathānyasya tadviṣayapratyakṣīkāreṇaiva so 'pi kṛtārtha iti kimavaśyamanumānamanveṣate / na cāptavacanādavyabhicāradarśanādanumānam / āptasya niścetumaśakyatvādityanyatra prasādhanāt / śāstrakāraṃ ca pṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭasaṃbandho 'pi dhṛmādagnimanumāsyata ityalaukikam / pratipattustu nāvaśyaṃ sannapi vyabhicāro gocarībhavati / na hi yatra vyabhicārastatraiva tāvati kāle deśe vāvaśyaṃ pratītimavatarati / apratīyamānaśca nāstyeveti na niyamaḥ / satyapi vyabhicāre darśanasāmagrayabhāvāt tasmādarśanāt / aticirakālavyavadhāne 'pi darśanāt brāhmaṇyādivyabhicāravat //
body.translated_text: If [the reply is:] 'Not so, because of the observation of deviation' — whose observation of deviation [is meant]? Some treatise-author's, or the individual cognizer's? In the first case, what concern is it of the cognizer, that he should not make this inference? Otherwise, the knowledge of another regarding that subject would

body.text: ghaṭapārthivādau pratipattaiva pravṛttaḥ / tadaiva krameṇa vā vyabhicāraṃ paśyediti cet / yadi tāvadasau kathañcit pravartate, pravṛtto 'pi vā sāmagryabhāvāvyabhicāraṃ na paśyet / vajraṃ vā lohena vyāpārayet / vyaktaṃ tasya tāvat tadapyamānamāpannamiti mahat pāṇḍityam / tasmād yadi vyabhicārādarśanādanumānaṃ tadādṛṣṭavyabhicārasya pratipatturghaṭapārthivatvādapyasti / tathā adarśanamātreṇa vyabhicārābhāvo na sidhyati, yogyānupalabdhereva sarvatrābhāvasādhane 'dhikārāt / tato bahulaṃ sahacāramātreṇa na vyabhicārī na vāvyabhicārī niścita iti śaṅkāvakāśaḥ //
body.translated_text: [Regarding] pot, earth-substance, and the like — the cognizer himself has proceeded [to infer]. Would he see the deviation at that very time, or gradually? If he somehow proceeds [to infer], and even having proceeded does not see the deviation due to the absence of the [complete] aggregate of [conditions] — or [if] diamond were pervaded by iron —

body.text: yadyevamadṛṣṭavyabhicārādapi dhūmādanumānaṃ mā bhūt / na / īdṛśasya śaṅkāvakāśasya sarvatra tadutpattirahite saṃbhavāditi / atha kadācit pratipattā pravṛtto vyabhicāraṃ paśyati / na tarhi yatra bhūyodarśanam, tatra niyatatvasthitiḥ / tatra kuto dhūme pratibandhasiddhiḥ / bhūyodarśanasyānyatra niyatatvopasthāpakatvakṣatau malinapauruṣatvena sarvatrānāśvāsāt //
body.translated_text: 'If so, then inference from smoke and the like should also not occur, since the deviation has not been seen [by the individual].' No — because such a ground for doubt [namely, that there might be an unseen deviation] is possible everywhere where the origination [of the effect from the cause] is absent. But if at some point the cognizer, having proceeded, does see a deviation — then wherever repeated observation [has occurred],

body.text: yadyevaṃ dvicandrādau cakṣurādipratyakṣaṃ malinapauruṣamupalabdhamiti ghaṭādikamapi nopasthāpayediti cet / na / indriyaviṣayakāryaṃ hi pratyakṣam / na dvicandrādijñānamīdṛśamarthakāryatvābhāvāt / (#Nibandh 109#) tato bhinnalakṣaṇasya pratyakṣābhāsattve 'pi ghaṭajñānaṃ pratyakṣameva / na caivaṃ dhūmādau pārthivatvādau ca vyāptigrāhakasya bhūyodarśanasya lakṣaṇabhedo yenaikatrāśvāsaḥ syāt //
body.translated_text: If so, [one might object:] in the case of double moons and the like, since visual and other perception is found to be impure human [cognition], it should not present pots and the like either. No, because perception is that which is the effect of sense faculty and object. Cognition of double moons and the like is not of this kind, due to the absence of being an effect of the object. (Nibandhāvalī 109) Therefore, even though what has a different characteristic is a pseudo-perception (<s>pratyakṣābhāsa</s>), cognition of a pot is perception indeed. And in this way, with respect to smoke and the like, and with respect to earthiness and the like, there is no distinguishing characteristic of repeated observation (<s>bhūyodarśana</s>), which grasps pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), such that there could be confidence in one [case but not the other].

body.text: ete evārthakāryatvākāryatve lakṣaṇabheda iti cet / na / ghaṭādijñānasya hyarthakāryatvavivāde pramāṇāntarato 'rthakriyālābhato vā niścayaḥ, na pratijñāmātreṇa / na cātra dhūmasyāgnisahacāraḥ sadātano 'yamatha suhṛddvayasyeva sātyayo gṛhīta iti saṃśaye sadātanasahacāraprasādhakapramāṇāntarasaṅgatirasti, tatkāryaṃ vā kiñcidupalabhyate / tarhi bādhyamānatvābādhyamānatvalakṣaṇo lakṣaṇabhedo bhaviṣyatītyapi na vaktavyam, avyabhicāragrāhakasya bhūyodarśanasya bādhitatvāsiddheḥ / abādhamātraṃ hi prasajyapratiṣedho 'pramāṇam / pramāṇāntarasaṅgatirarthakriyālābho vā paryudāsaścāsiddha iti na tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ / nāpi dvitīyaḥ / niyatatvābhāve 'pi pārthivatvādau bhūyodarśanasaṃbhavāditi na bhūyodarśanagamyā vyāptiḥ //
body.translated_text: If [one says:] these very [properties of] being an effect of the object and not being an effect of the object constitute the distinguishing characteristic — no, because the certainty regarding the cognition of a pot and the like being an effect of the object, when disputed, comes from another <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) or from obtaining causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), not from mere assertion.
