body.text: yathā hi deśāntaraparāvṛttamanīlādiparāvṛttaṃ ca svahetorutpannaṃ vastu tathā dvitīyakṣaṇāntaraparāvṛttamapi / yathā cānyadeśānavasthāyitvaṃ taddeśāvasthāyitvenāviruddham, viruddhaṃ ca deśāntarāvasthāyitvenaiva tathā dvitīyakṣaṇāvasthāyitvaṃ prathamakṣaṇāvasthāyitvenāviruddham, viruddhaṃ punardvitīyakṣaṇāvasthāyitvenaiva / kevalaṃ deśāntaradvitīyakṣaṇayostatpracyutimātraṃ vyavahriyate / tadanyonyābhāvapradhvaṃsābhāvayoḥ padārthayoḥ sadbhāve 'pyavāryam, abhāvāntarāsvīkāre 'pi bhāvābhāvayorapyamiśratvāsvīkāre tādātmyaprasaṅgāt / tasmād bhāvābhāvayostādātmyamiti / yathārthakriyākāritvasya taddeśavartitvanīlatvādibhinnavirodhastathā dvitīyakṣaṇānavasthāyitvenāpīti vivakṣitam / paramārthatastu dharmidharmayostādātmyaṃ vyāvṛttikṛto bhedavyavahāra iti apohasiddhau prasādhitam / etaccoktakrameṇāviruddhamāpāditam / etāvati tu tattve vākchalamātrapravṛttā dveṣaviṣajvalitātmānaḥ kṣudrāḥ pralapantīti kimatra brūmaḥ /
body.translated_text: For just as an entity produced from its own cause is excluded from another place and excluded from non-blue and the like, so too it is excluded from the second moment. And just as non-abiding-in-another-place is not contradictory with abiding-in-that-place, but is contradictory only with abiding-in-another-place — so too non-abiding-in-the-second-moment is not contradictory with abiding-in-the-first-moment, but is contradictory only with abiding-in-the-second-moment. The departure from another place and the second moment is merely conventionally designated. This is unavoidable even if the two entities — mutual absence and destruction-absence — exist; even without accepting any additional absence, since [we] do not accept that being and non-being are unmixed, identity would follow. Therefore, being and non-being are identical. Just as the contradictory opposition of causal-efficacy-bearing with abiding-in-that-place, being-blue, and so forth [is resolved through exclusion], so too with non-abiding-in-the-second-moment — this is what is intended. In ultimate truth, however, the identity of property-bearer and property, and the conventional usage of difference being produced by exclusion — this has been established in the <s>Apohasiddhi</s>. And this has been shown to be non-contradictory by the method stated above. But when the truth is just this much, petty persons, their souls ablaze with the poison of hostility, prattle on, moved by mere verbal trickery — what more can we say?

body.text: tataśca vyatiriktanivṛttyutpattimantareṇa svarūpanivṛtterupapatteḥ kathaṃ kṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ prāktanasattāvasthitiḥ / tasmādutsṛṣṭavibhramaṃ naṣṭavyavahāramātramastu, na tvasyānyat kiñcij jāyeta, bhāvasya tādavasthyaprasaṅgāt / abhāvaḥ kathaṃ niṣidhyata iti cet / na, tadanutpattimātraviṣayasya vācāniścayena ca paścādabhāvavyavahāramātrapravartanasyeṣṭatvād vastūtpattereva niṣiddhatvāt /
body.translated_text: Consequently, since the cessation of [a thing's] own nature is explained without a distinct cessation or production, how can the prior state of existence persist beyond one moment? Therefore, let there remain only the abandoned confusion and the destroyed convention — but nothing else is born [from it], since the entity...

body.text: nanu keyaṃ vācoyuktiḥ, abhāvavyavahāramātramiṣyate paścānnābhāva iti / evaṃ sati visaṃvāditāprasaṅgo 'bhāvavyavahārasya / abhāvaśca mithyeti bhāva eva pratiṣedhyasya syāt / sa cābhāvaḥ paścā(d) bhavatīti sphuṭataramasya kādācitkatvātsahetukatvam, vastutvaṃ ceti / asadetat, abhāvākhyavastvantarāsvīkāre 'pi pracyutimātrāpekṣayāpi vyavahārasya caritārthatvapratipādanāt /
body.translated_text: But [you object:] what kind of verbal sophistry is this — that merely the convention of non-existence is accepted afterward, but not [actual] non-existence? In that case, the absurd consequence of deceptiveness of the convention of non-existence [would follow]. And if non-existence is false, then the thing to be negated would simply be existence. And that non-existence, occurring afterward...

body.text: yattu tadviviktabhūtalāderviṣayatvamāśaṅkyoktam, na bhūtalādervastvantaratvāt / na ca vastvantare pratipādite pratīte vā ghaṭādi vastubhūtamiti pratipāditaṃ pratītaṃ (#Nibandh 123#) vā bhavati / evaṃ vastvantarameva nāśa iti asmin mate yad dūṣaṇamuktaṃ tat svayameva parihṛtaṃ syāditi, tadapyasaṃbaddham, kevalaṃ hi bhūtalamasya viṣaya iti kathaṃ na ghaṭāderabhūtatvabodhaḥ / yaiva hi ghaṭādyapekṣayā kaivalyāvasthā pradeśasya sa eva ghaṭavirahaḥ / vacanādināpyevaṃ kevalapradeśapratipādane kathamiva na prakṛtaghaṭādyabhāvapratipādanam / kaivalyaṃ cāsahāyapradeśādavyatibhinnameva //
body.translated_text: As for the objection raised by imagining that the ground-surface devoid of that [pot] and such is the object [of the non-existence cognition] — [we reply:] no, because the ground-surface and such are a different entity. And when a different entity has been conveyed or cognized, [Nibandh 123] the pot and such, which are [actual] real entities, are neither conveyed nor cognized. Thus...

body.text: na ceha ghaṭo nāstīti pratyayasya ghaṭavatyapi pradeśe prasaṅgaḥ, svahetostathotpannasya saghaṭapradeśasya kevalapradeśādanyatvāt / na ca pratyabhijñānataḥ saghaṭāghaṭapradeśayorekatvam, pūrvamasya nirākaraṇāt / na ca vināśahetorasāmarthyavaiyarthyābhidhāne 'ṅkurādihetorapi tathābhidhātumucitam / asiddhe hi kārye hetorāśrayaṇamavārtham / siddhe ceyaṃ cintā, yadi hetornityo 'nityo vārtho jātaḥ kiṃ nāśakāraṇeneti hetupuraskāreṇaiva pravṛtteḥ / na caivamasiddhe 'ṅkurādau kārye śakyamabhidhātum, svarūpasyaivābhāt taddharmakatvā(tad) dharmakatvādiparyanuyogasya nirviṣayatvāt //
body.translated_text: And the cognition 'there is no pot here' does not apply even to a location where there is a pot, because [a location] with a pot, having been produced by its own cause in that manner, is different from a mere location. And one cannot [establish] the identity of the location-with-pot and the location-without-pot through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), because that [identity] has already been refuted...

body.text: nanu tvayāpi bhāvābhāvayorlakṣaṇabhedo 'bhihitaḥ / tatkathamekatvaṃ sarvārthānām / lakṣaṇabhedādeva bhedavyavasthā / tato 'pi cenna bhedavyavasthitiḥ, na kasyacit kutaścid bhedavyavasthitirityadvaitaprasaṅga iti cet / na / yo hi naśvarasvabhāvaḥ sa eva nāśoḥ, naśyatīti bahulādhikārāt kartari ghañaḥ prasādhanāt, taṃ nāśaṃ bhāvasvabhāvamicchāmaḥ / naśanaṃ nāśa iti tu prasajyātmā dvidhā kartavyaḥ / tattvatastāvad vastutvavirahāt tattvānyatvavirahita evāsau bhāvo na bhavatīti tadbhāvaniṣedhamātrapātaṃ tu bhavati kharaśṛṅgādivat / saṃvṛtau tu yathā kālabhedena vikalpyamānaḥ kādācitka iva pratibhāti tathā sarvopākhyāviraharūpatayā bhāvādbhinna iva pratibhātīti nāvastutvopalakṣaṇabhedākhyānavirodhaḥ / evaṃ ca sati saṃvṛttyā lakṣaṇabhede bhāvābhāvayorbhedasyeṣṭatvāt / tatvena ca lakṣaṇaikatāvirahe bhāvasya tenaikyaniṣedhāt kathamadvaitaprasaṅgopālambhaḥ //
body.translated_text: But [you object:] you yourself have stated a difference of defining characteristics between existence and non-existence. How then can there be identity of all things? [Reply:] The [apparent] establishment of difference is merely from the difference of defining characteristics. And even from that, there is no [real] establishment of difference — [according to the principle that] there is no establishment of difference of anything from anything — this is the <s>advaita</s> (non-dual) principle...

body.text: syādetat / na ca vivekāpratītau tadviviktagrahaṇaṃ bhavati / tadvivekaśca na bhūtalādisvarūpameva viśeṣaṇatvāditi / tadetannyāyabahiṣkṛtam / viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo hi saṅkalpāruḍhe rūpe bāhyārthasparśe vikalpaśabdaliṅgāntarāṇāṃ vaiyarthyaprasaṅgāditi śāstre vistareṇa pratipādanāt / sa ca saṅkalpo 'bhinnamapi bhāvaṃ bhinnamivākalayati / yathā śilāputrakasya śarīram, śarīre karaṇādayaḥ, lambakarṇo devadatta ityādi / tasmāt kalpanādhīno viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ / abhinne 'pi bhāve bhedavivakṣāpekṣo bhedavyavahāraḥ kathaṃ bhedaniyatamātmānamātanotu //
body.translated_text: It might be [objected]: the apprehension of something as 'devoid of that' cannot occur without the cognition of separateness. And that separateness is not merely the own-nature of the ground-surface and such, since it functions as a qualifier. [Reply:] This falls outside proper reasoning. For the relation of qualifier and qualified pertains to a form that has been mentally constructed, not touching the external object...

body.text: skhaladgatirayaṃ rāhoḥ śira ityādinirdeśa iti cet / yadi satyametat, tadā śiro 'tiriktasya rāhoriva kṣmātalāderatiriktasya vivekasya dṛśyānupalambhabādhitatvādayamapi nirdeśaḥ skhaladgatireva, tathāpi neti koṣapānaṃ pramāṇam / tasmātsaghaṭāt (#Nibandh 124#) pradeśāntarāt pradeśa evāyamanyo ghaṭaviviktaḥ svahetorutpanno na tu ghaṭavivekena viśeṣitaḥ, svahetorutpannasya viviktasyābhāve vivekasyābhāvāt / kiṃ ca
body.translated_text: [Objection:] This designation [of absence] is like the faltering usage 'the head of <s>Rāhu</s>' [who is only a head]. [Reply:] If this is true, then just as the separateness [of a head] distinct from <s>Rāhu</s>, and [similarly] the separateness distinct from the ground-surface and such, are sublated by the non-apprehension of what is fit to be perceived (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>), this designation too is equally faltering. Even so...

children.text: vyāptaṃ bhidā yadi viśeṣyaviśeṣa(ṇa)tvaṃ bhedātyayānnanu tadā tadabhāva eva /
children.translated_text: 'If the qualifier-qualified relation is pervaded by difference, then upon the cessation of difference, there would simply be its non-existence.'

children.text: deśo viśiṣṭa iti cāsti yathā tathedamapyasti dṛśyamatabhedadṛgasti neti //
children.translated_text: 'And just as it is [said] "the place is qualified [by absence]," so too this [can be said]. [But] is there a cognition of the perceptible as non-different [from the place]? — [the answer is:] no.'

body.text: tasmānnābhāvo nāma kaścid yatra kāraṇavyāpāraḥ / tadevaṃ sahetukavināśatvāditi hetuḥ svarūpāsiddha iti sthitam //
body.translated_text: Therefore, there is nothing called non-existence where causal operation [applies]. Thus it is established that the reason 'because [things] have a destruction that requires a cause' is unestablished in its own nature.

body.text: satāmakṣaṇikatvaṃ kāra(ṇa)vattvādityapyasaṃbaddhameva, kṣaṇikatvakāraṇavattvayorvirodhābhāvādakṣaṇikatvena kāraṇavattvasya vyāpterasiddheḥ sandigdhavyatirekitvāt / na cāsya viparyaye vṛttiśaṅkā nāśasya sahetukatvameva nivartayati, uktakrameṇa nāśasyaivābhāvāditi //
body.translated_text: The [argument] 'non-momentariness of existing things, because they have causes' is also incoherent, because since there is no contradiction between momentariness and having causes, the pervasion of having-causes by non-momentariness is unestablished — [the reason] has doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatirekatva</s>). Nor should there be suspicion of [the reason] obtaining in the counter-instance, [since] destruction...

body.text: tathā prameyatvādapi sthirasiddhirmanorathamātram / sākāravedanodayapakṣasthitau hi dvitīyakṣaṇānuvṛttāvapyarthasya vyavahitatvāt, prakāśānupapatterviṣayasvarūpavedanameva jñānasya viṣayavedanam / evaṃ ca vartamānānurodhaḥ / atīte 'pi tatpratyāsatterapracyuteḥ / na cātiprasaṅgaḥ, anantarātītādanyena kṣaṇena sārūpyāsamarpaṇāt / tataśca kāraṇatvād yadi nāma prameyatvasya pūrvakālasattvena vyāptistathāpi prameyatvavat pūrvakālasattvamapi kṣaṇike 'viruddhamiti prameyatvākṣaṇikatvayorvyāptisādhano vyāpakānupalambho 'siddhaḥ / jñānākārārpakatvaṃ hi hetutvam, prameyatvaṃ prāmāṇikapratītatvam / taccānantarātīta eva kṣaṇe samupapadyate //
body.translated_text: Likewise, [the proof of] the permanence [of things] from [their being] objects of knowledge (<s>prameyatva</s>) is also mere wishful thinking. For if the position that cognition arises with a form (<s>sākāra-vedana</s>) is maintained, then even if the object persists to the second moment, since it is separated [from the cognition by a temporal gap], and since illumination [of a temporally distant object] is impossible, the cognition's awareness of the object is precisely [its] awareness of the object's own form [reflected within itself]. Thus...

body.text: jñānasattvāsamaye 'rthānuvṛtterabhāvānnirviṣayateti cet / nanvanuvṛttāvapi tadarpitākārasvarūpasaṃvedanameva tadvedanam / tadeva ca saviṣayatvam / iyaṃ ca pratyāsattiranantarātīte 'pi kṣaṇe 'kṣīṇeti na dvitīyakṣaṇānuvṛtteranurodha ityuktam / ataḥ sandigdhavyatirekitvādanaikāntikameva prameyatvam //
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Since the object does not persist at the time that knowledge exists, [knowledge] would be objectless. [Reply:] But even if [the object] persists, awareness of it is precisely the self-awareness of the form donated [to cognition] by that [object]. And that alone constitutes having an object. And this proximity [of form] is not diminished even in the immediately past moment — thus there is no [fault]...

body.text: atha sākāravādavidveṣādanākārajñānagrāhyatvaṃ prameyatvamabhipretaṃ tadāsiddhatāsya hetoḥ / indriyārthasannikarṣāderjñānamutpadyatāṃ nāma / taccānubhavaikarasatvena sarvatrārthe sadṛśākāratvāt kasya grāhakamastu, yenābhisaṃbaddhamiti cet / ātmamanaḥsaṃyogādīnāmapi grahaṇaṃ syāt / janakasya grahaṇamiti cet / tathāpyātmādīnāṃ grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ / viṣayatvena janakasya grahaṇamityapyasādhu, viṣayatvasyādyāpyaniścayāt / idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vedamityadhyavasāyo yatrārthe sa viṣaya iti cet / nanvastyeva pratiniyato vyavahāraḥ / kaḥ punaratra pratyāsattiniyama iti pṛcchāmaḥ / sa cedupavarṇayituṃ na śakyate, vyavahāro 'pi tvanmate niyato na syāditi brūmaḥ / asti tāvaditi cet / ata evārthasārūpyamasādhāraṇaṃ pratyāsattinimittamastu, nirmimitte niyamāyogāt //
body.translated_text: If, out of hostility to the <s>sākāravāda</s> (doctrine that cognition has form), the intended meaning of 'being an object of knowledge' is 'being graspable by formless knowledge,' then this reason is unestablished. Let knowledge arise from the contact of sense organ and object — granted. But since it is of the nature of homogeneous experience throughout, and has a similar form in every case of every object, of which [object] would it be the apprehension? ...

body.text:
(#Nibandh 125#)
nanu sārūpyamapyarthādarśane kathamavadhāryate / tacca kimekadeśena, sarvātmanā vā / ādye pakṣe sarvaṃ sarvasya vedanaṃ syāt / dvitīye tu jñānamajñānatāṃ vrajet / kiṃ ca sārūpyādarthavedane 'nantaraṃ jñānaṃ tulyaviṣayaṃ viṣayaḥ syāditi cet / mābhūdarthasya darśanam / ākāraviśeṣabalādadhyavasitārthasyārthakriyāprāpterevārtho 'pīdṛśa iti sārūpyavyavahāro 'viruddhaḥ / ata eva sthūlagataṃ paramāṇugataṃ vā sārūpyaṃ na cintyate / jñānākārasya sthūlatve 'pyekasāmagrīpratibaddhapuñjaviśeṣādapyabhīṣṭakriyākaraṇāt puruṣārthasiddheḥ / sārūpyaṃ caikadeśenaiva / na cātra sarvavedanaprasaṅgaḥ, sarveṣāṃ jñānaṃ pratyajanakatvāt / janakānāṃ ca svavyapadeśanimittāsādhāraṇaikadeśārpakatvena grāhyatvāt / nāpi tulyaviṣayāntarajñānagrahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ, tasya svasaṃvedanādeva pramāṇāt siddhatvāt / pramāṇāntarasya tatra vaiyarthyāt / jaḍatve satyākārārpakasya vastuno grāhyatvādityasyārthasyābhīṣṭatvācca / bāhyārthasthitau ceyaṃ cinteti sarvamanavadyam / tadevamayaṃ prameyatvāditi hetuḥ sākāravādapakṣe sandigdhavyatirekaḥ, nirākārapakṣe cāsiddha iti sthitam /
body.translated_text: [Nibandh 125] But [you ask:] how is conformity [of cognition] with the object ascertained in the absence of seeing the object [directly]? And is that [conformity] partial or complete? In the first case, every [cognition] would be an awareness of everything. In the second, knowledge would become non-knowledge [by being identical with the object]. Moreover, from conformity [alone, how is] the object [known]? ...

body.text: na cārthāpattirati sthirātmasādhanī, kāryakāraṇabhāvagrahaṇādīnāmanyathopapatteḥ / tathā hi upādānopādeyabhāvasthitacittasantatimapyāśrityeyaṃ vyavasthā sustheti kathamātmānaṃ pratyujjīvayatu / tatra kāryakāraṇabhāvapratītistāvadanākulā / tathāpi prāgbhāvivastuniścayajñānasyopādeyabhūtena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa paścādbhāvivastujñānenāsmin satīdaṃ bhavatīti niścayo janyate / tathā prāgbhāvivastvapekṣayā kevalabhūtalaniścāyakajñānopādeyabhūtena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa paścādbhāvivastvapekṣayā kevalabhūtalaniścāyakajñānenāsminnasatīdaṃ na bhavatīti vyatirekaniścayo janyate / yathoktam
body.translated_text: Nor does <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) establish a permanent self, because the apprehension of cause-and-effect relations and the like can be explained otherwise. For this orderly arrangement [of cognitions] can be sustained by relying upon the continuum of mind situated in the relation of appropriator and appropriated — [this explanation] stands well. So how could it revive [the argument for] a self? In that [regard]...

children.translated_text: The cognition born immediately after a single determination produces the reflection of positive concomitance through another cognition.

Likewise, the cognition of exclusion (<s>vyatireka-buddhi</s>), arising from the experience of the absence of that single [entity] and being the exclusion from what is other, manifests the understanding of negative concomitance.

body.text: ata eva devadattenāgnau pratīte yajñadattena ca dhūme pratīte na kāryakāraṇabhāvagrahaṇaṃ tajjñānayorupādānopādeyabhāvābhāvāt / yatra tvekasantāne jñānakṣaṇayorupādānopādeyabhāvastatra kāryādigrahaḥ sugrahaḥ / anyathā satyapi nityātmani pratisandhātari kāryakāraṇabhāvādīnāmapratītireva syāt /
body.translated_text: For this very reason, when <s>Devadatta</s> has cognized fire and <s>Yajñadatta</s> has cognized smoke, there is no apprehension of the cause-effect relation, because there is no relation of substratum and supervenient between their cognitions. But where, within a single continuum, there is the relation of substratum and supervenient between cognitive moments, there the apprehension of cause and the like is easily grasped. Otherwise, even if there were a permanent self as the connector, the cognition of cause-effect relations and the like would simply not occur.

body.text: tathā hi ātmanaḥ sakāśāt pratisandheyabuddhīnāmabhedo bhedo vā bhedābhedo vā / prathamapakṣe ātmaiva syāt pratisandhātā, buddhya eva vā syuḥ pratisandheyā iti kaḥ pratisandhānārthaḥ / bhedapakṣa 'pi buddhibhyo bhidyamānasya jaḍasyātmanaḥ kaḥ pratisandhānārtha iti na vidmaḥ / buddhiyogād draṣṭutvavat pratisandhātṛtvamiti (#Nibandh 126#) cet / buddhi reva tarhi draṣṭī pratisandhātrī cetī niyamasvīkāre tadyogādasya tathātvamiti kimanena yācitakamaṇḍanena / buddhīnāṃ kartṛtvābhāvāditi cet / taddvāreṇāpi tarhi tasyātmano draṣṭṛtvādivyavahārānupapattiḥ / yadi hi buddhirhetoḥ phalasya vā draṣṭrī syāt tadānantaryapratiniyamasya cānusandhātrī kalpitā / tadyogād draṣṭṛtvaṃ pratisandhātṛtvaṃ cocyata iti syādapi prativiṣayamalabdhaviśeṣāyāṃ ca buddhau saṃbandho 'pi na viśeṣaṃ vyavahārayitumīśaḥ - adhunā nibandhanādhigantā, adhunā phalasya, idānīṃ pratisandhāteti / tathāvidhabuddhigataviśeṣasvīkāre tu kimapareṇātmanā kartavyam, tāvataiva paryāptatvād vyavahārasya /
body.translated_text: For consider: are the cognitions to be connected non-different from, different from, or both different and non-different from the self? In the first alternative, either the self itself would be the connector, or the cognitions themselves would be what is to be connected — so what purpose does the connection serve? In the alternative of difference too, we do not understand what purpose the connection of an inert self, which is different from the cognitions, would serve. If [it is said that] the capacity to connect is like the capacity to see, due to association with cognition — then if one accepts the rule that cognition itself is the seer and the connector, and that this [self] is such merely through association with it, then what is the use of this borrowed ornament [i.e., the self]? If [it is said that] cognitions lack agency — then even through that [association], the practical usage of the self as seer and so forth would be untenable. For if cognition were the seer of the cause or the effect and were posited as the connector of the invariable succession — and if it is said that the capacity to see and to connect is [attributed to the self] through association with it — then it might be so; but when cognition has not acquired a distinction with respect to each object, even the [self’s] connection is not capable of establishing the distinction: ‘now it apprehends the ground, now the effect, now it connects.’ But if one accepts such distinctions as belonging to cognition, what need is there of yet another self, since practical usage is complete with just that much?

body.text: sthirātmānamantareṇa saiva buddhirna syāditi cet / kenaivaṃ pratārito 'si / aho mohamāhātmyaṃ yadīdṛśānapi paravaśīkaroti / tathā hi nedamidamantareṇa yaducyate tat khalvanyatra pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ sāmarthyāvadhāraṇe sati yujyate vahneriva dhūme, cakṣurādivadvā dṛṣṭakāraṇāntarasāmagryā kāryādarśane paścād darśane ca kiñcidanyadapekṣaṇīyamastīti sāmānyākāreṇa /
body.translated_text: If [it is objected that] without a permanent self, that very cognition would not exist — by whom have you been so deceived? Ah, how great is the power of delusion, that it subjugates even such [thinkers] as you! For the claim that ‘this cannot exist without that’ is proper only elsewhere, where the capacity [of one thing to produce another] is ascertained through perception and non-apprehension, as fire [is ascertained] in smoke; or, as with the visual faculty and the like, when in a general way [one infers that] there must be something else required, because the effect is not seen when the observed aggregate of other causes is present, and is seen [when something additional is present].

body.text: ādyaḥ pakṣastāvannāstīti vyaktam / dvitīyo 'pi na saṃbhavī / na hi kāraṇabuddhisamanantaraṃ kāryabuddhau satyāṃ niścayapravṛttasyedamasyānantaraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ mayeti pratisandhānamadṛṣṭapūrvaṃ kadācit yato 'nyasya sāmarthyaparikalpanaṃ syādityudasya vyāmohamuktakrameṇaiva kāryakāraṇagrahaṇavyavasthā svīkartavyā /
body.translated_text: The first alternative clearly does not hold. The second too is not possible. For when, immediately after the cognition of the cause, the cognition of the effect arises, and one who has proceeded to ascertainment [thinks] ‘this was seen by me immediately after that’ — such connection has never been observed [to require a separate self]; therefore, there is no [ground for] fabricating the capacity of another [entity]. Setting aside this confusion, the establishment of the apprehension of cause-effect relations should be accepted in the very manner already explained.

body.text: bhedābhedapakṣastu dhikkāra eva, tasyaiva tadapekṣayā bhedābhedaviruddhadharmādhyāsādekatvānupapatteḥ / tataśca yadbhinnaṃ bhinnamevābhinnaṃ cābhinnamiti naikasya bhedābhedau /tathāpyabhede viśvamekamiti yugapadutpādasthitipralayaprasaṅgaḥ / evaṃ kramivastugrāhakaiḥ kramijñānairupādānopādeyabhūtaiḥ sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa krameṇāmī jāyanta iti niścayo janyate / aikakālikānekavastugrāhakaireva tajjñānairekopādānatvāt sakṛdimāni jātānīti vikalpaḥ kriyata iti kramākramagrahaṇamapyanavadyam /
body.translated_text: The alternative of both difference and non-difference is simply contemptible, because, given the superimposition of contradictory properties — difference and non-difference — upon the very same thing considered from the same perspective, unity is untenable. And yet, if there were non-difference, the universe would be one, and there would follow simultaneous origination, persistence, and destruction. Thus, through sequential cognitions that apprehend sequential objects and that stand in the relation of substratum and supervenient,

body.text: kathamanekajñānādekavikalpa iti cet / ki doṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: If asked how a single <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) [arises] from many cognitions — what is the fault?

children.translated_text: Let the cognitions be different; nevertheless, they, standing in the relation of substratum [and supervenient], produce a single conceptualization.

children.text: na bhinnasaṃkhyā phalahetubādhinī na cānyasantānabhavā ivākṣamāḥ //
children.translated_text: The plurality of causes does not obstruct the [production of] the result, nor are [cognitions in the same continuum] incapable like those belonging to another continuum.

body.text: yadapyuktaṃ śaṅkareṇa pūrvottarakṣaṇayoḥ saṃvittīḥ, tābhyāṃ vāsanā, tayā hetuphalabhāvādhyavasāyī vikalpa iti cet / kimidānīṃ yatkiñcidāśaṅkitena vaktavyamityevaṃ vidhiranuṣṭhīyate bhavatā / vikalpo hi gṝhītānusandhānamatadrūpasamāropo vā syāt / na tāvat pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ, adṛṣṭānvayavyatirekasya puruṣasya hetuphalabhāvāgrahe 'nusandhānapratyayahetorvāsanāviśeṣasyaivānupapatteḥ / agṛhītasya cānusandhāne 'tiprasaṅgāditi /
body.translated_text: And as for what <s>Śaṅkara</s> has said — that there are awarenesses of the prior and subsequent moments; from those two, <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression); and from that, a <s>vikalpa</s> that determines the cause-effect relation — if so objected: is this kind of rule observed by you, that one must respond to whatever objection anyone might raise? For the <s>vikalpa</s> would be either the recollection of what has been apprehended, or the superimposition of what is not of that nature. The first alternative does not hold, because the person [attempting to establish the invariable concomitance and its absence] has not observed [them],

body.text:
(#Nibandh 127#)
tadetanna samyagālocitam / yato hetuphalabhūtayoḥ pūrvottarakṣaṇayorekaikena jñānenānanubhave 'pyupādānopādeyabhūtābhyāṃ kramijñānābhyāṃ hetuphalatve gṛhīte eva / kevalaṃ hetukāle phalābhāvāt / tadviṣayasāmarthyagrahaṇe 'pi phalādarśanāt tadavasāya evāpravṛttaḥ kāryadarśanena pravartyate / tathā phalāvalokane 'pi tatkāryatā gṛhītaiva vikalpenānusandhīyata iti gṛhītānusandhānarūpa evāyaṃ vikalpa iti yatkiñcidetat /
body.translated_text: This has not been properly considered. Because even without both the prior and subsequent moments being experienced by a single cognition, when the cause-effect relation is apprehended through sequential cognitions that stand in the relation of substratum and supervenient — [this suffices]. It is simply that at the time of the cause, the effect is absent. Even when the capacity regarding that object is apprehended, because the effect is not seen, that determination itself [remains] inoperative; [but] upon seeing the effect, it operates.

body.text: yadāha mahābhāṣyālaṅkāraḥ
body.translated_text: As the great commentator of the <s>Alaṅkāra</s> says:

children.translated_text: Even if a single perception does not possess [awareness of] prior and subsequent [moments],
when two perceptions exist, how [is there] the awareness of the prior through the later?

body.text: tathā smaraṇamabhilāṣaḥ, svayaṃ vihitapratyanumārgaṇam, dṛṣṭārthakutūhalaviramaṇam, karmaphalasaṃbandhaḥ, saṃśayapūrvakanirṇayaśca pūrvapūrvānubhavaikopādānakāraṇaiḥ samarpitasaṃskāragatairuttarottarārthānubhavaivopādeyabhūtairjanyamāno yujyata iti kimadhikenātmanā parikalpitena / upādānopādeyabhāvaniyamādeva ca na santānāntare smaraṇādiprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ / kimidamupādānamiti cet / ucyate / yatsantānanivṛttyā yadutpadyate tattasyopādānakāraṇam / yathā mṛtsantānanivṛttyotpadyamānasya kumbhasya mṛdupādānamiti śāstre prapañcitam / na cātra paralokakṣatiḥ //
body.translated_text: Likewise, recollection, desire, the retracing of one’s own previous path, the cessation of curiosity about a previously seen object, the connection of action and result, and the ascertainment preceded by doubt — these, being produced by subsequent experiences of objects which serve as the supervenient [cognitions], [and which receive] dispositions transmitted by earlier experiences serving as the substratum-causes — are all properly [explained]; what need is there of a fabricated additional self? The relation of substratum and supervenient

body.text: yadapyuktam - cittaśarīrayoḥ kiyatkālasthitinibandhanasya dṛṣṭasya nivṛttau cittasyāpi nivṛttiprasaṅgaḥ / maraṇavedanayā hi cittaṃ vikalam / tato 'vikalā cittāntarajananāvasthā na saṃbhavati / tasmādupasthite maraṇaduḥkhe sarvasaṃskāravirodhini cittamapyucchidyeteti nāstikyamāyātamiti / tadayuktam / yato maraṇaduḥkhaṃ cittaviśeṣa eva, tasya cittāntarajananasāmarthyasvabhāvasya svabhāvādavāryaiva jñānotpattiriti / bandhānmokṣo 'pi saṃsāricitta sabandhādanāśravacittaprabandho yaḥ / śubhādimokṣayorapi pravṛttiravāryā / yataḥ satyapyātmanyahameva mukto bhaviṣyāmi sukhī cetyātmagrahaṇakṣaṇādadhyavasāyāt pravartate / na punarātmanā galahastitaḥ / sa cānādyavidyāparamparāyātaḥ pūrvāparayorekatvāropako mithyāsaṅkalpo bādhite 'pyātmanyavyāhataprasara iti kathamapravṛttiḥ / nanu
body.translated_text: And as for what was said — that upon the cessation of the observed basis for the duration of mind and body, there would follow the cessation of mind as well; for the mind is impaired by the sensation of death; from that, an impaired condition would not be able to produce another mind; therefore, when the suffering of death — which opposes all dispositions — is at hand, the mind too would be annihilated, and thus nihilism would result — that is incorrect.

body.text:
nairātmyavādapakṣe (tu) pūrvamevāvabudhyate /
madvināśātphalaṃ na syānmatto 'nyasyāthavā bhavet // iti /
body.translated_text:
In the position of the <s>nairātmya-vāda</s> (doctrine of no-self), one understands beforehand:
‘From my destruction, there would be no result; or it would belong to another.’

body.text: apravṛttirevāstviti cet / astu, ko doṣaḥ / yadyayamātmagraho nirviṣayo 'pi pravṛttimanākṣipta kṣaṇamapi sthātuṃ (na) prabhavati / yathā hi jātasyāvaśyaṃ mṛtyuriti (#Nibandh 128#) jñātavatopyapratikriyaputrādimaraṇe sorastāḍamākrando maraṇādau ca yatnaḥ śokodrekāt evamavidyodrekādeva nairātmyaṃ jānannapi pravartate, na sukhamāsta iti kimatra kriyatām, avidyāyāḥ pravartanaśakteravāryatvāt / pratyabhijñā ca pūrvameva dhvastā / kāryakāraṇabhāvaniyatā paścādbhāvipūrvabhāvitā / sā ca kṣaṇike 'pyaviruddhā / upādānopādeyatā ca kramisvasaṃvedanajñānadvayena sākṣātkṛtā tatpṛṣṭhabhāvinā niścīyata iti, asatyapyātmani pratisandhātari kāryakāraṇagrahaṇādaya upapadyamānā nātmānamupasthāpayituṃ prabhavanti / ato 'rthāpattirati na kṣameti bhāgyahīnamanorājyamiva sthirasiddhirviśīryata eva / tathā ca kṣaṇabhaṅgasandehe sattvādyanumānaṃ prāptāvasaram //
body.translated_text: If [it is said that] there would simply be no engagement [in virtuous action] — let it be so; what is the fault? Even if this grasping of a self is without a [real] object, it is unable to remain even for a moment without impelling activity. For just as even one who knows that death is certain for one who is born, upon the death of a son and the like against which there is no remedy, [still] lets out a cry of lamentation, and makes effort at the time of death and the like, due to the surge of grief — so too, even knowing <s>nairātmya</s> (no-self), due to the very surge of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),

body.text: // sthirasiddhidūṣaṇaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇa</s> (Refutation of the Proof of a Permanent [Self]) is completed.

body.text: // citrādvaitaprakāśavādaḥ //
body.translated_text: // <s>Citrādvaitaprakāśavāda</s> (Discourse on Variegated Non-Dual Luminosity) //

body.text: // namastārāyai //
body.translated_text: // Homage to <s>Tārā</s> //

children.translated_text: This direction of discourse, which establishes [the refutation of] all opposing positions, both one’s own and others’,
destroys the mass of darkness that is the ignorance of the <s>citrādvaita</s> (variegated non-dual) doctrine.

body.text: iha khalu sakalajaḍapadārtharāśau pratyākhyāte nirākṛte ca nirākāravijñānavāde pratihate cālīkākārayogini pāramārthikaprakāśamātre samyagunmūlite ca sākāravijñānālīkatvasamārope pratisantānaṃ ca svapnavadabādhitadehabhogapratiṣṭhādyākāraprakāśamātrātmake jagati vyavasthite yasya yadā yāvadākāracakrapratibhāsaṃ yadvijñānaṃ parisphurati tasya tadā tāvadākāracakraparikaritaṃ tadvijñānaṃ citrādvaitamiti sthitiḥ / tadevaṃ citramadvaitaṃ vijñānamiti padatrayamiha pratyupasthitam //
body.translated_text: Here, when the entire mass of inert entities has been rejected, and the doctrine of formless consciousness (<s>nirākāra-vijñāna-vāda</s>) has been refuted, and the [position that admits] unreal forms [in consciousness] has been defeated, and the superimposition of unreality upon consciousness-with-form (<s>sākāra-vijñāna</s>) has been properly uprooted in [the doctrine of] ultimate luminosity alone — and when the world has been established as, in each continuum, consisting of mere luminosity of form like a dream, with uncontradicted appearances of body, enjoyment, and support — whoever, whenever, and to whatever extent the assemblage of forms

body.text: atra ca vipratipattirnāma kiṃ citratāyāmadvaite vijñānatve sarvatraiveti vikalpāḥ //
body.translated_text: And here, the disagreement is as follows: is it regarding variegatedness, regarding non-duality, regarding the nature of consciousness, or regarding all [of these]? — these are the alternatives.

body.text: na tāvadasau citrasvarūpānusāriṇī bhavitumarhati, tanmātrasya sarvajñānubhavasiddhatvāt, anyathā śaśaviṣāṇādāviva jaḍamidamalīkaṃ vijñānaṃ veti vipratipattīnāmanavakāśaprasaṅgāt / nāpi vijñānatve vivādaḥ kartuṃmucitaḥ,
body.translated_text: To begin with, that [disagreement] cannot pertain to the variegated nature, because that alone is established by everyone’s experience; otherwise, just as with a hare’s horn, there would follow the impossibility of disagreements such as ‘this is inert,’ ‘this is unreal,’ ‘this is consciousness,’ and so forth. Nor is it proper to dispute the nature of consciousness,

body.text: sahopalambhaniyamād
body.translated_text: because of the rule of co-apprehension (<s>sahopalambha-niyama</s>) —

body.text: ityādinā pūrvameva nīlādīnāṃ sākāravijñānatvaprasādhanāt / ata eva sarvatrāpi vimatirasaṅgatā, sākāravijñānasiddhāveva citrādvaitavādāvatārāt / tasmāccitrateyamadvaitavirodhinīti vyāmohādekatva eva vipratiprattiriti tatra prasādhanaṃ sādhanamidamucyate //
body.translated_text: and so forth — since the nature of blue and the like as consciousness-with-form has been previously established. For this very reason, disagreement regarding all [aspects] too is incoherent, since the <s>citrādvaita-vāda</s> (doctrine of variegated non-duality) enters [the discussion] only upon the establishment of consciousness-with-form. Therefore, because this [disagreement about] variegatedness contradicts non-duality, it is due to confusion that the disagreement pertains to unity alone — and the proof establishing that is now stated.

body.text: yat prakāśate tadekam / yathā citrākāracakramadhyavartī nīlākāraḥ / prakāśate cedaṃ gauragāndhāramadhurasurabhisukumārasātetarādivicitrākārakadambakamiti svabhāvahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Whatever is luminous is one — like the blue aspect situated within a variegated assemblage of forms. And this variegated cluster of forms such as white, Gāndhāra [tone], sweet, fragrant, soft, pleasant, and so forth is luminous — this is a reason based on essential nature (<s>svabhāva-hetu</s>).

body.text: na tāvadasyāsiddhirabhidhātuṃ śakyate, pratyakṣapramāṇaprasiddhasadbhāve vijñānātmakanīlādyākāracakre dharmiṇi prakāśamānatāyāḥ pratyakṣasiddhatvāt / na cāsya (#Nibandh 130#) hetorviruddhatā saṃbhavati, vicitrākāramadhyavartini nīlākāre dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi prakāśamānatālakṣaṇasya sādhanasya dṛṣṭatvāt / nanu caikatve sādhye yadaparamekatvādhikaraṇaṃ tadiha dṛṣṭāntīkartumucitam / na cāsya nīlākārasya ekatā vidyate, viruddhadharmādhyāsaprasiddhasyānekatvasya saṃbhavāt / deśakālākārabhedo hi viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ / tataśca yathā citritākāracakrasyākārabhedato bhedastathā nīlākārasyāpi deśabhedato bhedaḥ / tadayaṃ sādhyaśūnyo dṛṣṭānto hetuśca vipakṣe paridṛśyamāno yadi tatraiva niyatastadā viruddhaḥ //
body.translated_text: To begin with, its unestablishedness cannot be asserted, because the property-locus — the assemblage of forms such as blue and the like, which are of the nature of consciousness — is well-established through the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) of perception; and the being-luminous of the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) is established through perception in the example-property-locus, namely the blue aspect situated within a variegated [assemblage]. Nor can the contradictoriness of this reason be maintained, because the probans characterized by being-luminous is observed in the example-property-locus, the blue aspect situated within a variegated form.

body.text: tatrāpi saṃbhave 'naikānta iti cet / atrocyate / yadi deśabhedato vijñānātmakasthūlanīlākārasya bhedastadāsya pratiparamāṇudeśabhede bhedasaṃbhavātu paramāṇupracayamātrātmako vijñānātmakasthūlanīlākāraḥ syāt / tathā ca sati sarveṣāṃ vijñāna(a)tmakanīlaparamāṇūnāṃ svasvarūpanimagnatvena saṃtamasanimagnānekapuruṣavat vyativedanābhāvāt sthūlanīlākhaṇḍalakapratibhāsābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ syāt, grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇayoḥ purastādapakartavyatvāt / na caivaṃ vaktavyam paramāṇūnāṃ svarūpanimagnatve 'pyekopādānatayā puñjātmaiva sthūlaḥ sthūlamātmānaṃ jñāsyatīti, satyapyekopādānatve svasvarūpanimagnatvādeva sthūlavyavasthāpakasya bhinnasyātmano 'nyonyaṃ vā grāhyagrāhakabhāvasyāyogāt / tādātmyena vyativedanasya cānabhyupagamāt /
body.translated_text: If one objects: 'Even there [in that case], when possibility [exists], it would be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>)' — to this we reply: If there is a difference in the consciousness-natured gross blue appearance due to spatial differentiation, then since its differentiation is possible with respect to each atomic locus, the consciousness-natured gross blue appearance would be nothing but an aggregate of atoms. And in that case, since all consciousness-natured blue atoms are absorbed in their own respective natures — like many persons immersed in darkness who do not cognize one another — there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of a single unbroken appearance of gross blue, which would be consistent [with the opponent's view], since the perceiver-perceived [distinction] is to be eliminated from the outset. Nor should one say: 'Even though the atoms are absorbed in their own nature, being of a single material cause, the gross [appearance] as an aggregate will cognize itself as gross' — because even though there is a single material cause, since [the atoms] are absorbed in their own respective natures, a distinct self that would establish the gross [appearance], or a mutual perceiver-perceived relation, is impossible. And because mutual cognition through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is not admitted.

body.text: vargo vargaṃ vetti
body.translated_text: 'A group knows a group' —

body.text: ityasyānupadatvāt / na ca yathā bāhyārthavāde sthūlaikākārajñānapratibhāsa eva bāhyaparamāṇupracayapratibhāsavyavasthā gatyantarābhāvāt, tathā jñānaparamāṇupracayavyavasthā(paka) sthūlaikākārayogivijñānāntarasthānabhyupagamāt / abhyupagame vā tasyaiva dṛṣṭāntatvāt / tasmād yāvad yāvat pratibhāsastāvattāvat sthūlatayaiva vyāptaḥ / asthūle paramāṇau sthūlanivṛttimātre ca pratibhāsasya dṛśyānupalambhabādhitatvāt / yathā prasiddhānumāne sattvaṃ kṣaṇikatvena vyāptaṃ kramākramakāritvenāpi, kṣaṇikatvābhāvācca karmākramanivṛttau nivartamānaṃ kṣaṇikatve niyataṃ sidhyati, tathātrāpi prakāśamānatvaṃ sādhanamekatvenāpi sthaulyenāpi, ekatvābhāvācca vipakṣāt paramāṇupuñjātmana ekatvanivṛttimātrātmanaśca svaviruddhopalambhāt sthaulyasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau nivartamānamekatvaṃ niyataṃ sidhyati / tataśca yathā bahirvyāptipakṣe ghaṭe dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalāt sattvaṃ kṣaṇikatvaniyatamavadhārya sattvāt pakṣe kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ, ta(thā) trāpi nīlākāre dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalādeva prakāśamānatvamekatvaniyatamavagamya prakāśamānatvād vicitrākāracakre sādhyadharmiṇyekatvasiddhiriti na dṛṣṭāntasya sādhyaśūnyatvam / nāpi hetorviruddhatā / na cānaikāntikatā //
body.translated_text: this [maxim] is inapplicable here. Nor [should one say]: 'Just as in the external realism position (<s>bāhyārthavāda</s>), the arrangement of external atomic aggregates is established through the very appearance of a single gross form in cognition, for lack of any other possibility — so too [one can establish] a consciousness-atomic-aggregate arrangement' — because a separate cognition of a yogin having a single gross form that would establish the arrangement of cognitive atoms is not admitted. Or if it were admitted, that very [cognition] would serve as the example [and the argument would be circular]. Therefore, to whatever extent there is appearance, to that extent it is pervaded by grossness alone. Because appearance is contradicted by the non-perception of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>) in [the case of] a non-gross atom and in the mere absence of grossness. Just as in a well-known inference, existence (<s>sattva</s>) is pervaded by momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) and also by sequential-and-simultaneous causal efficacy, and [the reason], turning away from [the <s>vipakṣa</s> which is characterized by] the absence of momentariness — [namely] the mere absence of sequential-and-simultaneous [efficacy] — is established as determined [to entail] momentariness; so too here, being-manifest (<s>prakāśamānatva</s>) is a reason for both unity (<s>ekatva</s>) and grossness (<s>sthaulya</s>), and since the pervader — grossness — is excluded from the <s>vipakṣa</s> (which is the mere aggregate of atoms and the mere absence of unity) through the perception of what is pervaded by the contrary, the absence of unity turns away [from that <s>vipakṣa</s>], and unity is established as necessary. Therefore, just as in the external pervasion thesis, having ascertained in the pot — the example-subject — by the force of the <s>pramāṇa</s> refuting the contrary that existence is necessarily [connected with] momentariness, the establishment of momentary destruction in the thesis-subject [follows] from existence; so too here, having understood in the blue appearance — the example-subject — by the very force of the <s>pramāṇa</s> refuting the contrary that being-manifest is necessarily [connected with] unity, the establishment of unity in the thesis-subject — the manifold array of forms — [follows] from being-manifest. Therefore the example is not devoid of the <s>sādhya</s>. Nor is the reason contradictory. Nor is it inconclusive.

body.text: nanvekatve sādhye tatpracyutirdvitvaṃ ca vipakṣaḥ, tasmācca vipakṣāddhetuvyatirekapratipattyavasare kiṃ vipakṣātmā prakāśate na vā / pratibhāsapakṣe prakāśamānatvasya (#Nibandh 131#) hetoḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntikatā, vipakṣe 'pi dṛṣṭatvāt / atha na prakāśate tadā sandigdhavyatirekitvam, kuto vyatireka ityavadherevāprakāśamānaśarīratvāt kathamataḥ sādhyasiddhipratyāśā /
body.translated_text: But [one objects]: When unity is the <s>sādhya</s>, the loss of that [unity] and duality constitute the <s>vipakṣa</s>; and at the occasion of comprehending the exclusion of the reason from that <s>vipakṣa</s>, does the <s>vipakṣa</s> itself appear or not? If it appears — then being-manifest (<s>prakāśamānatva</s>), the reason, (Nibandha 131) is commonly inconclusive (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), since it is seen in the <s>vipakṣa</s> too. If it does not appear — then [the reason has] doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>); for since the body [of the <s>vipakṣa</s>] is precisely of the nature of not-appearing, whence comes the exclusion? — and how can there be hope of establishing the <s>sādhya</s> from this?

body.text: atrocyate / iha dvividho vijñānānāṃ viṣayaḥ grāhyo 'dhyavaseyaśca / pratibhāsamāno grāhyaḥ / agṛhīto 'pi pravṛttiviṣayo 'dhyavaseyaḥ / tatrāsarvajñe 'numātarisakalavipakṣapratibhāsābhāvānna grāhyatayā vipakṣo viṣayo vaktavyaḥ, sarvānumānocchedaprasaṅgāt, sarvatra sakalavipakṣapratibhāsābhāvāt tato vyatirekāsiddheḥ / pratibhāse ca deśakālasvabhāvāntaritasakalavipakṣa sākṣātkāre sādhyātmāpi varākaḥ sutarāṃ pratīyata ityanumānavaiyarthyam / tasmādapratibhāse 'pyadhyavasāyasiddhādeva vipakṣād dhūmādervyatireko niścitaḥ / tat kimarthamatra vipakṣapratibhāsaḥ prārthyate / yadi punarasyādhyavasāyo 'pi na syāttadā vyatireko na niścīyata iti yuktam, pratiniyataviṣayavyavahārābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: To this we reply: Here, the object of cognitions is twofold: the grasped (<s>grāhya</s>) and the determined (<s>adhyavaseya</s>). What appears is the grasped. What is not grasped but is the object of practical activity is the determined. In that case, for a non-omniscient reasoner, since the entire <s>vipakṣa</s> does not appear, the <s>vipakṣa</s> should not be claimed as an object in the mode of being-grasped — for there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of all inference, since in all [inferences] there is no appearance of the entire <s>vipakṣa</s>, and therefore the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) from it would be unestablished. And if all the <s>vipakṣa</s> separated by space, time, and nature were directly perceived in appearance, then the poor <s>sādhya</s> itself would be all the more evident — and inference would be pointless. Therefore, the exclusion of smoke and the like from the <s>vipakṣa</s> is ascertained through determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) alone, even without appearance. So why is the appearance of the <s>vipakṣa</s> demanded here? If, however, there were not even a determination of it [the <s>vipakṣa</s>], then it would be proper [to say] that the negative concomitance is not ascertained, because there would be no practical activity with a determinate object.

body.text: nanvasmanmate vastvavastvātmakasakalavipakṣapratipattisaṃbhavāt tato hetuvyatirekaḥ saṃpratyetuṃ śakyata eva / na ca pratibhāsamātreṇa sattvaprasaṅgaḥ, arthakriyākāritvalakṣaṇatvāt sattvasya / tvanmate tu prakāśa eva vastutvam / ato vipakṣayorekatvapracyutirdvitvayoḥ pratibhāse prakāśamānatvasādhanasya vipakṣasādhāraṇatā / apratibhāse casandigdhavyatirekitvamiti codyaṃ duruddharameveti cet / tadetadasaṅgatam / tathā hi dhūmādiravahnyādervipakṣād vyāvṛtto vahnyādiniyataḥ sidhyati, tasya ca vastvavastvātmakasakalavipakṣapadārtharāśeḥ svarūpanirbhāsa iti kiṃ nirvikalpakajñāne kalpanāyāṃ vā / nirvikalpe cet / pratibhāsa iti ca ko 'rthaḥ / kiṃ nirākāre jñāne sakalavipakṣādisvarūpasya sākṣāt sphuraṇam, yadi vā tadarpitabuddhisvabhāvabhūtasadṛśākāraprakāśaḥ, atha samanantarapratyayabalāyātabuddhigatabāhyasadṛśākārapratibhāsaḥ, āhosvid buddherātmabhūtavipakṣasadṛśālīkākāraparisphūrtiḥ /
body.translated_text: But [one objects]: In our [Buddhist] system, since the comprehension of the entire <s>vipakṣa</s> — consisting of both real and unreal entities — is possible, the exclusion of the reason from it can indeed be understood. Nor does the mere appearance [of something] entail its existence, because existence is defined as possessing causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>). But in your system, appearance itself constitutes reality (<s>vastutvam</s>). Therefore, if there is appearance of the two <s>vipakṣas</s> — the loss of unity and duality — then the reason of being-manifest is common to the <s>vipakṣa</s>. And if there is no appearance, then there is doubtful negative concomitance — so the objection is irrefutable. If one says this — that is incoherent. For smoke and the like are established as excluded from the <s>vipakṣa</s> — fire-absence and the like — and as necessarily connected with fire and the like; and does the entire mass of <s>vipakṣa</s> objects consisting of real and unreal entities manifest its own form in non-conceptual cognition or in conceptual cognition? If in non-conceptual [cognition] — then what does 'appearance' mean? Is it the direct shining forth of the intrinsic form of the entire <s>vipakṣa</s> in a formless cognition? Or the manifestation of a similar form that is of the nature of cognition and imparted by that [object]? Or the appearance of a similar form of the external [object] that has come into cognition through the force of the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>)? Or the manifestation of a false form resembling the <s>vipakṣa</s> that is intrinsic to cognition?

body.text: na tāvadādyaḥ pakṣo yuktaḥ, deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭānāṃ padārthānāmarvācīne jane nirākāre ca jñāne sphuraṇāyogādityasyārthasya śāstre eva vistareṇa prasādhanāt / sphuraṇe cāsādhyasyāpi prakāśanaprasaṅge 'numānavaiyarthyasya pratipādanāt /
body.translated_text: The first alternative is not tenable, because it is extensively demonstrated in the treatise itself that things distant in space, time, and nature cannot shine forth in a cognition of an ordinary person and in a formless cognition. And because it has been shown that if they were to shine forth, even the <s>sādhya</s> would be evident, making inference pointless.

body.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ, deśādiviprakṛṣṭatvādeva sākṣātsvākārasamarpaṇasāmarthyābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is the second alternative [tenable], because due to the very remoteness in space and so forth, there is no capacity [of the object] to directly impart its own form.

body.text: na ca tṛtīyaḥ saṅgataḥ, sādṛśyasaṃbhave 'pi samanantarabalādevāyātasya bāhyena saha pratyāsatterabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: Nor is the third coherent, because even if similarity is possible, for [a form] that has come merely through the force of the immediately preceding [condition], there is no proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>) with the external [object].

body.text: na caturtho 'pi prakāra saṃbhavati, asatprakāśayorvirodhāt, sphurato 'lokatvāyogāt / tathā hyasatprakāśa iti kimasadīśvarādeḥ khyātiḥ, bhāsamāno vā ākāro 'san, san vā na kaścit khyātīti vivakṣitam / tatra yasya padārthasya svarūpaparinirbhāsaḥ sa kathamasanniti prāṇadhāribhirabhidhātavyaḥ / sphurataḥ keśoṇḍukākārasya (#Nibandh 132#) bāhyarūpatayā bādhyatve 'pi jñānarūpatayārthatvasya ācāryeṇa pratipāditatvāt grāhakābhimatanirākāraprakāśasyāpyasattvābhidhānaprasaṅgāt //
body.translated_text: Nor is the fourth manner possible, because there is a contradiction between unreality (<s>asat</s>) and manifestation (<s>prakāśa</s>) — for what shines forth cannot logically be unreal. For what is meant by 'manifestation of the unreal'? Is it: (a) the appearance of an unreal [entity] such as <s>Īśvara</s>? Or (b) that the appearing form is unreal? Or (c) that something real does not appear at all? Regarding the first: how can one who breathes say that that whose intrinsic form shines forth is unreal? For even though the appearance of floating-hair forms (Nibandha 132) may be refuted as an external reality, the Master has demonstrated that it has reality as a form of cognition. And there would be the absurd consequence of declaring even the admitted formless illumination of the apprehending [consciousness] to be unreal.

body.text: pratibhāse 'pi bādhanādasatyatvamiti cet / kiṃ tad bādhakam, pratyakṣamanumānaṃ vā / yadyekatra svarūpasākṣātkāriṇi pratyakṣe 'viśvāsaḥ kathamanyatra bādhake svarūpāntaraprakāśa eva nirvṛttistatpūrvakamanumānaṃ ca sutarāmaviśvāsabhājanamiti na bādhakavārtāpi / yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: If one says: 'Even in appearance, [it is] unreal due to being contradicted' — then what is the contradicting [factor]: perception or inference? If there is distrust in perception, which directly apprehends the intrinsic form [of a thing], in one [instance], how [can there be trust] in another [instance]? [And if] confidence comes only from the manifestation of another intrinsic form [by the contradicting perception], then inference, which depends on that [perception], is all the more untrustworthy — so there is not even talk of a contradicting [factor]. As the Masters say:

children.translated_text: 'How can that whose intrinsic form shines forth be unreal?
If [you say] because of being contradicted — but that [contradiction] too is surely [known through] one of perception or inference.

body.text:
pratyakṣe yadyaviśvāsaḥ ekatrānyatra kā gatiḥ /
tatpūrvamanumānaṃ ca kathamāśvāsagocaraḥ // iti /
body.translated_text: If there is distrust in perception in one [case], what recourse [is there] elsewhere? And how can inference, which depends on that, be an object of confidence?'

body.text: nanu
body.translated_text: But [one objects]:

children.translated_text: 'Even what is seen is contradicted, as in the appearance of a double moon and the like;
there is no impossibility in what is seen [being contradicted]; what is known [in one way] may also be refuted.'

body.text: iti cet / na / bādhyasyāpratibhāsanāt / pratibhāsinaścābādhyatvāt / tathā hi

children.translated_text: 'The manifestation belongs to the form in cognition; the refutation is of the external object.
If [there is] distrust even in what shines forth, where then [can there be] trust?' — thus it has been declared.

body.translated_text: No, [we reply], because what is refuted does not appear, and what appears is not refuted. For:

body.text: etena bhāsamāno vā ākāro 'sanniti dvitīyo 'pi pakṣaḥ pratikṣiptaḥ, pratibhāsādeva sattāsiddherbādhakābakāśābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: By this, the second alternative too — 'the appearing form is unreal' — is rejected, because existence is established from appearance itself, and there is no room for a contradicting [factor].

body.text: tathā san vā kaścinna khyātīti tṛtīyasaṅkalpo 'pi vyākulaḥ, prakāśavyāptatvāt sattāyāḥ / aprakāśasyāsattayā grastatvāt //
body.translated_text: Likewise, the third supposition — 'something real does not appear at all' — is also confounded, because existence is pervaded by manifestation. Because what does not manifest is consumed by non-existence.

body.text: nanu prakāśo nāmaḥ vastunaḥ sattāsādhakaṃ pramāṇam / na ca pramāṇanivṛttāvarthābhāvaḥ / arthakriyāśaktistu sattvam / taccāprakāśasyāpi na virudhyata iti cet / satyametat / bahirarthabāde 'prakāśasyāpi sāmarthyābhyupagamāt / keśoṇḍukādipratibhāse 'dhyavasitasyārthakriyāśaktiviyogādevābhāvasiddheḥ / sarvathā bahirabhāve tu jñānasya prakāśāvyabhicārāttāvataiva sattve kimarthakriyayā /
body.translated_text: But [one objects]: Manifestation is [merely] a <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the existence of a thing. And the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> does not [entail] the absence of the thing. Rather, causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāśakti</s>) is existence. And that is not contradicted even for what does not manifest. If one says this — that is true [in a sense]. Since even in the refutation of external objects, the capacity [for causal efficacy] is admitted even for what does not manifest. And since in the appearance of floating hairs and the like, the absence of what is determined [to exist externally] is established by the very separation from causal efficacy. But when external [objects] are entirely absent, since manifestation (<s>prakāśa</s>) never deviates from cognition, existence is [established] by that much alone — what need is there for causal efficacy?

children.translated_text: 'How would the existence of what is in another's heart [be established] if not from manifestation alone?

children.text: nārthakriyāpi sarvasmai kvacicced bhāsanaṃ na kim //
children.translated_text: If causal efficacy too [is required, it] is not [available] to everyone; and if [something] appears somewhere, why [is that] not [sufficient]?'

body.text: iti / nirvikalpe tāvat svasaṃvedanasiddhasvākāramantareṇa vipakṣādayo na parisphuranti / athāmī vikalpe pratibhāsanta iti dvitīyaḥ saṅkalpo 'bhyupagamyate, asminnapi pakṣe pratibhāsamāna ākāro 'sādhāraṇo 'śabdasaṃsṛṣṭatayā svasaṃvedanatādātmye praviṣṭatvādvastusanneva /
body.translated_text: In non-conceptual [cognition], without [considering] one's own form established by self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), the <s>vipakṣa</s> and the like do not shine forth. If, however, the second supposition is accepted — that they appear in conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) — even in this case, the appearing form, being uncommon and having entered into identity with self-awareness through not being mixed with words, is a real entity indeed.

body.text: adhyavaseyatayā vipakṣādayo gṛhyanta iti cet / tadāpi teṣāṃ svarūpasya nirbhāso 'sti na vā / nirbhāse pratyakṣasiddhataiva, nāsatkhyātiḥ / śāstre 'pi
body.translated_text: If one says: 'The <s>vipakṣa</s> and the like are grasped in the mode of being-determined (<s>adhyavaseya</s>)' — even then, does their intrinsic form shine forth or not? If it shines forth, it is established by perception itself — there is no cognition of the unreal (<s>asatkhyāti</s>). In the treatise too:

body.text:
(#Nibandh 133#)
'svarūpasākṣātkāritvameva pratyakṣatvam'
body.translated_text: (Nibandha 133) 'Being a direct apprehender of the intrinsic form is itself perceptuality (<s>pratyakṣatva</s>)' —

body.text: uktam / tasya cetarapratyakṣeṣviva vikalpe 'pi svīkāre viruddhavyāptopalambhena vikalpabhrāntatvayordūramapāstatvādvikalpe 'pi tvanmate pratyakṣatvamakṣatam / tat kathaṃ tatsiddhasya pratyakṣāntarānumānābhyāṃ bādhābhidhānam, tayorapi svarūpāntaraprakāśapauruṣatvāt //
body.translated_text: this has been stated. And if that [perceptuality] is accepted in conceptual cognition just as in other [forms of] perception, then since the perception of what is pervaded by the contradictory (<s>viruddhavyāptopalambha</s>) has thoroughly eliminated the [claim that] conceptual [cognition] is erroneous, perceptuality in conceptual cognition too is unimpaired in your system. How then can refutation by another perception or inference be asserted for what is established by that [conceptual perception], since those [other perceptions and inferences] too have their power only in manifesting another intrinsic form?

body.text: atha vikalpabhrāntatvayorvyāpakaviruddhayoḥ saṃbhavāt vikalpe pratyakṣatvamevāsaṃbhavi / nanvasya pratyakṣatvamasaṃbhavīti svarūpasākṣātkāritvamasaṃbhavītyuktam / atha vipakṣādirartho 'smin prakāśata iti vācā svarūpasākṣātkāritvaṃ kathitamiti mātā me bandhyeti vṛttāntaḥ / iṣyate ca tvayā vipakṣādisvarūpasākṣātkāritvaṃ bikalpasyeti pratyakṣatānatikramaḥ, apratyakṣatve vastusvarūpasphuraṇāyogāt / tataśca tatpratibhāsino 'pi rūpasya sata eva khyātirnāsatkhyātiḥ / na ca tadeva vikalpe parisphuradrūpamasatāmīśvarādīnāṃ svarūpam, asattvasyaivābhāvaprasaṅgāt / svarūpasphuraṇe 'pyasattve 'nyatrāpi prakāśinyanāśvāsāt /
body.translated_text: If [one says]: 'Because the two contradictory pervaders — conceptuality and erroneousness — are possible [together], perceptuality is simply impossible in conceptual cognition' — well, to say 'perceptuality is impossible for it' is to say 'direct apprehension of intrinsic form is impossible [for it]' — [and yet] to say in words 'the <s>vipakṣa</s> and other objects manifest in it' while [claiming] direct apprehension of intrinsic form [is impossible] — that is like the tale of 'my mother is barren.' And since you yourself accept that conceptual cognition directly apprehends the intrinsic form of the <s>vipakṣa</s> and the like, perceptuality is not transcended; because without perceptuality, the shining forth of the real intrinsic form of a thing is impossible. And therefore, the appearance of even that which appears in conceptual cognition is the appearance of a real [entity], not of an unreal one (<s>asatkhyāti</s>). Nor is the very form that shines forth in conceptual cognition the intrinsic form of unreal things such as <s>Īśvara</s> — because there would be the absurd consequence of the non-existence of non-existence itself. And even if the intrinsic form shines forth, if [one insists on] unreality, then there would be lack of confidence in any other manifesting [cognition] as well.

body.text: tato yat sākāravāde jalpitam
body.translated_text: Therefore, what has been argued in the doctrine of [cognition having] form (<s>sākāravāda</s>) —

body.text: nityādayaḥ santa eva syuḥ
body.translated_text: 'Permanent [entities] and the like would have to be real' —

body.text: iti tadātmana eva patitam / yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: that has fallen upon [the proponent] himself. As the Masters say:

children.translated_text: 'Perceptuality arises from the direct apprehension of intrinsic form and from nothing else;
and precisely for this reason, the ground for [claiming that] conceptual [cognition] is erroneous is refuted.

children.text: yadi nādhyakṣatā tasya rūpanirbhāsa eva na /
children.translated_text: If there is no perceptuality for it, then there is no manifestation of [the <s>vipakṣa</s>'s] form;
therefore, [to say] "the unreal <s>Īśvara</s> and the like appear" is incoherent.

children.text: yadi tu pratibhāseta rūpamasya sadeva tat /
children.translated_text: If, however, a form does appear to it, that [form] is real indeed;
and [to say] "the unreal appears" — that too shines as unreal in your [view].'

body.text: athādhyavasāye 'dhyavaseyasvarūpasya pratibhāso nāstītyucyate / na tadā kasyacidadhyavasāyaḥ / kathamataḥ pratiniyatavastuvyavasthāsiddhiḥ / kiṃ ca ko 'yamadhyavasāyonāma / kiṃ vyāvṛttibhedaparikalpitasya prakāśāṃśasya, svākārāṃśasya, alīkākārasya, bāhyavastuno 'vastuno vā sphuraṇamadhyavasāyārthaḥ / yadi vā svākāre bāhyāropaḥ, bāhye vā svākārāropaḥ, svākārabāhyayoryojanā, tayorekīkaraṇamekapratipattirabhedena pratipattiḥ bhedāgraho 'dhyavasāyārtha iti vikalpāḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, if it is said that in <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) there is no appearance of the real nature of the object to be determined—then there is no determination of anything at all. How then is the establishment of the arrangement of determinate objects achieved? Moreover, what is this so-called <s>adhyavasāya</s>? Is the meaning of <s>adhyavasāya</s> the manifestation of: the cognitive aspect (<s>prakāśāṃśa</s>) constructed by the differentiation of exclusions (<s>vyāvṛttibheda</s>); the own-form aspect (<s>svākāra</s>); the false form (<s>alīkākāra</s>); the external object; or a non-entity? Or is it: the superimposition of the external onto the own-form; the superimposition of the own-form onto the external; the conjunction of own-form and external; the unification of the two; a single apprehension; apprehension as non-different; or non-apprehension of difference? These are the alternatives.

body.text: tatra na tāvadādimau pakṣau kalpanāmarhataḥ / svarūpe sarvasyaiva sphuraṇasya nirvikalpatvādavasāyānupapattiḥ / itarathā nirvikalpakajñānābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Of these, the first two alternatives do not merit consideration. Since everyone's manifestation of the own-nature [of cognition] is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), determination (<s>avasāya</s>) is impossible. Otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that non-conceptual cognition would not exist.

body.text: alīkasphuraṇaṃ tu prāk pratyākhyātam /satyapi sphuraṇe 'sphuṭatvānnirvikalpakametat / dvicandrādijñānavat / astu svagrāhye tannirvikalpakam, bāhye tu adhyavaseye (#Nibandh 134#) adhyavasāya iti cet / na tatsaṃbandhābhāvāta, tadapratibhāsācca / anyathātiprasaṅgādityuktaprāyam / bāhyavastusvarūpasphuraṇe tu pratyakṣapratipattirevāsāviti ko 'dhyavasāyaḥ / avastusphuraṇaṃ punastridhā vikalpya prāgeva pratyākhyātam /
body.translated_text: The manifestation of a false [form] has already been refuted. Even if there were manifestation, since it is indistinct, this would be non-conceptual—like the cognition of a double moon etc. 'Let it be non-conceptual with respect to its own object, but <s>adhyavasāya</s> with respect to the external object that is to be determined'—no, because of the absence of a connection with that, and because of the non-appearance of that; otherwise there would be over-extension—this has essentially been stated. If it were the manifestation of the real nature of the external object, that would simply be direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>)—so what is <s>adhyavasāya</s>? And the manifestation of a non-entity, analyzed in three ways, has already been refuted.

body.text: svākāre tu bāhyāropo na saṃbhavatyeva / tathā hi jñānaṃ kenacidākāreṇa satyenālīkena vopajātaṃ nāma / bāhyāropastu tadākāre tatkṛto 'nyakṛto vā syāt / tatkṛtatve na tāvat tatkāla eva vyāpārāntaramanubhūyata iti kutastadāropaḥ / kālāntare ca svayamevāsat kasya vyāpāraḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: The superimposition of the external onto the own-form is simply impossible. For cognition arises with some form, whether real or false. But the superimposition of the external onto that form would be either caused by that [cognition itself] or by something else. If caused by it—no other operation is experienced at that very moment, so whence the superimposition? And at another time, [the cognition] itself being non-existent, whose operation would it be?

body.text: dvitīyapakṣe jñānāntaramapi nākārāroparāgasaṅginīmutpattimantareṇa vyāpārāntareṇa kvacit kiñcitkaraṃ nāma / tadetadarvācīnajñānasadṛśākāragocarīkaraṇe 'pi na bāhyāropavyāpāramaparaṃ spṛśati tadākāraleśānukāramapahāya / na ca śabdāmukhīkaraṇamatirikto vyāpāraḥ, śabdākārasyāpi svarūpa evāntarbhāvāditi nākārādanyo jñānavyāpāraḥ / āropyamāṇaścāsāvartho bāhyaḥ / tatra buddhau yadi svarūpeṇa sphurati satyapratītirevāsau, ka āropaḥ / atha na parisphurati tathāpi ka āropaḥ / sphuraṇe vā adhikaraṇabhūtasvākārātiriktasyāropyamāṇākārasyāpi pratibhāsaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the second alternative [superimposition by another cognition]: another cognition too, without producing an appearance tinged with the form-superimposition, does not accomplish anything through any other operation. And this [subsequent cognition], even in making the form similar to the earlier cognition its object, does not touch any other operation of superimposing the external, apart from imitating a trace of that form. Nor is there any operation beyond making the word-[form] one's primary focus, since even the word-form is included within the own-nature [of cognition]—hence there is no cognitive operation beyond the form. And the object to be superimposed is external. If it appears in the cognition in its own nature, that is simply a real apprehension—what superimposition? If it does not appear, then too—what superimposition? And if there is manifestation, there would be the absurd consequence of the appearance of an additional form-to-be-superimposed, beyond the own-form that serves as the substrate.

body.text: tadākārasphuraṇameva tasya sphuraṇamiti cet / na / tasyāropaviṣayatvāt / na hi marīcisphuraṇameva jalasphuraṇamiti na svākāre bāhyāropaḥ / ata eva bāhye svākārāropo nāsti, āropaviṣayasya bāhyasyāsphuraṇāt / tata eva svākārabāhyayoryojanāpyasaṃbhavinī, yogyayorapratibhāsāt / na caikīkaraṇamadhyavasāyaḥ / ko 'yamekīkaraṇārthaḥ / yadyekatāpattau prayojakatvaṃ tadāropyāropaviṣayayoḥ kadācidekībhāvābhāvādasaṃbhava eva / na hi śaśaviṣāṇe kāraṇaṃ kiñcit / na ca pūrvamanekamekatāmetīti kṣaṇikavādinaḥ sāṃpratam / arthāntarotpattimātraṃ tu syāt / na ca tadupalabdhigocaro 'nyatrāropaviṣayāt svākārāt / na ca tāvatāpyarthasya kiñciditi kathamekīkaraṇam /
body.translated_text: 'The manifestation of that form is itself the manifestation of that [external object]'—no, because that [external object] is the object of superimposition. For the manifestation of a mirage is not itself the manifestation of water. Therefore there is no superimposition of the external onto the own-form. For this very reason, there is no superimposition of the own-form onto the external either, since the external—the object of superimposition—does not appear. For this very reason, the conjunction of own-form and external is also impossible, since the two items to be conjoined do not [both] appear. Nor is unification (<s>ekīkaraṇa</s>) the meaning of <s>adhyavasāya</s>. What is the meaning of 'unification'? If it means being productive of the attainment of unity—that is simply impossible, because the superimposed and the object of superimposition never become one. For there is no cause of a hare's horn. And 'what was formerly many now becomes one' is not tenable for the momentariness-doctrinalist at the present time. There could only be the production of a different entity. But that is not within the range of apprehension apart from the own-form, which is the object of superimposition. And even with that much, nothing [is accomplished] with respect to the [external] object—so how can there be unification?

body.text: athaikapratītiradhyavasāyaḥ / tathāpi na dvayorekapratipattiradhyavaseyānubhavābhāvāt / na ca dvayoḥ pratītirityevādhyavasāyaḥ nīlapītavat /
body.translated_text: If [it is said:] '<s>Adhyavasāya</s> is a single apprehension'—even so, there is no single apprehension of the two, because of the absence of experience of the object-to-be-determined. And it is not the case that <s>adhyavasāya</s> is the apprehension of two [things]—like blue and yellow [grasped separately].

body.text: na cābhedena pratītiradhyavasāyaḥ / yataḥ paryudāsapakṣe aikyapratītiruktā bhavati / sā ca pratyuktā, adhyavaseyapratipattyabhāvāt / bhedena pratītiniṣedhamātre 'pi na bāhyasya pratītirukteti kutastadadhyavasāyaḥ / yadi hi bāhyaṃ prakāśeta ekatvenānekatvena vā satā asatā vā pratītiriti yuktam /
body.translated_text: Nor is <s>adhyavasāya</s> an apprehension-as-non-different. For in the exclusion-alternative (<s>paryudāsa</s>), this amounts to an apprehension of unity. And that has been answered: because of the absence of apprehension of the object-to-be-determined. Even in [the alternative of] mere negation of apprehension-as-different, there is no apprehension of the external—so whence its <s>adhyavasāya</s>? For if the external were to appear—whether as one or many, as existent or non-existent—it would be proper to speak of an apprehension.

body.text: sarvākāratatsvarūpatiraskāreṇa sā pratītirityekapratītiriti cet / tatsvarūpatiraskāre tarhi tadapratibhāsanameva / kasyacidaṃśasya pratibhāsanāditi cet / na / niraṃśatvādvastunaḥ sarvātmanā pratibhāso 'pratibhāso veti śāstramevātra vistareṇa parīkṣyate /
body.translated_text: 'That apprehension is one in which the own-nature of that [external object] is concealed in every respect through all forms'—if the own-nature is concealed, then it simply does not appear. 'Because some aspect of it appears'—no, because the object is partless; [therefore] the teaching is examined here in detail: either it appears entirely or does not appear at all.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 135#)
na ca bhedāgraho 'dhyavasāyo vaktavyaḥ / tathā hi kiṃ bāhye gṛhyamāṇe 'gṛhyamāṇe vā / na ca prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ, bāhyagrahaṇasya pratikṣiptatvāt / grahaṇe vādhyavasāyasya pratyakṣatāprasaṅgāt / agṛhyamāṇe tu bāhye pravṛttiniyamo na syāt, anyeṣāmapi tadānīmagrahaṇādanyatrāpi pravṛttiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Nor should 'non-apprehension of difference' be called <s>adhyavasāya</s>. For is the external grasped or not? The first alternative is impossible, since the grasping of the external has been refuted. Or, if grasped, the <s>adhyavasāya</s> would absurdly become perception. But if the external is not grasped, there would be no restriction of practical activity, since other things too are not grasped at that time, and there would be the absurd consequence of activity toward other objects as well.

body.text: trilocano 'pītthamadhyavasāyaṃ dūṣayati / ko 'yamadhyavasāyaḥ / kiṃ grahaṇam, ahosvit karaṇam, uta yojanā, atha samāropaḥ / tatra svābhāsamanarthamartha kathaṃ gṛhṇīyāt, kuryād vā vikalpaḥ / na hi nīlaṃ pītaṃ śakyaṃ grahītuṃ kartuṃ vā śilpakuśalenāpi / nāpyagṛhītena svalakṣaṇena svākāraṃ yojayitumarhati vikalpaḥ / na ca svalakṣaṇaṃ vikalpagrahaṇagocaraḥ / na ca svākāramanarthamarthamāropayati / na tāvadagṛhītasvākāraḥ śakya āropayitumiti tadgrahaṇameṣitavyam / tatra kiṃ gṛhītvā āropayati, atha yadaiva svākāraṃ gṛhṇāti tadaivāropayati / nādyaḥ / na hi kṣaṇikaṃ vikalpavijñānaṃ kramavantau grahaṇasamāropau kartumarhati / uttarasmiṃstu kalpe 'vikalpasvasaṃvedanapratyakṣādvikalpākārādahaṅkārāspadādanahaṅkārāspadaḥ samāropyamāṇo vikalpena svagocaro na śakyo 'bhinnaḥ pratipattum / nāpi bāhyasvalakṣaṇakatvena śakyaḥ pratipattum, vikalpākāre svalakṣaṇasya bāhyasyāpratibhāsanāditi /
body.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s> too refutes <s>adhyavasāya</s> in this way: What is this <s>adhyavasāya</s>? Is it grasping, or producing, or conjoining, or superimposing? Now, how could a conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) grasp or produce an object that does not appear [in it] and is not an [actual] object? For even one skilled in crafts cannot grasp or produce yellow as blue. Nor can <s>vikalpa</s> conjoin the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), which is not grasped [by it], with its own form. For the particular is not within the range of conceptual apprehension. Nor does [<s>vikalpa</s>] superimpose an [actual] object onto its own form, which is not an [actual] object. First, [the own form] that is not grasped cannot be superimposed upon, so its grasping must be sought. There, does it first grasp and then superimpose, or does it superimpose at the very moment it grasps the own-form? Not the first, for a momentary conceptual consciousness cannot perform the two sequential operations of grasping and superimposing. In the latter alternative, the [object] being superimposed by <s>vikalpa</s>—which, unlike the own-form [that is] the basis of ego-sense, is not a basis of ego-sense—cannot be apprehended from the non-conceptual self-awareness-perception of <s>vikalpa</s> as identical [with the own-form]. Nor can it be apprehended as having the nature of an external particular, since the external particular does not appear in the conceptual form.

body.text: bācaspatirapi adhyavasāyaṃ pratikṣipati / anarthaṃ svābhāsamarthamadhyavasyatīti nirvacanīyametat / nanvayamāropayatīti kiṃ vikalpasya svarūpānubhava evāropaḥ, uta vyāpārāntaraṃ svarūpānubhavāt / na tāvat pūrvaḥ kalpaḥ, anubhavasamāropayorvikalpāvikalparūpatayā dravakaṭhinavattādātmyānupapatteḥ / vyāpārāntaratve tu kramaḥ samānakālatā vā / na tāvat kramaḥ, kṣaṇikasya vijñānasya kramavadvyāpārāyogāt / akṣaṇikavādināmapi buddhikarmaṇorviramya vyāpārānupapatteḥ na kramavadvyāpārasaṃbhavaḥ / anubhavasamāropau samānakālāviti cet / bhavatu samānakālatvaṃ kevalam / ātmā svabhāvasthita eva vedyaḥ, parabhāvena vedane svarūpavedanānupapatteḥ / tathā cātmā jñānasya grāhyagrāhakākāro 'nubhūto 'rthaśca samāropitaḥ / na tvātmā vedyamānaḥ samāropito nārthaḥ samāropyamāṇaḥ pratyakṣavedyaḥ / sa ca samāropaḥ sato 'sato vā grahaṇameva / na ca jñānātiriktasya grahaṇaṃ saṃbhavatītyupapāditam /
body.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s> too rejects <s>adhyavasāya</s>: 'It determines as an [actual] object what appears as its own [form] but is not an [actual] object'—this needs to be explained. Is this 'superimposition' by <s>vikalpa</s> simply the experience of its own nature, or is it a different operation from the experience of its own nature? Not the first alternative, because identity between experience and superimposition is impossible, since they have the natures of <s>vikalpa</s> and non-<s>vikalpa</s> respectively, like liquid and solid. If it is a different operation, [it occurs] either sequentially or simultaneously. Not sequentially, because a momentary consciousness cannot perform operations in sequence. Even for non-momentariness-advocates, since the operation of cognition and its object cannot pause and resume, sequential operation is impossible. 'Experience and superimposition are simultaneous'—let there be simultaneity, but: the self must be known as abiding in its own nature, since if known through another's nature, the knowing of its own nature would be impossible. And thus, the self of cognition, the apprehended-apprehender form, is experienced, and the object is superimposed. But it is not the case that the self is being superimposed while being known, or that the object is perceptually known while being superimposed. And that superimposition is simply the grasping of an existent or non-existent [entity]. And it has been demonstrated that the grasping of something other than cognition is impossible.

body.text: svapratibhāsasya bāhyādbhedāgraho bāhyasamāropastato bāhye vṛttiriti cet / sa kiṃ gṛhyamāṇe bāhye na vā / na tāvad gṛhyamāṇe / uktaṃ hyetanna tadgrahaṇaṃ saṃbhavatīti / agṛhyamāṇe tu bhedāgrahe na pravṛttiniyamaḥ syāt, anyeṣāmapi tadānīmagrahādanyatrāpi pravṛttiprasaṅgāditi / tasmād yathā yathāyamadhyavasāyaścintyate tathā tathā viśīryata eva / tathā vikalpāropābhimānagrahaniścayādayo 'pyadhyavasāyavat svākāraparyavasitā eva sphuranto bāhyasya vārtāmātramapi na (#Nibandh 136#) jānantītyadhyavasāyasvabhāvā eva śabdapravṛttimittabhede 'pi tatkathaṃ yuktyāgamabahirbhūto 'nātmasphuraṇamācakṣīta /
body.translated_text: 'The non-apprehension of the difference of one's own appearance from the external constitutes superimposition on the external, and hence activity toward the external'—is the external grasped or not? Not grasped—for it has been stated that the grasping of that is impossible. And if not grasped, when there is non-apprehension of difference, there would be no restriction of practical activity, since other things too are not grasped at that time, and there would be the absurd consequence of activity toward other objects as well. Therefore, however this <s>adhyavasāya</s> is analyzed, it simply falls apart. Likewise, [the concepts of] conceptual superimposition (<s>vikalpāropa</s>), identification (<s>abhimāna</s>), apprehension (<s>graha</s>), ascertainment (<s>niścaya</s>), and the rest—terminating only in their own forms when they manifest—do not know even a whiff of the external [object]. Being of the nature of <s>adhyavasāya</s> alone, even when there is a difference in the basis of verbal activity—how could one declare [that they] manifest what is not the self [of cognition], while standing outside reasoning and scripture?

body.text: nanvevaṃ vikalpādīnāmasaṃbhave saṃbhave 'pyanātmaprakāśakatvānabhyupagame sarvajanaprasiddhavidhipratiṣedhavyavahārocchedaprasaṅga iti lokavirodhaḥ / vikalpa ityadhyavasāyaityāropa ityabhimāna iti graha iti niścaya ityādikaṃ śāstre pratipadaṃ pratipāditam, tatsiddhaṃ ca bahirarthādikamabhyupagatamityācāryavirodhaḥ, nyāyavirodhaśca / tathā hi savareva prakārairaviparītasvarūpasaṃvedanād bhrānteratyantamabhāvaḥ syāt / tataśca sarvasattvāḥ sadaiva samyaksambuddhā bhaveyuḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: If <s>vikalpa</s> etc. are thus impossible, or even if possible, if their non-revelatory nature regarding non-self [i.e., external objects] is not accepted—then there would be the destruction of all the well-known practical activity of affirmation and negation familiar to all people; hence a conflict with the world. And in the <s>śāstra</s>, at every step, [terms such as] '<s>vikalpa</s>,' '<s>adhyavasāya</s>,' '<s>āropa</s>' (superimposition), '<s>abhimāna</s>' (identification), '<s>graha</s>' (apprehension), '<s>niścaya</s>' (ascertainment) have been taught, and the external objects etc. established thereby have been accepted—hence a conflict with the teacher. And a conflict with reasoning: for if awareness of one's own nature is in every respect non-erroneous, error (<s>bhrānti</s>) would be completely non-existent. And then all beings would always already be perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: vikalpitā buddhirbhrāntiḥ, svapratibhāse 'narthe 'rthādhyavasāyāditi cet / kathamavasīyamānastayā so 'rtho na prakāśate / prakāśamāno vā kathamasau tasyāṃ na prakāśate / atha prakāśata eva, tadārthasya tādātmyaprasaṅgaḥ / asati cārthe sārasyāt abhūnmāndhātā, bhaviṣyati śaṅkho 'styātmā, nityaḥ śabda iti sarvātmanā ca niścayaḥ syāt / gauriti spaṣṭena ca svena lakṣaṇena prakāśeta / svalakṣaṇe ca saṅketāyogāt vikalpikaiva sā buddhirna syāt / tasmādaśeṣagovyaktisādhāraṇena gotvena gobuddhiralīkena sābhilāpena viplavāt prakhyātīti tathā prakāśanamasyā gavārthāvasāya ityeṣṭavyam / evaṃ hyete doṣā na syuḥ, apratibhāsamānasyāpi svalakṣaṇasya bhrāntyāvasāyāditi //
