body.translated_text: 'Conceptualized cognition is error, because of the determination of an [actual] object in [what is merely] the own-appearance, which is not an [actual] object'—then how does that object, [supposedly] being determined by it, not appear? Or, appearing, how does it not appear in that [cognition]? If it does appear, then there would be the absurd consequence of the object having an identical nature [with cognition]. And in the absence of the object: 'There was <s>Māndhātā</s>,' 'There will be <s>Śaṅkha</s>,' 'The self exists,' 'Sound is eternal'—all these would be complete certainties. And [the cognition] 'cow' would appear with a clear particular of its own. And since convention is impossible with respect to the particular, that cognition would not be conceptual at all. Therefore, it should be maintained that the cow-cognition, through the universal cow-ness common to all cow-instances, is a conceptual cognition with verbal expression, appearing through the false [universal], becoming prominent; and thus her manifestation constitutes the determination of the cow-object. For in this way these faults would not arise, because the particular, even though not appearing, is determined through error.

body.text: atrābhidhīyate / na tāvallokaśāstravirodhau, agṛhīte 'pi bāhye pravṛttinivṛttyādisamarthanāt svaparavādiduratikramādhyavasāyasvarūpanirvacanāt / nyāyavirodhasya tu gandho 'pi nāsti /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: There is no conflict with the world or the <s>śāstra</s>, because even when the external is not grasped, the ability to account for practical activity and withdrawal is maintained, and because of the explanation of the nature of <s>adhyavasāya</s> that is insurmountable by proponents of both our own and opposing positions. As for conflict with reasoning—there is not even a trace of it.

body.text: tathā hi kā punariyaṃ bhrāntirasatkhyātiratasmiṃstadgraho vā yadabhāvādidānīmeva muktirāsajyate /
body.translated_text: For what is this 'error'? Is it the apprehension of the non-existent (<s>asatkhyāti</s>), or the grasping of that [which something is not] in that [which it is not] (<s>atasmin tadgraha</s>)—the absence of which would now entail liberation?

body.text: na tāvadādyaḥ pakṣaḥ, asatkhyāteḥ pratyākhyānāt / yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: The first alternative is not [tenable], because <s>asatkhyāti</s> has been refuted. As the teachers say:

children.text: yasya svarūpanirbhāso bādhakād yadi tanna sat /
children.translated_text: If [one says] the appearance of something's own nature is not real because of a sublating cognition—
what confidence is there even in the sublating cognition, which appears as another own-nature?
The removal of that [first] nature by the introduction of another nature—
regarding that [sublating cognition] too, doubt arises, from the observation of prior sublation.
If this non-apprehension [of the first] is the [only] sublation, and there is no other [sublation] for the first—
then let the first too have the manifestation of its nature equally.

children.text: nānyā va bhāvinītyatra pramāṇaṃ kiñcidasti vaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Nor will there be another [sublation]'—for this you have no <s>pramāṇa</s>,
since even when there is an appearance of own-nature, a sublating cognition is possible.
When there is non-appearance of own-nature and the examination of reasons collapses,
if there is such [collapse] even when the suspicion of sublation does not appear—then great indeed is the collapse. Thus.

body.text: śāstre ca atasmiṃstadgrahāt svapratibhāse 'narthe 'rthādhyavasāyād dṛśyavikalpyayorekīkaraṇād bhrāntiruktā / tāmayaṃ samarthayitumasamarthaḥ svātantryeṇālīkasphuraṇaṃ bhrāntiriti kāvyaṃ viracayya vistārayati //
body.translated_text: And in the [Buddhist] treatises, error (<s>bhrānti</s>) is said to consist in: the apprehension of X as Y (<s>atasmiṃs tad-graha</s>), the determination of [a non-existent] object in one's own appearance which is not [truly] an object, and the identification of the perceptible and the conceptual. Being unable to justify this [definition of error], [the opponent] composes poetry [i.e., fictions] such as 'error is the independent manifestation of the unreal' and holds forth...

body.text: nanvatasmiṃstadgraho 'pi bhramaḥ svākāraparyavasitajñānādatirikto bahubhirbahudhā vicāryaṃ pratyākhyātaḥ / tat kathaṃ tasminnapi pakṣe na bhrāntikṣatiryenedānīmeva muktiprasaṅgo na syāditi cet / tadetad bhagavato bhāṣyakārasya matavidveṣaviṣavyākulavikrośitamatikātarayati kṛpāparavaśadhiyaḥ / tathā hi samanantarapratyayabalāyātasvapratibhāsaviśeṣavedanamātrādagṛhīte 'pi paratra pravṛttyākṣepo 'dhyavasāyaḥ / na cāsau pūrvoktavāgjālaiḥ pratihantuṃ śakyaḥ, sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ pratyātmaviditatvāt, kaiścidapyanudbhinnatvāt / ayameva ca saṃsārastatkṣayo mokṣa iti kvedānīmeva tadvārtāpi / tathā hi vicitrānādivāsanāvaśāt prabodhakapratyayaviśeṣāpekṣayā vikalpaḥ kenacidākāreṇopajāyamāna eva bahirmukhapravṛttyanukūlamarthakriyāsmaraṇābhilāṣādiprabandhamādhatte / tataḥ puruṣārthakriyārthino bahirarthānurūpāṇi pravṛttinivṛttyavadhāraṇāni bhavanti / pṛthagjanasantānajñānakṣaṇānāṃ tādṛśo hetuphalabhāvasya niyatatvāt / aniścitārthasaṃbandhavikalpakāle 'pi sadasattānirṇayādipravṛttiprasavaḥ / tatra yadubhayathā pravṛttisādhanasāmarthyamasya svahetubalāyātamayameva pravṛttiviṣayatvāropo 'dhyavasāyāparanāmā / yathā candrādijñānasya bhrāntasyābhrāntasya vā taddarśanāvasāyajananameva grahaṇavyāpāraḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But the apprehension of X as Y has also been rejected in many ways by many [thinkers] as a form of illusion that is nothing beyond cognition confined to its own form. How then, even in that [your] position, is there no loss of error, so that liberation would not be absurdly entailed right now? [Reply:] This very [point]...

body.text: svavidapīyamarthavideva kāryato draṣṭavyeti
body.translated_text: Is to be understood on the basis of [the principle that] 'even this [cognition that is] self-aware is to be regarded functionally as object-aware' —

body.text: nyāyāt / tathā vikalpasyāpyagniratretyādinākāreṇotpadyamānasya pravṛttyākṣepakatvameva bāhyāvasānaṃ nāma / yathā ca nirvikalpadvicandrādyākārataiva tathāvasāyasādhanī, evamavasāyasyāpi tādṛśākārataiva viṣayāntaravimukhapravṛttisādhanī //
body.translated_text: By this reasoning. Likewise, even a conceptual cognition, arising with a form such as 'fire is here,' has as its external terminus precisely its capacity to prompt purposive activity. And just as in the case of non-conceptual [perception] the two-moon [illusion] and such, the having of that form is what establishes the determination, so too the having of that form by the determination itself [establishes the next step]...

body.text: nanu tathā ca tacca tena pratipādyate na ca tajjñāne tat prakāśata iti śapathenāpi na saṃpratyaya iti cet / asaṃbaddhametat / na hyadhyavasāyād bāhyasya paṭādervastuno bādhakāvatārāt pūrvasandigdhavastubhāvasya kṣaṇikāderavastuno vā śaśaviṣāṇāderasphuraṇe 'pi siddhipratibandho brahmaṇāpi pratividhātuṃ śakyaḥ / dvividho hi viṣayavyavahāraḥ, pratibhāsādadhyavasāyācca / tadiha pratibhāsābhāve 'pi parāpoḍhasvalakṣaṇāderadhyavasāyamātreṇa viṣayatvamuktam, sarvathā nirviṣayatve pravṛttinivṛttyādisakalavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgāt / tataśca tena ca tat pratipādyate na ca jñāne tatprakāśa iti saṅgatirastyeva, prakāśyaprakāśakabhāvābhāve 'pyadhyavasāyādhyavasāyakabhāvenāpi viṣayaviṣayibhāvopapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But [you say] 'that [external object] is conveyed by that [cognition], yet that [object] does not appear in that cognition' — even by taking an oath, there is no credibility in this. [Reply:] This is incoherent. For the previously doubtful status of the external real thing such as cloth is not [changed] by there being a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>) [intervening] after the determination...

body.text:
(#Nibandh 138#)
nanu yadi nādhyavaseyapratītistadāgṛhīte 'pi svalakṣaṇādau pravṛttiriti sarvatrāviśeṣeṇa prasajyeta, sarvatrāgṛhītatvena viśeṣābhāvāt, tataśca prāptirapi nābhimatasya niyamenetyanumānamapi viplutam / atra brūmaḥ / yadyadhyavaseyamagṛhītaṃ viśvamapyagṛhītam, tathāpi niyataviṣayaiva pravṛttirna sarvatra, tathābhūtasamanantarapratyayabalāyātaniyatākāratayā niyataśaktitvādvikalpasya / niyataśaktayo bhāvā hi pramāṇapariniṣṭhitasvabhāvāḥ, na śaktisāṅkaryaparyanuyogabhājaḥ, asadutpattivat sarvatrāsattve 'pi hi bījādaṅkurasyaivotpattiḥ, tatraiva tasya śakteḥ pramāṇena nirūpaṇāt / tathehāpi hutavahākārasya vikalpasya dāhapākādyarthakriyārthinastatsmaraṇavato hutavahaviṣayāyāmeva pravṛttau sāmarthyaṃ pramāṇapratītaṃ kathamatiprasaṅgabhāgi / pratyāsatticintāyāṃ ca tāttvikasyāpi vahnerjvaladbhāsvarākāratvaṃ vikalpollikhitasyāpīti, tāvatā tatraiva pravartanaśaktirjvalanavikalpasya na jalādau //
body.translated_text: [Nibandh 138] [Objection:] If there is no cognition of the thing determined, then even without apprehending the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) and such, purposive activity would absurdly follow everywhere indiscriminately, since there is no distinguishing feature because [the object] is unapprehended everywhere. And thus inference too would not [yield] the desired certainty through restriction [to a specific object]...

body.text: nanu ca sādṛśyāropeṇa kiṃ svākārasya bāhye svākāre vā bāhyasyāropaḥ / ubhayathāpyasaṅgati, āropyāropaviṣayayoḥ svākārabāhayayordvayorgrahaṇāsaṃbhavāditi cet / na vayamāropeṇa pravṛttiṃ brūmaḥ / kiṃ tarhi, svavāsanāparipākavaśādupajāyamānaiva sā buddhirapaśyantyapi bāhayaṃ bāhaye pravṛttimātanotīti viplutaiva saṃsārātmikā ca / yat śāstraṃ
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Is the [purposive activity based on] superimposition through resemblance a superimposition of one's own form onto the external, or of the external onto one's own form? In either case there is incoherence, because the apprehension of both — the superimposed and the locus of superimposition, i.e., the own-form and the external — is impossible. [Reply:] We do not say that purposive activity [occurs] through superimposition. Rather...

body.text:
na jñāne tulyamutpattito dhiyaḥ /
tathāvidhāyāḥ
body.translated_text: 'It is not that in knowledge [there is similarity]; rather, [the capacity comes] from the origination of a cognition [of a specific type].'

body.text: iti / tasmānna rūpyādivadāropadvāreṇa pravṛttirapi tu tathāvidhākārotpattipratibaddhaśaktiniyamāt / na ca vicārakasya vastvadarśananiścayādapravṛttiḥ saṅgacchate / darśane 'pi hi pravṛttirarthakriyārthitayā / arthakriyāprāptiśca vastusattāniyame / sa ca niyamo yathā darśanād vastupratibandhakṛtaḥ, tathā vikalpaviśeṣādapi pāramparyeṇa vastuprativastupratibandhakṛta ityadarśane 'pi adhyavasāyāt pravṛttiryujyata iti nānumānamanavasthitam / etena tacca na pratīyate, tena cābhedābhāsanamityupālambho 'saṃbhavītyupadarśitam, apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkaraṇamityabhedādiniṣṭhāyā darśitatvāt / tasmādavicāraramaṇīyo 'tasmiṃstadgraha eva bhrāntirāropāparanāmā, tatkṣayaśca mokṣa iti yuktam /
body.translated_text: Of such a kind — thus. Therefore, purposive activity does not [occur] through superimposition, as in the case of silver [on nacre] and such, but rather through the restriction of capacity that is bound to the origination of a form of that kind. Nor does the non-engagement [in activity] of the investigator square with the certainty of not seeing the real thing. For even upon seeing [the real thing], purposive activity is for the sake of causal efficacy...

body.text: yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: As the masters say:

children.translated_text: 'Therefore, since purposive activity is prompted by the origination of a conceptual form,
The superimposition of water and such too is considered equal between the real and the unreal.'

children.text: tato yadyapi tattvena nāropo nāma kasyacit /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, although in truth there is no superimposition of anything whatsoever,
This [superimposition], being made [only] for the sake of convention, cannot be denied.'
'Just as [there is the illusion of] water in a mirage, so [there is] the imagination of self in what is not-self;

children.text: bhrama eva hi saṃsāro nirvāṇaṃ tattvasaṃsthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: For <s>saṃsāra</s> is indeed error, and <s>nirvāṇa</s> is abiding in reality.'
[Nibandh 139]

children.text: tataśca yāvanna vicārasaṃbhavo bhavo 'yamanyaḥ śama ityayaṃ nayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, as long as investigation has not arisen, this is <s>bhava</s> (existence/suffering), and that [investigation itself] is <s>śama</s> (peace) — such is this teaching.

children.text: vicāralīlālalite tu mānase bhavaḥ śamo vā ka iheti kathyatām //
children.translated_text: But when the mind is graced by the play of investigation, who here can say "this is <s>bhava</s>" or "this is <s>śama</s>"?'

body.text: tathā āryamaitreyanāthapādā api
body.translated_text: Likewise, the noble <s>Maitreyanāthapāda</s> also [says]:

children.text: na cāntaraṃ kiṃcana vidyate 'nayoḥ sadarthavṛttyā śamajanmanoriha /
children.translated_text: 'And there is no difference whatsoever between these two — peace and birth — when [one abides] in the practice of the real object.

children.text: tathāpi janmakṣayato vidhīyate śamasya lābhaḥ śubhakarmakāriṇām //
children.translated_text: And yet, from the cessation of birth, the attainment of peace is prescribed for those who perform virtuous deeds.'

body.text: āryanāgārjunapādāśca
body.translated_text: And the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>:

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ ca bhavaścaiva dvayameva na vidyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> and <s>bhava</s> (existence) — these two do not [truly] exist.
The full understanding of existence itself is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: iti sarvaireva prakāśairaviparītasvarūpasaṃvedane 'pi bhrāntivyavasthāsaṃbhavādasti saṃsāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, since the establishment of error is possible even when all cognitions (<s>prakāśa</s>) have a non-distorted self-awareness, <s>saṃsāra</s> exists [conventionally].

body.text: yadapyuktaṃ vikalpasyāviṣayaśca bāhyam grahaṇaṃ cāsya śabdena saṃyojyeti vikalpatvamapi duryojam, ātmani ca śabdayojanā nāstīti vikalpo nāma nāstyeva, tatkasya vikalpacinteti / atrabhidhīyate / ihāgniratretyadhyavasāyo yathā kāyikīṃ vṛttiṃ prasūte tathāgnirmayā pratīyata iti vācikīmapi prasūte, etadākārānuvyavasāyarūpāṃ mānasīmapi prasavati / evaṃ ca sati yathā vikalpenāyamartho gṛhīta iti niścayaḥ, tathā śabdena saṃyojya gṛhīta ityapi, arthākāraleśavacchabdākārasyāpi sphuraṇāt / tasmādarthagrahābhimānavān mānavastāvadabhidhānasaṃyuktagrahaṇābhimānavānapītyavasāyānurodhādeva vikalpavyavasthā na tattvataḥ / yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: As for the further objection — 'the external is not an object of conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>), and its apprehension is to be conjoined with words, so the nature of being conceptual is also hard to establish; and since there is no conjunction of words with the self, conceptual thought does not exist at all — so whose is this analysis of conceptual thought?' — to this we reply: Here, [the word] 'fire'...

children.text: na śabdaiḥ saṃsargaḥ kvacidapi bahirvā manasi vā-
children.translated_text: 'There is no conjunction with words anywhere, neither externally nor in the mind —
But a fragment of the form of an object, pervaded by the form of syllables, flashes forth.
Though both forms belong to cognition alone, determination

children.text: vidhatte tau bāhye vacasi ca vikalpasthitirataḥ //
children.translated_text: Establishes them in the external [object] and in speech — hence the status of conceptual thought.'

children.text: abhāne pratibhāne vā na cāropo 'pi kasyacit /
children.translated_text: 'Whether [the object] does not appear or does appear, there is no superimposition of anything;
Such orderly arrangement is merely [established] through the distinction of dependent origination.'
'When, from non-conceptual [perception], there arises conceptual thought that partially resembles [it],
And from the utterance of one who has established the convention, [there arises] a distinguishing feature in the form of cognition —'
[Nibandh 140]

children.text: saṅketaḥ kṛta ityāsthā tādṛk śabdaśrutau punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The conviction "the convention has been established" [arises]; and upon hearing the word again,
The establishment of the expressed [meaning occurs] through the cognition whose nature is to prompt purposive activity.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tasmād vastu vā ghaṭapaṭādi sandigdhavastu vā sādhakabādhakātikrāntam, avastu vātmadikkālākṣaṇikādikamadhyavasitamiti, apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtamityarthaḥ / ayameva cāropaikīkaraṇādhyavasāyābhedagrahādīnāmarthaḥ sarvatra śāstre boddhavyaḥ / tasmādadhyavasāyasyākāraviśeṣayogādagṛhīte 'pi pravartanayogyatā nāma yo dharmastayā bāhyādhyavasāyayorgrāhyagrāhakabhāvaścet saṃvṛttyā duṣpariharaḥ, tadā viṣayiviṣayabhāvo 'pi labdha ityadhyavasāyamātreṇa viṣayaviṣayitvamuktamiti yuktam / yadāha alaṅkārakāraḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, whether [the object] is a [real] thing such as a pot or cloth, or a doubtful thing that has transcended both proving and disproving [cognitions], or a non-thing (<s>avastu</s>) such as self, direction, time, atoms, and the like — [in each case] it is determined, i.e., made the object of purposive activity even without [directly] appearing — this is the meaning. And this is the [true sense of] the terms superimposition, identification, and determination...

body.text: kathaṃ tadviṣayatvaṃ tatra pravartanāditi /
body.translated_text: How is [something] the object of that [cognition]? — because [one] engages [in activity] toward it.

body.text: etena yaduktam kathamavasīyamānastayātmārtho na prakāśyata ityādi, tannirastam, tadaprakāśe 'pi tadadhyavasāyasya vyavasthāpitatvāt / asati cārthe sā na syādityapyayuktam, ātmāderadhyavaseyasya pratibhāsapratikṣepe buddhyā saha tādātmyābhāvāt / na ca sarvākāraniścayaprasaṅgadoṣaḥ saṅgataḥ / sarvākāraniścayo hi sarveṣvākāreṣu pravṛttikārakatvātmā niruktaḥ, na caikākārollekhino vikalpasyākārāntare pravartanaśaktiranubhavaviṣaya iti kutaḥ śabdapramāṇāntarānapekṣeti yuktam / tatra nirvikalpakaṃ spaṣṭapratibhāsatvād grāhakaṃ vyavasthāpyate / vikalpastu spaṣṭaikavyāvṛttyullekhādāropakādivyavahārabhājanam / yathā ca bāhye sati kvacid bhramavyavasthā tathāntarnaye 'pi sarvatra / kevalaṃ bahirmukhapravṛtyapekṣayā kriyamāṇo nātmani kaścid bhrama ityuktaṃ bhavati / na ca gosvalakṣaṇaprakāśāvakāśaḥ, svākārasyaiva sphuraṇāt, svalakṣaṇe ca saṃketāyogāt / vikalpikaiva na syāditi tu svarūpāpekṣayā siddhasādhanam / bāhyāpekṣayā tvadhyavasāyavad vikalpikaiva sā buddhistathā / tasmādaśeṣagovyaktisādhāraṇena gotvena gobuddhiralīkena sābhilāpena viplavāt prakhyātīti tathā prakhyānamasyā gavāvasāya ityeṣṭavyamityapi neṣṭavyameva, caraṇamardanādinā pratyavasthāne 'pi yuktiśāstrabahirbhūtatvādetadabhāve 'pi kathitadoṣapradhvaṃsāt / na hi vikalpabuddhāvalīkākārasphuraṇameva bāhyasyādhyabasāya iti kācidarthasaṅgatiḥ, arthasyeti saṃbandhānupapatte / buddheratra kramābhāvāt pratyakṣataiva, kathamadhyavasāyaḥ / apratibhāsamānasyāpi svalakṣaṇasya bhrāntyāvasāyāditi tu na budhyāmahe / avasāyena hi tadvitisparśe pratibhāsaḥ ko 'paraḥ / tadvittāvapyaspaṣṭatvādadhyavasāya ityapyayuktam, tadrūpavittāvaspaṣṭatvasyaivābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: By this, what was stated — "How is the object, whose nature is being determined, not made manifest?" and so forth — that is refuted, because <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) of that is established even without its manifestation. And the claim that "it would not exist if the object is absent" is also unjust, because when the object to be determined, such as the self and so on, is denied in appearance, there is no identity with cognition. Nor is the fault of the consequence of ascertaining all forms applicable. For the ascertainment of all forms has been defined as having the nature of being a cause of activity toward all forms, and the capacity of a <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual thought) that apprehends only one form to impel action toward another form is not a matter of experience — so how is it justified to say it does not depend on scripture and other means of knowledge? In this regard, <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual cognition) is established as the apprehender because of its having clear appearance. <s>Vikalpa</s> (conceptual thought), however, because it clearly apprehends a single exclusion, is the subject of conventional practices such as superimposition. And just as there is the establishment of error somewhere when an external object exists, so too in the internalist view everywhere. The only difference is that with respect to outward-directed activity, no error regarding the self is being made — this is what is stated. Nor is there scope for the manifestation of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular) of a cow, since only one's own form flashes forth, and because conventional designation is impossible with respect to <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particulars). The objection "there would be no conceptual cognition at all" is, with respect to intrinsic nature, proving what is already established. But with respect to externals, that cognition is conceptual just like <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination). Therefore, the claim that "cow-cognition, through a universal 'cowness' common to all cow-individuals, being unreal and accompanied by verbal expression, manifests through error, and thus its manifestation is the determination of a cow — this should be accepted" — even this need not be accepted, because even when countered by foot-pressing and such methods, since it falls outside reasoning and scripture, and because the stated faults are destroyed even without this. For there is no logical connection in the claim that "the flashing forth of an unreal form in conceptual cognition is itself the <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) of the external," because the genitive relation 'of the object' cannot be established. Since there is no sequence in cognition here, it is perception itself — how can it be <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination)? As for the claim that "even a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) that does not appear is determined through error" — we do not understand this. For if there is contact with that thing through determination, what other appearance is there? And the claim that "it is <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) because of indistinctness even when that is cognized" is also unjust, because there is simply no indistinctness in the cognition of that form.

children.translated_text: There arose a mutual support among cognitions with respect to that object —
How can a single entity have a form that appears with different aspects?

body.text:
(#Nibandh 141#)
iti ācāryaḥ smaryatām / na ca tadāsau bhrāntirbhavitumarhati, vastusvarūpasyaiva nirbhāsāt //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Ācārya</s> (Master) should be recalled. And that cannot be an error, because what shines forth is the very nature of the real thing.

body.text: alīkavṛtteriti cet / saivāstu / bāhyasyāsphurato 'dhyavasāyaḥ katham / saiva sa iti cet / alīkamidamiti viduṣo bāhyādhyavasāyavyasthābhāvāt, bāhyāsphuraṇāt tadapratibaddhatvācca / pratibandhe 'pi tasyepi syāt, na punastadadhyavasāyaḥ, tadasphuraṇasphuraṇayorapi tadayogādityalamatinirbandhena / tadevamapratibhāsino 'pi vipakṣādadhyavasāyamātrasiddhādeva vyāvṛtto doṣatrayanirmuktaḥ prakāśamānatātmako heturyāvatprakāśāvadhijñānātmakacitrākāracakrasyaikatvaṃ sādhayatyeva //
body.translated_text: If one objects: "because of unreal cognition" — let it be so! How can there be <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) of the external when it does not flash forth? If one says "that itself is it" — because for one who knows "this is unreal," there is no establishment of external determination, because the external does not flash forth, and because cognition is not dependent on it. Even if there were dependence, that too would follow, but it would not be <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) of that, because both the flashing-forth and the non-flashing-forth of that are equally unsuitable for it — enough with this obstinacy! Thus, the <s>hetu</s> (logical reason), whose nature is being-manifest, which is distinguished from the opposite side through mere determination alone even though it does not appear, and which is free from the three faults, establishes precisely the oneness of the variegated circle of cognitive forms whose nature is cognition up to the limit of manifestation.

body.text: yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: As the masters say:

children.translated_text: What appears is one, just as the white form in a painting —
And the entire painting appears — yellow, cool, pleasant, and so forth.
Here there is no non-establishment of manifestation, since it is seen in the painting as the property-possessor.
Nor is the example seen to be devoid of the property to be proved.
Since each atom is submerged in another, cognitions do not perceive each other;
Nor is there manifestation of a single atom — therefore only the gross appears.
The appearance of external atoms is a single, gross cognition;
But what single appearance will there be for the atoms of cognition?
Therefore, the appearance pervaded by grossness, through the cessation of that,
Ceasing from multiplicity, is determined as unity.
Just as from that side of the homogeneous, the negation of difference from that part,
So too from the heterogeneous side, through the consequence of non-appearance.

children.text: tannāstu sādhyo dṛṣṭānto na ca śaṅkāviparyaye /
children.translated_text: Let neither the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) nor the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) be challenged, nor the reversal of the objection —
Therefore, from the faultlessness of the <s>hetu</s> (reason), the establishment of <s>citrādvaita</s> (variegated non-duality) stands firm.

body.text: saṃgrahaślokaśca
body.translated_text: And the summary verse:

children.translated_text: Just as the appearance accepted as unity by one with authority is pervaded,

children.text: sthaulyenāpyaṇuśo na hi kvacididaṃ svapne 'pi nirbhāsanam /
children.translated_text: By grossness too, atom by atom — for nowhere is this appearance even in a dream.
Therefore, since the elimination atom by atom has ceased, due to the departure of that which pervades it,
This assemblage of forms, encompassed by unity, shines forth.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: nanu cātra dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayorubhayamātrāpyekatvaṃ pratyakṣato 'numānācca viruddhadharmādhyāsalakṣaṇāt pratihatam, tat kathamanumānādekatvasiddhiriti cet / ucyate / yadetat pratyakṣaṃ bhedasādhakamupanīyate, tat kiṃ nīlādīnāmanātmabhūtamātmabhūtaṃ (#Nibandh 142#) vā / prathamapakṣe, āstāṃ tāvadeṣāmato bhedasiddhiḥ, sattāmātramapi na sidhyet / sa hi nīlādiko 'rtho jaḍo vijñānāntarātmālīkasvabhāvo vā svīkartavyaḥ / triṣvapi pakṣeṣu prakāśyaprakāśakabhāvābhāvaḥ / tathā hi jñānasya prakāśakatvaṃ nāma kiṃ vidyamānatvaṃ vyāpārāveśo vā / prathamapakṣe sarvasarvadarśitvaprasaṅgaḥ, sarvapuruṣajñānavidyamānatāyāḥ sarvaṃ pratyaviśiṣṭatvāt / tathā nīlādibhirapi jñānasya grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ, teṣāmapi vidyamānatvalakṣaṇagrāhakatvasaṃbhavāt //
body.translated_text: Now, if one objects: in both the example and the exemplified here, the unity of both is refuted by perception and by inference characterized by <s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s> (superimposition of contradictory properties) — so how can unity be established through inference? We reply: This perception that is brought forward as proving difference — does it belong to the non-self-nature of blue and so forth, or to their self-nature? In the first case, let alone the establishment of their difference from this, even their mere existence would not be established. For that object such as blue must be accepted as either inert, or having a nature internal to another consciousness, or having an unreal nature. In all three alternatives, there is absence of the relation of illuminated and illuminator. For what is the so-called illuminating capacity of cognition — is it being-existent, or the application of an operation? In the first case, there would be the consequence of everything perceiving everything, because the existence of all persons' cognitions is undifferentiated with respect to everything. Likewise, there would be the consequence of blue and so forth also grasping cognition, because for them too there is the possibility of grasping characterized as being-existent.

body.text: atha jñānatve sati vidyamānatvamiti saviśeṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇamucyate / tat kiṃ nīlādīnāmajñānatve kośapānamāyuṣmatā kartavyam, yena sattāmātreṇa samasamayaṃ sphuratorvijñānanīlādyoḥ pratijñāmātrādekasya jaḍatvālīkatvabādhyatvāprakāśatvādi vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: Now if a qualified definition is stated — "being-existent while being cognition" — then must one toast to the non-cognition-nature of blue and so forth? For when consciousness and blue etc. flash forth simultaneously with mere existence, on what basis is the inertness, unreality, sublatability, non-manifestness, and so on of one established by mere assertion alone?

body.text: atha dvitīyastadā sa kiṃ vyāpāraḥ pratyakṣasyātmā jñānāntaram, arthasyātmārthāntaraṃ vā syāt / prathamavikalpe svātmani kāritravirodhaḥ / dvitīyapakṣe jñānāntaraṃ yadyanyaviṣayam arthasya na kiñcit / tadviṣayatvaṃ cādyāpi na siddham, tatpratyāsattereva cintyamānatvāt //
body.translated_text: Now the second alternative: what would that operation be — the self of perception, another cognition, the self of the object, or another object? In the first option, there is a contradiction of activity upon one's own self. In the second option, if another cognition has a different object, it accomplishes nothing for the object. And the objecthood of that is not yet established, since it is still under investigation precisely because of its proximity to that.

body.text: tṛtīye punaḥ saṅkalpe nīlādikaṃ kṛtameva syāt, na prakāśitam, tailavartyādibhiriva pradīpaḥ / prakāśastu svayameva / tathā ca jñānāntaratvāt santānāntaravadapratibhāsaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the third alternative, blue and so forth would be made, not illuminated — just as a lamp is made by oil, wick, and such things. But light is self-originating. And thus, because it would be something other than cognition, there would be the consequence of non-appearance, as with another mental continuum.

body.text: caturthe tu vikalpe arthāntare kṛte nīlādikaṃ tadavasthameva / na cānātmaprakāśanasāmarthyaṃ jñānasya svīkartumucitam, vyāpāravat prakāśanasyāpyevaṃ nirākartavyatvāt / na cāgnidhūmayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāva iva jñānajñeyayorapi svābhāviko grāhyagrāhakabhāvo vaktavyaḥ, pramāṇasiddhakāryakāraṇabhāvavad grāhyagrāhakasvarūpayoradyāpi nirvaktumaśakyatvāditi kva nīlādivārtāpi yadbhedasiddhipratyāśā pratyakṣataḥ sampadyate //
body.translated_text: In the fourth alternative, when another object is produced, blue and so forth remain in their same state. Nor is it proper to accept that cognition has the capacity to illuminate what is not itself, because illumination, like operation, is to be refuted in the same way. Nor should one say that there is an intrinsic apprehended-apprehender relation between cognition and the knowable, as there is a cause-effect relation between fire and smoke — because the intrinsic natures of apprehended and apprehender cannot be articulated to this day in the way that the cause-effect relation is established by valid cognition. So where is even the mention of blue and so forth, that the hope of establishing difference through perception would be fulfilled?

body.text: athātmabhūtaṃ tat pratyakṣamiti dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadātmasvasaṃvedanameva bhedasādhakamabhyupagataṃ bhavet / tacca yadi pratyākāraṃ bhinnaṃ tadā sarveṣāṃ svasvarūpanimagnatvāccitraprakāśapraṇāśaprasaṅga ityuktam /
body.translated_text: Now the second alternative — that perception belongs to the self-nature — then what is accepted as establishing difference would be <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) of that very nature. And if that is different for each cognitive form, then because all are submerged in their own respective natures, the consequence would be the destruction of variegated manifestation — as was stated.

body.text: athaitaddoṣabhayāt sarveṣāmākārāṇāmekatvameva svabhāvabhūtaṃ svasaṃvedanamiṣyate, tadaitadeva citrādvaitaṃ vijñānamucyate, yadanekābhimatānāṃ sahopalabdhānāṃ nīlasukhādyākārāṇāṃ svabhāvabhūtākhaṇḍasvasaṃvedanapratyakṣaṃ nāma / yadāhurguravaḥ
body.translated_text: Now if, out of fear of this fault, the unity itself of all cognitive forms is accepted as their innate <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness), then precisely this is called <s>citrādvaita</s> (variegated non-dual) consciousness — namely, the <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) that is the undivided, innate <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) of the forms such as blue, pleasure, and so on, which are considered to be many and are cognized simultaneously. As the masters say:

body.text:
bhramābhramākalpanakalpanāni, śātāsitādīnyakhilākṣajāni /
jñānānyabhinnāni sahopalabdheḥ, pūrvāparatvaṃ tu na vedyameva // iti /
body.translated_text: "Cognitions born from all the senses — erroneous and non-erroneous, conceptual and non-conceptual, pleasant and white and so forth — are non-different because of simultaneous cognition; but temporal sequence is simply not perceived." Thus.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 143#)
tadevaṃ dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayorubhayatrāpi svasaṃvedanapratyakṣasiddhamekatvamavidyāvaśād vipratipattau satyāmanumānataḥ sādhyate / ata eva svasaṃvedanapratyakṣādanumānācca ekatvasiddhau na pratyakṣāntaram / nāpi viruddhadharmādhyāsalakṣaṇamanumānaṃ bhedasādhanāya prāptāvasaram, bhedagrāhakasya bhinnasya pratyakṣasyoktakrameṇāprāmāṇyāt, pakṣasya pratyakṣādibādhitatvāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, in both the example and the exemplified, the unity established by the <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) of <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) is proved through inference when there is, due to the force of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), a contrary understanding. For this very reason, when unity is established through the <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) of <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) and through inference, there is no other perception, nor does the inference characterized by <s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s> (superimposition of contradictory properties) obtain the occasion to establish difference — because the perception that would grasp difference, being itself differentiated, is non-authoritative in the manner stated, and because the thesis is sublated by perception and other means.

body.text: nanu brūyānnāma kiñcit, tathāpi pratibhāsabhedād bheda eva, na hi dṛṣṭe 'nupapannaṃ nāmeti cet / hanta 1 pratibhāsaśabdena kimabhipretam, kimākāracakraṃ sphuraṇaṃ vā / tatra yadi prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadā bāhye 'rthe pratyetavye buddhyākāraḥ pramāṇam / tathācākārabhedo vyavahartavya eva / anyathā bāhyabhedo na sidhyet / yadā punarākāracakrameva prameyam svasaṃvedanaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ tadā tenaiva nīlādīnāṃ svabhāvabhūtenākhaṇḍātmanā ekīkṛtānāṃ kathamapramādī bhedamācakṣīta /
body.translated_text: Now if one says: "Let something be said, still, because of the difference of appearances, there is difference indeed — for what is seen is not unreasonable" — well then! What is meant by the word 'appearance'? Is it the circle of cognitive forms, or the flashing-forth? In the first case, when an external object is to be cognized, the cognitive form is the means of valid cognition. And thus the difference of forms is indeed to be employed in conventional practice. Otherwise, external difference would not be established. But when the circle of cognitive forms itself is the object of knowledge and <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) is the means of valid cognition, then how could one who is not careless declare difference among blue and so forth that have been unified by their innate, undivided nature through that very <s>svasaṃvedana</s>?

body.text: dvitīyapakṣe tu sphuraṇaṃ svabhāvabhūtākhaṇḍasvasaṃvedanamevoktamiti / tathāpi kathaṃ bhedastasmād yathordhvamindriyapratyakṣataḥ kṣaṇabhede pratīte 'pyavidyāvaśādekatvādhyavasāyaḥ tathā tiryaksvasaṃvedanapratyakṣeṇākārābhede 'dhigate 'pyavidyāvaśādeva bhedāvasāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the second alternative, the flashing-forth has been stated to be the innate, undivided <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) itself. Even so, how would there be difference? Therefore, just as when temporal difference of moments is cognized through vertical sense-perception, there is nevertheless a determination of unity due to the force of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), so too when the non-difference of cognitive forms is apprehended through horizontal <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) perception, the determination of difference is due to the force of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) alone.

body.text: yadyevaṃ viruddhadharmādhyāsato vijñānākāracakravad vyāpto 'pi na bhidyeteti cet / na, bāhye dharmiṇyanekatvasya sādhyasya pratyakṣādyabādhitatvāt / buddhyākārakadambake tūktakrameṇa svasaṃvedanādisiddhaikatve 'nekatvasya pratyākhyānād bādhakāvatāra eva nāsti / tasmād vijñānatve satīti hetuviśeṣaṇaṃ kartavyam yena bāhyasyaiva bhedaḥ sidhyati //
body.translated_text: If one objects: "If so, then even the circle of cognitive forms of consciousness, though pervaded by <s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s> (superimposition of contradictory properties), would not be divided" — no, because in the case of external property-possessors, the plurality that is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is not sublated by perception and so forth. But in the case of the cluster of cognitive forms, since unity is established by <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) and other means in the manner stated, and plurality is thereby rejected, there is simply no entry for a sublating cognition. Therefore, the qualifying condition 'while being of the nature of consciousness' must be added to the <s>hetu</s> (reason), by which only the difference of the external is established.

body.text: nanu yadi vijñānātmakaṃ vicitrākāracakramekaṃ tadā nīlākāra eva pītādyākāravṛndaṃ praviśet / tathā prakāśākāracakrayorabhedo vyaktisāmānyavat prakāśa eva, ākāracakrameva vā syāditi cet / asadetat / tathā hi dvayorapyanayoḥ prasaṅgaviparyayayoḥ bhedaḥ, sa ca bāhyārthavāda eva yujyate, tatra bhedagrāhakasyendriyapratyakṣasyeṣṭatvāt / vijñānavāde tvanātmaprakāśābhāvāt svasaṃvedanamevaikaṃ pramāṇam / tato 'pi viparyayasya bhedasya siddheḥ prasaṅgo 'pyasaṅgataḥ ityadvaitameva /
body.translated_text: Now if one objects: "If the variegated circle of forms that is of the nature of consciousness is one, then the blue form would merge into the yellow and other forms. Likewise, the non-difference of the manifestation and the circle of forms, like universal and particular, would mean either manifestation alone or the circle of forms alone exists" — this is wrong. For the difference in both these consequences and their reversals is justified only in the externalist doctrine, because in that system, sense-perception that grasps difference is accepted. But in the consciousness-only doctrine, since there is no illumination of what is not the self, <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) alone is the single means of valid cognition. Since even the reverse — namely difference — is established from that, the consequence too is untenable — therefore it is non-duality alone.

body.text: kiṃ ca evaṃ sthūlanīlādyākāro 'pi paramāṇumātre praviśedityapratibhāsaṃjagadāpadyeta / asti ca pratibhāsaḥ / tasmād yathāvasthitānāmevākārāṇāmakhaṇḍasvasaṃvedanātmataivaikatvam, na bhedo na saṃkocaḥ svīkartavyo 'pratibhāsaprasaṅgāt / tathā kṛtakatvasyānityatvavastutvādibhirabhede kṛtakatvamevānityatvameva vā syādityapi prasaṅgo vaktavya āpadyeta, sāmānyavyaktyoriva tayorvastuto 'bhedo 'khaṇḍātmatvāt //
body.translated_text: Moreover, in this way even gross forms such as blue would merge into a single atom, and the world would become non-apparent. But there is appearance. Therefore, the unity of forms as they actually are consists in their having the nature of undivided <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) — there is no difference, nor should contraction be accepted, because of the consequence of non-appearance. Likewise, if <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being-produced) were non-different from <s>anityatva</s> (impermanence), <s>vastutva</s> (real-entity-ness), and so forth, the consequence would have to be stated that it would be only being-produced or only impermanence — but this consequence too would apply, since like universal and particular, their real non-difference is due to their having an undivided nature.

body.text: vyāvṛttibheda eva paramiti cet / yadyevaṃ prakāśanīlādyorapyayameva kramo jāgartītyekāvaśeṣaprasaṅgo bālapralāpaḥ / tadevaṃ
body.translated_text: Objection: The ultimate reality is merely the difference in exclusions. Reply: If so, then this same sequence applies to luminosity and blue and the like as well, leading to the absurd consequence that only one [entity] remains — this is the prattle of a child. Thus,

children.translated_text: [Nibandh 144]
The external does not perish, since even down to atoms it has existence; [and there would be] confusion of identity if causal efficacy were absent.

children.text: buddhistu naśyati bhidaiva vidaiva sattvāccitrāpyato na bhidameti kimatra kurmaḥ //
children.translated_text: But cognition perishes — division itself is awareness itself, since it is existence. The variegated [cognition] too therefore does not admit of division — what can we do about this?
Objection: The attainment of spatial extension does not belong to what is not separated from another self;
and it can also be said that without the loss of spatial extension, there is no appearance.

body.text: iti cet /
body.translated_text: If so objected,

children.translated_text: [Reply:] What is other than one's own self is another self — that applies only to the external. For cognition, which rests on self-awareness, what becomes of that which is other than it?

children.text: buddheḥ svavittiniṣṭhāyāḥ yaḥ parastasya kā gatiḥ //
children.translated_text: [This is the question.]

body.text: hanta tathāpi
body.translated_text: Yet even so,

children.translated_text: Objection: If it is one, like blue and the like, how does it come together?
Blue is a different part, and yet it is one — how does it appear as coherent?

children.text: neṣṭaṃ tadapi cet tarhi kvāṇvantarbhidi bhāsanam /
children.translated_text: If that too is not accepted, then where is the appearance within the division of atoms?

children.text: na parīkṣākṣamaṃ cāṇuḥ kutastasya tadā bhidā //
children.translated_text: And the atom cannot withstand examination — so from what source is its division then?
Objection: Let it not exist, because of being unreal. Reply: That too would follow upon the destruction of unity.
When unity is established through mere appearance, the reality of self-awareness is established.
Neither dependent origination nor non-origination is a contradicting factor for this,
since, even in the absence of unity and multiplicity, there is existence through mere manifestation alone.
Moreover, in non-duality there is no prior and subsequent cognition;
therefore, dependent origination, being itself unestablished, is also not a means of proof.
Non-origination too is inconclusive, having the form of neither effect nor cause;
even upon the abandonment of cause and effect, where would the manifest form go?
If the pervasion of real entities by unity or multiplicity were established somewhere,
the reason would destroy the desired position at the time of [asserting] universal emptiness.
Now, in worldly convention too, not everything conceived by all people

children.text: vastuvyavasthā śaraṇaṃ kiṃ tu mānena saṅgatam //
children.translated_text: constitutes the settled nature of reality — rather, [only] what accords with a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means).
And by perception and inference, nothing partless has ever been observed

children.text: yasya rāśiranekaṃ syānnāpi vastu ca kiñcina //
children.translated_text: whose aggregate would be a multiplicity, nor any real entity whatsoever [that is truly partless].
Let whoever maintains the pervasion of existence by either unity or multiplicity be refuted;
but the proponent of existence through mere non-erroneous awareness alone is victorious.

body.text: // samāptaścitrādvaitaprakāśavādo 'yam //
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Citrādvaitaprakāśavāda</s> (Doctrine of Variegated Non-Dual Luminosity).

children.text: grāhayaṃ na tasya grahaṇaṃ (na) tena jñānāntaragrāhayatāpi śūnyaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no grasping of it as an object of apprehension, nor is there any other cognition that grasps it;

children.text: tathāpi ca jñānamayaḥ prakāśaḥ pratyakṣapakṣastu tavāvirāsīt //
children.translated_text: yet the luminosity, consisting of cognition, appeared to you as the thesis of perception.

body.text: (#Nibandh 145#)
body.translated_text: [Nibandh 145]
Section 10:

body.text: // santānāntaradūṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: Refutation of Other Mind-Streams (<s>Santānāntaradūṣaṇam</s>).

body.text: atheha prakāśasahopalambhādisādhanabalena jaḍapadārtharāśāvapāste nīlapītādyaśeṣapadārthajāte ca svacittapratibhāsātmani svapnamāyādivadadvayarūpe siddhe santānāntarasadasattānirūpaṇārthamidamārabhyate /
body.translated_text: Now, here, when the entire mass of inert entities has been removed by the force of proofs such as co-apprehension with luminosity, and when the entire class of entities — blue, yellow, and so forth — has been established as having the nature of an appearance in one's own mind,

body.text: evaṃ hi kecidāhuḥ / astyeva santānāntaramanumānapratītam / tathā hīcchācittasamanantaravyāhāravyavahārābhāsasya darśanāt tadabhāve cādarśanādupalambhānupalambhasādhanamanvayavyatirekaśarīramicchācittena saha vyāhārādyābhāsasya kāryakāraṇabhāvamātmasantāne 'vadhāryecchācittasyāpratisaṃvedanasamaye 'pi vicchinnavyāhārādyābhāsadarśanāt tatkāraṇabhūtamicchācittamanumīyamānaṃ santānāntarameva vyavatiṣṭhata iti /
body.translated_text: some say thus: 'Other mind-streams do indeed exist, as known through inference. For one observes the appearance of verbal behavior and conventional usage immediately following a desire-mind' —

body.text:
atredamālocyate / tadicchācittaṃ vyāhārādyābhāsasya kāraṇatayā vyavasthāpyamānamanumāturdarśanayogyamatha dṛśyādṛśyaviśeṣaṇānapekṣamicchāmātram / yaditāvadādyovikalpastadānumāturdarśanayogyatvādicchācittasyānumānakāle 'nupalabdhirabhāvameva gamayatītyanupalambhākhyapratyakṣabādhitatvāt kvānumānāvakāśastasya / yadi punaricchācittamanumānakāle 'pyanubhūyeta, tadā kimasyānumānena / athaivamagnidhūmayostadutpattisiddhyanantaraṃ naganikuñje dhūmamupalabhamāno nāgnimapyanuminuyāt, tatrāpyagneranupalabdhibādhitatvāt, upalambhe cānumānavaiphalyāt / naivam, anumānasamaye deśaviprakarṣavato vahnerdarśanāyogyatvena dṛśyānupalabdhivirahāt, adṛśyānupalambhasya cābhāvasādhanatvavirodhāt / icchācittasya tu nāsti deśaviprakarṣaḥ / icchācittaṃ hi svasaṃbaddhamevānumāturdarśanayogyam, tasya ca deśādiviprakarṣa ityalaukikametat /
atha dvitīyo vikalpaḥ / tathā hīcchācittamātraṃ svaparasantānasādhāraṇadṛśyādṛśyaviśeṣaṇānapekṣaṃ vyāhārādyābhāsaṃ prati kāraṇatayāvadhāryate / tadavadhāraṇaṃ kena pramāṇena / vyāhārādyābhāsasya hīcchāmātrābhāve 'bhāvaṃ pratītya tadutpattisiddhigaveṣaṇā / na cecchāmātrasya svaparasantānasādhāraṇasya svasaṃvedanenānyena vābhāvaḥ śakyāvagamaḥ / yathā hi vahnimātrasya deśakālavyavahitasyāpi dhūmotpādadeśakālayoryadi syādupalabhyetaiva mayeti saṃbhāvitasyānumātṛpuruṣendriyapratyakṣeṇa (#Nibandh 146#) dhūmotpādāt prāgabhāve 'vadhāryamāṇastadutpattisiddhimadhyāsayatīti vyavahitadeśakālasyāpi vahnerdhūmamātraṃ prati kāraṇatvāvadhāraṇam, svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭasya tu jaṭharabhavādisādhāraṇasya sarvathānumātṛpuruṣāśakyābhāvapratītikasya vyāptibahirbhāva eva / tathātrāpīcchācittaṃ parasantānasādhāraṇamapi yāvadyadīya syādupalabhyetaiva mayeti yadi saṃbhāvayituṃ śakyeta tadā tadvyatirekasiddhidvāreṇa kāraṇatayāvadhāryate / kevalaṃ svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭe cittamātre 'stamiteyaṃ katheti //
body.translated_text: Here this is considered: Is the desire-mind, which is to be established as the cause of the appearance of verbal behavior and the like, such that it is fit to be perceived by the inferring person? Or is it to be established without distinguishing between the visible and the invisible?

body.text: na ca paracittaṃ kālaviprakṛṣṭaṃ vartamānatvādasya, atītānāgatayoreva kālaviprakṛṣṭatvena vyavahārāt /
body.translated_text: And the other's mind is not temporally remote from the present, since only past and future things are conventionally designated as temporally remote.

body.text: nāpi deśaviprakṛṣṭam, yasminneva hi śuklaśaṅkhādideśe svacittaṃ śuklākārapratibhāsi svasaṃvedanena vedyate taddeśavartyeva pītākārapratibhāsi parasantānabhāvi cittaṃ na vedyate / tat kathameṣa deśaviprakarṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Nor is it spatially remote, for at the very location where one's own mind manifesting a white-conch and the like is cognized through self-awareness — at that very location

body.text: athecchācittamātraṃ svasaṃvedanamātrāpekṣayā na svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭam / na hyagnirapyeko yenaivendriyavijñānena dṛśyate tenaivānyo 'pi dṛśyam / tatra yathā cakṣurvijñānamātrāpekṣayā agnimātraṃ dṛśyamiti vyavasthāpyate tathātrāpi svasaṃvedanamātrāpekṣayā icchācittamātraṃ svaparasantānasādhāraṇamapi dṛśyameveti /
body.translated_text: If the mere desire-mind is not essentially different with respect to mere self-awareness alone — for even fire is not perceived by the very same sensory cognition by which [something else is perceived]

body.text: atrocyate / kimatra mātraśabdenānumātṛpuruṣasaṃbandhāsaṃbandhābhyāmaviśeṣitaṃ yasya kasyacit puruṣasyendriyajñānaṃ vastuviṣayīkurvāṇamasya dṛśyatāsaṃbhave 'pinānimitamabhimatam / yadyevaṃ piśācādirapi dṛśyaḥ syāt / so 'pi hi kasyacit puṃso yogyādeḥ svajātīyasya vā piśācāntarasya bhavatyevendriyajñānagocara iti na kaścit svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭaḥ syāt / tasmādanumātṛpuruṣasaṃbandhitvamanapāsya vijñānasya svalakṣaṇādibhedanirāsapara eva mātraśabdo yuktaḥ / etadevāśaṅkaya dharmottareṇābhihitam -
body.translated_text: To this we reply: What does the word 'mere' mean here? Does it refer to a sensory cognition of any person whatsoever, without distinguishing between connection and non-connection with the inferring person?

body.text: ekapratipattrapekṣaṃ cedaṃ pratyakṣalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: 'This definition of perception is relative to a single cognizer' —

body.text: ityādi / tenaivaṃ dṛśyatāsaṃbhāvanā yadīha deśe kāle vā syād ghaṭādirniyamenopalabhyeta, madīyasya cakṣurvijñānamātrasya viṣayībhavediti / paracitte tu na śakyamevam / yadīha paracittaṃ syāt niyamena madīyasya svasaṃveda(na) mātrasya viṣayi syāditi //
body.translated_text: and so forth. Therefore, the supposition of visibility means: if an entity such as a pot were invariably perceived at this place and time, and if by my visual cognition alone

body.text: yadi cecchācittamātraṃ tadutpattigrahaṇasamaye dṛśyatayā saṃbhāvayitavyam, tadānumānakāle 'pi dṛśyatayā saṃbhāvya tadanupalambhenābhāvasādhane kathamanumānaṃ pravartayitumidamārabdham, pratyakṣeṇaiva pakṣabādhāt / na ca kālabhedena svabhāvaviprakarṣetarāviti yatkiñcidetat / tasmādicchācittamātrasya svaparasantānasādhāraṇasya dṛśyatayā saṃbhāvayitumaśakyatvāt vyahārādyutpādāt prāganupalambhe 'pyabhāvasiddhau na tadabhāvaprayukto vyāhārādyabhāvaḥ pratīyata iti kathaṃ kāraṇatvasiddhiryataḥ kāryahetudvāreṇānumīyeta / icchācittaviśeṣastu svasantānabhāvī na bhavatyevānumāturdṛśyaḥ / kiṃ tu tasya dṛśyānupalambhājjijñāsitaviśeṣe dharmiṇi bādhitasya kathamanumānamityuktameva //
body.translated_text: And if the mere desire-mind should be supposed as visible at the time of grasping its arising, then at the time of inference too, having supposed it as visible, and then not apprehending it,

body.text:
(#Nibandh 147#)
tadevamicchācittaviśeṣe svasantānabhāvini sādhye pakṣasya pratyakṣabādhaḥ, icchācittamātre 'pi svaparasantānasādhāraṇe sādhye yadyanupalambhamātreṇa dṛśya viśeṣaṇānapekṣeṇa pratibandhasiddhisamaye tasyābhāvaḥ pratīyate, tadā pakṣīkṛte dharmiṇi tatheti sa eva doṣaḥ / atha na pratīyate tadā sandigdhavyatireko hetvābhāso vyāhārādiriti sthitam /
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved) is a particular desire-mind existing in one's own mind-stream, the thesis is contradicted by perception; and even when it is merely desire-mind in general, whether one's own or another's

body.text: evaṃ tarhi santānāntarasādhakasyābhāvād bādhakasyāpi kasyacidadarśanādbhavatu tatra sandeha eveti kecit / tairidaṃ bādhakamabhidhīyamānamavadhīyatām / yadi hi santānāntaraṃ saṃbhavet tadā tato bhedena svasantānasyāvaśyaṃ bhavitavyam / anyathā svasantānādapi prakāśamānāttasya parasantānābhimatasya bhedo na syāt / na cābhedastayoriti svasantānād bhedābhedābhyāmabādhyasya parasantānasya sāmānyaśaśaviṣāṇādivadabhāva evāyāta iti kathaṃ sandehaḥ / tasmāt parasantānāpekṣayā svasantānasya bhedo 'pyavaśyambhāvyaḥ / sa ca bhedaḥ santānasya svabhāvaḥ svasantāne pratibhāsamāne niyamena pratibhāseta / kathamaparathā pratibhānāpratibhānalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmādhyāse 'pi svasantānasya parasantānād bhedaḥ svabhāvatāmāsādayet //
body.translated_text: Objection: Since there is no proof of other mind-streams and also no contradicting evidence is seen, let there simply be doubt about it. Reply: Some hold this. But this contradicting evidence

body.text: na cāsau bhedaḥ pratibhāsate / bhedapratibhāse hi upagamyamāne tadavadhibhūtasyāpi parasantānasya pratibhāso durapahnavaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: And that difference does not appear. For if the appearance of difference were accepted, then the appearance of the other mind-stream, which would serve as its delimiter, would also be irrefutable,

children.translated_text: Objection: 'This is different from me' — if this is the own-nature of one's own mind,

children.text: sāvadherasya bhāsaḥ syānna vā grāhyaṃ tadātmanā //
children.translated_text: then its appearance would have a delimiter, or else it would not be graspable in that form.

body.text: bhede 'nyaleśamapi naiti kuto bhinnaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the case of difference, it does not attain even a trace of the other — so how is there difference?

body.text: evamādikamaśeṣamiha pravacanapradīpaśrīsākārasaṅgrahādivacanamanusmaryatām /
body.translated_text: Thus all statements of this kind should be recalled from the <s>Pravacanapradīpa</s>, the <s>Sākārasaṅgraha</s>, and similar works of <s>Śrī</s> [<s>Jñānaśrīmitra</s>].

body.text: yathā hi svasantānamātre parisphurati śaśaviṣāṇādasphurato na bhedaḥ pratibhāti tathā parasantānādapi sphuraṇavirahiṇo na bhātyeva bhedaḥ / na hi parasantānāpekṣayā kaścid viśeṣaleśaḥ svasantānasya parisphurati yo nāsti śaśaviṣāṇāpekṣayā / na ca śaśaviṣāṇaparasantānāvapekṣya samāne svasantānapratibhāse śaśaviṣāṇāpekṣayā na bhedo nāpyabhedaḥ pratibhāti / parasantānāpekṣayā tu bheda eva bhātītyevamavasthāpayituṃ śakyam /
body.translated_text: For just as, when only one's own mind-stream is manifest, no difference appears from the non-manifest hare's horn; likewise, from another mind-stream too, which is devoid of manifestation, no [difference appears].

body.text: bhedābhedayorabhāvaparihāreṇa hi yathā bhedo vyavasthitaḥ tadvad bhedapratibhāso 'pi bhedābhedābhāvapratibhāsavilakṣaṇa evocito bhavitum, na ca tathānubhūyate / tathāpi bhedaḥ pratibhātīti vacanaracanametat / bhāṣyakāranyāyo 'pyatra bhedapratibhāsadūṣaṇe vistarato 'vagantavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For just as difference is established through the elimination of the non-existence of both difference and non-difference, so too the appearance of difference ought to be distinctly different from the appearance of the non-existence of both difference and non-difference. But it is not so experienced. [The statement] 'Nevertheless, difference appears' is merely verbal fabrication. The reasoning of the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) in the refutation of the appearance of difference is also to be understood here in detail.

body.text:
(#Nibandh 148#)
yadi cāvadhipratibhāsavirahe 'pi bhedapratibhānamidaṃ paracittānu(kampayā) kṣamitavyaṃ (tarhi) bahirarthasyāpi kathamabhāvaḥ sidhyati / śakyaṃ hi tatrāpi sandehamavatārayitum, na bahirarthaḥ kasyacidābhāsate, parasantānastu parasya pratibhāsata eva, tataścātraiva sandeho na bahirartha iti cet / etadapi sakalaṃ sandigdhameva / na hyavaśyaṃ parasantānaḥ parasyābhāsate, kadācidasau nāstyeva na cāsāvavabhāsata ityapi vaktuṃ śakteḥ /
body.translated_text:
(#Nibandh 148#)
If this [claim of] the appearance of difference is to be tolerated out of compassion for others' minds even in the absence of the appearance of a limit [between cognitions] — then how is the non-existence of external objects established [either]? For doubt can be introduced there too: no external object appears to anyone; another mental stream, however, does appear to another [person]. Therefore, doubt pertains only here [to external objects], not to other minds — if [you say] so, even all of this is simply doubtful. For it is not necessarily the case that another mental stream appears to another; one can equally say: perhaps it does not exist at all, and it does not [really] appear.

body.text: kiṃ ca mā nāma bhāsīṣṭa bahirarthaḥ kasyacidapi tathāpi kathaṃ tadabhāvasiddhirbhedapratibhāsābhyupagamavādina itīyanmātramiha vivakṣitam / na cātra kaścid doṣaḥ / tasmād bahirarthena sādhāraṇaṃ santānāntaramiti kathaṃ vijñaptivādināmapi saṃmataṃ bhaviṣyati / kiṃ ca kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pi vijñānadvayasya bhedapratibhāsavādinā bādhitumaśakyaḥ / pūrvabhāvinī hi saṃvittiḥ parasaṃvittyapekṣayā bhedaṃ pūrvatvaṃ cātmano gṛhṇātyevāvadhipratibhāsavigame 'pi //
body.translated_text: Moreover, even if an external object does not appear to anyone at all, how is the establishment of its non-existence achieved by one who accepts the appearance of difference? This alone is what is intended here. And there is no fault in this. Therefore, how will it be acceptable even to the proponents of <s>Vijñaptivāda</s> (consciousness-only doctrine) that another mental stream is on the same footing as an external object? Moreover, even the causal relation between two cognitions cannot be sublated by one who holds the appearance of difference. For a prior cognition, with respect to a subsequent cognition, apprehends difference and priority in itself, even in the absence of the appearance of a limit.

body.text: parabhāvinyapi saṃvittiḥ pūrvasaṃvittyapekṣayā bhedaṃ paratvaṃ cātmano 'dhigacchatyeva santānāntaravaditi niyatapūrvāparabhāvalakṣaṇe kāryakāraṇabhāve 'vabhāsamāne 'vasīyamāne ca nīlādicitrākāravat katham
body.translated_text: A subsequent cognition too, with respect to the prior cognition, apprehends difference and posteriority in itself — just as with another mental stream. Thus, when the causal relation characterized by invariable priority and posteriority both appears and is ascertained — like the variegated forms of blue and so forth — how [can you say]:

body.text: saṃvṛttyāstu yathā tathā
body.translated_text: "But as regards conventional [truth], let it be as it is" —

body.text: iti bhagavato vārtikakārasya vacanena phalitamatra mate / api ca citrākāracakre dharmiṇyadvaitasādhanārthamupanyastasya prakāśamānatvādihetorbhedagrāhakapratyakṣāpahṛtaviṣayatvamudbhāvayataḥ prativādino bhedagrahaṇamanumanyamānena santānāntarasandehaṃ ca vinā kathamuttaritavyaṃ bhavatā //
body.translated_text: This is what is entailed here in [your] doctrine by the words of the revered <s>Vārtikakāra</s> (the author of the <s>Vārtika</s>). Moreover, when the opponent, in the domain of variegated forms, raises the objection that the <s>hetu</s> 'being manifest' and so forth — which was presented for the purpose of proving non-duality in the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) — has had its object stolen by the <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) that grasps difference, and when you [the proponent] concede the apprehension of difference — how, without [also admitting] doubt about other mental streams, is [the opponent] to be answered by you?

body.text: nanvevamapi santānāntarābhāvaḥ kena pramāṇena siddhaḥ / na tāvat pratyakṣeṇa, tasya vidhiviṣayasya pratiṣedhasādhanātadhikārāt / nāpyanumānena, tasya dṛśyābhāvasādhananiyatasyātīndriyaparacittābhāvasādhane 'navatārāditi cet / atra brūmaḥ / santānāntarasaṃbhave niyatabhāvaḥ tatao bhedaḥ svacittasya / abhede svasantānāt parasantāna eva syāt / yathā ca yadupalabhyamānaṃ yenaṃ rūpeṇa na bhāsate na tat tena rūpeṇa sadvyavahārayogyaṃ yathā nīlaṃ pītarūpeṇa / nopalabhyate ca svacittamupalabhyamānaṃ parasantānād bhinne(na)rūpeṇeti bhedasya svacittatādātmyaniṣedhe dṛśyaviśeṣaṇaprayogānapekṣā svabhāvānupalabdhiriyam //
body.translated_text: Objection: Even so, by what <s>pramāṇa</s> is the non-existence of other mental streams established? Not by <s>pratyakṣa</s>, since that, having a positive entity as its object, has no jurisdiction to establish a negation. Nor by <s>anumāna</s>, since that, being limited to establishing the absence of visible things, cannot descend to the establishment of the absence of super-sensory other minds — [we reply:] To this we say: If other mental streams exist, then there is necessarily difference between them and one's own mind. In the absence of difference, the other stream would simply be one's own stream. And just as whatever is being apprehended, if it does not appear in a certain form, is not fit for the practical usage of 'existing in that form' — as blue does not [appear] in the form of yellow — so too one's own mind, though apprehended, is not apprehended as having a form different from another mental stream. Therefore, this is a <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s> (non-perception of an essential nature) which negates the identity of one's own mind with difference, without requiring the qualification 'visible.'

body.text: nāpyasiddhiḥ, bhedapratibhāse tadavadherapi pratibhāsaprāpteḥ / avadhyapratibhāse tu bhedapratibhāsābhāvaḥ śaśaviṣāṇabhedapratibhāsābhāvavat siddha eva / evamanena pramāṇena santānāntarasya svacittāpekṣayā bhede pratikṣipte abhede ca svayamevāsaṃbhavini bhedābhedābhyāmavācyatvaṃ siddham / sāmānyādivad vastutāpahatiriti, kathaṃ (#Nibandh 149#) bādhakābhāvāt santānāntare sandeho 'bhidhīyate / etacca śāstrīyaprameyasmāraṇamātraphalaṃ kiñcillikhitamiti / paramiha svayamanusandheyam /
body.translated_text: Nor is there non-establishment [of the <s>hetu</s>], since when difference appears, its limit too must appear. But when the limit does not appear, the non-appearance of difference is established, just as the non-appearance of the difference of a hare's horn is established. Thus, by this <s>pramāṇa</s>, when difference of another mental stream with respect to one's own mind is refuted, and when non-difference is itself impossible, the inexpressibility through both difference and non-difference is established — just like universals and so forth, [which are] negated in their reality. (#Nibandh 149#) How then, in the absence of a sublating [cognition], can doubt regarding other mental streams be asserted? This has been written as merely the fruit of recalling textual matters. The rest should be investigated independently by the reader.

body.text: api ca santānāntare tāvadarvāgdṛśāṃ sandeho bhavadbhiranumanyate / bhagavatastu kimavasthāpyatām / saṃdehāvasthāpane kathaṃ sarvajñatā / vidyamānameva kadācit santānāntaraṃ bhagavatā nāvadhāryate tathāpyasau sarvajña iti kathametat / anumānaṃ ca santānāntaraviṣayaṃ prāgeva cintitam / na cānumānena pratītāvapi sarvajñatā bhavitumarhati / pratyakṣeṇa paracittapratītau grāhyagrāhakabhāvo 'pi paracittasya bhagavaccittena sahāyāta iti bahirarthavāda eva mukhāntareṇopagataḥ syāt, kathamayaṃ vañcayati vādaḥ //
body.translated_text: Moreover, you [Buddhists] concede that ordinary people have doubt regarding other mental streams. But what is to be established regarding the <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Blessed One, the <s>Buddha</s>)? If doubt is posited [even for him], how can there be <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)? If perhaps other mental streams do exist, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> at some point does not ascertain them — yet he is still omniscient — how is that [consistent]? And inference regarding other mental streams has already been considered earlier. But even if [other minds] are cognized through inference, omniscience cannot be established thereby. If other minds are cognized through <s>pratyakṣa</s>, then the relation of apprehended and apprehender between other minds and the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mind would also arise — and thus the doctrine of external realism would have been adopted by another route. How does this [<s>Vijñaptivāda</s>] doctrine not become self-deceptive?

body.text: asmadīyamatena tu paracittaṃ nāstyeveti tadavadhāraṇakṛto(na) bhagavataḥ sarvajñatākṣatidoṣaḥ / yāvacca bhedagrahaṇābhimānarūpā saṃvṛsttitāvat santānāntare sandehāttadavabodhanārthaṃ vacanādirapi pravartata iti svavacanavirodho 'pi na saṃbhavatyeva / na khalu santānāntaraviṣayaḥ sarvathā sandeho nāstyevetyabhimatamasmākam, api tu paramārthagatiriyamupadarśitā / idaṃ hi santānāntarābhāvasādhanamadvayasādhanena sādhāraṇamiti naikaniyataḥ svavacanādivirodhastatparihāro vā / citrākārasaṃbhavamātreṇāpi ca vedāntadhvāntāpasāro bhāṣyakāreṇa darśitaḥ / tathā ca
body.translated_text: On our own view, however, other minds simply do not exist; therefore, the fault of any diminution of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) due to [failure to] ascertain them does not arise. And as long as the conventional [truth] in the form of the notion of grasping difference [persists], so long [do] verbal teaching and so forth proceed regarding other mental streams for the purpose of communicating understanding — hence no contradiction with one's own statements is even possible. For it is not our position that doubt regarding other mental streams is entirely nonexistent in every respect; rather, this is the ultimate purport that has been shown. For this proof of the non-existence of other mental streams is shared with the proof of non-duality; hence [any objections such as] self-contradiction and the like, or their resolution, are not confined to this [topic] alone. And the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> has shown that even through the mere possibility of variegated appearances [within a single consciousness], the darkness of <s>Vedānta</s> is dispelled. And thus —

body.text: ātmā sa tasyānubhavaḥ sa ca nānyasya kasyacit
body.translated_text: "The self is that [consciousness]; its experience belongs to no other whatsoever" —

body.text: ityādivārtikavyākhyānabhāṣyam /
body.translated_text: so states the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) on the <s>Vārtika</s>.

body.text: ātmavādastarhi prasakta iti cet / na citrākārasaṃvedanāt ityādi dveṣavikaluṣāśeṣā eva tuṣākāro 'pi vedāntasiddhānta iti alakṣita tadgranthānutthāpayantī santānāntarāpekṣayā paṭhitavatītyavasthā (?) sarvā saṃvṛtisatyāntaḥ pātinī hyevāpai(tī) ti sakalamanākulamiti //
body.translated_text: If [the objection is raised:] then the doctrine of a [permanent] self would follow — [the reply is:] No, because of the awareness of variegated forms — and so forth. The entirety of the <s>Vedānta</s> position, which is entirely free from the stain of aversion, is even of the nature of a husk [devoid of kernel]. [This passage], composed without raising those texts, was recited with reference to other mental streams — this is the situation (?). All [of this] falls within the scope of <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth), for it [the investigation] indeed departs [at the ultimate level]. Thus everything is without confusion.

body.text: // santānāntaradūṣaṇaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Santānāntaradūṣaṇam</s> (Refutation of Other Mental Streams) is concluded.
